en: Those who move as thrice-seven, bearing all forms—may the Lord of Speech today bestow their powers and bodies upon me. (1)
Come back again, O Lord of Speech, together with the divine mind.
O Lord of Wealth, cause [the word] to rest within me; let what has been heard abide in me.
Right here, let the Lord of Speech bind both these bodies together like two notches with a bowstring; let there be [the power of] hearing in me alone, in me alone. //3//
The Lord of Speech has been invoked; may the Lord of Speech invoke us.
May we be united with what is heard; may I not be deprived of what is heard.
We know Parjanya, the father of the arrow, the one who bestows abundant nourishment;
we know his mother, the earth, who possesses manifold forms. //1//
(2a) Bend around us like a bowstring; make our bodies as hard as stone.
(2c) Make us firm and more spacious; drive away hostilities and enmities. //2//
When the cows, embracing the tree, sing their praise to the quivering arrow, the skillful one—O Indra, ward off that arrow, that missile, from us. 3.
Just as the shaft stands between heaven and earth,
so may the muñja grass stand within to hold back both disease and discharge.
We know Parjanya, the father of the arrow, who possesses a hundredfold virility.
With him, I shall bring well-being to your body; let your outpouring be upon the earth, and let your residue be outside, O Bāla.

We know the father of the arrow, Mitra, who possesses a hundredfold virility. With him, I shall bring well-being to your body. May your outpouring be upon the earth; let your residue be outside, [saying] "bāl."

We know the father of the arrow, Varuṇa, who possesses a hundredfold virility; with him, may I bring well-being to your body. Let your outpouring be upon the earth; let your residue be outside, [as] *bāh*. //3//
We know the father of the arrow, the moon, possessed of a hundred virile powers;
with that, may I bring well-being to your body. May your discharge be upon the earth; let your residue be outside. //4//

We know the father of the arrow, Sūrya, who possesses a hundredfold virility; with him, I shall bring well-being to your body. May your outpouring be upon the earth; let your residue be outside. //5//
Whatever [is stuck] in the entrails, in the two groins, or whatever has settled upon the bladder—
let your urine be released thus, outside, O Bāla, with all its force.
I split open your urethra as one splits the dam of a river;
thus let your urine flow out—bāl iti sarvakam. //7//
Your bladder-duct is opened wide like that of the ocean, the great sea;
even so let your urine be released outside—thus for all [the ailments]. 8.
Just as an arrow flies away when released from the bow, even so let your urine be discharged; "outwardly, O Bāla!"—thus [it is] for all purposes. 9.
The mothers go along their paths, the sisters of those performing the sacrifice,
blending milk with honey.
Those [waters] which are near the sun, or those with which the sun is joined—
may they speed our sacrifice.
I invoke the divine waters where our cattle drink;
an oblation is to be prepared for the rivers.
Within the waters is immortality; within the waters is healing.
And by the praises of the waters, may you become swift horses, O steeds; may you become vigorous cows. 4.
O Waters, you are indeed sources of bliss;
grant us strength for great joy and for the sake of vision.
Whatever most auspicious essence you possess, grant us a share of it here,
like longing mothers.
To him for whose abode you quicken us, to him let us go readily;
O Waters, give us life. 3.
Mistresses of all desirable things, ruling over the peoples—I beg the waters for healing. //4//
May the divine waters be auspicious for our aid and for our drink;
may they flow toward us with peace and well-being. //1//
Soma has told me that within the waters are all healing medicines, and Agni, the source of universal well-being.
O Waters, provide healing medicine as a protection for my body, so that I may long behold the sun. //3//

May the waters of the desert be auspicious to us, and may the waters of the marshes be auspicious; may the waters dug from the earth be auspicious to us, and those brought in jars be auspicious; may the waters of the rainy season be gracious to us. //4//
O Agni, bring here the sorcerer and the Kimīdin who praises [thee];
for you, O God, when lauded, have become the slayer of the Dasyu.
O Agni, supreme lord, knower of all beings, master of your own body, consume the clarified butter of the *taula* plant; cause the sorcerers to wail.
Let the sorcerers, the devouring *attri*s, and those who are *kimīdin*s, cry out.
And now, O Agni, may you and Indra both graciously accept this our oblation. 3.
Let Agni take hold first; let Indra, the possessor of the arm, drive it away.
Let every sorcerer come and say, "I am this one. 4.
May we behold your power, O Jātavedas; proclaim to us, O observer of men, the sorcerers.
Let them all, scorched by you from of old, come hither confessing this.
Take hold, O Jātavedas; you have been born for our sake.
Having become our messenger, O Agni, cause the sorcerers to wail.
O Agni, bring here the sorcerers who are bound;
then may Indra shatter their heads with his thunderbolt.
(1.8.1a) This oblation carries away the sorcerers like foam from the river.
(1.8.1c) Whether it was a woman or a man who performed this here, let that person be praised. //1//
This one has come praising; welcome him!
O Bṛhaspati, having brought him under your control, O Agni and Soma, pierce him through! 2.
O Soma-drinker, destroy the offspring of the sorcerer and lead them away. Strike down both the upper and lower eye of the one who reviles you.
O Agni Jātavedas, where you know the secret births of these devouring demons who dwell in hiding—
strengthened by our prayer, O Agni, strike them down, crushing them by the hundreds.
In this [world], may the Vasus hold wealth—the Vasus, Indra, Pūṣan, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni.
And may the Ādityas and all the gods hold him in the higher light. //1//
May there be light in his direction—Sūrya, Agni, or even gold, O gods!
May our rivals be lower than we; may we cause him to ascend to the highest heaven. 2.
O Jātavedas, with that supreme prayer by which you brought forth the milks for Indra, with that do you, O Agni, cause this man to prosper here; bestow upon him preeminence among his kinsmen. //3//
From them I have taken the sacrifice and the luster, O Agni, as well as the increase of wealth and their thoughts.
May our rivals be lower than we; may we cause this man to ascend to the highest heaven. 4.
This Asura of the gods rules far and wide, for he is the true sovereign will of King Varuṇa.
From there, exulting through the sacred word (*brahman*), I lead this man forth from the fierce wrath of the Mighty One.
Homage be to you, O King Varuṇa, and to your wrath; for you, O fierce one, perceive every act of malice.
I release thousands of others at once; may this man live a hundred autumns under your protection.
Whatever falsehood you have spoken with your tongue, whatever many crooked things— From King Varuṇa, whose law is truth, I release you. //3//
I release you from Vaiśvānara, from the great ocean on every side.
Speak here to your kinsmen, O fierce one, and perform our sacred prayer (*brahman*). 4.
“Vaṣaṭ to you, O Pūṣan! May Aryaman, the wise Hotṛ-priest, perform this at this birth.
Let the women, having given birth in accordance with the cosmic order (*ṛta*), move away; let her joints relax so that she may give birth. (AVŚ 1.11.1)
The four quarters of heaven and the four of earth—the gods have impelled the embryo; may they unfold it for birth.
May Sūṣā draw it forth; we cause the womb to open wide.
O Sūṣaṇā, loosen it; do you release it, O Biṣkalā. 3.
Neither in the flesh, nor in the fat, nor in the marrow have you struck me. Let the speckled placenta go away; let the afterbirth fall off for the dog to eat. //4//
I split open your urethra, I split open the womb, and I split open the two labia.
I split apart both mother and son; let the child fall away from the afterbirth. //5//
As the wind, as the mind, as birds fly, so do you, O ten-month-old one, fly forth together with the afterbirth; let the afterbirth fall away.
The first-born of the dawn, born from the womb, the bull born of wind and cloud, goes thundering with rain.
May he, moving straight, breaking [the obstacles], who strode out the single [universe] threefold by his might, be gracious to our bodies.
Resting limb upon limb with your radiance, we shall worship you with oblation while paying homage.
We shall worship with oblation those who have joined the joints together, he who has grasped its knuckles and seized its parts. 2.
Release him from headache and from cough; let that which has entered him joint by joint depart.
Let the vigor born of the clouds and born of the wind attend upon the trees and the mountains.
May there be well-being for my upper body; may there be well-being for my lower body. May there be well-being for my four limbs; may there be well-being for my entire frame. 4.
Homage be to you, O lightning; homage be to you, O thunder.
Homage be to you, O stone, with which you strike the ill-sacrificer.
Homage to you, O grandson of the mountain, from whom you gather heat!
Be gracious to our bodies; grant well-being to our offspring.
O Son of the Slopes, let there be homage indeed to you; we offer homage to your weapon and to your heat.
We know your supreme abode which is in secret; you are the navel placed within the ocean. 3.
O Goddess, you whom all the gods created, fashioning you into a bold arrow for the purpose of striking—may you be gracious to us in the assembly while being praised; homage be to you, O Goddess! 4.
I have taken her fortune and her splendor from you, like a garland from a tree.
Like a mountain with a vast base, may she remain long among her fathers.
O King Yama, let this maiden, your bride, be set down for you;
let her be bound in the house of her mother, and likewise in the house of her brother and her father.
This is your family-guardian, O King; we entrust her to you.
May she sit long among the ancestors, from the head down to the soles of the feet. //3//
By the sacred word (*brahman*) of Asita, of Kaśyapa, and of Gaya, I bind your vulva, O sister, like a sheath within a chest. 4.
(1) May the rivers flow together; may the winds and the winged birds come together.
May they take pleasure in this sacrifice of mine from of old; I offer with an oblation that flows together. //1//
Come here indeed to my call; come here to these libations and cause these songs of praise to increase.
Let every animal that exists come here; let whatever wealth there is remain in this place.
Those perennial, inexhaustible springs that flow from the rivers—with all those flowing waters, we cause wealth to flow together for me. 3.
Whatever flows together of clarified butter, of milk, and of water—with all those outpourings, we cause wealth to flow together for me. //4//
Those devourers who rose up against the pen on this night of the new moon—
may Agni, the fourth slayer of demons, speak for our protection.
Upon lead Varuṇa speaks; upon lead Agni bestows his favor.
Indra gave me lead; that indeed is the dispeller of the malevolent spirits.
This [charm] overcomes Viṣkandha; this drives away the devourers.
By means of this, I have overcome all the creatures born of Piśācī.
Whether you kill our cow, or our horse, or our man—
we pierce you with lead so that he shall not be a slayer of our heroes.
Those women who go there, the veins clothed in red—
like sisters without brothers, let them stand, their luster destroyed.
Stand still, O lower one; stand still, O upper one; and you too, stand still, O middle one!
Let the smallest one stand still, and let this great vein stand still as well.
Of the hundred arteries and the thousand veins, these middle ones have stood firm; their ends have come to rest together.
The great, sandy bow has stepped around you;
stand still and rest well.
We drive away misfortune, we drive away that which is loathsome, we drive away the enemy.
And those things which are auspicious, those we bring to our offspring; we lead the enemy away from them. //1//
Savitṛ has impelled the fire-drill from our feet; Varuṇa, Mitra, and Aryaman have impelled it from our hands.
Anumati, bestowing gifts upon us, has impelled it; the gods have impelled this [fire] for our good fortune.
Whatever terrible thing is in your self, in your body, or whatever is in your hair or in your gaze—all that we drive away with our speech; may the god Savitṛ prepare you for us. 3.
Riśyapadī, Vṛṣadatī, Goṣedhā, and Vidhamā;
Vilīḍhyā and Lalāmyā—these we cause to perish away from us. 4.
Let not those who pierce from afar find us, nor let those who pierce from close by find us;
O Indra, strike down the arrows far away from us in all directions.
Let our missiles fly in all directions—those that are thrown and those that belong to her.
O divine impetuses of men, pierce through my enemies! 2.
Whoever is our own kin, whoever is a stranger, whether a fellow clansman or a foreigner, whoever assails us—may Rudra pierce all these enemies of mine with his arrow. 3.
Whoever is our rival, whoever is not our rival, and whoever, being an enemy, lies in wait for us—may all the gods destroy him; may the sacred word (*brahman*) be my inner armor. 4.
O divine Soma, may you not be one who causes the breaking of the house; O Maruts, be gracious to us at this sacrifice.
Let not the overpowering one find us, nor the curse; let not the crooked, hateful things find us. //1//
Whatever murderous weapon of the wicked ones rises up today against the army,
O Mitra and Varuṇa, keep that far away from us.
Whatever [threat] comes from here and whatever from there, O Varuṇa, ward off that slaughter. Extend great protection; grant us wider space and ward off the slaughter.
(4a) Thus you are a great ruler, O conqueror of enemies, invincible;
(4c) he whose friend is never slain nor ever overcome. //4//
Bestower of well-being, Lord of the people, slayer of Vṛtra, dispeller of foes, the controller;
may the bull-like Indra, the Soma-drinker who grants fearlessness, go before us. //1//
O Indra, strike down our adversaries; cast those who attack us low. Send into the deepest darkness him who seeks to harm us.
Drive away the Rakṣas, strike down the adversaries; break apart the jaws of Vṛtra.
O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, drive away the fury of the enemy who assails us.
O Indra, turn away the mind of the hater, turn away the weapon of him who seeks to conquer us.
Grant us great protection, grant it more widely, and drive away the weapon.
May the heart-glittering and the jaundice depart after the rising sun;
with the color of the red cow, with that we enclose you. //1//
We clothe you in ruddy colors for the sake of long life,
so that this man may be free from disease and likewise free from jaundice.
The cows whose deity is Rohiṇī, and those which are themselves ruddy—of every form and every age, with them we enclose you. 3.
We place your yellowness in the parrots, in the *ropaṇākās*; and so we deposit your yellowness in the *hāridravas*. //4//
Born at night, O herb, you are lovely, dark, and blackish; O dyer, dye this away—the leprosy and whatever is gray. 1.1
O spotted one, drive away and destroy from here both leprosy and gray hair! Let your own natural color enter you; cast off the white hairs! 2.
Black is your dissolution, black is your abode; O herb, you are black—drive away the speckled one from here! 3.
The white mark caused by bone-born leprosy, skin-born leprosy, and that which is produced on the skin by a corrupting agent—by means of this *brahman*, I have destroyed it. 4.
The first-born was Suparṇa; you were his bile. Then the Asurī, conquered in battle, took on the form of the trees.
The daughter of Asura first prepared this medicine for leprosy; it is the destroyer of leprosy. It has destroyed the leprosy and made the skin uniform in color.
Sarūpā is the name of your mother, Sarūpa is the name of your father;
you, O herb, are a maker of likeness—make this one like unto him.
The dark one, the maker of beauty, raised up from the earth;
accomplish this well, fashion the forms anew! 4.

When Agni, having entered the waters, burned them, where those who uphold the cosmic order (dharmadhṛt) offered their salutations—there they say is your highest place of origin; O Takman, knowing this, spare us. 1.
Whether you are the flame or the glowing heat, whether you are in the wood-chip or in your place of birth—O god, whose name is Hrūḍu of the green [wood], being well-aware, spare us from *takman*! 2.
Whether you are sorrow, or affliction, or the son of King Varuṇa; O god, you whose name is Hrūḍu, belonging to the green one—being fully aware, spare us from Takman. 3.
Homage to the cold fever, homage to the burning glow; I pay homage to the fever that comes on the next day, on both days, and every third day—to that fever, let there be homage. //4//
May that weapon of yours, O gods, be far from us;
may the stone you hurl be far away. //1//
May he be our friend, a gift; may Indra, Bhaga, and Savitṛ of wondrous bounty be our friends. //2//
O Maruts, you who are the grandsons of the mountain and possess sun-bright skins,
grant us wide-reaching protection.
Be well-prepared; be gracious; have mercy upon our bodies. Grant happiness to our offspring. 4.
Those three times seven egg-born serpents are on the far shore;
with their shells we wipe away the eyes of the malevolent one who lies in wait as an adversary.
Let her go away in all directions, cutting [us] down like one bearing a bow; let the ill-intentioned ones, unsuccessful in their minds, go forth everywhere again and again. 2.
The many were not able; the small ones did not dare to attack.
Like the joints of a bamboo on both sides, the malevolent ones have failed to prosper.
O departed one, let your feet quiver; carry [the offerings] to the houses of those who give.
Let Indrāṇī go first, unconquered and unharmed, before us.
The divine Agni has arrived, the slayer of demons, the driver away of disease;
burning away the double-dealing sorcerers and the Kimīdins.
Burn up the sorcerers; O God, burn up the Kimīdins.
Turn them back, O you whose path is black, and utterly consume the female sorceresses.
She who cursed with a curse, she who placed a heavy burden upon the fool, she who strove to seize the essence of the offspring— may she devour her own child.
Let the sorceress devour her own son, her sister, and even her grandson;
then, with disheveled hair, let the sorceresses strike one another down, and let the Arāyīs be torn asunder. //4//
With the *abhīvarta* amulet by which Indra grew preeminent—with that, O Brahmaṇaspati, cause us to grow preeminent for the sake of sovereignty. //1//
Turning against our rivals, against those who are hostile to us, stand against the one who attacks us, against him who seeks to harm us.
Thee, O god, Savitṛ has strengthened; thee, Soma has strengthened; all beings have strengthened thee, so that thou mayest be victorious. 3.
The over-rolling, overpowering amulet, which destroys rivals—
let it be bound for my kingdom, so that I may overcome my rivals.
Yonder sun has risen; so too has this word of mine arisen, so that I may be a slayer of enemies, one without rivals, a destroyer of rivals.
The bull, the destroyer of rivals, the assailing, the all-conquering— may I, as he is, rule over these heroes and over the people.
O All-Gods, O Vasus, protect this man; and you, O Ādityas, remain watchful over him.
Let no death from kin of the same lineage, nor from those of different lineage, nor any human slaughter reach him. 1.
O gods who are my fathers and those who are my sons, you who are of one mind, hear this which I have spoken:
I entrust him to you all; carry him safely to old age.

O gods who dwell in heaven, you who are on earth, you who are in the intermediate space, in the plants, in the cattle, and within the waters—grant him long life reaching old age; let him bypass another hundred deaths. //3//
Those gods for whom there are fore-offerings and after-offerings, both those who partake of oblations and those who do not eat offerings;
you whose five directions have been apportioned—to them, the dwellers of the sacrificial session, I make you over for this man. 4.
To the quarters and to the four guardians of the quarters, the immortal ones—to these overseers of what has come into being, we offer this oblation. 1.
O gods, you four who are the guardians of the quarters, may you release us from the snares of Nirṛti and from every distress.
Unlame, I worship you with an oblation; uncrippled, I offer you with clarified butter.
He who is the guardian of the quarters, the fourth god of the quarters—may he bring us well-being here. 3.
May there be well-being for our mother and for our father; may there be well-being for our cattle, for all living beings, and for men.
May everything be auspicious and easy for us to find; may we long behold the sun.
O people, know this: he shall proclaim a great sacred formulation (*brahman*).
It is not on earth nor in heaven—that by which the plants breathe. (1)
Their standing place is in the intermediate space, like that of those who have grown weary;
whether it is the station of this existing world or not, let the wise one know that.
Whatever you two, O Heaven and Earth, fashioned while trembling, and the moist ground that you carved out—
that today remains ever-present, like the currents of the ocean.
The one [is] all-encompassing; that rests upon the other.
To Dyaus, the all-knowing, and to Pṛthivī, I have paid homage. 4.
Golden-hued, pure, and purifying, those waters in which Savitṛ was born and in which Agni was born;
those golden ones who have received Agni as their embryo—may those waters be auspicious and pleasant for us. 1.
In whose midst King Varuṇa moves, beholding the truth and falsehood of men;
those golden waters who have borne Agni as their embryo—may they be auspicious and pleasant to us. 2.

Those whose portion the gods make in heaven, those who exist manifoldly in the intermediate space, those golden ones who have taken Agni as their embryo—may those waters be auspicious and pleasant for us. 3.
Behold me with a gracious eye, O Waters; touch my skin with your gracious body.
May those waters—dripping with clarity, pure, and purifying—be auspicious and pleasant for us. 4.
This plant is born of honey; we dig thee up with honey.
Thou art born from honey; make us full of honey.
On the tip of my tongue is honey; at the root of my tongue is the sweet liquor. Truly, you abide in my resolve; you follow my thought. 2.
Sweet is my stepping forth; sweet is my departure.
With my speech I speak sweetness; may I become full of sweetness, appearing as sweetness. 3.
I am honey; I am sweeter than honey, more full of sweetness than those who possess honey.
Surely you would have chosen me alone, as one chooses a honey-sweet branch.
I have come around you with an encompassing cane, so that there may be no enmity; so that she may be one who loves me, and so that she may not turn away from me. //5//
The gold which the Dākṣāyaṇas, being well-disposed, bound upon Śatānīka— that I bind upon you for long life, for luster, for strength, and for a lifespan of a hundred autumns. //1//
Neither the *rakṣas* nor the *piśācas* prevail over him, for this is the first-born vigor of the gods.
He who wears the gold of the Dākṣāyaṇas secures long life among the living. (AVŚ 1.35.2)

The brilliance of the waters, the light, the vigor, and the strength, as well as the heroic powers of the trees—like Indra, we bestow these sensory faculties upon him; may he, exerting himself, bear that gold. //3//
With the juices of the months and the seasons, I nourish you with the milk of the year.
May Indra and Agni, and all the gods, grant their approval to you without resentment.
Vena beholds that which is supreme in the secret cave, wherein all becomes one in form.
Being born, the dappled cow has milked this; the hosts who have found the light of heaven have shouted their acclaim. //1//
Let the Gandharva, who knows the immortal, proclaim that supreme abode which is hidden in the cave;
three steps of his are placed in the secret place—he who knows them shall be the father of the Father. //2//
He is our father, our progenitor, and he is our kinsman; he knows all domains and all beings.
He alone is the one who bestows names upon the gods; to him, as the object of inquiry, all worlds go. 3.
In an instant I have gone around heaven and earth; I have approached the first-born of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*).
Like speech in a speaker, he stands firm among the worlds; here indeed is that Agni who is about to bestow [blessings]. //4//
I have encompassed all worlds so that the outstretched thread of *ṛta* may be seen,
wherein the gods, having attained immortality, took their stand upon a common womb.

The divine Gandharva, who is the lord of the world, the one and only to be revered among the people and worthy of praise—O divine god, I seek you with a sacred prayer; homage be unto you; your dwelling is in heaven. 1.
Touching the sky, worshipful, with a sun-like skin, he wards off the divine heat.
May the Gandharva, who is the lord of the world, the one and only one worthy of homage, be most gracious. //2//
(2.2.3a) He has come together with these blameless ones; even among the Apsarases there was a Gandharva.
(2.2.3c) They say that the ocean is their dwelling place, from which they go forth and return again instantly. //3//
O lightning, O starry one, you who attend upon Viśvāvasu the Gandharva—to you, O goddesses, I pay homage. //4//
Those who are noisy, who dwell in darkness, who desire the dice, and who delude the mind—to those *gandharvas* and *apsarases* I have paid homage. (5)
That which flows down from the mountain as a spring—that I make for you a remedy, a good remedy, so that you may be well. 1.
Indeed, O member, how many indeed are your remedies?
Of these, you are the best—free from discharge and free from disease.
The Asuras dig this great wound-deep;
that is the remedy for the flow, and it has destroyed the disease. //3//
The ants bring forth the medicine from the ocean;
that is the remedy for the discharge, and it has quieted the disease.
This great [remedy] for the swelling has been brought forth from the earth;
it is the medicine for the discharge, and it has destroyed the disease. //5//
May the waters and the plants be auspicious and gracious to us.
May Indra’s thunderbolt strike down the demons; may arrows released from afar fall upon the demons.
For long life and for great joy, always remaining unharmed and exerting ourselves, we wear the *jaṅgiḍa* amulet, the destroyer of *viṣkandha*. 1.
From the *jaṅgiḍa*, from the *jambha*, from the *viśara*, from the *viṣkandha*, and from the burning fever—
may this amulet of a thousandfold power protect us on every side.
This Jaṅgiḍa overcomes Viṣkandha; this one drives away the Attrins. This all-healing Jaṅgiḍa shall protect us from distress.
With the jewel Jaṅgiḍa given by the gods, which brings well-being, we overcome Viṣkandha and all demonic powers through our exertion. //4//
May both the hemp and the jaṅgiḍa protect me from viṣkandha;
one was brought from the forest, the other from the juices of cultivation.
This amulet is a destroyer of sorcery and a destroyer of enemies;
moreover, may the powerful Jaṅgiḍa prolong our lifespans.
O Indra, take pleasure; come hither, O hero, with your two bay steeds.
Drink of the pressed soma, longing here for the sweet draught, you who are lovely for exhilaration. 1.
O Indra, fill your belly anew with the honey of heaven; may the exhilarations of this pressed juice, like the sun, go toward you with sweet voices. //2//
Indra, the overcomer of the swift, who like Mitra struck down Vṛtra;
he shattered Vala like Bhṛgu, and in the exhilaration of Soma, he overcame his enemies. //3//
(2.5.4a) May the pressed juices enter you; O Indra, fill your belly! O Śakra, partake [of them] through our prayers; come to us!
(2.5.4c) Hear my call, enjoy my songs, O Indra; exhilarate yourself here with your own companions for great delight. //4//

I shall now proclaim the heroic deeds of Indra, those which the wielder of the thunderbolt performed for the first time: he slew the serpent, he pierced the channels of the waters, and he split open the bellies of the mountains. //5//
(2.5.6a) He slew the serpent as he lay coiled upon the mountain; Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned for him the thunderbolt that roars aloud.
(2.5.6c) Like lowing cows, the flowing waters have gone straight down to the ocean. //6//
Acting like a bull, he chose the Soma; at the Trikadruka rites, he drank of the pressed juice.
Maghavan took up his missile, the thunderbolt; he slew him, the first-born of the serpents.
O Agni, may the seasons increase you, and the years, the seers, and those truths;
shine forth with the celestial light, and illuminate all four quarters.
Be kindled, O Agni, and cause this man to prosper; rise up for great good fortune.
Let not those who sit near thee, O Agni, come to harm; let the *brahmans* be glorious through thee, and not others. 2.
(2.6.3a) These Brahmins choose you, O Agni; be auspicious to us in our dwelling, O Agni.
(2.6.3c) O Agni, be a slayer of rivals and a conqueror of adversaries; watch over your own household, never being heedless. //3//
O Agni, take hold with your own sovereign power; O Agni, as a friend, strive to establish friendship. Standing in the midst of your kinsmen, O Agni, shine here, you who are to be invoked by kings.

Beyond the deceivers, beyond the destroyers, beyond the thoughtless, and beyond the haters—O Agni, for you indeed cross over all difficulties; therefore, grant us wealth together with heroic sons. //5//
Hated by the wicked, born of the gods, the plant that neutralizes curses—
may it drive away all curses from me, as water washes away impurity.
The curse of a rival wife and the curse of a sister, whatever curse a Brahmin may utter in his anger—all that is beneath our feet. 2.
Its root is extended down from heaven; it is stretched up from the earth.
With that [plant] of a thousand stalks, protect us on every side. //3//
Protect me, protect my offspring, and protect whatever wealth we possess.
Let not the enemy overcome us; let not our adversaries overcome us. //4//
Let the curse go back to the curser who is well-disposed toward us;
we crush even the ribs of the evil-hearted one with the mantra of sight. //5//
The two blessed stars named Vicṛtī have risen;
may they release us from the lowest and the highest bond of *kṣetriya*.
May this night dawn away; may the attacking [diseases] depart. May the plant that destroys *kṣetriya* drive away the *kṣetriya*.
With the chaff of the brown, white-stalked barley, and with the husk of the sesame seed—may the plant that destroys *kṣetriya* drive the *kṣetriya* away. //3//
Homage to your plowshares, homage to your poles and yokes! O plant that destroys *kṣetriya*, may it drive away the *kṣetriya* disease. 4.
Homage to those with sunken eyes; homage to those who are to be pointed out.
Homage to the Lord of the Field! O plant that destroys *kṣetriya*, may it drive away the *kṣetriya* disease. 5.
O ten-wooded tree, release this man from the *rakṣas* and the *grāhī* who has seized him by his joints;
and so, O Lord of the Forest, lead him up to the world of the living. 1.
He has come; he has risen up; he has joined the company of the living. He has become the father of sons and the most blessed among men.
This one has gone over the recitations; he has gone over the living cities.
For he has a hundred physicians and a thousand plants.
The gods, the Brahmans, and the plants have found your consciousness;
all the gods have found your consciousness upon the earth.
He who made it can undo it; he indeed is the best physician. He alone, the pure healer, shall prepare medicines for you.
I release you from hereditary disease, from destruction, from the curse of kin, from malice, and from the noose of Varuṇa.
By means of this sacred prayer, I make you sinless; may both Heaven and Earth be auspicious for you. 1.
May Agni be auspicious to you along with the waters; may Soma be auspicious to you along with the plants.
Thus do I release you from hereditary disease, from Destruction, from the curse of kin, and from malice—from the noose of Varuṇa.
By means of the sacred word (*brahman*), I make you sinless; may both Heaven and Earth be propitious to you. 2.
May the wind in the mid-air bestow vigor upon you for your peace; may the four quarters be auspicious for you.
Thus do I release you from hereditary disease, from Destruction, from the curse of kin, and from malice—from the noose of Varuṇa.
By means of the sacred word (*brahman*), I make you sinless; may both Heaven and Earth be gracious to you. 3.
These four divine quarters, whose lords are the winds, which the sun surveys;
even so do I release you from *kṣetriya*, from destruction, from the curse of kin, and from malice—from the noose of Varuṇa.
By means of the sacred word (*brahman*), I make you sinless; may both Heaven and Earth be auspicious for you. 4.
Into these [fingers] I place you within old age; let consumption and Destruction depart far away.
Thus do I release you from hereditary disease, from Destruction, from the curse of kin, and from malice—from the noose of Varuṇa.
By means of the sacred word (*brahman*), I make you sinless; may both Heaven and Earth be auspicious for you. (5)
You have been released from consumption, from misfortune, from reproach, and from the noose of malice; you have also been released from the grasp of seizure.
Even so do I release you from hereditary disease, from destruction, from the curse of kin, from malice, and from the noose of Varuṇa.
By means of the sacred word (*brahman*), I make you sinless; may both Heaven and Earth be auspicious for you.

(7a) You have found freedom from hostility; you have become gracious in the world of the well-done. (7c) Thus do I release you from hereditary disease, from Destruction, from the curse of kin, and from malice—from the noose of Varuṇa.
(7e) By means of the sacred word (*brahman*), I make you sinless; may both Heaven and Earth be auspicious for you. //7//

The gods, releasing the sun—the truth—from the grasp of darkness, set him free from sin. Even so do I release you from hereditary disease, from destruction, from the curse of kin, and from malice; I release you from the noose of Varuṇa.
By means of this sacred prayer (*brahman*), I make you sinless; may both Heaven and Earth be auspicious for you. 8.
You are the defiler, the defiler you are; you are the weapon, the weapon you are; you are the missile, the missile you are.
Reach for one who is better; leap beyond your equal!
You are the headband; you are the amulet; you are the counter-attack.
Attain what is better; surpass the equal. 2.
Attack him who hates us and whom we hate;
reach one who is better, surpass your equal. //3//
You are a patron; you are the bestower of splendor; you are the protector of the body.
Attain that which is better; surpass your equal. 4.
(5a) You are the bright; you are the radiant; you are the heavenly light; you are the light.
(5c) Attain what is better; surpass your equal. //5//
Heaven and Earth, the wide mid-air, the two wives of the field, the far-striding and wondrous one— may the wide mid-air, whose guardian is Vāta, heat themselves here for me as I am heated.
Hear this, O gods, you who are worthy of sacrifice: Bharadvāja recites hymns for me.
Let him who injures this mind of ours be bound in fetters and cast down into misfortune. 2.
Hear this, O Indra, drinker of Soma, when I call upon you with a grieving heart.
Like a tree with an axe, I cut down him who injures this mind of ours. 3.

With the three groups of eighty Sāma-singers, with the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Aṅgirases—may the merit of our sacrifices and charitable works protect the ancestors; I bestow that upon him by divine power.
Heaven and Earth, look upon me with favor; all you gods, take hold of me!
O Soma-loving Fathers, the Aṅgirases, let the evil reach the one who acts against my will. 5.

O Maruts, whoever thinks too highly of himself toward us, or whoever reviles the sacred formulation (*brahman*) as it is being performed—for him let his crooked deeds become burning fires; may the sky scorch the hater of the sacred formulation.
Seven are the vital breaths, eight you consider them; those I cut away for you with a sacred prayer (*brahman*).
By this [prayer], Agni has been made ready as a messenger to the abode of Yama. //7//
I place your footprint in the kindled Jātavedas;
may Agni pervade your body, and may speech enter into the vital breath. //8//

Bestowing long life, O Agni, choosing old age, you whose face is ghee, whose back is ghee, O Agni—having drunk the ghee and the sweet, pleasant product of the cow, protect this man as a father protects his sons. 1.
Clothe him, clothe him with splendor; make this one free from death through old age, grant him long life.
Bṛhaspati has bestowed this garment upon King Soma to put on.
You have put on this garment for well-being; you have become the protector of the young cows against curses.
Live for a hundred abundant autumns, and clothe yourself in the increase of wealth.
(2,13.4a) Come, step upon the stone; let your body become as firm as stone.
(2,13.4c) May all the gods grant you a lifespan of a hundred autumns. //4//
(5a) May all the gods protect you, whose first garment we take away from you.
(5c) May many brothers, increasing well, be born after you as you grow, O well-born one.
The houseless, bold Dhiṣaṇā, the one who utters a single cry, the ravenous one—we destroy all the granddaughters of Caṇḍa, the Sadānvās. 1.
We drive you out from the cow-pen, out from the axle, out from the wagon-seat;
O daughters of Magundi, we expel you from your houses.
In that house which is down below, let there be the Arāyī-demons; let exhaustion settle there, and all the sorceresses as well.
May Bhūtapati and Indra drive away the Cetanas and Sadānvās;
may Indra, with his thunderbolt, stand over those who sit at the foundation of the house. //4//
Whether you belong to those with hereditary skin diseases, or whether you are sent by men,
or if you are born from the Dasyus— perish from here, O Sadānvās!
I have run around their domains like a swift horse to its goal;
I have conquered all your races. Let the Sadānvās perish from here!
Just as heaven and earth neither fear nor suffer harm,
so, O breath, do not fear for me.
Just as day and night do not fear and do not suffer harm,
so, O Prāṇa, do not fear for me.
Just as the sun and the moon neither fear nor suffer harm, so, O breath, do not fear for me. 3.
Just as the Brahman and the Kṣatra do not fear and do not come to harm, even so,
O Prāṇa, do not fear for me.
Just as truth and falsehood neither fear nor suffer harm,
so, O Prāṇa, do not fear for me.
As that which has been and that which is to be do not fear nor suffer harm,
even so, O Prāṇa, do not fear for me.
O out-breath and in-breath, protect me from death; svāhā! //1//
O Heaven and Earth, having heard me, protect me; svāhā!
O Sūrya, protect me with your eye; svāhā!
O Agni Vaiśvānara, protect me with all the gods; svāhā!
O All-sustainer, protect me with all-sustaining nourishment; Svāhā!
(1) You are vigor; grant me vigor! Svāhā!
(2) You are power; grant me power! Svāhā!
(2.17.3a) You are strength; grant strength, svāhā!
Life art thou; give me life, svāhā! //4//
(5) You are hearing; grant me hearing, svāhā!
(6) You are sight; grant me sight, svāhā!
(7) You are a protection; grant me protection, svāhā!
(1) You are the destroyer of rivals; grant me the driving away of rivals. Svāhā!
(2.18.2a) You are the destroyer of rivals; grant me the driving away of rivals. Svāhā!
(2.18.3a) You are the destruction of the *arāya* worm; grant me the exorcism of the *arāya*; *svāhā*!
You are the destroyer of Piśācas; grant me the driving away of Piśācas. Svāhā! //4//
(5) You are the constant pursuer; grant me the constant driving away [of enemies]. Svāhā!
O Agni, with that heat which is yours, burn against him who hates us and whom we hate. //1//
O Agni, with that heat which is yours, strike back at him who hates us and whom we hate. //2//
O Agni, with that flame which is yours, strike back at him who hates us and whom we hate. //3//
O Agni, with that flame of yours which is thine, burn against him who hates us and whom we hate. //4//
O Agni, with that splendor which is yours, make him lusterless who hates us and whom we hate. //5//
O Vāyu, with that heat which is yours, burn him who hates us and whom we hate. 1.
O Vāyu, with that heat which is yours, strike back at him who hates us and whom we hate. //2//
O Vāyu, with that flame which is yours, strike back at him who hates us and whom we hate. //3//
O Vāyu, with that heat which is yours, burn him who hates us and whom we hate. //4//
O Vāyu, with that splendor which is yours, deprive of splendor him who hates us and whom we hate. //5//
O Sūrya, with that heat which is yours, burn against him who hates us and whom we hate. //1//
O Sūrya, with that heat which is yours, strike back at him who hates us and whom we hate. //2//
O Sūrya, with that radiance which is yours, strike back at him who hates us and whom we hate. //3//
O Sūrya, with that splendor which is yours, burn against him who hates us and whom we hate. //4//
O Sūrya, with that splendor which is yours, render splendorless him who hates us and whom we hate. //5//
O Moon, with that heat which is yours, burn him who hates us and whom we hate. //1//
O Moon, with that heat which is yours, strike back at him who hates us and whom we hate. //2//
O Moon, with that radiance which is yours, shine back upon him who hates us and whom we hate. //3//
O Moon, with that radiance which is yours, burn against him who hates us and whom we hate. //4//
O Moon, with that splendor which is yours, render powerless him who hates us and whom we hate. //5//
O Waters, with that heat which is yours, burn against him who hates us and whom we hate. //1//
O Waters, with that heat which is yours, strike back at him who hates us and whom we hate. //2//
O Waters, with that radiance which is yours, strike back at him who hates us and whom we hate. //3//
O Waters, with that heat which is yours, burn against him who hates us and whom we hate. //4//
O Waters, whatever brilliance is yours, with that make him lusterless who hates us and whom we hate. //5//
O Śerabhaka, O Śerabha, let your sorceries go back again, and back the missile of the Kimīdin!
Devour him from whom you come; devour him who sent you; devour your own flesh! 1.
O increasers of prosperity, O increasers of prosperity! Let your sorceries go back, let the missile of the *kimīdin*s go back!
Devour him by whom you are sent; devour him who sent you; eat your own flesh! 2.
Mrokas and Anumrokas, let your sorceries go back again; back, O Kimīdins, let your missile go!
Eat him from whom you come, eat him who sent you; eat your own flesh! 3.
Crawl away, O serpent; let your sorceries go back to you, and back the missile of the *kimīdin*s!
Devour him from whom you come, devour him who sent you; eat your own flesh! //4//
(5) Let your sorceries go back to the scorched; back, O Kimīdin, let your missile go!
Devour him by whose side you are; devour him who sent you forth; eat your own flesh!
Let your sorceries go back to their noise, let the missile of the *kimīdin*s go back!
Devour him from whom you come; devour him who sent you; eat your own flesh! 6.
O Arjunī, let your sorceries go back to you; back, O Kimīdin, let your missile return!
Devour him from whom you come; devour him who sent you; devour your own flesh! 7!
O Bharūjis, let your sorceries go back; back, O Kimīdins, let your missile go! Eat him from whom you come, eat him who sent you here; eat your own flesh!
May the goddess Pṛśniparṇī bring us peace; she has brought peace away from Nirṛti.
For she is mighty, the crusher of the Kaṇvas; I have partaken of her, the powerful one. 1.
This *pṛśniparṇī*, the first of those that endure, was born.
With it, I sever the head of the ill-named one, as if that of a bird.
The *arāya* that drinks blood, and he who seeks to steal our prosperity—O *pṛśniparṇī*, destroy the embryo-eater and the *kaṇva*, and overcome them! 3.
Lead these Kaṇvas, who offer life as a gift, into this mountain;
O Goddess Pṛśniparṇī, go forth, consuming them like fire.
Drive them away, these Kaṇvas who seek to take away life;
I have sent the flesh-eaters to that place where the darknesses go.
(1) Let the cattle come hither, those that have passed away, and those whose companion Vāyu has enjoyed.
May Tvaṣṭṛ, who knows their forms, and Savitṛ establish them here in this pen. 1.
May the cattle flow together into this pen; may Bṛhaspati lead them here, knowing the way. May Sinīvālī lead them to the forefront; O Anumati, restrain those who have arrived.
May the cattle flow together, may the horses and the men likewise; whatever abundance there is of grain, that I offer with the flowing oblation. 3.
I pour together the milk of the cows, together with the strength and essence of the clarified butter.
May our heroes be well-sprinkled; may the cows be secure while I am the lord of the herd. 4.
I bring the milk of the cows; I have brought the essence of grain. Our heroes have been brought back, and so have our wives—this is our home.
Let not the enemy swallow the portion; you are the subduer, the overcomer.
O Herb, strike down the one who swallows the portion in return, and render them sapless.
The eagle found you; the boar dug you up with its snout.
O herb, destroy the consumer and the one who consumes further; make them sapless.
Indra indeed placed you in his arm to overcome the Asuras.
O herb, destroy the eater and the one who eats back; make them sapless! 3.
Indra has consumed the *pāṭā* plant in order to overcome the Asuras.
O herb, destroy the consumer and the one who consumes in return; make them sapless! 4.
By that [power], may I overcome my enemies as Indra overcomes wild dogs;
O herb, strike down the devourer and the one who devours in return, and make them sapless!
O Rudra, whose medicine is cooling, blue-crested one, performer of deeds! O herb, drive away the consumer and the one who consumes in return; make them sapless.
Destroy his power, O Indra, who assails us;
speak for us with your strengths, and make me superior to him.
For you alone, O Old Age, let this man increase; let not other deaths, those hundredfold, harm him.
Like a mother her son, well-disposed in her lap, may Mitra protect him from distress as a friend protects a friend. 1.
May Mitra and Varuṇa, the destroyers of enemies, acting in harmony, ordain for him death at old age.
Then Agni, the Hotṛ-priest who knows the sacred ways, shall proclaim all the generations of the gods. 2.
(2.28.3) You rule over the terrestrial cattle, both those that have been born and those yet to be born.
Let not my out-breath depart, nor my in-breath; let neither friends nor enemies slay me. (3)
May Heaven as your father and Earth as your mother, acting in harmony, grant you long life unto old age;
so that you may live for a hundred winters, protected by out-breath and in-breath in the lap of Aditi.
O Agni, lead this man to long life and splendor; O King Varuṇa and Mitra, grant him dear seed.
Like a mother, O Aditi, bestow protection upon him, so that all the gods may grant him the full span of life. 5.
In the essence of the earthly king, in the body of Bhaga, and in strength—may Agni, Sūrya, and Bṛhaspati bestow long life and splendor upon him. 1.
Bestow long life upon him, O Jātavedas; bestow progeny upon him, O Tvaṣṭṛ. O Savitṛ, send forth for him an abundance of wealth; may he live a hundred autumns under your protection. //2//
Grant us blessings, nourishment, and good progeny; bestow upon us skill and wealth, O you two who are of one mind.
May this Indra, by his might, conquer the fields and bring low our other rivals.
Given by Indra, instructed by Varuṇa, sent forth by the Maruts, this fierce one has come to us.
O Heaven and Earth, in your lap, may he not hunger nor thirst. 4.
Bestow vigor upon him, O you who are vigorous; bestow milk upon him, O you who are rich in milk.
May Heaven and Earth bestow vigor upon him; may all the gods, the Maruts, and the waters [bestow] vigor. //5//

With auspicious [waters] I satisfy your heart; free from disease and full of luster, may you rejoice. Having assumed the form of the Aśvins through their creative power (*māyā*), may you two, dwelling together, drink this stirred drink (*mantha*).
Indra created this at the beginning when he was pierced; it is the undecaying essence of nourishment, and it is yours.
Live through many autumns with it, full of luster; let it not fail you—the physicians have prepared it for you.
Just as the wind stirs this blade of grass upon the earth,
so do I stir your mind, that you may be in love with me and never turn away from me.
If you two, O Aśvins, lead [us] together as lovers, and carry us together; may blessings come together for you both, and may your thoughts and your vows be in harmony.
Where the fair-winged ones, eager to speak, are free from disease and eager to speak— there let my fever go, like a thorn from a sprout.
That which is within is without; that which is without is within.
O herb, seize the heart of the maidens of manifold forms! 4.
(5a) Here I have come, desiring a husband; I have come seeking a wife. (5c) Like a neighing horse, I have come together with good fortune.
That great stone of Indra, which crushes every worm—
with it I grind the worms together like grain upon a millstone.
I have crushed the seen and the unseen; I have crushed the *atṛha* and the *kurūru*. All the *algaṇḍu* and *chaluna* worms—we crush them with our word.
I strike down the *algaṇḍu*s with a great weapon; the scorched and the unscorched have become sapless.
Whether they be taught or untaught, I drive them away with my word, so that not one of the worms shall remain.
The intestinal worms, the head-worms, and those in the back;
the downward-creeping and the piercing worms—we crush them all with our word.
The worms that are in the mountains, in the forests, in the plants, in the cattle, and within the waters—
those which have entered our bodies, all those broods of worms I destroy.
Rising, may the Sun slay the worms; setting, may he slay them with his rays—those worms that are within the cow.
The worm Viśvarūpa, four-eyed, speckled and white—
I crush his ribs and I cut off his head.
Like Atri, I slay your worms; like Kaṇva and Jamadagni. With the sacred spell of Agastya, I grind the worms to pieces.
Slain is the king of the worms, and their chief architect is slain;
slain is the worm whose mother is slain, whose brother is slain, and whose sister is slain.
Slain are his attendants, slain are his followers;
and likewise, all those who are like tiny insects—they too are slain. //5//
I break off your two horns with which you pierce; I split open your poison-bag, that which is your receptacle for venom.
From your two eyes, from your two nostrils, from your two ears, and from your chin— I pull out the consumption (*yakṣma*) from your head, from your brain, and from your tongue. //1//
From your neck, from your uṣṇihā-veins, from your vertebrae, and from your spine; the consumption residing in your shoulders, from your shoulder-blades and from your arms—I tear it away from you.
From your heart, from your lungs, from your liver, and from both your sides;
from your kidneys, from your spleen, and from your liver—we tear away the consumption. 3.
From your entrails, from your intestines, from the large intestine and from the belly;
from both sides of your abdomen, from the bladder, and from the navel—I tear away your consumption. 4.
From your thighs, from your knees, from your heels, and from your forefeet—
Yakṣma residing in the anus, and that which resides in the hips, I pull out from your groin.
From your bones, from your marrow, from your sinews, and from your veins— from your hands, from your fingers, and from your nails— I tear away the disease for you.
In every limb, in every hair-follicle, in every joint of yours—
whatever consumption (*yakṣma*) is in your skin, we root it out from all sides with the uprooting-tool of Kaśyapa.

He who is the Lord of Cattle, master of animals, both those that are four-footed and those that are two-footed—may he, being ransomed, go to his sacrificial portion; may the increases of wealth attend the sacrificer.
Releasing the seed of the world, O gods, grant a path for the sacrificer. May that which has been offered, which stood striving, go to the dear domain of the gods.
Those who, observing with mind and eye, looked on while [the victim] was being bound—
may the god Agni release them first, and may Viśvakarman, rejoicing in his offspring, set them free.
Those domestic animals which are multiform, though being diverse in shape, yet are of one form in many ways—
may the god Vāyu release them first, and Prajāpati, rejoicing together with his offspring.
May the ancestors, being aware, receive back the breath as it moves away from the limbs.
Go to heaven; establish yourself with your bodies; go to the world of light by the paths traveled by the gods. //5//

Those who, while consuming [the offerings], did not prosper in wealth, and for whom the hearth-fires (*dhiṣṇyā agnayaḥ*) felt remorse—may Viśvakarman make that ill-sacrifice of theirs a well-sacrificed one for us. (AVŚ 2.35.1)
The seers have declared the lord of the sacrifice to be guilty of sin, excluded from his offspring and filled with remorse.
Whatever drops he has spilled that were liable to be lost—may Viśvakarman reunite him with them.
Thinking himself one who gives and drinks the Soma, the wise one knows the proper time for the sacrifice;
O Viśvakarman, release him from the bond for his well-being, he who has committed an offense and is bound. //3//
Terrible are the seers; let there be homage to them, for that which is their vision and the truth of their mind.
To Bṛhaspati, O buffalo, the radiant one, homage! To Viśvakarman, homage! Protect us. 4.
The eye and the beginning of the sacrifice, and its mouth—with speech, with hearing, and with the mind, I offer this sacrifice.
May the gods, being well-disposed, come to this sacrifice spread out by Viśvakarman. //5//
O Agni, may the bridegroom come to our favor; may this maiden come to us together with fortune.
May she be beloved among suitors, beautiful in assemblies; may there be prosperity for her through her husband. 1.
Pleasant to Soma, pleasant to Brahma, gathered together by Aryaman and Bhaga—
by the truth of the divine Dhātṛ, I effect the finding of a husband.
O Agni, may this woman find a husband; for King Soma makes her fortunate.
Giving birth to sons, she shall become a queen; having gone to her husband, may she shine forth as one blessed with good fortune. 3.
Just as this lovely ass, O Maghavan, has become dear to the wild beasts and a pleasant seat for them,
so may this woman be pleasing to Bhaga, beloved by her husband, and not causing him harm.
Mount the ship of Bhaga, which is full and overflowing;
with it, ferry across him who is the desirable suitor.
(6) O Lord of Wealth, cry out! Make our mind favorable;
make everything auspicious, whatever boon is desired.
This gold, this bdellium, this bull, and furthermore Bhaga—these have given you over to husbands who desire you, so that you may find one.
May Savitṛ lead you; may he who is desirable as a husband lead you.
May Agni, the wise one, advance against our enemies, burning away their curses and hostility.
May he, Jātavedas, confound the armies of our foes and render them handless. 1.
(3.1.2a) O Maruts, you who are fierce, you stand ready for such a task as this; go forth, strike them down, and overcome them!
(3.1.2c) These suppliants have not been struck down, O Vasus; for Agni, the wise one, shall come forward as their messenger. //2//
O Maghavan, against the enemy army that treats us as foes, do you two, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, and Agni, burn it up! //3//
Impelled by you, O Indra, let your two bay horses go down the slope; let your thunderbolt go forth, crushing the enemies.
Slay those who face you, those who follow behind, and those who flee away; make their resolve truly subject to you.
O Indra, confound the army of our enemies;
by the rushing force of Agni and Vāta, destroy them, scattering them in all directions.
May Indra confound the army; may the Maruts strike it down with their might.
May Agni restore its eyesight; let the defeated host return.
May Agni, our wise messenger, come toward us, burning away the curse and the enemy.
May he, Jātavedas, confound the minds of our adversaries and render them handless. 1.
This Agni has cleared away those thoughts that were in your hearts; let him blow you apart from your dwellings, let him blow you away from every side.
O Indra, bewildering their minds, come hither with our intention; by the swift force of Agni and Vāta, destroy them, scattering them in all directions. //3//
Let their intentions go astray, and likewise let their thoughts be confounded;
furthermore, whatever is now in their hearts, drive that out from them completely.
Bewildering the minds of these men, seize their limbs, O Apvā;
go away! Advance against them, burn them up with sorrows in their hearts; pierce the enemies with darkness, strike down the foes.
(6a) That army of the enemies, O Maruts, which approaches us, vying with us in its might— (6c) Pierce it with lawless darkness, so that not one among them can recognize another. //6//
The skillful one has roared; may he be present here, O Agni. Disclose the two wide worlds.
May the all-knowing Maruts harness you; lead that [sacrificer] who offers oblations with reverence.

(3.3.2a) May the ruddy ones bring hither from afar Indra, the inspired sage, for friendship; (3.3.2c) when the gods, through the Sautrāmaṇī, boldly bestowed upon him the Gāyatrī, the Bṛhatī, and the hymn. //2//
(3) Let King Varuṇa call you from the waters; let Soma call you from the mountains.
Let Indra call you from these subjects; becoming a falcon, fly to these people.
(4) May the falcon carry the offering from beyond, [to him] who wanders in another’s field, having been driven away.
May the Aśvins make a path easy for you; O kinsmen, enter into this man together.
(4) Let the rival clans call upon you; let the allies rain favors upon you.
May Indra, Agni, and all the gods establish security for you in the clan. (5)
(6) Whoever among your own kin or whoever is a stranger disputes your call—O Indra, having turned him away, bring this man here.
(7) Let the kingdom come to you together with splendor; go forward! As the lord of the people and sole ruler, rule over them.
O King, let all the quarters invoke you; may you be one to be approached and honored here. 1.
(3.4.2a) May the people choose you for sovereignty; may these five divine quarters choose you.
(3.4.2c) Rest upon the height, upon the summit of the kingdom; from there, as a mighty one, distribute wealth to us. 2.
(3) Let your kinsmen come hither with oblations; let Agni, the swift messenger, move among them.
May wives and sons be well-disposed; may the fierce one look upon their abundant tribute. //3//
(3.4.4a) Let the Aśvins first call upon you, and both Mitra and Varuṇa; let all the gods and the Maruts call upon you.
(3.4.4c) Then direct your mind toward the giving of wealth; thereafter, as a mighty one, distribute riches among us. 4.
Run forth from the furthest distance! May both Heaven and Earth be auspicious for you.
Thus has King Varuṇa spoken; he has called you here—come hither! 5.
O Indra, O Indra, go forth among men, for you have attained union with Varuṇa through sacred knowledge.
He has called you here to his own dwelling; as a god, he shall sacrifice to the gods and he shall ordain the people.
The Pathyās, the Revatīs, manifold and diverse in form—all of them having come together, have made you more excellent.
May they all, being in agreement, call you hither; O fierce one, being well-disposed, enter here on the tenth day.
This leaf-amulet has come hither, powerful with power, crushing rivals.
May the vigor of the gods, the sap of the plants, quicken me with splendor, they who are never negligent. 1.
In me, O amulet of leaves, let sovereignty and wealth be established;
may I be the highest, the most intimate one, in the attainment of the kingdom.
The leaf of Soma has come with power; given by Indra, instructed by Varuṇa, may I wear it as a dear ornament, shining brightly for long life through a hundred autumns. //4//
The leaf-amulet has ascended unto me for great safety, so that I may be superior to Aryaman and to those who hold common counsel. //5//
Those who are thinkers, chariot-makers, smiths, and those who are wise—
O Parṇa tree, do you place me above all these people on every side.
Those who are kings, those who serve the king, the charioteers, and the village headmen— O Parṇa, do you place them all around me as my attendants.
(8) You are a leaf, a protector of the body, sharing a common womb with me, a hero with me, a hero.
With the splendor of the year, with that I bind you, O amulet! (8)
A male born from a male, the *aśvattha* tree from the *khadira*—may it slay my enemies, those whom I hate and those who hate me. //1//
O Aśvattha tree, crush those enemies who are fiercely attacking;
fight with Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, and with Mitra and Varuṇa. //2//
Just as the *aśvattha* tree was shattered within the great ocean, even so shatter all those whom I hate and those who hate me. 3.
O Aśvattha tree, you who move about overcoming all, like a bull that has conquered, through you may we overcome our rivals. //4//
(3.6.5a) May Destruction seize them with the unloosable nooses of Death!
(3.6.5c) O Aśvattha tree, [seize] my enemies—those whom I hate and those who hate me! //5//
Just as the aśvattha tree, ascending among the lords of the forest, makes them inferior,
so do you shatter the head of my enemy on every side and overcome him.
Let them float downward, like a boat severed from its mooring;
for those driven away by the Vaibādha spell, there is no returning.
I drive them away with my mind, with my thought, and with my sacred prayer;
with a branch of the *aśvattha* tree we drive them away. //8//
Upon the head of the swift-moving deer is the healing medicine;
with its horn, it has driven away the *kṣetriya* disease in all directions.
The tawny bull has followed you with his four feet;
O two horns, unbind that which is knotted in his heart as *kṣetriya*.
That which shines down there, like a roof with four sides—with that we cause all your *kṣetriya* disease to perish from your limbs. //3//
Those two auspicious stars in heaven named Vicṛtī—may they release from the disease of the field (*kṣetriya*) the lowest and the highest bond. 4.
The waters indeed are healers; the waters drive away disease. The waters are the healers of everything; may they release you from *kṣetriya*.
Whatever *kṣetriya* has entered into you while the pressing of the Soma was being performed—I know the remedy for that; I destroy the *kṣetriya* from you.
May there be the departure of the constellations, and the departure of the dawns; may all that is ill-fortuned depart from us, and may the *kṣetriya* disease vanish! 7.7a-c.
May Mitra come, conforming himself to the seasons, laying to rest the earth with the rays of dawn;
then may Varuṇa, Vāyu, and Agni bestow upon us a vast kingdom fit for repose. //1//
May Dhātṛ, Rāti, and Savitṛ take pleasure in this; may Indra and Tvaṣṭṛ welcome my word.
I invoke the goddess Aditi, mother of heroes, so that I may stand in the midst of my kinsmen. //2//
(I) invoke Soma and Savitṛ with prostrations, and all the Ādityas, for my superiority.
This Agni has shone forth for a long time, kindled by his kinsmen who do not speak against him. 3.
Stay right here; do not go elsewhere. May Aryaman, the protector and lord of prosperity, drive you hither.
For this desire, may all the gods come together toward you, O longing ones. 4.
We bend together your minds, together your vows, and together your intentions.
Those who are here with divergent vows, them we cause to bend together for you. 5.
I seize your minds with my mind; follow my thought with your thoughts. I bring your hearts under my control; follow the path of my coming.
Of Karśapha and Viśapha, Heaven is the father and Earth is the mother.
As the gods have willed it, so do you bring it back again. 1.
Without spitting, they have held it fast; even so was it done by Manu. I make the *viṣkandha* impotent, like the castrator of bulls.
Upon a tawny cord the wise ones bind that hook;
may the bandager make Śravasyu, Śuṣma, and Kābava into eunuchs.
By which you two, seeking glory, move like gods through the power of the Asuras—like the monkey who destroys dogs, and the kinsman of Kāvava. //4//
For I shall revile you for your wickedness; I shall corrupt the descendant of Kābu. Like swift chariots, you shall rush forth with curses.
One hundred and one *viṣkandha* demons are stationed throughout the earth;
from among them, they first extracted you, the amulet that destroys the *viṣkandha*.
She indeed shone forth as the first; she became the milch-cow for Yama.
May she, rich in milk, yield for us [milk] in each succeeding year.
The night which the gods welcome as she approaches like a milch-cow,
she who is the consort of the year— may she be auspicious for us.
O Night, you whom we worship as the image of the year—may you endow us with long-lived progeny and with the increase of wealth. 3.
This very one is she who first shone forth; having entered into these other [days], she moves within them.
Within her are great powers; the bride, the mother of the ninefold, has gone forth. 4.
The pressing-stones of wood have raised their voice, preparing the oblation that belongs to the year.
O Ekāṣṭakā, may we be possessed of good offspring and brave sons, and may we be lords of riches.
The footprint of Iḍā is full of ghee, O Jātavedas; it is crawling. Accept the oblations!
May the delight of those seven domestic animals of all forms abide in me. //6//
O Night, may we be in the good favor of the gods for prosperity and nourishment.
O full ladle, fly away; well-filled, fly back again.
Enjoying all sacrifices, bring us food and strength.
This year has come, O Ekāṣṭakā, as your husband.
As such, endow us with long-lived progeny and with the increase of wealth. //8//
Sacrifice to the seasons, to the lords of the seasons, and to the seasonal periods; sacrifice to the years, the full years, and the months—to the Lord of Being, I offer sacrifice. //9//
For the seasons, for the seasonal periods, for the months, and for the years;
for Dhātṛ, for Vidhātṛ, for Samṛdh, and for the Lord of Being, I sacrifice.
(11) As we offer with the *iḍā* and worship the gods with oblations of clarified butter,
may we enter together into houses that are not stingy and are rich in cattle.
The Ekāṣṭakā, performing austerities, gave birth to a child, Indra, the great one;
by him the gods overcame their enemies, and he became the lord of power, the slayer of the Dasyus. //12//
O daughter of Prajāpati, daughter of Indra, daughter of Soma:
fulfill our desires; accept our oblation. //13//
I release you by means of this oblation so that you may live, from unknown consumption and from royal consumption.
If the Grāhi has seized him, O Indra and Agni, release him from her!
Whether his life is exhausted, or he has departed, or if he is already at the very presence of death— I bring him back from the lap of Destruction, untouched by harm, for a hundred autumns.
With the thousand-eyed, hundred-fold powerful oblation that grants a hundred-year lifespan, I have brought him here;
so that Indra may lead him through the autumns to the further shore of all misfortune. 3.
Live for a hundred autumns, growing strong; live for a hundred winters and a hundred springs.
May Indra, Agni, Savitṛ, and Bṛhaspati grant you a hundred years; with this oblation, I have brought him back to a life of a hundred years. 4.
Enter, O out-breath and in-breath, like two oxen into their pen;
let other deaths pass away—those which they call the hundred others.
Stay right here, O out-breath and in-breath; do not depart from here. Carry this body’s limbs back again for the sake of old age.
I entrust you to old age; I settle you down for old age.
May auspicious old age lead you away; let other deaths pass by—those which they call the hundred.

Old age has bound you, O man, as one binds an ox with a rope. That death which seized you with a strong noose as you were being born—Bṛhaspati has released it from you by means of his hands of truth. //8//
Right here I fix the firm house; may it stand in safety, dripping with clarity.
O House, may we approach you with all our heroes, with good heroes, with unharmed heroes. 1.
Right here, O house, stand firm—rich in horses, rich in cattle, rich in pleasantness; full of vigor, full of clarity, full of milk. Rise up for great good fortune!
(3) You are a support, O house, with great meters and abundant grain.
May the calf come to you, may the boy come, and may the milch-cows come in the evening, lowing. 3.
May Savitṛ, Vāyu, Indra, and Bṛhaspati, who are all-knowing, set up this hall.
May the Maruts sprinkle it with water and ghee; may King Bhaga extend our cultivation.
O wife of Māna, you are a refuge, a pleasant one; O goddess, you were fashioned by the gods at the beginning.
Wearing grass, you were well-disposed; therefore, grant us wealth together with heroic sons. 5.
By means of *ṛta*, ascend the pillar, O mighty beam; shining forth, drive away our enemies.
Let those who dwell near you not come to harm; in this house, O hall, may we live for a hundred autumns with all our heroes.
Hither comes this young boy, the child, together with the moving world;
hither have come the flowing juices in jars, along with the vessels of curd.
O woman, bring forward this full pitcher, filled with a stream of ghee prepared with immortality.
Anoint these drinkers with immortality; may it protect this [act] of sacrifice and charity. 8.
I bring forth these waters, free from disease and destroyers of disease;
I settle into my home together with the immortal fire.
When you were flowing together there and cried out at being struck by the *ahau*, from that [reason] you are called "Rivers" (*nadyas*); those are your names, O rivers (*sindhavas*). //1//
When, sent by Varuṇa, you moved together swiftly, Indra reached you as you were going; therefore, O Waters, you flow according to him.
Flowing away against your will, you have indeed opened the way for him; O goddesses, Indra has overcome you with his powers. Therefore, the name "Vārs" has been bestowed upon you.
"A single god stood over you as you flowed according to your will;
they brought you forth as the great ones—therefore you are called *udaka*. (AVŚ 3.13.4)
The waters were auspicious; the waters were indeed clarified butter. Those waters bear Agni and Soma within them.
May the intense essence of those honeyed ones, reaching us readily, come to me with breath and with splendor. 5.
Then indeed I see, or else I hear; the sound of them comes unto me, their voice. I think that I have partaken of immortality even then, when I was satiated by you who are golden-hued.
This, O Waters, is your heart; this is your calf, O you who follow the cosmic order (*ṛtāvarī*).
Come here in this manner, O powerful ones (*śakvarī*), to where I settle you.
May you be united with a comfortable cow-pen, united with wealth, and united with prosperity.
With that name which was born on the day [of your birth], we unite you. 1.
May Aryaman unite you; may Pūṣan unite you; may Bṛhaspati unite you;
and may Indra, the winner of wealth, unite you. May whatever riches there are flourish within me. 2.
Gathering together, fearless, dwelling in this cow-pen,
bearing the Soma-sweetness, come hither free from disease.
Right here the cows come; right here, like Śakī, do you thrive. Right here indeed beget offspring; let there be harmony among you within me. 4.
May your stall be auspicious; thrive like the *śāriśāka* plant!
Multiply right here; we unite you with me.
O cows, be united with me, your master! This is your stall here, which shall nourish you.
Becoming abundant through the increase of wealth, may we, living and keeping you alive, dwell near you.
I impel Indra the merchant; may he come to us and be our leader.
Driving away the hostile spirit, the waylayer, and the wild beast, may he, as the sovereign lord, be a giver of wealth to me. 1.
The many paths leading to the gods that traverse between heaven and earth—may they favor me with milk and ghee, so that having purchased [the goods], I may bring back wealth. //2//
O Agni, desiring [success] with fuel and ghee, I offer this oblation for speed and strength; as much as I am able, praising with a sacred prayer, I offer this divine hymn for a hundredfold gain. 3.
O Agni, forgive us this transgression on this path which we have traveled so far.
May our buying and selling be auspicious, as well as our bargaining; may it make me successful in my trade.
Accepting this oblation together, may you both enjoy it; may our going out and our returning be auspicious. 4.

With that wealth with which I conduct my trade, O gods—with that wealth, seeking further wealth—may it become more for me and not less. O Agni, slayer of the plunderer, settle the gods with our oblation. //5//
With that wealth by which I carry on trade, O gods—seeking wealth with that very wealth—may Indra, Prajāpati, Savitṛ, Soma, and Agni bestow upon me a desire for it. //6//
(3.15.7a) With homage we praise you, O Hotṛ Vaiśvānara;
(3.15.7c) as such, be watchful for us among our offspring, our selves, our cattle, and our vital breaths. //7//
(8a) May we always bring [offerings] to you at all times, O Jātavedas, as one brings fodder to a standing horse.
(8c) Rejoicing in the increase of wealth and in nourishment, may we, your neighbors, O Agni, never come to harm. //8//
At dawn we invoke Agni; at dawn Indra; at dawn Mitra and Varuṇa; at dawn the Aśvins.
At dawn Bhaga, Pūṣan, and Brahmaṇaspati; at dawn we invoke Soma and Rudra. //1//

We invoke the fierce Bhaga, the winner in the morning, the son of Aditi who is the distributor. Even the weak man, even the swift one, and even the king, thinking of him, says, "May I partake of Bhaga."
O Bhaga, leader; O Bhaga, whose gifts are true; O Bhaga, favor this prayer and grant us wealth.
O Bhaga, cause us to prosper with cattle and horses; O Bhaga, may we be rich in men through our heroes. 3.
And may we now be blessed, both at the journey's end and in the midst of the days;
and at the rising of the sun, O Maghavan, may we abide in the favor of the gods. //4//
May the god Bhaga indeed be the Blessed One; through him may we be blessed. O Bhaga, I call upon you, everyone, with fervent cries; as such, O Bhaga, be our leader here.
Let the Dawns bow down to the sacrifices, as [they do] to the pure station of Dadhikrāvan.
May the horses, like spirited steeds, bring hither to me Bhaga, the finder of wealth, as they draw a chariot.

May the auspicious Dawns, rich in horses, rich in cattle, and rich in heroes, shine upon us always. Yielding clarified butter, overflowing on every side, do you protect us ever with your blessings. (AVŚ 3.16.7)
The seers yoke the ploughs; they stretch out the yokes separately, the wise ones, seeking favor among the gods.
Yoke the ploughs, stretch out the yokes; sow the seed here in the prepared womb. May the Virāj be our fruitful yield, bringing abundance; may the sickles come closer to reap the ripened grain.
The plough, sharp-pointed, well-holed, with a handle for Soma,
let it throw up the cow and the sheep, the wagon for the chariot, the fat one, and the prolific mare.
May Indra take hold of the furrow; may Pūṣan protect it.
May she, rich in milk, yield for us [milk] for each succeeding year.
May the good ploughshares cleave the earth; may the good ploughmen follow after their draft-animals.
O Śuna and Sīra, being gratified by the oblation, make the plants bear good fruit for this man.
May the draft-animals be auspicious, may the men be auspicious; may the plough furrow auspiciously.
May the leather thongs be bound on auspiciously; move the goad-stick auspiciously.
O Śuna and Sīra, may you both take pleasure here in my offering;
with that milk which you created in heaven, sprinkle this [earth]! 7.
O Sītā, we revere you; O auspicious one, turn toward us.
So that you may be well-disposed toward us, so that you may bear us good fruit. //8//
(9) Anointed with ghee and honey, approved by all the gods and the Maruts—
O Sītā, turn toward us with milk, swelling with vigor and abounding in ghee.
I dig up this herb, the most powerful of plants,
by which one overcomes a rival wife and by which one finds a husband.
O you with upturned leaves, auspicious one, impelled by the gods, victorious one:
drive my rival far away; make my husband mine alone.
For you have not grasped his name, nor do you take delight in this husband.
We send your rival wife away to the furthest distance. 3.
I am the superior one; O superior one, may I rise above those who are superior. Below is my rival; she who is lower than me, let her be lower than those who are lower. //4//
I am the conqueror, and you are the victorious;
having both become powerful, let us together overcome my rival wife.
I have placed the victorious one before you; I have placed the more powerful one near you.
May your mind run toward me like a cow toward her calf; may it run along the path like water to the furrow.
Sharpened for me is this sacred formulation (*brahman*), sharpened is my vigor and strength;
may the sovereign power (*kṣatra*) of those for whom I am the domestic priest be sharpened, undecaying, and victorious. //1//
May I prevail over their kingdom; may I prevail over their vigor, prowess, and strength. With this oblation, I sever the arms of my enemies.
Let them fall low and be beneath us—those who would attack our patron, our bountiful lord. With my sacred word (*brahman*), I destroy the enemies; I raise up my own people. 3.
Sharper than an axe, and even sharper than fire, more keen than Indra’s thunderbolt are those for whom I am the domestic priest. //4//
I bind together their weapons; I cause their kingdom, rich in heroes, to increase.
May their sovereignty be invincible and undecaying; may all the gods favor their intent. (AVŚ 3.19.5)
Let the strengths of the bounteous one be uplifted; let the shout of the conquering heroes go up.
Let the various shouts, the tumultuous cries, and the banners rise up.
Let the gods, with Indra as their chief, come with the Maruts as their army.
Advance, O men, and conquer! May your arms be mighty;
with sharp arrows and strong bows, you who possess fierce weapons, may you, with your powerful arms, slay the weak.
Loosed, fly away, O arrow, sharpened by the sacred word (*brahman*).
Conquer the enemies, fall upon them; slay their best man after best man; let not one among them escape me.
This is your seasonal womb, from which once born you shone forth;
knowing it, O Agni, ascend it and increase our wealth for us. //1//
O Agni, speak here for us; turn toward us with a gracious mind.
Bestow upon us, O Lord of the People; you are the giver of wealth to us. 2.
May Aryaman grant us [wealth], may Bhaga, may Bṛhaspati; may the goddesses and Sūnṛtā grant it. May the goddess bestow wealth upon me. //3//
