We invoke King Soma for protection, Agni with our songs of praise, Āditya, Viṣṇu, Sūrya, and Bṛhaspati the priest. //4//
O Agni, with your fires, increase our prayer and our sacrifice.
O God, impel us to bestow wealth upon us for the sake of giving. 5.
Indra and Vāyu, both of you who are easy to invoke, we summon here; so that in this assembly all people may be well-disposed toward us and desirous of giving to us.
Urge Aryaman, Bṛhaspati, and Indra to bestow gifts;
[urge] Vāta, Viṣṇu, Sarasvatī, and the powerful Savitṛ.
We have indeed come together at the impulse of strength, within all these worlds.
May he, knowing, cause him who is unwilling to give to give; and bestow upon us wealth consisting of all heroic sons. 8.
May the five regions yield for me; may the wide expanses yield according to my strength.
May I attain all my intentions with my mind and my heart. 9.
May I utter speech that wins cattle; may splendor rise up to meet me. May Vāyu encompass me from all sides; may Tvaṣṭṛ bestow prosperity upon me.
The fires that are within the waters, those in Vṛtra, those in man, and those in stones;
those that have entered the plants and those that have entered the trees—may this oblation be offered to all those fires. //1//

That which is within the Soma, that which is within the cows, that which has entered into birds and that which is in wild beasts; that which has entered bipeds and that which has entered quadrupeds—let this be an oblation to those fires. //2//

The god Vaiśvānara who travels in the same chariot as Indra, and who is the giver of all wealth—he whom I invoke repeatedly in battles as the victorious; let this oblation be offered to those Agnis. //3//
The god who is all, whom they call desire, whom they call the giver and the receiver; he who is wise, powerful, encompassing, and undeceivable—let this be an offering to those Agnis. //4//

To you, whom the thirteen Bhauvanas and the five Mānavas have recognized in their minds as the Hotṛ-priest—to those Agnis, may this offering be made for the sake of splendor, glory, and true joy. //5//
To him whose food is the bull, whose food is the cow, the ordainer with Soma upon his back—
to those Agnis, of whom Vaiśvānara is the eldest, let this be the oblation.
To those who traverse the sky, the earth, and the intermediate space, following the lightning;
to those who are within the quarters or within the wind—to those fires, let this be offered. //7//
We invoke Savitṛ of the golden hands, Indra, Bṛhaspati, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni;
we invoke all the gods and the Aṅgirases—may they pacify this flesh-eating Agni. 8.
The flesh-eating fire is stilled; stilled is the one that seeks out men.
And so, that which consumes all things—I have quelled that flesh-eater.
The mountains whose backs are Soma, the waters with their surfaces turned upward,
Vāta, Parjanya, and Agni— these have quelled the flesh-eater.
May the great glory of the elephant’s luster spread forth—that which was produced from the body of Aditi.
All the gods and Aditi, acting in harmony, have bestowed this entirely upon me.
May Mitra and Varuṇa, Indra and Rudra, take heed;
may the gods, the all-sustainers, anoint me with splendor. 2.

By that splendor through which the elephant came into being, by which the king [arose] among men within the waters, by which the gods attained godhood in the beginning—with that splendor, O Agni, make me radiant today. 3.
Whatever great splendor belongs to you, O Jātavedas, arising from the oblation—
As much as is the splendor of the sun and of the elephant of the Asuras, so much splendor may the Aśvins, garlanded with lotuses, bestow upon me. //4//
As far as the four quarters extend, and as far as the eye reaches—so much may that sensory power, the splendor of an elephant, come together within me. 5.
For the elephant among wild beasts became preeminent among those easy to mount;
with his fortune and splendor, I sprinkle myself.
That by which you became a barren cow—that we cause to perish from you.
Here we place that far away from you, in the distance.
May a male embryo enter your womb like an arrow into a quiver;
may a heroic son be born here for you, ten months old.
Give birth to a male son; may a man be born after him. May you be the mother of sons already born, and give birth to those yet to be born. (3)
Whatever excellent seeds the bull produces, through those may you find a son; become a prolific milch-cow.
I prepare for you that which belongs to Prajāpati; let the embryo enter your womb.
O woman, find a son for yourself, and may you be auspicious to him, and he likewise to you. 5.
Of those plants whose father is heaven, whose mother is earth, and whose root is the ocean—
may those divine herbs aid you for the sake of obtaining offspring.
The plants are full of milk; full of milk is my speech. Therefore, I bring hither by the thousands [the essence] of those that are full of milk.
I know him who made the milk-filled grain abundant;
that god whose name is "Accumulator" (Saṃbhṛtvan), him we invoke, whoever dwells in the house of the non-sacrificer. 2.
These five directions, the five tribes of men— like rivers when it rains, may they bring here an abundance and ward off the curse.
Like a spring with a hundred streams, a thousand streams, inexhaustible— so be this grain of ours, with a thousand streams, inexhaustible.
O hundred-handed one, gather it together; O thousand-handed one, scatter it.
Bring about the increase here of what has been done and what is to be done. 5.
Three measures belong to the Gandharvas, four to the housewife;
of these, with that which is most full, we touch you.
Both Upoha and Samūha are your two attendants, O Prajāpati;
let them bring here abundant prosperity and inexhaustible abundance.
Let the piercer pierce you; do not hold fast upon your own bed. With that arrow of desire which is terrible, I pierce you in the heart. //1//
The arrow whose feathers are longing, whose barb is desire,
and whose nock is volition— having made it well-straightened, let Desire pierce you in the heart.
That well-aimed arrow of desire which withers the spleen—the burning one with forward-pointing feathers—with that I pierce you in the heart. 3.
Pierced by grief, withered by fever, and parched-mouthed, crawl away from me!
Be gentle, free from anger, devoted solely to me, speaking kindly, and faithful to your vows.
I have brought you forth from the mother and from the father, O noble one;
so that you may abide in my will and follow my thought.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, cast away from her heart its thoughts;
then, having rendered her devoid of will, bring her under my control alone.
O you gods named Hetis who are in this eastern quarter, Agni is your arrow; may you be gracious to us, may you speak for us; homage to you, to you svāhā!
O gods who are in this southern quarter, you whose name is Aviṣyavas, may your desires be our arrows. Be gracious to us; speak for us. Homage to you! To you, Svāhā! //2//
O you gods who are in this western quarter, named Vairājas, water is your arrow; may you be gracious to us, may you speak for us; homage to you, to you svāhā! //3//
O you gods named Pravidhyantas who abide in this northern quarter, the wind is your arrow; may you be gracious to us, may you speak for us; homage to you, to you svāhā!
O gods named Nilmipas who dwell in this fixed quarter, the plants are your arrows; may you be gracious to us, may you speak in our favor. To you [we offer] homage; to you, Svāhā!
Those gods who abide in this upward direction, named the *avasvanta*s—Bṛhaspati is your arrow. Be gracious to us; speak for us. Homage to you! To you, svāhā!

The eastern direction has Agni as its overlord; the black snake is its guardian; the Ādityas are its arrows. Homage to them, the overlords; homage to the guardians; homage to the arrows; let there be homage to these!
Whoever hates us and whom we hate, him we place within the jaws of you [the arrows]. 1.

The southern direction has Indra as its overlord; the cross-lined snake is its guardian; the ancestors are its arrows. Homage to them, the overlords; homage to the guardians; homage to the arrows; let there be homage to these!
Whoever hates us and whom we hate, him we place within the jaws of you [the arrows]. 2.
The western quarter has Varuṇa as its overlord, the viper as its guardian, and food as its arrows.
Homage to them, the overlords; homage to the guardians; homage to the arrows; let there be homage to these!
Whoever hates us and whom we hate, him we place within the jaws of you all. 3.
The northern direction; Soma is its overlord, the *svaja* serpent its guardian, and thunderbolts its arrows.
Homage to them, the overlords; homage to the guardians; homage to the arrows; let there be homage to these!
Whoever hates us and whom we hate, him we place within the jaws of you all. //4//
The fixed direction; Viṣṇu the overlord; Kalmāṣagrīva the protector; plants the arrows. Homage to them, the overlords; homage to the protectors; homage to the arrows; let there be homage to these!
Whosoever hates us, and whomever we hate—him we place within the jaws of you [the arrows]. //5//
The upward direction has Bṛhaspati as its overlord, Śvitra as its protector, and rain as its arrows.
Homage to them, the overlords; homage to the protectors; homage to the arrows; let there be homage to these!
Whoever hates us, and whomsoever we hate—him we place within the jaws of you [the arrows]. //6//
By each single act of creation she came into being, there where the creators of beings released the cows of every form.
There, she who is born without a season, the restrainer—she, the hissing, the ruddy one, destroys the cattle.
This [night] destroys livestock, becoming a flesh-eater and a devourer;
therefore, one should give her to a Brahmin, so that she may be pleasant and auspicious.
Be auspicious toward men, auspicious toward cows and horses;
be auspicious toward this entire field, and be auspicious to us here.
Here is nourishment, here is sap; here become the best at winning a thousandfold.
O restrainer, cause the cattle to thrive. //4//
Where those of kind heart and virtuous deeds rejoice, having cast off disease from their own bodies—to that world Yamī has gone; may she not harm our men and cattle.
Where there is the world of those who are kind-hearted, of the doers of good deeds, and of those who have offered the *agnihotra*—to that world has Yamī gone; may she not harm our men and our cattle.
When the kings, the members of Yama’s assembly, divide the sixteenth part of one’s sacrifices and pious works,
from that [debt] the white-footed sheep, given as a *svadhā* offering, releases him.
Fulfilling all desires, prevailing, prevailing over all, prevailing; the one born of intention, the ram given as a gift, the white-footed one does not fail us. //2//
He who gives a white-footed sheep, commensurate with the world, ascends to the firmament where no toll is levied by the weak against the stronger. //3//
One who gives a ewe with five cakes and white feet, equal in measure to the world,
lives on inexhaustibly in the world of the ancestors.
The sheep with five cakes and white feet, commensurate with the world—
he who gives it lives on the inexhaustible [portion] of Sūryā and Māsa.
Like a stream it does not fail; like the ocean its great waters;
like two gods dwelling together, the white-footed one does not fail.
Who has given this to whom? Desire has given it to desire. Desire is the giver; desire is the receiver; desire has entered the ocean.
With desire I receive you; O Desire, this is yours.
(8) May the earth receive you; may this great intermediate space [receive you]. Having received [you] back, may I not be deprived of breath, of self, or of offspring. 8.
I create for you a shared heart, harmony, and freedom from enmity.
Cherish one another as the cow longs for her newborn calf.
May the son be obedient to his father; may he be in harmony with his mother. May the wife speak to her husband words that are sweet and peaceful.
Let not brother hate brother, nor sister her sister; becoming harmonious and of one purpose, speak your word with auspiciousness.
That by which the gods do not fall apart and do not hate one another— that we establish as a sacred bond (*brahman*) in your house, for the sake of concord among men.

O you who possess excellence and wisdom, do not be divided; acting in harmony and moving together as companions, speak kindly to one another. I make you all turn toward one another, of one mind. //5//
Common is the water-trough for you, common your share of food; with a single thong I bind you together.
Together, pay honor to Agni, as spokes encircle the nave.
I make you all turn toward one another, of like mind, with a single will, through this act of reconciliation.
Like the gods guarding the nectar of immortality, may there be goodwill among you every evening and morning.
O gods, drive away old age; O Agni, drive it away from ill-will. May I be separated from all evil and from disease, and united with long life.
May Pavamāna purify me from affliction; may Śakra purify me from evil-doing. May I be purified from every evil, and from consumption, and united with long life.
May the domestic animals be separated from those of the forest; may the waters flow away from thirst.
May I be separated from all evil and from consumption, and united with long life.
May Heaven and Earth separate me from this; may the paths [separate] me from every direction.
May I be separated from all evil and from consumption, and be united with long life.
"Tvaṣṭṛ yokes his daughter for her bridal procession"—thus this entire world goes forth.
May I be separated from all evil, separated from consumption, and united with long life. (AVŚ 3.31.5)
Agni restores the vital breaths; the Moon is joined with the vital breath. May I be separated from all evil and from consumption, and be united with long life.
By means of the vital breath, the gods brought together the sun, whose strength is everywhere. May I be separated from all evil and from consumption, and united with long life.
O long-lived ones, makers of life, live by means of breath; do not die!
May I be separated from all evil and from consumption, and united with life. 8.
With breath, breathe for those who breathe; remain right here, do not die!
I have separated myself from all evil, from consumption, and been united with life. 9.
Up with life, together with life, with the essence of the plants!
May I be separated from all evil, separated from consumption, and united with life.
Through the rain of Parjanya we have arisen as immortals; may I be released from all evil and from consumption, and united with long life.
The Brahman, first born in the east, Vena has revealed from the radiant horizon;
he has disclosed its lowest and highest stations, the womb of both the existent and the non-existent. //1//
Let this ancestral, royal power go forth at the head, established among the worlds for the first-born.
For him, let them prepare this bright, glowing oblation, the heated milk, for the first nourisher.
He who was born knowing his kinship proclaims all the generations of the gods.
From the midst of the sacred word (*brahman*), he has raised up the sacred word; he has established himself toward the self-sustaining powers (*svadhā*), both low and high. 3.
For he, the knower, established upon the earth according to the cosmic order (*ṛta*), has propped up the two great worlds for their security.
Great, once born, he has propped up the sky; he has supported his seat in the earthly realm. //4//
Bṛhaspati, the sovereign lord of the gods, has risen from the primordial foundation toward the summit of his birth;
since the bright day was born from the light, may the inspired sages now shine forth with splendor.
Surely Kāvya stirs up that ancient majesty of this great god;
he was born together with many, and thus he has slept in the loosened eastern half.

He who shall go with reverence to Atharvan, the father, the kinsman of the gods, Bṛhaspati—he shall be as the progenitor of all; he shall be a seer, a god, and a self-dependent one who cannot be deceived. (4.1.7)

He who is the giver of self, the giver of strength, whose command all the gods revere—he who rules over these two-footed beings and four-footed beings—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation? //1//
He who by his greatness became the sole king of the breathing and blinking world;
whose shadow is immortality and whose [shadow] is death—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation? //2//
He upon whom the two clamorous ones depend when they are propped apart, and whom the two trembling worlds invoked;
he whose path measures out this mid-air—to which god shall we offer worship with our oblation? 3.
He to whom belong the wide sky and the great earth, and to whom belongs this vast intermediate space;
he to whom that sun is extended by its greatness—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation? 4.
He whose greatness all the snowy mountains proclaim, and of whom they say the ocean is the very essence;
he whose two arms are these quarters of space—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation? //5//
In the beginning, the waters, knowing the cosmic order (*ṛta*), protected all things while holding the germ of immortality.
In those goddesses upon whom the god was established—to which god shall we offer worship with our oblation? //6//

In the beginning, the Golden Germ (Hiraṇyagarbha) came into being; once born, he was the sole Lord of all that exists. He supported both the earth and the sky. To what god shall we offer worship with our oblation? (7)
The waters, giving birth to the calf, first brought together the embryo. And as it was being born, its fetal membrane was golden. To which god shall we offer worship with our oblation? 8.
Up from here have three stepped forth: the tiger, the man, and the wolf.
For the rivers flow apart; the divine tree stands apart; let the enemies bend away. //1//
May the wolf go by another path, and the thief by the farthest way; may the toothed rope pass by, and may the malevolent one flee afar.
We cause your two eyes and your mouth to gape open, O tiger;
then all twenty of your claws as well. //3//
First we crush the tusked tiger; then the thief, the serpent, the sorcerer, and the wolf. 4.
The thief who comes today goes away crushed;
let him go by the ruin of his paths; may Indra slay him with his thunderbolt. //5//
The teeth of the beast are crushed, and its ribs are shattered;
let the lizard be your snare, and let the beast lie low when it seeks its rest.
That which is restraint and not separation, and separation and not restraint—
born of Indra, born of Soma, you are the Atharvanic [charm] that crushes the tiger.
You whom the Gandharva dug for Varuṇa when his virility was destroyed— you, that plant, we dig up now, the one that causes the penis to bristle with excitement.
Up has risen Uṣas, up has risen Sūrya, and up has risen this word of mine.
Let Prajāpati, the bull, stir upward with his vigorous strength.
Just as your body, while growing, was as if scorched by heat, so may this plant make it even more vigorous for you. 3.
The swelling strength of the plants, the essence of the bulls— O Indra, lord of your own body, bestow that virility upon this man.
You are the first-born essence of the waters, and likewise of the trees;
you are even the brother of Soma, and you are the virile power of the arrow.
Today, O Agni; today, O Savitṛ; today, O Goddess Sarasvatī;
today, O Brahmaṇaspati, stretch taut his sinew like a bow.
I stretch your feet like a bowstring upon a bow;
stride always without weariness, like a falcon toward the red bird.
Of the horse, the mule, the goat, and the ram,
and also of the bull— whatever strengths they possess, bestow those upon this man, O Lord of the Body.
The bull with a thousand horns who has risen up from the ocean—with that powerful one, we lull the people to sleep. //1//
The wind does not blow across the earth, and no one sees anything;
lull all the women to sleep and the dogs as well, O Indra’s companion, as you wander.
The women who sleep on couches, those who sleep on beds, and those who sleep in litters;
all those women who possess auspicious fragrances, we cause them all to sleep. //3//
I have seized that which moves and that which moves not; I have seized sight and breath.
I have seized all the limbs at the deep end of the nights. 4.
(5) He who sits, he who moves about, and he who looks while standing—
of them we set the eyes together, so that they may see as this palace does.
(6a) Let the mother sleep; let the father sleep; let the dog sleep; let the lord of the household sleep.
(6c) Let her kinsmen sleep; let this people around her sleep. 6.
O Sleep, by means of the instrument of sleep, lull all the people to rest.
Make others sleep until the sun rises; may I remain awake until dawn, unharmed and undecaying like Indra.
The Brahmin was born first, ten-headed and ten-faced;
he was the first to drink the Soma, and he made the poison sapless.
As far as heaven and earth extend in breadth, as far as the seven rivers have spread out—
I have uttered from here that speech which destroys poison.
The fair-winged Garuḍa first swallowed you, O poison. You did not intoxicate him, nor did you mangle him; indeed, you became like a father to him.
The poison of that five-fingered [arrow] which was aimed at you from the curved bow—even from the bolt of the Apaskambha, I have spoken the poison away. 4.
From the barb I have spoken the poison out; from the ointment and from the feather-case;
from the haft, from the horn, and from the point of the arrow, I have spoken the poison out. 5.
(6) Tasteless is the shaft of your arrow, and so too is your poison tasteless; even the bow of that tree is tasteless, and your [arrow] is utterly devoid of taste.
Those who squeezed, those who sucked, those who bit, and those who released [the poison]—all of them have been made castrated; the mountain of poison has been made castrated. //7//
(8a) Castrated are your diggers; you, O herb, are castrated. (8c) Castrated is that mountain, that peak, from which this poison was born. //8//
This water wards off [evil] upon Varanāvati; there the nectar of immortality has been poured. With that, I ward off your poison. //1//
Tasteless is the poison from the east, tasteless is that which comes from the north; even this [poison] from below is neutralized by the *karambha* porridge. //2//
Having made a side-dish of parched grain, a swelling drink, a source of strength—O you of evil intent, it was indeed hunger that caused you to devour it; thus you have not destroyed him.
O you who possess intoxication, we cause your rapture to fall like an arrow; we steady you with our word, as one steadies a moving vessel of boiled rice. //4//
Like a village that has been plundered, we settle you with our word.
Stand firm like a tree in its place; do not be shattered when struck by the axe.
They have purchased you with winnowing-baskets, with speckled skins, and even with antelope hides.
You are bought, O herb; once dug up, do not cause us further pain.
Those first deeds of yours which were performed unattainably—may they not deceive our heroes here; I place that very thing before you.
The Being bestows milk upon all beings; he has become the sovereign lord of beings.
Death performs his *rājasūya* sacrifice; may that King grant his approval for this. //1//
Go forward; do not shrink back, O fierce one, perceiving and slaying the rival! Stand firm, O increaser of friends; the gods have spoken in favor of you.
All have honored him as he ascends; clothed in splendor, he moves, self-luminous.
Great is that name of the bull-like Asura; assuming all forms, he has taken his stand upon the immortal realms.
O tiger, stride forth upon the tiger-skin toward the great quarters.
May all the tribes desire you, and may the celestial waters, rich in milk, long for you.
The waters that are celestial, which rejoice with milk in the intermediate space or upon the earth—
of all those waters, I sprinkle you with splendor.
The celestial waters, rich in milk, have sprinkled you with splendor, so that you may be a multiplier of friends; may Savitṛ make you thus.
Embracing this tiger, they urge on the lion for great good fortune;
like well-faring ones [urging] the ocean, they groom the leopard standing within the waters.
Come, O living one, to this eye of the mountain that protects;
may it be a protective fence for the sake of life, granted by all the gods.
You are the protection for men, the protection for cattle;
you stand as the protection for horses and coursers.
And you are a protection from all sides, O ointment that crushes the sorcerers;
you know the way to immortality, and you are the sustenance for the living, as well as the healing medicine of the green [plant]. //3//
O ointment, as you creep into every limb, joint by joint,
from there you drive away the consumption, like a fierce man who sits in the midst.
Neither curse, nor sorcery, nor burning grief reaches him;
neither does *viṣkandha* seize him, O ointment, who wears you.
From evil spells, from bad dreams, from misdeeds, and even from defilement—
from the terrible eye of the malevolent heart, protect us from that, O Ointment!
Knowing this, O collyrium, I shall speak the truth and not falsehood:
may I win back the horse, the cow, and my own self, O man. (AVŚ 4.9.7)
Three slaves of the ointment are fever, consumption, and the serpent;
the highest of mountains, named Trikakuṭ, is your father. //8//
The collyrium from Trikakud, produced from the Himalayas—
may it crush all malevolent spirits and all female sorceresses.
Whether you are called Traikakuda or Yamuna, both these names of yours are auspicious; with them, O ointment, protect us! 10.
Born from the wind, from the intermediate space, and from the light of lightning—
he who is born of gold, the conch, the pearl, may he protect us from distress.
(4.10.2a) You who were born from the ocean, foremost among the luminous realms;
(4.10.2c) having struck down the Rākṣasas with our conch, we shall overcome the devourers. //2//
With the conch, [ward off] disease and mental distress; with the conch, also [ward off] the *sadānvās*.
May the conch, the all-healing one, and the golden ornament protect us from misfortune.
Born in heaven, born from the ocean, brought forth from the river—may that conch, born of gold, the amulet that prolongs our life, protect us. //4//
The jewel is born from the ocean; the sun is born from Vṛtra.
May it protect us from all sides against the weapon of the gods and the asuras. //5//
(4.10.6a) You are the one among golden things; you were born from Soma.
(4.10.6c) You are visible in the chariot, you are radiant in the quiver; may he prolong our lifespans. //6//
The bone of the gods became a pearl; it moves within the waters, endowed with a living soul.
That I bind upon you for life, for splendor, for strength, for long life lasting a hundred autumns. May the pearl protect you! 7.
The ox has supported the earth and the sky; the ox has supported the broad mid-air. The ox has supported the six wide quarters; the ox has entered the entire world. //1//
Indra is the draft-ox; he looks out for the sake of the cattle. The Mighty One measures out the three paths.
Milking the past, the future, and the worlds, he carries out all the ordinances of the gods. //2//
Indra, having been born among men, moves as the heated *gharma* vessel, glowing with intense heat.
May he who knows the ox possess good offspring; let him not sit down in that noble place if he would eat [the meat] of the ox. 3.
The ox yields milk in the world of the righteous; Pavamāna nourishes him from the front.
Parjanya is his udder, the Maruts its teat, sacrifice is his milk, and the sacrificial fee is his milking. 4.

He over whom neither the lord of the sacrifice nor the sacrifice itself has power, nor does the giver have power over him, nor the receiver—he who is the winner of all, the sustainer of all, the maker of all; tell us of that four-footed *gharma* which he is. 5.
By that path by which the gods ascended to heaven, leaving behind the body— the navel of immortality—
by that may we go to the world of the well-done, through the observance of the *gharma* and through austerity, seeking glory.
Indra by his form, Agni by his vehicle, Prajāpati, Parameṣṭhin, and Virāj stepped upon Viśvānara; he stepped upon Vaiśvānara; he stepped upon Anaduhr.
He made it firm; he supported it.
This is the middle of the ox where this yoke is placed;
as far as it extends backward, so much is its extent forward.
He who milks the seven milkings of the Vedas that flow down in succession, attains both progeny and the world; thus the Seven Seers have known.
Treading upon the sediment with his feet, uprooting the nourishing moisture with his shanks,
the ox and the plowman together reach the sweet mead through their toil.
They say that these twelve nights belong to Prajāpati as days of observance;
therein lies the sacred formulation (*brahman*) for one who knows it, and that indeed is the vow of the ox.
She yields in the evening, she yields in the morning, she yields throughout the midday. We know those milkings of hers which come together, following one another.
You are the healer; you are the healer of the broken bone. O Arundhatī, may you heal this! 1.
Whatever of yours is injured, whatever of yours is shattered, or whatever of yours is crushed within your own self— may Dhātṛ restore that with his auspicious power, joint by joint.
May your marrow unite with marrow, and may your joint meet with joint;
may what is loosened of your flesh and your bone grow together again. 3.
Let marrow be joined with marrow; let skin grow together with skin. Let your blood grow upon the bone; let flesh grow together with flesh. //4//
Let hair join with hair; let skin join with skin.
Let your blood and bone grow together; mend what is broken, O herb!
Arise, go forth, run forward! This chariot has good wheels, good felloes, and a good nave; stand upright upon it.
If the spear, having fallen, has shattered, or if the stone hurled has struck him,
may he knit the joint together joint by joint, as a craftsman repairs the parts of a chariot.
O gods, raise up again that which has been cast down; O gods, restore again that which has committed sin. O gods, you bring the dead back to life once more.
(2) These two winds blow from the ocean and from the far distance.
May one blow strength upon you; may the other blow away whatever is harmful.
O Wind, blow hither healing; O Wind, blow away whatever is harmful.
For you, possessing all remedies, go as the messenger of the gods. 3.
May the gods protect him; may the hosts of Maruts protect him; may all beings protect him, so that he may be free from harm. 4.
I have come to you with healing remedies and with means for your safety; I have brought you powerful skill, and I drive away your consumption.
This hand of mine is blessed; this hand of mine is more blessed.
This hand of mine possesses all healing remedies; this hand has a propitious touch.
With these two hands, which have ten fingers, and with the tongue, the leader of speech—
with those two healthy hands, we touch you.
For the goat was born from the heat of Agni; he beheld his progenitor in the beginning.
By him the gods attained the highest divinity; by him the worthy ones ascended to the heights. //1//
Step forth toward the sky with Agni, carrying the fire-pan in your hands;
having gone to the back of heaven, the light, join yourselves with the gods.
From the back of the earth I have ascended to the intermediate space; from the intermediate space I have ascended to heaven.
From the back of the vault of heaven, I have gone to the light of the sun.
Going to the light, they look not back; they ascend to heaven, to both worlds—those who, being well-knowing, have extended the sacrifice that flows in every direction.
O Agni, go forward as the first among the deities, the eye of both gods and men.
May the sacrificers, desiring to worship in harmony with the Bhr̥gus, go safely to the light of heaven. 5.
I anoint the unborn one with milk and ghee—the divine, well-winged, milky, and vast one.
By means of him, may we go to the world of the well-done, ascending to the light, toward the highest firmament.
Lift up this fivefold rice with the five fingers using the ladle;
place the head of the Unborn in the eastern direction, and place his right side in the southern direction.
Place his buttock in the western direction; place his northern flank in the northern direction.
Place the spine of the Unborn One in the upward direction; place his belly in the fixed direction, and his middle in the midst of the intermediate space.
The goat is cooked; clothe it with its cooked skin, it which is composed of all its limbs and possesses every form.
Let it rise up from here toward the highest firmament; stand firm in the quarters with your four feet. //9//

Let the cloud-bearing quarters of the sky rise up; let the clouds, driven by the wind, come together. May the waters, lowing like the bellowing of a great bull, satisfy the earth as it thunders with moisture.
May the powerful ones, the bounteous givers, look upon us; may the essences of the waters unite with the plants.
May the outpourings of rain glorify the earth, and may plants of every form spring forth in abundance.
Look down upon the songs of those who sing; let the floods of the waters surge forth separately.
Let the outpourings of rain glorify the earth; let plants of every form spring up everywhere. //3//
Let the hosts of Maruts, thundering like Parjanya, sing for you individually;
let the streams of the raining rain fall upon the earth.
Arise from the ocean, O Maruts; let the brilliant hymn cause the cloud to fly up.
May the waters, lowing like cows, satisfy the earth after the great bull has roared with his thunder. 5.
Roar out, thunder, and strike the ocean; O Parjanya, drench the earth with milk!
Let the rain released by you come down in abundance; let the one who seeks the wind and is emaciated go to his end.
May the bounteous ones protect you, as well as the springs and the serpents;
may the clouds, driven forth by the Maruts, rain down upon the earth.
Let every quarter flash with lightning; let the winds blow from every direction.
Let the clouds, driven forth by the Maruts, gather over the earth.
May the waters, lightning, cloud, and rain—O you of liberal gifts—protect you together; may the springs and the serpents, and the clouds driven forth by the Maruts, protect the earth. //9//

Agni, who is in harmony with the bodies of the waters and has become the sovereign lord of the plants—may he, Jātavedas, win rain for us, and may he bring forth from the sky life-breath and immortality for our progeny. 10.
Prajāpati, driving forth the waters from the ocean and the flood, causes the sea to swell. Let the seed of the stallion swell; come hither with this thundering roar.
Pouring out the waters, our father Asura, let the gargling sounds of the waters resound; O Varuṇa, release the downward-flowing waters.
Let the frogs with speckled arms croak along the pools.
Having lain dormant for a year, the Brahmins who observe their vows—the frogs—have raised their voices, which are quickened by Parjanya. 13.
Speak forth, O female frog; speak toward the rain, O Tādurī!
Swim in the middle of the lake, having spread out your four feet.
Khaṇvakha! Khaimakha! O Taduri, in the midst [of it]! Send down the rain, O Fathers; seek the mind of the Maruts! 15.15
Pour forth upon the great treasure-chest; let it be accompanied by lightning, and let the wind blow.
Let the winds spread the sacrifice in many ways, and let the plants be full of joy.
Their great overseer sees as if from close at hand;
though one thinks himself moving while wandering, all the gods know this. //1//
He who stands, he who moves, and he who deceives; he who moves in concealment and he who moves openly—whatever two people sit together and whisper, King Varuṇa knows it as the third.
And this earth belongs to King Varuṇa, as does that great heaven with its distant limits;
and both oceans are the belly of Varuṇa, and even in this small amount of water he is hidden.
Even he who might crawl beyond the sky to the far distance shall not be released from King Varuṇa.
His spies move forth from heaven; with their thousand eyes, they behold this earth.
King Varuṇa beholds all that which is between the two worlds and that which is beyond;
he has counted the twinklings of the eyes of men; like a gambler casting down the dice, he ordains them all.
Those snares of yours, O Varuṇa, seven by seven, which stand released in three groups, full of wrath—let them all cut the one who speaks untruth, and let them release him who speaks the truth. //6//
Bind him with a hundred snares, O Varuṇa; let not the speaker of untruth escape you, O watcher of men!
Let this wretch sit with his belly hanging down, like a jar being cut off at its base.
Varuṇa who is from those nearby, he who is from those afar; Varuṇa who is from the same region, he who is from a different region;
Varuṇa who is divine, and he who is human. //8//
With all these snares I bind you, O [Name], son of [Father's Name] and [Mother's Name]. And all of them I assign to you. 9.
We take hold of you for victory, you who are the sovereign of healing medicines;
O herb, we have made you of a thousandfold power for everyone.
I have invoked all the plants—the truth-conquering, oath-averting, overpowering, and regenerating—so that they may carry us safely across from here. 2.
She who cursed with a curse, she who placed a blight upon the grain, she who undertook the seizing of the essence for her offspring—may she devour her own child. 3.
The spell which they made for you in an unbaked vessel, that which they made in blue and red, the magic spell (*kṛtyā*) which they made upon raw flesh—with that, slay the makers of the spell! 4.
Bad dreams, a miserable life, the demon, the monster, and the mischievous spirits—all those with evil names and evil voices, we cause them to perish from us. //5//
The death of hunger, the death of thirst, the lack of cattle, and childlessness—
O Apāmārga, by means of you, we wipe all that away.
The death of thirst, the death of hunger, and likewise the defeat at dice—
O Apāmārga, by means of you we wipe all that away.
Apāmārga, among all plants, you alone are the sole controller.
With it, we wipe away what has settled upon you; now move about free from disease. 8.
The light is equal to the sun; night is equal to the day. I make this true for my protection: let the sorceresses be rendered sapless. //1//
O gods, may he who, having fashioned a *kṛtyā*, carries it off to the house of one who knows not, fall back upon him like a sucking calf to its mother. 2.
He who, having internalized evil within himself, seeks to strike down another with it—when that [evil] is burnt away, many stones crackle loudly. 3.
O thousandfold abode, with your shadow, seize the Viśikhas and the Vigrīvas;
take back the spell to the one who fashioned it, as a beloved gift for the lover.
By means of this herb, I have corrupted all sorceries—
those which they have wrought against your field, those against your cattle, or those against your men.
He who did this was unable to undo it; he broke his foot and a toe.
May he do us good, but let him bring torment upon himself.
May the Apāmārga plant wipe away the *kṣetriya* disease and whatever curse there is; may it drive away the sorceresses and all the *arāyī* demons.
Wiping away the sorcerers and all the *arāyyas*,
O *apāmārga*, through you we wipe away all that.
(1) You are the one who makes us friendless, and you are the one who makes us kinless; moreover, cut off the offspring of the sorcerers like a reed in the rainy season.
You have been consecrated by the Brahmin Kaṇva Nārṣada.
Like an army, you go forth, radiant; there is no fear where you arrive, O herb.
You shall go to the forefront of the plants, illuminating them as if with light;
you are the protector of the simple-minded and the slayer of the Rākṣasa.
When the gods, O plant, first drove away the Asuras with you,
from that time on you were born, O herb, as the *apāmārga*.
Splitting [them] with a hundred branches, your father is named Vibhindu;
split him back, you, against whoever assails us. //5//
From the non-existent ground it came into being; that which is a vast expanse—let that indeed, from there, having been shaken off, strike back at the doer.
For you have come forth facing us; you are one whose fruit is directed toward us.
Ward off all curses from me and keep the deadly weapon far away.
Protect me with a hundred; guard me with a thousand!
O Indra, lord of plants, may you, the fierce one, bestow vigor upon me.
She looks hither, she looks thither, she looks away; she looks.
From heaven, from the intermediate space, and from the earth—O Goddess, she sees all that. 1.
The three heavens, the three earths, and these six directions separately—
by you, O divine herb, may I behold all beings.
(4.20.3a) You were indeed the pupil of that divine Suparṇa;
(4.20.3c) you have descended to the earth like a weary bride upon her bridal litter. //3//
The thousand-eyed god placed that [vision] into my right hand;
with it, I see everything—both the Śūdra and the Ārya.
Reveal your forms; do not hide yourself away.
And so, O thousand-eyed one, look upon the Kimīdins.
Show me the sorcerers, show me the female sorceresses;
show me all the *piśācas*—thus do I grasp you, O herb!
You are the eye of Kaśyapa and the four-eyed Śunī; do not let the piśāca pass you by, like the sun moving through a cloudless sky.
From the protective barrier I have seized the sorcerer, the *kimīdin*.
By means of that, I see everything—both the *śūdra* and the *ārya*.
He who flies through the intermediate space and he who glides across the sky—he who regards the earth as his protector, show that *piśāca* to him! 9.
The cows have come; they have brought auspiciousness. Let them sit in the cow-pen and rejoice with us.
May they be here, prolific and many-formed, yielding their milk for Indra through many dawns.
Indra bestows gifts upon the sacrificer and the singer; he gives to him and does not steal back what is his own.
Increasing his wealth more and more, he establishes the one devoted to the gods upon an unbroken field.
They do not perish, nor does the thief harm them; no enemy or calamity dares to attack them.
With those [cows] by which one worships the gods and gives gifts, the master of the herd shall long remain in their company. //3//
Neither does the dust-raising steed overtake them, nor do they go toward the prepared place of sacrifice.
Far-striding and fearless, those cows roam about following that mortal who is a sacrificer.
Cows are Bhaga; cows are Indra; may the cows desire me. Cows are the first draught of Soma.
O people, these which are the cows—Indra am I; with my heart and even with my mind, I seek Indra. 5.
O cows, you make even the emaciated fat; you make even the unlovely beautiful of countenance.
You make the home auspicious, O you of auspicious speech; your great vitality is proclaimed in the assemblies.
May you, rich in offspring, radiant, drinking pure waters at a good watering-place where fine grass abounds—may no thief nor evil-plotters master you; may the missile of Rudra pass you by.
O Indra, strengthen this Kṣatriya of mine; make him the sole bull among the people. Strike down all his enemies; subject them to him, so that he may prevail over those who oppose him. //1//

(4.22.2) Portion this man out among the villagers, among the horses, and among the cattle; let him who is his enemy be deprived of his share. Let him be the pinnacle of dominions, O Indra, the king; subject every enemy to him. (2)
May he be the lord of wealth among riches; may he be the king, the lord of the people.
O Indra, bestow great splendors upon him; deprive his enemy of luster. (3)
For him may Heaven and Earth milk forth abundant wealth, like two milch-cows yielding warm milk.
May this king be dear to Indra; may he be dear to the cows, the plants, and the cattle. 4.
I yoke for you Indra, the superior one, by whom men conquer and are not conquered; he who shall make you the sole bull among the people and the highest of kings among men.
You are above; your rivals are below, O King—whosoever they may be who oppose you.
A sole bull, the friend of Indra, victorious, bring hither the enjoyments of those who act as enemies.
With the face of a lion, devour all the tribes; with the face of a tiger, strike down the enemies. O sole bull, Indra’s friend, victorious, seize away the provisions of those who act as foes.
I meditate upon Agni, the first, the wise one, whom the people of the five tribes kindle in many ways; him who has entered into every clan, we implore: may he deliver us from distress. 1.
Just as you carry the oblation, O Jātavedas, and just as you arrange the sacrifice with full knowledge, so bring us a favorable mind from the gods; may he deliver us from distress. 2.
I praise Agni, who is most effective on every journey, who is to be employed in every rite, and who shares in the sacrificial portion;
he who slays the Rakṣases, who prospers the sacrifice, and is offered with clarified butter—may he deliver us from distress. 3.
We invoke the well-born Jātavedas, Agni Vaiśvānara, the all-pervading, the bearer of oblations; may he deliver us from distress. //4//
With that companion by which the seers displayed their power, and by which they overthrew the magic illusions of the Asuras;
with that fire by which Indra conquered the Paṇis—may it deliver us from distress. //5//
That by which the gods found immortality, by which they made the plants honey-sweet,
by which the gods brought forth the light— that may it release us from distress.
That which shines here in every direction, whatever has been born and whatever is yet to be born—all this belongs to him alone.
I praise Agni; seeking protection, I call upon him repeatedly. May he deliver us from distress.
We meditate upon Indra; indeed, we ever meditate upon him. The hymns of praise have come unto me, O slayer of Vṛtra.
May he who comes to the call of the donor who performs good deeds deliver us from distress. //1//
He who, with fierce arms, went among the fierce ones, he who shattered the strength of the Dānavas;
by whom the rivers were won and by whom the cattle—may he deliver us from distress. //2//
He who is the bull, the protector of the people, the finder of light, for whom the pressing-stones proclaim manly strength;
whose sacrifice, with its seven priests, is most intoxicating—may he deliver us from distress.
He for whom the barren cows, the bulls, and the oxen exist, for whom the sacrificial posts are set up—he who knows the light;
he for whom the bright Soma flows, purified by prayer—may he deliver us from distress. //4//

He whose favor the Soma-pressers desire, whom they invoke as the wielder of the arrow in the quest for cattle—he upon whom the hymn is based, in whom vigor resides—may he deliver us from distress. (AVŚ 4.24.5)
He who was first born for the performance of action, whose power was first awakened,
by whom the raised thunderbolt was hurled at Ahi— may he deliver us from distress.

He who, having mastery, leads armies into battle, he who unites the two kinds of flourishing [prosperities]—I praise Indra; seeking protection, I call upon him repeatedly: may he deliver us from distress.
We meditate upon the ordinances of Vāyu and Savitṛ, you two who enter into living beings and who protect them;
you two who have become the encompassers of the universe—deliver us from distress. //1//
Whose breadth is measured across the earthly realms, by whom the dust of the mid-air has been fixed;
whose limit no one at all has ever reached—may those two deliver us from distress.
In your service the people settle down; when you have risen, O you of wondrous luster, they stir forth.
You two, Vāyu and Savitṛ, protect all beings; as such, deliver us from distress. //3//
Depart, O Vāyu and Savitṛ, from this evil deed; drive away the *rakṣas* and the *śimidā*.
For you two unite us with vigor and with strength; release us from distress. //4//

May Savitar and Vāyu bestow upon me wealth, nourishment, and well-being; may they inspire in my body skill that is most auspicious. Grant us here great health free from disease; may you two release us from distress.

O Savitṛ and Vāyu, you two delight in our excellent thought for the sake of aid; you exhilarate the great, intoxicating [Soma]. Draw near and bestow upon us the downward flow of your favor; may you two release us from distress.
May the most excellent blessings be established in the abode of the two gods.
I praise the god Savitṛ and Vāyu; may those two release us from distress. //7//
I honor you two, Heaven and Earth, the bountiful and harmonious ones, who have spread yourselves out through immeasurable leagues;
for you have become the foundations of all treasures—deliver us from distress. //1//
For you two have become the foundations of riches, O divine ones, increased, auspicious, and far-reaching;
O Heaven and Earth, be gracious to me, and deliver us from distress. //2//
I invoke the two who are free from heat, who perform great penance, the broad and deep ones who are honored by the sages;
O Heaven and Earth, be gracious to me, and deliver us from distress. //3//
O you who bear the nectar of immortality, who bear the oblations, who bear the rivers, and who sustain human beings—O Heaven and Earth, be gracious to me; may you two release us from distress. //4//
O you two who support the ruddy cows, who support the lords of the forest, and within whom all beings dwell—Heaven and Earth, be gracious to me; deliver us from distress. //5//
O Heaven and Earth, you whom they satisfy with sweet syrup and with clarified butter, without whom nothing at all can be accomplished—be gracious to me; deliver us from distress. //6//
Whatever distress afflicts me, or whatever has been done by human agency and not by fate—I praise Heaven and Earth; seeking protection, I call upon you both: release us from this suffering. //7//
I meditate upon the Maruts; may they speak for me; may they favor this strength in the contest for booty.
Like swift horses easy to control, I have invoked them for aid; may they deliver us from distress.
They who always open the inexhaustible spring, they who pour the sap into the plants—those Maruts whose mother is Pṛśni, I place before me; may they deliver us from distress. //2//
The milk of the milch-cows, the sap of the plants, the speed of the horses—O Seers, you who impel these;
may the Maruts be helpful to us, may they be gracious; may they deliver us from distress. //3//
They carry the waters from the ocean up to heaven; they pour them down from heaven upon the earth.
May those Maruts, who move about as lords through the waters, release us from distress. //4//
Those Maruts who satisfy [the earth] with sweet juice, those who [satisfy it] with ghee, or those who mix it with marrow;
those powerful ones who cause rain by means of waters—may they release us from distress. //5//

If this [injury] here, O Maruts, was done by the Marut-host, or if, O Gods, it was done by the divine host—such as this has occurred—O Vasus, you alone have the power for its remedy; may they deliver us from distress.
Sharp is their face, renowned is the powerful host of Maruts, fierce in battles;
I praise the Maruts, I cry out to them in distress—may they release us from suffering.
I honor you two, Bhava and Śarva; know this [offering] of mine, you to whose direction all that shines belongs.
You who are lords over the bipeds and the quadrupeds of this world—release us from distress. //1//
Those two who are superior even in the nearness, and who are known even in the distance as the most excellent among the wielders of arrows;
those two who have mastery over these bipeds and quadrupeds—may they release us from distress.
I invoke the two thousand-eyed slayers of Vṛtra; praising the two fierce ones who provide pasture even from afar, I approach them.
Those two by whose power bipeds and quadrupeds thrive—may they release us from distress.
As many times as you two seized [them] together in abundance at the beginning, and as you have sent forth overwhelming power among the people;
you two who rule over these bipeds and quadrupeds—release us from distress. //4//
From the slaughter of whomsoever among gods or among men none escapes; those two who have mastery over his bipeds and his quadrupeds—may they release us from distress. //5//
Against the sorcerer who performs witchcraft, the root-caster, the Yātudhāna—against him, O fierce ones, hurl the thunderbolt!
O you two who have power over his bipeds and his quadrupeds, deliver us from distress.
Speak for us in battles, O ye two fierce ones; strike with your thunderbolt him who is a *kimīdin*.
I praise Bhava and Śarva; seeking protection, I call upon them repeatedly: may they two deliver us from distress.
I honor you two, Mitra and Varuṇa, increasers of cosmic order, who are of one mind and who drive away the deceitful.
You two protect the speaker of truth in battles; as such, deliver us from distress. //1//
O you two who, being of one mind, drive away the malicious ones and protect the speaker of truth in battles;
O you two who, as observers of men, go to the brown juice—deliver us from distress.
As you protect Aṅgiras, as you protect Agasti, Jamadagni, and Atri, O Mitra and Varuṇa;
as you protect Kaśyapa and Vasiṣṭha—may you both release us from distress. //3//
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you who protected Śyāvāśva, Vadhryaśva, Purumīḍha, and Atri;
you who protected Vimada and Saptavadhri—may you two deliver us from distress. //4//
O Varuṇa and Mitra, you who protect Bharadvāja, you who protect Gaviṣṭhira, Viśvāmitra, and Kutsa;
you who protect Kakṣīvat and Kaṇva—may those two deliver us from distress. //5//
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you who protect Medhātithi, you who protect Triśoka and Uśanas Kāvya;
you who protect Gotama and likewise Mudgala—may those two deliver us from distress.

Whose chariot follows the path of truth with straight reins, pursuing and corrupting him who walks deviously—I praise Mitra and Varuṇa; seeking protection, I call upon them repeatedly: may they two deliver us from distress. //7//
I move with the Rudras and the Vasus; I am with the Ādityas and the Viśvedevas.
I support both Mitra and Varuṇa; I [support] Indra and Agni, and I [support] both the Aśvins. //1//
I am the sovereign, the gatherer of treasures, the conscious one, the first among those worthy of sacrifice.
The gods have distributed me in many places, making me dwell in many locations and entering into many forms.
I myself declare this, which is pleasing to both gods and men: whomsoever I desire, him I make fierce; him I make a Brahman, him a seer, him a man of great wisdom.
He who perceives, he who breathes, and he who hears what is spoken—he eats the food provided by me.
Those who do not understand dwell near me; hear, O you who have heard! Listen, for this I shall tell you. 4.
I bend the bow for Rudra, so that his arrow may slay the hater of sacred knowledge.
I stir up strife against the people; I have entered heaven and earth. 5.
I bear Soma Āhanas; I [bear] Tvaṣṭṛ, as well as Pūṣan and Bhaga.
I bestow riches upon the one who offers oblations, the sacrificer who presses the juice, providing excellent protection.
I bring forth the father upon its summit; my source is within the waters, in the ocean.
From there I spread out through all the worlds, and I touch that very sky with my highest point.
I alone blow forth like the wind, setting all worlds in motion; beyond heaven and beyond this earth, I have come to be so great by my own majesty.

With you, O Manyu, as our fellow-charioteer, may they break through, exulting and thrilled, accompanied by the Maruts—men with sharp arrows, whetting their weapons, having the form of fire; let them advance! //1//
Like fire, O Manyu, blaze forth; as our victorious general, O Conqueror, be present when invoked.
Having slain the enemies, distribute their wealth; measuring out your power, drive away the adversaries.
Overpower the adversary, O Manyu; breaking, crushing, and utterly destroying him, go forth against the enemies.
Your fierce power has indeed been held back; as the subduer, you alone, O sole-born one, bring them under your control.
(4) You alone are the one praised among the many; sharpen every tribe for battle.
With you as our ally, O Akṛttaruk, we raise a brilliant shout for victory. //4//
Victorious like Indra, unopposed, O Manyu, be our protector here.
We celebrate your dear name, O Conqueror; we know that spring from which you have arisen. 5.
O Vajra, O Arrow, you who are born together with power, you possess superior might as one who is co-existent with it;
O Manyu, invoked by many, be present with us through our ritual will, and join us in the distribution of great wealth.
May Varuṇa and Manyu bestow upon us the combined wealth of both sides gathered together;
let the enemies, placing fear in their hearts, lie prostrate, utterly defeated.
O Manyu, wielder of the thunderbolt and arrow, he who honors you nourishes all power in succession.
With you as our ally—born of might, powerful, and full of force—may we overcome both the Dāsa and the Ārya. //1//
Wrath is Indra; Wrath indeed was the god; Wrath is the Hotṛ, Varuṇa, and Jātavedas.
The human tribes that exist worship Wrath. O Manyu, being in harmony with our fervor, protect us.
Come hither, O Manyu, you who are stronger than the strong; with fervor as your ally, strike down our enemies.
You are the slayer of foes, the slayer of Vṛtra, and the slayer of Dasyus; bring to us all treasures. 3.

For you, O Manyu, are of overpowering strength, self-existent, radiant, and the subduer of adversaries; you are the observer of all people, victorious, and more powerful than the strong—bestow power upon us in battles! 4.
Having no share, O wise one, I have departed from you by the power of you, the mighty.
I, lacking in will, have provoked your anger; come to us in your own form as the giver of strength. //5//
I am here for you; come toward us, O victorious and all-bestowing one! O Manyu, wielder of the thunderbolt, turn toward us; let us two slay the Dasyus, and be mindful of your kinship.
Come forward; be on our right side, and then let us two strike down many Vṛtras.
I offer you the sustaining first portion of the honeyed liquor; let us both drink the first draught in silence.
May our evil be burned away; O Agni, shine wealth upon us. May our evil be burned away. 1.
With a desire for good fields, a good path, and wealth, we sacrifice;
may he burn away our evil.
When he is most celebrated among these, and our wise patrons as well, may he burn away our evil. 3.
When, O Agni, the wise patrons [attain] through thee, may we also be born through thee;
may he burn away our evil. 4.
When the rays of the powerful Agni go forth in all directions,
may he burn away our evil.
For you, O you who face in every direction, encompass everything on every side;
burn away our evil with your light.
O you whose face is turned everywhere, carry us across our enemies as if with a boat;
burn away our evil.
May he carry us across for our well-being, as one crosses the river by boat;
may he burn away our evil.

The *brahman* is its head, the *bṛhat* is its back, and the *vāmadevya* is the belly of this rice-mash. The meters are its wings, and truth is its mouth; the sacrifice was born from heat, spreading wide. //1//
Boneless, purified by the wind, cleansed and pure, they go even to the world of purity.
Jātavedas does not burn their genitals; in the heavenly world, there is an abundance of women for them.
Those who cook the spreading-out rice-offering—never shall misfortune attend them.
Yama sits; he goes to the gods; he rejoices with the Soma-loving Gandharvas. //3//
Yama does not steal away the seed of those who cook the spreading-out porridge;
having become a charioteer, he travels on his chariot-vehicle; having become a bird, he flies beyond the sky.
This sacrifice, most extensive among sacrifices, having cooked the spreading [oblation], has entered heaven.

The *āṇḍīka*, the *kumuda*, the lotus-fiber, the *śālūka*, the *śaphaka*, and the *mulālī*—let all these streams come toward you, swelling with sweetness in the heavenly world; let the lotus-pools stand around you on every side. //5//

Pools of ghee, honey-banked, with wine for water, filled with milk, water, and curds—may all these streams flow toward you, swelling with sweetness in the heavenly world; may lotus-ponds stand around you on every side.
I give four jars, divided into four parts, filled with milk, water, and curds.
May all these streams come toward you, swelling with sweetness in the heavenly world; may lotus-pools stand around you on every side.
I place this rice-offering among the Brahmins—spreading abroad, world-conquering, and leading to heaven.
May it not waste away for me, swelling with the *svadhā* offering; may it become for me a cow of all forms, a granter of desires. 8.

The rice-meat which Prajāpati, the first-born of Cosmic Order, cooked for the Brahman through his ascetic fervor—that which is the supporter of the worlds and their navel—with that rice-meat may I cross over death. //1//
By that rice-meat with which the creators of beings crossed beyond death, which they discovered through austerity and exertion;
by that ancient *brahman* which they cooked for the sake of *brahman*, may I cross beyond death. //2//
He who supported the earth that nourishes all, who filled the mid-air with essence, who propped up the sky upright by his greatness—with that rice-milk, may I overcome death. //3//
Since the month was fashioned from thirty spokes, and the year was fashioned from twelve spokes;
since they have not reached the end while revolving through days and nights—by means of that rice-offering, may we overcome death. 4.
He who was the giver of breath, who possessed breath, for whom the worlds flow with ghee—he by whose food all the quarters are full of light, through that food may I overcome death. //5//
From that cooked food from which the nectar arose, who became the sovereign lord of the Gāyatrī,
in whom all the Vedas of manifold forms are deposited— by means of that rice, may I overcome death.
I drive away the hater, the scorner of the gods; let my rivals be defeated.
I cook the all-conquering *brahmaudana*; may the gods listen to me as I have faith. (AVŚ 4.35.7)
May Agni Vaiśvānara, the bull of true might, burn them up—him who would harm us, him who seeks to deceive us, and him who would act with hostility toward us. 1.
Whoever would harm us who do not wish to harm, or whoever harms one who wishes to harm—him I place within the two tusks of Vaiśvānara Agni. //2//
Those who seek [us] in the house, in the cry of protest, or on the new moon night—
those flesh-eaters and those who wish to harm others, all of them I overcome with force.
I overpower the Piśācas; by force I take away their wealth. I slay all those who wish me ill; may my intention be fulfilled.
Those gods who rejoice with him, who measure their speed against the sun—those who are in the rivers and on the mountains—with those cattle may I find you. 5.
I am the scorcher of the Piśācas, like a tiger among cattle;
seeing me, they find no way to escape, just as dogs do upon seeing a lion.
I am not able to coexist with piśācas, nor with thieves, nor with forest-dwellers;
therefore, the piśācas perish from whatever village I enter.
To whatever village this fierce power of mine enters, from that place the *piśācas* perish; they do not find any evil.
Those who provoke me to anger with their chatter, like gnats against an elephant— I consider them ill-disposed toward people, like those who dwell in a small nest.
Let Destruction seize him, as a horse is caught by its halter;
he who is malicious toward me shall not escape his bonds.
By you, O herb, the Atharvans formerly slew the Rākṣasas;
by you Kaśyapa slew them, and by you Kaṇva and Agastya.
Through you we drive away the Apsarases and the Gandharvas;
O goat-horned one, O goat, destroy all the Rākṣasas with your scent. 2.
Let the Apsarases go to the river, the crosser of waters, the one who makes [him] breathless:
Gulgulū, Pīlā, Naladī, Aukṣagandhi, Pramandanī.
Depart from there, O Apsarases; you have been discovered.
Where there are *aśvattha* and *nyagrodha* trees, great trees with crests; there, O Apsarases, you have awakened from your departure. 4.
Wherever your green and white swings are, and wherever the *aghātā* and *karkarya* birds converse—go there, O Apsarases; you have been awakened.
This one has come from among the plants, the potent herb;
may the goat-horned, the *arāṭakī*, the sharp-horned, drive him away.
Of the dancing Śikhaṇḍin, the Gandharva, lord of the Apsarases—I split his testicles; even his penis I go away with.
Terrible are the weapons of Indra; a hundred are his iron spears.
With these, may he strike down the Gandharvas who consume the oblation and devour the lotuses. 8.
Terrible are Indra’s weapons; a hundred are his golden spears.
With these, may he strike down the Gandharvas who eat the oblation and who devour the *avaka* plants. 9.
O Herb, consume the Avakādās and the Abhiśocas; cause my lights to shine within the waters. Crush all the Piśācas and overcome them!
Like a lone dog, like a lone monkey, like a boy with all his hair intact—having become as pleasing to behold as a Gandharva, he haunts women.
Him we cause to vanish from here by means of a potent sacred formulation (*brahman*). //11//
The Apsarases are indeed your wives; you, O Gandharvas, are their husbands.
Run away, O immortals; do not consort with mortals! 12.
The Apsaras who breaks through, who conquers, who plays well at dice, who makes all stakes her own—that Apsaras I summon here. 1.
I invoke here that Apsaras who gathers and scatters, who plays the game well, and who takes up the stakes won at the gambling table.
She who dances around, taking up the stake from the game—may she, seeking our winnings, win the prize by her magic power.
May she come to us, rich in milk; may they not conquer this wealth of ours. //3//
Her who delights in dice, who bears sorrow and anger—
her, the Apsaras Ānandinī and Pramodinī, I summon here.
Those which move along the rays of the sun, or those which move along the light-beams;
he whose bull, rich in vigor, from afar instantly traverses all the worlds while guarding them—may he come to this oblation, enjoying it, together with the atmosphere, rich in vigor. //5//
O possessor of strength, together with the mid-region, protect the dappled calf here, O vigorous one!
These abundant drops are yours; come hither, O steed! Let this dappled cow be yours here; let your mind be directed toward this place.
O possessor of strength, together with the mid-air, protect the speckled calf here, O strong one!
This is the fodder, this is the stall; here we bind the calf. As we have power over you by name, *svāhā*!
On earth they bowed down to Agni; he prospered.
Just as on earth they bowed down to Agni, so may all bowings bow down to me. 1.
The earth is the cow; Agni is her calf. May she, with Agni as her calf, milk for me food, strength, desire, long life first, progeny, nourishment, and wealth—svāhā!
In the intermediate space, they bowed down to Vāyu; he prospered.
Just as in the intermediate space they bowed down to Vāyu, even so may all bowings bow down to me. 3.
The intermediate space is the cow; its calf is Vāyu.
May she, with Vāyu as her calf, milk for me food, vigor, desire, long life first, progeny, nourishment, and wealth—svāhā!
To the divine Āditya they bowed down; he prospered.
Just as they bowed down to the divine Āditya, so may they bow down in homage to me. 5.
Heaven is the cow; its calf is Āditya.
May she, with Āditya as her calf, milk for me food, strength, desire, long life first, progeny, nourishment, and wealth—svāhā!
In all directions they bowed down to the Moon; he prospered.
Just as they bowed down in all directions to the Moon, so may all obeisances bow down unto me. 7.
The quarters are the milch-cows; the moon is their calf.
May they, with the moon as their calf, milk for me food, vigor, desire, long life, offspring first, nourishment, and wealth—svāhā!
Fire moves, having entered into fire; the son of the seers, the protector against curses.
With salutation and reverence, I offer to you: may I not, through error, miss the portion of the gods. 9.
O Jātavedas, purified by the heart and by the mind, O God who knowest all ways, there are seven mouths of thine; into these I offer [this oblation]; do thou graciously accept the offering. 10.

Those who offer oblations from the east, O Jātavedas, and those who seek to harm us from the eastern quarter—having encountered Agni, let them be driven back and shaken; with this *pratisara* I strike them down. //1//

(4.40.2) Those who offer oblations from the south, O Jātavedas, and those who seek to harm us from the southern quarter—having encountered Yama, let them turn back and tremble; I strike them down with this counter-spell. 2.

O Jātavedas, those who offer oblations from behind, seeking to harm us from the western quarter—having encountered Varuṇa, let them be turned back and shaken; with this *pratisara* I strike them down. //3//

O Jātavedas, those who offer oblations from the north and who seek to harm us from the northern quarter—having encountered Soma, may they turn back and tremble; with this *pratisara* I strike them down. //4//

O Jātavedas, those who offer oblations from below and those who seek to harm us from the northern direction—having reached the earth, let them be struck down and distressed; with this *pratisara* spell, I strike them back. //5//

O Jātavedas, those who offer oblations from the intermediate space, and those who seek to harm us from the cross-quarter direction—having encountered Vāyu, let them be turned back and shaken; with this *pratisara* I strike them down.

O Jātavedas, those who offer oblations from above and those who seek to harm us from the upward direction—having reached the sun, let them be struck down and scattered; with this *pratisara* amulet, I strike them back.

Those who from the quarters and the intermediate directions offer [oblations] to Jātavedas, and who from all directions seek to harm us—may they, by the truth of the sacred word (*brahman*), be driven away; turning back, I strike them down with this *pratisara*.
The mantra has succeeded, he who has occupied the womb, the immortal one with divine life-force, increasing, of noble birth;
undecaying in his life-force, shining like the sun, Trita, the sustainer, has upheld the three. //1//
He who, as the first, established the cosmic orders (*dharmāṇi*), from him you create many forms;
he, the first to dwell, entered the womb—he who understood speech before it was uttered. //2//
(5.1.3) He who, for the sake of your sorrow, has released his body—let him flow with gold, pure along his own paths.
Herein they two establish the immortal names; let the people bring forth garments for us. 3.

When these [priests] have gone forth further toward the ancient seat, ascending the ageless station after station—O Kavi, you who lick the parents of the dry wood, do you two set in motion the fellow and the master of the yoke for the sake of kinship. //4//

Therefore, O you of broad stride, I, a seer, offer this great homage to you with my poetic skill—homage for those two who, moving together toward the earth, increase here as the two great banks of the river. //5//
The seers have fashioned seven boundaries; the oppressor has gone beyond only one of them.
The pillar of Āyu stands in the nest of the highest, at the parting of the paths, upon the foundations.
And I go upon the immortal life-force, performing the vow; O Asura, you are the self within the body, well-disposed toward me.
Or indeed, the powerful one bestows treasure, or that which the giver of the oblation possesses through strengthening power. //7//
(5.1.8a) And the son prays for dominion to his father; O men, you have called upon the eldest as a boundary for your well-being.
(5.1.8c) Now behold those forms of yours, O Varuṇa; from your own holy ordinance, you manifest wondrous splendors. //8//
(5.1.9a) With half you fill [the vessel] with half of milk; with the other half, O Amura, you increase your strength.
(5.1.9c) We have magnified the helpful friend, Varuṇa, the vigorous son of Aditi.
(5.1.9e) We have proclaimed for him these forms praised by the seers, O Heaven and Earth, whose word is truth. //9//
That indeed was the eldest among all beings, from whom the fierce sacrifice of terrible prowess [arose].
As soon as he was born, he overcomes his enemies, when all the helpers rejoice after him. //1//
Increasing in power and possessing abundant strength, you, as an adversary, instill fear in the Dāsa.
Both the non-moving and the moving have been won; they cry out to you when the offerings are presented in the exhilarations of the soma.
(5.2.3a) They augment your abundant power of will when these helpers become twice or thrice [in number].
(5.2.3c) Mix that which is sweeter than sweet with sweetness; join that honey with honey in combat! //3//

If indeed the inspired singers rejoice after you as you win the spoils in battle after battle, O mighty one, exert your more powerful and firm strength; let not the evil-minded Kaśoka-s harm you. //4//
Through you we prevail in battles, beholding many things worthy of war.
I urge on your weapons with my words; I sharpen your vital powers with my prayer.
(5.2.6a) You have taken that [power] in this lower and that higher dwelling, in which you have protected us with your aid.
(5.2.6c) Establish the swift Mother; set many deeds in motion from here!
Praise him at his height, the one with many paths, the skillful, the most powerful, the Aptya among the Aptyas.
He of abundant vigor shall display himself through his might; he shall overcome the very measure of the earth.
(5.2.8a) May this priest Bṛhaddiva, the foremost winner of light, create strength for Indra.
(5.2.8c) As a self-ruling king, he dwells in the great stall of cattle; powerful and fervent, he overcomes every flood. 8.
Thus has the great Atharvan Bṛhaddiva spoken to Indra as his own body;
the two sisters, dwelling in the mother and free from blemish, impel him and strengthen him with power. 9.
O Agni, may splendor be mine in the invocations; kindling you, may we nourish our own bodies.
May the four quarters bow down to me; with you as our overseer, may we conquer the hostile armies. 1.
O Agni, repelling the wrath of our enemies, do you, as our protector, guard us on every side.
Let those who seek to harm us go away downward into the depths; let the minds of these awakened ones perish.
(5.3.3a) May all the gods be present at my invocation—the Maruts accompanied by Indra, Viṣṇu, and Agni.
(5.3.3c) May the wide world of the intermediate space be mine; may the wind blow for me for this desire. 3.
(5.3.4a) May they sacrifice for me; may my intentions be fulfilled; may the desire of my mind become true.
(5.3.4c) May I not fall into any sin whatsoever; may all the gods protect me here. //4//
(5) May the gods bestow wealth upon me through sacrifice; may the prayer be with me, may the invocation of the gods be with me.
O divine Hotṛ-priests, may you win this for us; may we be unharmed in body and possessed of brave sons. //5//
O divine six wide ones, make wide space for us; O all-gods, rejoice here.
Let not the overpowering one find us, nor the curse; let not the crooked, hateful things find us.
O three goddesses, grant us great protection for our offspring, for our bodies, and for that which is nourishment.
May we not be abandoned by our offspring nor by our bodies; may we not fall into the power of the enemy, O King Soma. 7.
May the far-reaching, mighty one, invoked by many, grant us protection in this call, abounding in food.
O Indra, Lord of tawny steeds, be gracious to our progeny; do not harm us, nor abandon us. //8//
May Dhātṛ, Vidhātṛ, the Lord of the world, and the god Savitṛ, the subduer of adversaries;
may the Ādityas, the Rudras, and both Aśvins—the gods—protect the sacrificer from destruction. //9//
May those who are our rivals be driven away; with Indra and Agni we repel them.
The Ādityas and Rudras, reaching upward, have made for us a fierce guardian, a sovereign overlord.

We invoke Indra from yonder to come hither—he who wins cattle, wins wealth, and wins horses; may he hear this sacrifice of ours at our call; O Lord of the bay steeds, you have become our gracious friend. 11.
O you who were born among the mountains, the most powerful of plants—
O Kuṣṭha, destroyer of *takman*, destroy the *takman* from here!
Born on the mountain where the fair-winged birds breed, from the Himalayas, they come hither, having heard of the riches; for they know the destroyer of *takman*.
The *aśvattha* tree, the abode of the gods, is in the third heaven from here; there the gods obtained the *kuṣṭha*, the manifestation of immortality. //3//
A golden ship with golden moorings moved through the sky;
there the gods obtained Kuṣṭha, the flower of immortality. //4//
The paths were golden; the oars were golden;
the ships were golden, by which they carried away Kuṣṭha.
O Kuṣṭha, bring this man here to me; drive him out. Make him free from disease for me.
Born from the gods, you are the well-disposed friend of Soma;
as such, be gracious to this breath, to this out-breath, and to my sight. //7//
Born in the north from the Himavat, you are led eastward to the people;
there they have distributed the most excellent names of the Kuṣṭha plant.
The highest is the name of the leprosy; the highest is the name of your father. Destroy every consumption and make the fever sapless.
Having struck away the disease of the head, the affliction of the eyes, and the blemish of the body— let Kuṣṭha drive all that away, along with the divine virility.
Night is your mother, the sky is your father, and Aryaman is your grandfather.
By name you are Silācī; you are indeed the sister of the gods. 1.
He who drinks you lives; you protect that man.
For you are the sustainer of all people and their downward guide.
Tree after tree you climb, like a maiden longing for a man; conquering and standing firm, you are indeed named "The Supporter. 3.
Whatever has been done with a staff, whatever with an arrow, or whatever has been done by Araru with his heat—of that you are the remedy; therefore, heal this man. //4//
From the auspicious *plakṣa*, from the *aśvattha*, the *khadira*, and the *dhava* you arise;
from the auspicious *nyagrodha* and the *parṇa*, come to us, O Arundhatī! 5.5.5a-cd.
O golden-hued one, fortunate one, sun-colored one, most beautiful one! You go to the prepared place; indeed, you are named "Preparation. //6//
O golden-colored, fortunate one, with swelling vigor and hairy breast;
you are the sister of the waters, O lac-dyed one; the wind has become your breath.
Silācī, the maiden, is your mother; Ajavābhu is your father. You are the grown son of Śyāva, that horse of Yama. //8//
That which fell from the horse's mouth flowed down upon the trees; becoming a winged stream, come to us, O Arundhatī! 9.
The Brahman, first born in the east, Vena has revealed from the radiant horizon; he has disclosed its highest stations in the depths, and the womb of both the existent and the non-existent. 1.
Those first deeds of yours which were unattainable—may they not deceive our heroes here; I place that very thing before you.
