In a thousand streams they have resounded together for you in the vault of heaven, honey-tongued and unfailing.
His watchful spies do not close their eyes; restless, at every step they bear snares for the one who would cross.
Flow forth indeed completely for the winning of booty, overcoming all obstacles;
from there you go toward the enemies. You are named Sanisrasa, the thirteenth month, the house of Indra. //4//
Now you have succeeded with this, O so-and-so; svāhā!
O Soma and Rudra, armed with sharp weapons and sharp missiles, most gracious ones, be very merciful to us here! 5.
By this you have succeeded for that person, svāhā!
O Soma and Rudra, armed with sharp weapons and sharp missiles, most gracious ones, be very merciful to us here. 6.
Depart! You have succeeded against that one, svāhā!
O Soma and Rudra, you who possess sharp weapons and sharp missiles, who are most gracious—be very merciful to us here! 7.
Release us from misfortune and from blame; enjoy our sacrifice and bestow immortality upon us. //8//
O agent of the eye, O agent of the mind, O agent of the sacred word, and O agent of ascetic heat!
You are a weapon; let those who seek to harm us be rendered weaponless by you. 9.
Whoever, being malevolent, should attack us with his eye, with his mind, with thought, or with intention—O Agni, make them subject to your wrath; Svāhā!
You are the house of Indra. To you I go for refuge; into you I enter—with all my cattle, all my men, all my self, and all my body, together with whatever belongs to me. 11.
(5.6.12a) You are the protection of Indra.
(5.6.12c) To you I resort; into you I enter—with my whole movement, with my whole person, with my whole self, with my whole body—along with whatever belongs to me. 12.
(5.6.13a) You are the armor of Indra.
(5.6.13c) To you I go for refuge; into you I enter—with my whole movement, my whole person, my whole self, and my whole body—along with whatever belongs to me. 13.
You are the protection of Indra.
I resort to you; I enter into you—with my whole movement, my whole person, my whole self, and my whole body—along with whatever belongs to me. 14.
Bring to us; do not withhold, O Arāti! Do not harm our sacrificial gift as it is being led away.
Homage to the one who seeks to obstruct, to failure; homage be to Arāti. //1//
O Arāti, the man whom you place before you, who is full of lamentation—to him we pay homage; do not disturb my gain.
May our god-fashioned prosperity prosper for us by day and by night. We turn away from ill-will; let there be homage to ill-will. 3.
Going forth, we invoke Sarasvatī, Anumati, and Bhaga;
I have uttered the beloved and honey-sweet speech at the invocations of the gods. //4//
(5) Whatever I request with speech joined to the mind by Sarasvatī— may Śraddhā find that today, bestowed by the tawny Soma.
Do not withhold our livelihood, nor our speech; O Indra and Agni, bring us both riches.
Today, all of you, desiring to give, take pleasure in warding off the stingy one.
Depart, O unsuccessful one; we lead away your weapon.
I know you, O Arāti, as you shrink away and strike.
And appearing naked and trembling, you haunt people in their sleep; O Arāti, you frustrate the thought and the intention of the man.
She who is great, of vast measure, and has pervaded all the quarters—to that Nirṛti with golden hair, I have paid homage. 9.
Golden-hued, fortunate, golden-matted, great;
to her, the one with a golden garment, to that Arāti, I have paid homage.
Carry the clarified butter to the gods with fuel-sticks of *vaikaṅkata* wood;
O Agni, delight them here, and let all come to my invocation. //1//
O Indra, come to my invocation; I shall perform this—listen to that! May these *atisara* offerings dedicated to Indra bend my intention toward success.
Through them, O Jātavedas, master of our bodies, may we be able to achieve heroic power.
Whatever that godless one over there seeks to accomplish against us from yonder, O gods—let not Agni carry his oblation; O gods, do not come to his call, but come to my call alone! 3.
Run past, O dysenteries; you are slain by the word of Indra!
Like a wolf seizing a sheep, tear them apart; let none of you escape alive, but bind up their very breath! 4.
(5a) Him whom these men have placed in front for their own protection— (5c) O Indra, him I cast beneath your feet; I hurl him down unto death. //5//

If they have perished from the cities of the gods and have made the *brahman* their armor, fashioning it as a protection for their bodies and a defense all around— whatever they have uttered, make all that sapless.
Those transgressions which he has committed and those which he may yet commit—
O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, turn them back again so that he may destroy that enemy host.
Just as Indra, having obtained the proclamation, cast them beneath his feet, so do I make those [enemies] low for all future years. //8//
Right here, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, pierce them in their vital parts with your fierce weapon! Right here, O Indra, trample them down; may I abide in your favor.
We take hold of you, O Indra; may we remain in your good graces. //9//
To the day, svāhā! //1//
To the Earth, Svāhā! //2//
To the intermediate space, svāhā! //3//
To the intermediate space, svāhā!
To the day, svāhā! //5//
To the Earth, Svāhā!
The sun is my eye, the wind my breath, the mid-region my self, and the earth my body.
Unconquered by name am I; here I am, this very one, who for the protection of heaven and earth, establishes himself within them. 7.
Up! Life-force, up! Strength, up! Deed, up! Sorcery, up! Intelligence, up! Power!
O you two who bestow life, O lords of life, you who possess the *svadhā* offering, be my guardians;
guard me! Be seated within my self; do not harm me! //8//
(5.10.1a) You are my stone armor, O you who would attack me from the eastern quarter with evil intent; (5.10.1c) may he meet with this [misfortune]. //1//
(5.10.2a) You are my stone armor, against whichever malevolent one would attack me from the southern quarter. (5.10.2c) May he meet with this [misfortune]. //2//
(5.10.3a) You are my stone armor, against whoever, being malevolent, would attack me from the western quarter. (5.10.3c) May he meet with this [consequence]. //3//
(5.10.4a) You are my stone armor; should any malevolent person from the northern quarter seek to harm me, (5.10.4c) may he meet with this [consequence]. //4//
(5a) You are my stone armor, against whoever, being malevolent, would attack me from the fixed quarter. (5c) May he meet with this [consequence]. //5//
(5.10.6a) You are my stone armor against the malevolent one who would attack from the upward direction; (5.10.6c) may he meet with this [consequence].
(5.10.7a) You are my stone armor, [against him] who, seeking to harm me, would attack me from the quarters or from the intermediate directions. (5.10.7c) May he meet with this [consequence]. //7//
With the great Mātariśvan, I summon mind, out-breath, and in-breath;
from the sun, sight; from the intermediate space, hearing; from the earth, the body.
With Sarasvatī, whose vehicle is the mind, we summon speech. 8.
How did you speak here to the great Asura? How, O you of brilliant valor, to your father Hari?
Having given away Pṛśni as a sacrificial fee, O Varuṇa, you, O bounteous one, pondered in your mind how to recover her again. //1//
I do not come again with desire, O Punarmagha; I have looked upon this spotted cow as my support.
By what poetic wisdom, O Atharvan, and by what birth are you Jātavedas? //2//
Truly, by my poetic wisdom I am profound; truly, by my birth I am Jātavedas.
Neither a slave nor a noble woman can, through their greatness, violate the vow that I shall uphold. 3.
There is no other more wise than you, nor more skilled in intellect, O Varuṇa, self-dependent one.
You know all these worlds; indeed, even that person who possesses magical power fears you. 4.
For you indeed, O Varuṇa, self-dependent one, well-guiding lord, know all generations.
What else is there beyond this space? And what is below it, O immortal one? 5.
One [step] of yours is beyond the dust; another is further than that by one [step]; even that which is difficult to reach is near by one more.
Knowing this, O Varuṇa, I declare it to you: let the Paṇis be those whose speech is downward-turned; let the Dāsas crawl low to the earth.
For you indeed, O Varuṇa, do proclaim many reproaches against those who turn back from their gifts.
Let there not be so many Paṇis for you; let not people call you one who bestows no wealth.
(5.11.8a) Let not people call me one who bestows no gifts; O singer, I give Pṛśni back to you.
(5.11.8c) Come to my entire hymn with your powers, among all the human quarters. //8//
(9) May your raised hymns of praise go forth into all the human quarters. Give now to me that which you have not given to me; you are my companion, my seven-step friend.
Equal is our kinship, O Varuṇa; equal is our birth. I know that which is this common bond between us.
I give back to you what I took from you; I am your companion, bound to you by the seven steps. 10.
The god, bestowing vital strength upon the god who praises him, the inspired sage, wise for the sage who lauds him;
for you, O Varuṇa, self-dependent one, begot Atharvan, the father and kinsman of the gods.
Therefore, grant him most highly praised wealth; you are our friend and our supreme kin. 11.

Kindled today in the dwelling of man, O Jātavedas, you, a god, sacrifice to the gods. Bring them hither, O you of Mitra-like luster; you are the wise messenger, the seer, and the discerning one. //1//
O Tanūnapāt, fair-tongued one, anointing the paths that lead along the way of Truth with honey, make them palatable;
fulfilling our prayers through our insights and our sacrifice, bring our ritual to the gods. //2//
Being invoked, worthy of praise, and to be celebrated, come, O Agni, in harmony with the Vasus!
You are the youthful Hotṛ-priest of the gods; as such, being impelled, sacrifice for them as the most skilled sacrificer. //3//
The sacrificial grass is strewn toward the east upon the earth by its direction, at the beginning of the days, for her covering.
It spreads itself out further and wider, a pleasant seat for the gods and for Aditi.
Let the spacious ones open wide, like wives adorning themselves for their husbands;
O divine, lofty, all-impelling doors, be easy of access for the gods. //5//
Pressing [the soma], the two worshipful ones, Dawn and Night, sit down close together in their place;
the two celestial maidens, lofty and richly adorned, bestowing splendor and radiant beauty.

The two divine Hotṛ-priests, the first, eloquent ones, fashioning the sacrifice for man to worship; the two poets who impel [the rite] in the assemblies, pointing toward the eastern light with their direction. //7//

May Bhāratī come quickly to our sacrifice; may Iḷā, manifesting here like a human, and the three goddesses—Sarasvatī and the others, skilled in their work—sit upon this pleasant sacrificial grass. //8//

(5.12.9a) He who, as the progenitor, adorned these two, heaven and earth, and all beings with their forms—(5.12.9c) him, O Hotṛ, being impelled and most skilled in sacrifice, do thou, the wise one, worship here today as the god Tvaṣṭṛ. //9//
Release [the victim] by yourself, anointing the offerings for the gods in due season at their place;
let Vanaspati, the immolator, and the god Agni sweeten the oblation with honey and ghee. //10//
As soon as he was born, Agni measured out the sacrifice; he became the leader of the gods.
By the command of this Hotṛ, at the speech of *ṛta*, may the gods eat the oblation consecrated with *svāhā*. 11.
For Varuṇa, the seer of heaven, has indeed granted me [the power] to destroy it; with my fierce words, I dissolve your poison.
Whether it be dug out, undug, or stuck fast, I have seized it; like a reed from the dry land, your poison shall wither away. //1//
Whatever waterless poison is yours, that of yours I have seized from these [plants]. I seize your middle, your highest juice, and even your lowest; through fear, let it perish from you.
My roar is like a bull, like thunder from the clouds; with my fierce word I have driven you away. I have seized that essence of his with my men; may the sun rise up as light from the darkness. //3//
With my eye I strike out your eye; with poison I strike out your poison.
O snake, die, do not live! Let the poison come back and strike you.
O Kirātas, Pṛśnis, Upatṛṇyas, Babhrus, Āsitās, and Alīkas, listen to me!
Do not stand in the way of my friend; making yourselves heard, take delight in your own dwelling.
Of Asita, Taimāta, Babhru, and Apodaka,
and of Sātrāsāha and Manyu— I unloose them as one unstrings the bowstring, like chariots.
Āligī and Viligī, father and mother—we know you from every side as kinsmen; being sapless, what will you do?
The daughter of Urugūlā was born as a slave-girl from Asiknī;
may the poison of all those who have contracted *prataṅka* be rendered sapless. //8//
The porcupine, dwelling in the mountain, said this:
"Of all these things that are dug out, the poison is the most tasteless. (AVŚ 5.13.9)
*Tābuvaṃ na, tābuvaṃ na; indeed, you are not *tābuva*.
By means of *tābuva*, [I neutralize] the sapless poison.* 10.
Whether it be moving or not moving, you are indeed not moving;
by means of that which is unmoving, [overcome] the sapless poison. 11.
The eagle found you; the boar dug you up with its snout.
O herb, you who desire to harm, strike down the one who desires to harm; slay the practitioner of sorcery.
Strike down the sorcerers; strike down the practitioner of witchcraft.
And furthermore, O Plant, strike down whoever seeks to harm us.
Like the skinning of a deer, having cut away the outer skin, O gods, fasten the spell back onto the spell-maker like a necklace.
Again, O performer of magic, having seized the magic spell by the hand, lead it away; deliver it visibly to the one who fashioned it, so that he may slay the maker of the magic spell. //4//
Let sorceries be [turned back] upon the sorcerer, and curses upon the one who utters a curse. Let the sorcery turn back again upon the sorcerer, like a comfortable chariot.
Whether it was a woman or a man who performed this *kṛtyā* for his own evil,
we lead that back to him like a horse by means of its halter.
Whether you were made by the gods or whether you were made by men,
we lead you back again, joined with Indra as our companion.
O Agni, conqueror of armies, overcome the hostile forces! We take back the *kṛtyā* from the maker of the *kṛtyā* by means of this counter-remedy. //8//
O you who pierce with the arrow, pierce him; strike down him who did this. We shall not sharpen our weapons for your slaughter when he has done no wrong.
Go like a son to his father; go like a well-placed arrow to its ten [notches].
Go like one entering a trap; go back to the doer of the spell as the spell itself.
Like a doe leaping toward a wild elephant, let the *kṛtyā* strike the one who made it. 11.
Let the straight-flying arrow fly toward heaven and earth;
let that *kṛtyā* seize the performer of the *kṛtyā* again, like a hunter seizing a deer. 12.
Like fire, let it go against the current; like water, let it flow with the current.
Like a comfortable chariot, let the *kṛtyā* turn back again upon the one who fashioned it. 13.
One and ten are my expellers, O herb;
born of *ṛta*, observer of *ṛta*, make honey for me, O honeyed one.
Two and twenty are my healers, O herb;
O you who are born of *ṛta*, O observer of *ṛta*, make honey for me, O sweet one.
O herb, you who are born of *ṛta* and abide in *ṛta*, you are my thirty-three expellers; O sweet one, make honey for me. 3.
O herb, you who are born of *ṛta* and rich in *ṛta*, may my forty-four expellers make me sweet with honey.
O herb, you who are born of Cosmic Order and rich in Cosmic Order, you have fifty-five expellers for me; O sweet one, make honey for me.
Six and sixty are my healers, O herb;
O you who are born of Order, O observer of Order, make honey for me, O honeyed one.
Seven and seventy are my healers, O herb;
born of Truth, O you who abide in Truth, make honey for me, O honeyed one.
Eight and eighty are my expellers, O herb;
born of *ṛta*, you who abide in *ṛta*, make honey for me, O honeyed one. (8)
Nine and ninety are my expellers, O herb;
born of *ṛta*, O observer of *ṛta*, make honey for me, O honeyed one.
Ten and a hundred are my healers, O herb;
born of the *ṛta*, rich in *ṛta*, do thou make honey for me, O honeyed one.
A hundred and a thousand are my speakers-against, O herb;
O you born of Order, O observer of Order, make honey for me, O honeyed one. //11//
If you are a single bull, release [the seed]; you are full of vigor. //1//
If you are a double-bull, release it; you are the essence. //2//
If you are threefold, release [the breath]; you are the essence. //3//
If you are four-bull, release it; you are the essence.
If you are five-bull, release it; you are the essence. //5//
If you are a six-bull, release [the seed]; you are a source of vigor.
If you are seven-horned, release [the seed]; you are the essence.
If you are eight-bull, release [the seed]; you are the essence. //8//
If you are a new bull, let loose; you are one who has lost his vigor.
If you are tenfold-strong, release it; you are full of vigor.
If you are the eleventh, you are one who has removed the water. //11//
They spoke first regarding the sin against Brahman: the boundless ocean, Mātariśvan, the firm-holding heat, the fierce one, the source of bliss, and the divine waters, the first-born of Cosmic Order.
King Soma, the first, gave back the wife of the Brahman without resentment.
Varuṇa and Mitra were the attendants; Agni, the Hotṛ, taking her by the hand, led her away. 2.
"The pledge must be taken by her own hand; 'She is born of Brahman,' so he said.
She must not be sent to a messenger; thus is the kingdom of the Kṣatriya protected. (AVŚ 5.17.3)

Her whom they call "The Star," the one with disheveled hair, who descends upon the village as a portent of misfortune—she, the wife of Brahmā, consumes the kingdom where the hare-marked moon has fallen like a flaming torch. 4.
The student of sacred knowledge (*brahmacārī*) moves about, performing his various duties; he becomes a single limb of the gods.
Through him, Bṛhaspati recovered his wife who had been led away by Soma, just as the gods recovered the *juhū* ladle. //5//
The gods indeed spoke concerning this woman, as did the seven seers of old who sat in ascetic fervor:
"The terrifying wife of a Brahmin, when driven away, brings instability even in the highest heaven."
Those fetuses that perish, and that which destroys the world,
those heroes who are slaughtered by one another— these the wife of the Brahmin slays.
Even though ten husbands, who were not Brahmins, preceded this woman, if a Brahmin has taken her hand, he alone is her husband in every way. (AVŚ 5.17.8)
Only a Brāhmaṇa is a husband, not a Rājanya nor a Vaiśya;
proclaiming this, Sūrya goes forth toward the five classes of men.
The gods gave her back; men gave her back.
Taking hold of truth, the kings gave back the wife of the Brahmin.
Having restored the wife of the Brahmin and been freed from sin by the gods, they partake of the nourishment of the earth and worship the wide-striding one. 11.
In that kingdom where the wife of a Brahmin is imprisoned through lack of sense, her husband shall have no virtuous wife who, riding a hundred steeds, lies upon his bed.
In that kingdom where the wife of a Brahmin is confined through thoughtlessness, no one with deformed ears or a broad head is born in that house.
In that kingdom where the wife of a Brahmin is detained through thoughtlessness, her charioteer, with a golden necklace around his neck, does not go before the sacrificial slaughtering grounds.
In that kingdom where the wife of a Brahmin is detained through thoughtlessness, even a white horse with black ears, when yoked to the pole, does not receive honor.
In his field no lotus pond grows, nor does the *aṇḍīka* lily or the lotus-root; in whatever kingdom the wife of a Brahmin is seized through thoughtlessness. (AVŚ 5.17.16)
They do not milk the speckled cow for him who waits upon her milking;
in whatever kingdom the wife of a Brahmin is confined through thoughtlessness.
Neither his noble cow nor his ox can bear the yoke, wherever a man of sacred knowledge dwells for a night with a wicked woman. 18.
The gods did not give this cow to you, O lord of men, for you to eat.
O Kṣatriya, do not covet the cow of a Brahmin, which is not to be eaten. //1//
The kṣatriya who has been cheated at dice, the wicked man defeated by his own self—he may eat the Brāhmaṇa’s cow today; let me live today, not tomorrow.
Like a female viper covered with its skin whose venom is manifest, O Kṣatriya, this cow of the Brāhmaṇa is harsh and unfit for consumption. //3//
It surely leads away the ruling power; it destroys splendor; like fire that has been kindled, it consumes everything.
He who considers a Brahmin to be merely food drinks the very poison of the blind one. 4.

He who strikes him, thinking him to be weak—the scorner of the gods, desiring wealth, not from his heart—Indra kindles fire within that man's very heart; he hates both [worlds] as he moves through the two skies.
A Brahmin must not be harmed, like a fire that is dear to one's body;
for Soma is his heir, and Indra is the protector against his curses.
He swallows the hundred-jawed [pestle], yet he cannot extract it; for that wicked man who eats the food of the Brahmins thinks, "I am eating something sweet. (AVŚ 5.18.7)

The tongue becomes the bowstring, the palate the bow-tip, and the teeth are sharpened by ascetic heat; with these, the Brahman pierces those who revile the gods, using bows whose strength is the heart and which are impelled by the gods. //8//
The Brahmins, possessing sharp arrows and missiles, do not miss the mark when they discharge their shaft;
pursuing him with ascetic fervor and wrath, they shatter him from afar.
Those thousand who were kings and even ten hundred besides—
those Vaitahavyas perished after they had eaten the cow of a brahmin.
The cow herself, while being slaughtered, overthrew those descendants of Vitahavya who had looked on at the last-born calf as it was being bound by its mane.
One hundred and one were those people whose land he shook;
having harmed the Brahmin’s offspring, they perished in a manner that could not be averted. 12.
The reviler of the gods wanders among mortals; having swallowed poison, he becomes a mere heap of bones.
He who harms a Brāhmaṇa, a kinsman of the gods, does not even go to the world of the fathers. 13.
Agni is indeed our guardian of the path; Soma is called the heir.
Indra is the slayer of the accuser; thus do the wise know it. 14.
Like a poisoned arrow, O lord of men; like a viper, O lord of cattle—such is the terrible arrow of the Brahmin; with it he pierces the one who drinks [the soma]. //15//
They grew beyond measure; they seemed to touch the very heavens.
Having harmed Bhṛgu, the Sṛñjayas, the descendants of Vitahavya, were utterly defeated. //1//
Those people who have harmed the Brāhmaṇa Bṛhatsāman, the descendant of Aṅgiras—
may the ram that eats both kinds of food destroy their sheep and their offspring.
Those who spat upon a brahmin, or those who sought a bride-price from him— those, in the middle of the stream, sit chewing their own hair.
As long as a Brahmin’s cow is being cooked and she cries out in distress, she destroys the vital energy of the kingdom; no heroic son is born there who is a bull among men.
Cruel is her devouring; she devours harsh flesh. That milk which is drunk from her—truly, that is an offense against the ancestors. //5//
The fierce king who, thinking himself powerful, seeks to devour a Brahmin—
his kingdom is utterly cast down where the Brahmin is oppressed.
Having become eight-footed, four-eyed, four-eared, four-jawed, two-faced, and double-tongued, she shakes down the kingdom of the oppressor of the Brahmin.
That kingdom indeed flows away like water from a broken boat;
for wherever they harm a Brahmin, misfortune destroys that kingdom.
The trees ward him off, saying, "Do not come into our shade," he who,
O Nārada, covets the righteous wealth of a Brāhmaṇa.
"This is a poison created by the gods," King Varuṇa has declared;
"no one at all can remain vigilant in the kingdom after having eaten the cow of a Brāhmaṇa. (AVŚ 5.19.10)
Nine indeed were those ninety [fingers] which the earth shook; having harmed the offspring of the Brāhmaṇī, they perished utterly, beyond recovery. //11//
That which they fasten to the dead man— the wall-creeper that wipes away the footprints—
that indeed, O oppressor of Brahmins, the gods declared to be your under-layer.
The tears that flowed from you as you wept in pity when you were conquered—
O oppressor of Brahmins, the gods have indeed ordained those as your portion of the waters.
That with which they wash the dead, that with which one moistens the beard—
that portion of the waters, O oppressor of Brahmins, the gods have indeed withheld from you.
The rain of Mitra and Varuṇa does not fall upon the one who oppresses the Brahmin;
neither the assembly nor a friend submits to his will. 15.
The drum, a loud-sounding vessel made of wood, brought together with the products of the cow;
making your voice heard, subduing our rivals, roar against them like a lion about to conquer.
Like a lion, he has roared while bound to the wooden post, bellowing like a bull toward a cow in heat.
You are a bull; your rivals are emasculated. Your vigor belongs to Indra; it overcomes those who attack us.
Like a bull among the herd, manifesting with force, seeking cattle, you roar as a conqueror of wealth.
Pierce the hearts of our enemies with your flame; let them abandon their villages and flee as outcasts. 3.
Conquering the armies, extending our life-span, seizing and holding fast, look out in many directions!
O Drum, utter the divine speech; as a creator, bring forth the wealth of the enemies! 4.
Hearing the resonant voice of the drum being struck, the woman, distressed and awakened by the sound,
shall run with her son grasped by the hand, like a female enemy in battle, terrified of slaughter.
O drum, speak first; speak your voice, shining upon the back of the earth.
Crushing the army of the enemy, O drum, speak with splendor and with truthful joy.
Let there be a sound between these two atmospheres; let your various noises go forth quickly.
Roar toward us, thunder like one who has drunk his fill; create a hymn for the sounding of Mitra, O you who possess the light of heaven!
Fashioned by inspired thoughts, let him utter his voice; rouse the weapons of the heroes!
O Indra-lover, summon the warriors; with your allies, strike down the enemies. //8//
Roaring aloud, shouting forth, with a bold army, making proclamations and resounding through many villages;
winning glories, knowing the sacred ways, distribute fame among the many in the dual kingdom.
O banner of excellence, winner of wealth, more powerful, victor in battle, you are sharpened by the sacred word (*brahman*).
Like a pressing-stone upon the filter for the stalks [of soma], dance over the drum, O drum, seeking cattle and the Veda.

O subduer of enemies, subduer of those who sit in ambush, overcomer of hostile forces, seeker of cattle, victorious, and a breaker-through—like one skilled in speech delivering a mantra, bring forth your voice; utter here a prayer for victory in battle and for nourishment.
Unshakable yet causing others to shake, equal in spirit, most swift to go, conqueror of the hostile, invincible leader;
protected by Indra, perceiving the assemblies, illuminating the heart—go quickly against our enemies! 12.
O drum, I utter heartbreak and despondency among our enemies;
I instill hatred, dejection, and fear in our enemies. O drum, strike them down! 1.
Trembling in mind, eye, and heart,
let the enemies run away in fear when the oblation is poured with terror.
Prepared from the wood of trees, gathered with the milk of cows from every lineage,
sprinkled with clarified butter, strike terror into our enemies.
Just as wild forest deer are terrified of a man, even so, O drum, roar out against the enemies; strike them with fear and bewilder their minds. 4.
Just as goats and sheep run from a wolf, greatly terrified, even so, O drum, cry out against the enemies; strike them with fear and confound their minds. //5//
Just as birds are terrified at every dawn by the hawk, and just as [they are] by the roar of the lion, even so, O drum, cry out against our enemies; terrify them and confound their minds.
With the drum and with the skin of a deer, all the enemies have been driven away;
even all the gods trembled before those who seek the battle.
With those foot-sounds with which Indra sports together with his shadow,
let those enemies of ours tremble who advance in military arrays.
Let the twang of bowstrings and the sounds of drums resound toward all directions,
as the armies of our enemies, being defeated, flee in their ranks.
O Āditya, take up our sight; O rays of light, run along after it!
Let them cling to our feet when the strength of our arms has departed.
O you fierce Maruts, sons of Pṛśni, with Indra as your ally, crush the enemies!
King Soma, King Varuṇa, Mahādeva, and even Death and Indra [are your allies]. 11.11
May these divine armies, whose banners are the sun, being of one mind, conquer our enemies; *svāhā*!
May Agni drive away the fever from here; may Soma, the pressing-stone, and Varuṇa of purified might [drive it away].
May the altar, the sacrificial grass, and the brightly blazing fuel-brands drive away hostilities to that other place. 1.
This one who makes all things yellow, burning and scorching like fire—therefore, O Fever, become sapless;
then turn away or go downward.
He who is harsh, full of harshness, ruddy like a crumbling ruin—drive away that fever, O you of all-pervading power, downward and far away! 3.
Having paid homage, I send Takman downward;
may the slayer of Śakambhara’s fist return to the great bulls. //4//
The Mūjavants are his dwelling place; the Mahāvṛṣas are his dwelling place.
As far as you have been born, O Takman, so great are you; you dwell among the Balhikas. //5//
O Takman, you serpent, depart! O you who cause lameness, go far away! Seek out the female servant who is a habitual sinner; strike her down with your thunderbolt.
O Takman, go to the Mūjavants or to the Balhikas, or even further away!
Seek out the Śūdra woman Prapharvyā; shake her off, O Takman, as if shaking dust!
Go forth, O Fever, and eat the great bulls and the Mūjavat mountains as your kin;
we declare these other fields or these [places] to you.
Being self-controlled, you do not delight in another’s field; have mercy on us.
Now the fever has become mild; it will go away to the Balhikas.
Whether you are cold or burning, and whether you cause us to tremble with coughing—O Takman, your weapons are terrible; with them, spare us!
Do not make these your friends—the *balāsa*, the cough, and the feverish onset.
Do not come back toward us again; O *takman*, that is what I say to you.
O Takman, together with your brother Balāsa and your sister Kāsikā, go away with your rival, the evil spirit, to that other people who are strangers.
The tertian fever, the quartan, the constant daily fever, and that which comes from autumn; destroy the *takman*—the cold, the *rūra*, the summer, and the rainy-season fever.
From the Gandhāris, from the Mūjavats, from the Aṅgas, and from the Magadhas—
like one departing for a treasure, we entrust Takman to the people.
Woven for me are Heaven and Earth; woven is the goddess Sarasvatī; woven for me are both Indra and Agni—let them crush the worm! //1//
O Indra, Lord of Wealth, slay the worms of this boy;
all enemies are slain by my formidable word.
The worm that crawls around the eyes, that crawls around the nostrils,
that goes into the midst of the teeth— that worm we crush.
Two of like form, two of different forms, two black ones, two red ones, the tawny one, the tawny-eared one, the vulture, and the *koka*—these have been slain. //4//
The worms that have white girdles, those that are black with white forelegs, and whatever others there are of every form—those worms we crush to pieces. //5//
The sun rises in the east, seen by all, the slayer of the unseen;
striking down both the seen and the unseen, it crushes all worms.
The *yevāṣas*, the *kṣkaṣas*, the wriggling ones, and those with hairy tails—let the worm that is seen be slain, and let the one that is unseen be slain as well. //7//
Slain is the Yevāṣa among the worms, slain is the Nadanimot;
I have crushed them all like grain upon a millstone. //8//
The three-headed, three-peaked, mottled, and white worm—
I crush its ribs and cut off its head.
Like Atri, I kill your worms; like Kaṇva and Jamadagni. With the sacred spell of Agastya, I crush the worms to pieces.
Slain is the king of the worms, and their chief architect is slain;
slain is the worm whose mother is slain, whose brother is slain, and whose sister is slain. 11.
Slain are his household attendants, slain are his surrounding followers;
and furthermore, all those who are like tiny insects—they too are slain. //12//
Of all the male worms and of all the female worms, I split their heads with a stone and burn their mouths with fire. 13.
Savitṛ is the lord of all impellings; may he protect me in this sacred formulation,
in this rite, in this priestly office, in this foundation,
in this thought, in this intention, in this blessing, and in this invocation of the gods— svāhā!

Agni is the overlord of the trees; may he protect me in this sacred formulation (*brahman*), in this rite, in this office of the domestic priest, in this foundation, in this thought, in this intention, in this blessing, and in this invocation of the gods—*svāhā*! 2.

May Heaven and Earth, the sovereign lords of givers, protect me in this sacred formulation (*brahman*), in this rite, in this priestly office, in this foundation, in this thought, in this intention, in this blessing, and in this invocation of the gods— *svāhā*!

Varuṇa is the lord of the waters; may he protect me in this sacred formulation (*brahman*), in this rite, in this office of the domestic priest, in this foundation, in this thought, in this intention, in this blessing, and in this invocation of the gods—*svāhā*! 4.

Mitra and Varuṇa, whose overlordship is rain—may they protect me in this sacred formulation, in this rite, in this priestly office, in this foundation, in this thought, in this intention, in this blessing, and in this invocation of the gods. Svāhā! 5.
The Maruts, the lords of the mountains, may they protect me;
in this sacred formulation (*brahman*), in this rite, in this priesthood, in this foundation, in this thought, in this intention, in this blessing, in this invocation of the gods— *svāhā*!

Soma is the overlord of plants; may he protect me in this sacred formulation (*brahman*), in this rite, in this priestly office, in this foundation, in this thought, in this intention, in this blessing, and in this invocation of the gods— *svāhā*!

Vāyu is the lord of the intermediate space; may he protect me in this sacred formulation, in this rite, in this priestly office, in this foundation, in this thought, in this intention, in this blessing, and in this invocation of the gods— svāhā!

Sūrya is the lord of eyes; may he protect me in this sacred formulation (*brahman*), in this rite, in this office of the domestic priest, in this foundation, in this thought, in this intention, in this blessing, and in this invocation of the gods— *svāhā*!

The Moon is the lord of the constellations; may he protect me in this sacred formulation (*brahman*), in this rite, in this priestly office, in this foundation, in this thought, in this intention, in this blessing, and in this invocation of the gods—*svāhā*! 10.

Indra is the overlord of heaven; may he protect me in this sacred formulation (*brahman*), in this rite, in this priestly office, in this foundation, in this thought, in this intention, in this blessing, and in this invocation of the gods—*svāhā*! 11.
The father of the Maruts, the lord of cattle, may he protect me in this sacred formulation,
in this rite, in this priestly office, in this foundation, in this thought, in this intention, in this blessing, in this invocation of the gods— *svāhā*! 12.

Death is the lord of creatures; may he protect me in this sacred formulation (*brahman*), in this rite, in this priestly office, in this foundation, in this thought, in this intention, in this blessing, and in this invocation of the gods—*svāhā*! 13.

Yama is the sovereign lord of the ancestors; may he protect me in this sacred formulation (*brahman*), in this rite, in this priestly office, in this foundation, in this thought, in this intention, in this blessing, and in this invocation of the gods—*svāhā*! 14.

May those ancestors who are beyond protect me in this sacred formulation (*brahman*), in this ritual act, in this priestly office, in this foundation, in this thought, in this intention, in this blessing, and in this invocation of the gods— *svāhā*! 15.

May those who are lower than you favor me in this sacred formulation (*brahman*), in this ritual act (*karman*), in this priestly office (*purodhā*), in this foundation (*pratiṣṭhā*), in this thought (*citti*), in this intention (*ākūti*), in this blessing (*āśis*), and in this invocation of the gods (*devahūti*). *Svāhā!* 16.
May those great-grandfathers protect me;

in this sacred formulation (*brahman*), in this ritual act, in this priestly office, in this foundation, in this thought, in this intention, in this blessing, and in this invocation of the gods—*svāhā*! 17.
Brought together from the mountain, from the womb of heaven, limb by limb;
may the penis, the placer of seed for the embryo, set it like a feather upon the shaft. //1//
Just as this great earth receives the embryo of living beings, so do I place the embryo within you; for that purpose, I call upon you for aid. 2.
Bestow the embryo, O Sinīvālī; bestow the embryo, O Sarasvatī.
May both the Aśvins, adorned with lotus-garlands, bestow an embryo upon you.
May Mitra and Varuṇa place the embryo within you; may the god Bṛhaspati place the embryo within you. May Indra and Agni place the embryo within you; may Dhātṛ place the embryo within you. //4//
May Viṣṇu prepare the womb; may Tvaṣṭṛ fashion the forms. May Prajāpati pour [the seed]; may Dhātṛ place the embryo within you. //5//
Whatever King Varuṇa knows, or whatever the goddess Sarasvatī knows, or what Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, knows—that which produces the embryo, drink that! 6.
You are the embryo of the plants, the embryo of the trees; you are the embryo of every living being. As such, O Agni, place the embryo here within us.
Climb up, display your heroism; place the embryo in the womb.
You are a bull, possessed of virility; we lead you here for the sake of progeny. //8//
Open wide, O Bārhatsāman; let your embryo lie within your womb.
The gods, the Soma-drinkers, have granted you a son who possesses both natures.
O Creator, with the most excellent form, place a male child within this woman’s womb, so that he may be born in the tenth month.
O Tvaṣṭṛ, with your most excellent form, place a male child within the womb-crevices of this woman, so that he may be born in the tenth month.
O Savitṛ, with your most excellent form, place a male child within the womb-crevices of this woman, so that she may give birth in the tenth month.
O Prajāpati, with your most excellent form, place a male child within the womb-crevices of this woman, so that she may give birth in the tenth month. 13.
May Agni, the wise one, join you here with the sacrificial formulas at the sacrifice as fuel, svāhā! 1.
May the god Savitṛ, the Great One, knowing [all], join [us] in this sacrifice; svāhā!
O Indra, you who are all-knowing, yoke the well-yoked [steeds] to the hymns and songs of praise at this sacrifice; Svāhā!
The calls at the sacrifice, the invocations, and the remaining portions, joined with the wives, carry [the offerings] here with the cry of "Svāhā. //4//
The *chandases* in the sacrifice, O Maruts—svāhā! Like a mother carrying her son, may you, being harnessed, carry us across here. //5//
Thus has Aditi come with the sacrificial grass and the sprinkling waters for those performing the sacrifice; Svāhā!
May Viṣṇu yoke his many heats; may they be well-yoked in this sacrifice, svāhā!
May Tvaṣṭṛ now yoke many forms; may he yoke well-yoked [forms] at this sacrifice—svāhā!
May Bhaga yoke blessings for him; may he, the wise one, yoke them well-yoked at this sacrifice—svāhā!
May Soma yoke the many streams; may they be well-yoked at this sacrifice—svāhā!
May Indra yoke the many streams of milk; may they be well-yoked in this sacrifice, svāhā!
O Aśvins, come hither with the sacred word (*brahman*), increasing the sacrifice with the *vaṣaṭ* call!
O Bṛhaspati, come hither with the sacred word; this is the sacrifice, this is the light for the sacrificer—*svāhā*! 12.
His fuel-sticks rise upward; the bright flames of Agni rise upward.
Most radiant, with a beautiful countenance, the son of strength, Tanūnapāt, the Asura with many hands. //1//
The god among gods, the divine one, anoints the paths with honey and ghee.
Approaching the sacrifice with honey, the benevolent Narāśaṃsa, Agni the god, Savitṛ who possesses all boons, is the performer of good deeds. //3//
He approaches with power, even as one who is offered oblations; the bearer comes, being impelled by our homage. 4.
Agni is the ladle in the sacrifices when they are performed; may he worship the majesty of this Agni. //5//
The Vasus and the bestowers of wealth stood forth amidst the delightful offerings.
The goddesses, the Doors, follow his every command; they guard his ordinance forever.
As they rule by the far-extending domain of Agni,
may Dawn and Night, the well-pressing, the worshipful, and close at hand, protect this sacrifice and our ritual service.
O divine Hotṛs, with the tongue of Agni, celebrate our sacrifice upward; sing for us so that it may be well-sacrificed.
May the three goddesses—Iḍā, Sarasvatī, and the great Bhāratī—being praised, sit upon this sacred grass.
O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, release for us that wondrous seed, rich in food, and open the navel of this abundance of wealth.
O Lord of the Forest, release [the victim], being gracious;
may Agni himself, as the immolator, make the oblation palatable for the gods. //11//
O Agni Jātavedas, perform the *svāhā* offering;
may all the gods enjoy this oblation for Indra. 12.
He measures out the nine vital breaths with nine [threads] for the sake of long life, for a hundred autumns;
three in the green [thread], three in the silver, and three in the iron, all pervaded by ascetic heat (*tapas*).

Agni, Sūrya, Candramas, Earth, Waters, Heaven, the intermediate space, and the quarters and intermediate directions—may these, in harmony with the seasonal deities through the seasons, carry me across by means of this threefold [hymn]. //2//
May the three prosperities rest upon the threefold [sacrifice]; may Pūṣan anoint them with milk and ghee.
May the abundance of food, the abundance of men, and the abundance of cattle rest here for you. 3.
O Ādityas, sprinkle this man with wealth; O Agni, being strengthened yourself, cause him to grow.
O Indra, endow this man with heroic power; let the threefold, nourishing [sacrifice] be established in him. 4.
May the Earth protect you with her greenness; may Agni, the sustainer of all, fulfill [your needs] with his iron-like power, being well-disposed.
May the plants, in harmony with Arjuna, bestow upon you skill and a well-pleased mind.
This gold was born threefold from this birth; one part became the most beloved of Agni; one part flew away when Soma was struck down;
they say one part was the seed of the waters, the ordainers. May that gold of yours be threefold for the sake of long life.
The triple life-span of Jamadagni, the triple life-span of Kaśyapa; the threefold manifestation of immortality—I have bestowed these three life-spans upon you. (7)
When the three birds, having become one syllable, came together as powerful ones with the threefold [sacrifice],
they struck back at death with immortality, warding off all misfortunes.
May the green [horse] protect you from heaven; may the white [horse] protect you from the middle [space].
May the iron-clad [horse] protect you from the earth; this one has gone forth toward the citadels of the gods. 9.
These three divine cities—may they protect you on every side.
Wearing them, may you be radiant and superior to your enemies.
The city of the gods, the immortal gold, which the first god bound at the beginning—homage to him I offer ten times toward the east; may he grant his approval for my threefold binding. 11.
May Aryaman, Pūṣan, and Bṛhaspati fasten you [to me].
By that name which belongs to one born of the day, with that we fasten you.
With the seasons and the seasonal periods, for the sake of life and splendor;
with the brilliance of the year, by that we make your jaw strong. 13.
Drawn from clarified butter, anointed with honey, a firm foundation for the earth, immovable and victorious—shattering my rivals and casting them down, ascend unto me for great good fortune! 14.
Yoked in front, carry us, O Jātavedas; O Agni, know this which is being done.
You are the physician, the maker of the remedy; through you may we win cattle, horses, and men. 1.
O Agni Jātavedas, acting in concert with all the gods, do likewise for us: so that whoever has played us false, whoever has devoured us, he shall fall into his own enclosures. //2//
O Agni Jātavedas, act in such a way that it shall fly into his enclosing-sticks,
acting in harmony with all the gods.
Pierce his eyes; pierce his heart; cut out his tongue; crush his teeth!
O Agni, youngest one, crush back whichever Piśāca has devoured him! 4.

Whatever of his has been taken away, scattered, or carried off, whatever has been devoured from himself by the *piśācas*—O Agni, you who know, bring that back; we shall infuse flesh and life-force into his body. //5//

Whether raw, well-cooked, variegated, or thoroughly cooked—whatever Piśāca has harmed me while eating, let those Piśācas be driven away by themselves and by their offspring; let this man be free from disease.
Whether it be in milk, in curd, in what has been harmed, or in grain that ripens after being ploughed—let the Piśācas drive that away from himself and his offspring; let him be free from disease. 7.

Whichever one among the flesh-eating sorcerers has harmed me while I was drinking water, or while I was lying down on my bed—let those Piśācas be driven away from that by themselves and their offspring; let this man be free from disease.

Whether by day or by night, whichever flesh-eater among the sorcerers has harmed me while I lay upon my bed—let those *piśācas* be driven away from themselves and from their offspring; let this man be free from disease. 9.
O Agni, Jātavedas, slay the flesh-eater, the blood-drinker, the Piśāca who steals the mind!
Let the vigorous Indra strike him down with his thunderbolt; let the bold Soma cut off his head.
From of old, O Agni, you have crushed the sorcerers; the *rakṣas* have never conquered you in battles.
Burn up the flesh-eaters along with their roots; let none escape your divine weapon.
Gather together, O Jātavedas, that which has been carried away and that which has been brought back;
may his limbs grow, and may this man swell like a stalk of grain.
Like a shoot of Soma, O Jātavedas, let this man swell;
O Agni, make him vigorous, pure, and free from disease, so that he may live. 13.
(14a) These, O Agni, are thy fuel-sticks that crush the Piśācas;
(14c) do thou enjoy them and accept them, O Jātavedas!
O Agni, accept these fuel-sticks of the *tārṣṭāghī* wood with your flame;
let the flesh-eater abandon his form, he who seeks to seize this man’s flesh. 15.
From near at hand we call you; from afar we call you.
Be right here; do not go away; do not follow after the ancestors of old. I bind your life-force firmly. 1.
Whether a man of your own kin or a stranger has practiced sorcery against you—
I declare both the binding and the loosening to you with my speech.
Whatever offense you have committed against a woman or a man through thoughtlessness,
whether it be an act of binding or an act of releasing, I declare both of them to you with my speech.
Whatever sin remains from what was done by your mother, and whatever from what was done by your father—I utter for you both the words of release and complete liberation. 4.
Whatever your mother, whatever your father, your kin, and your brother have discharged—turn toward that remedy; I make you one who reaches old age. //5//
Stay here, O man, with your whole mind;
do not follow the two messengers of Yama; go to the dwellings of the living.
Summoned back again, O wise one, come hither; ascend the rising of the path, the ascent, the stepping forth, the way of every living being.
Do not fear; you shall not die. I grant you a full life reaching old age. I have driven the *yakṣma* disease from your limbs, the fever that afflicts your body.
The breaking of your limbs, the fever in your limbs, and that disease of your heart— the consumption has flown away like a hawk, overcome by our word, far beyond.
The two seers, Bodha and Pratibodha, he who is sleepless and he who is watchful— may those two be your guardians of the vital breath, remaining awake by day and by night.
This fire has been approached; here let the sun rise for you.
Rise up from the deep death, even from the black darkness. 11.
Homage to Yama, homage be to Death; homage to the Fathers and to those who lead [the dead].
I place that Agni at my front, he who knows the crossing over, for my safety and well-being. 12.
Let breath come back, let mind come back, let sight and likewise strength come back;
may his body find consciousness, and may it stand firm upon its two feet.
O Agni, unite this man with breath and sight; impel him with body and strength.
You know the path to immortality; let him not go astray, nor let him become one who dwells in the earth. 14.
Let not your out-breath perish, nor let your in-breath be withheld;
may Sūrya, your sovereign lord, deliver you from death with his rays.
This tongue speaks within, bound and unable to utter a sound;
through you, I have spoken away the consumption and the hundred fevers of *takman*.
This world is most dear to the gods and unconquered;
for whatever death you were destined here at birth, O man, we call you back toward that—do not die before old age. 17.
The sorcery (*kṛtyā*) which they wrought for you in an unbaked vessel, which they wrought in mixed grain,
and that sorcery which they wrought in raw meat— that I bring back again.
The sorcery which they have wrought for you against the cock, or that which they have placed upon the goat wearing a crest;
that sorcery which they have wrought against you with wool—this I take back again.
The sorcery which they have wrought against you, the single-hoofed among animals, the one with two rows of teeth—the sorcery they have wrought against the donkey, that I take back again. //3//
The spell which they have cast against you in the rootless *narācī* plant, or the magic (*kṛtyā*) which they have cast upon your field—that I bring back again to them. //4//
The sorcery which the ill-disposed have wrought for you at the *gārhapatya* fire or at the former fire, and that sorcery which they have wrought within the hall—that I drive back again. (AVŚ 5.31.5)
The sorcery which they wrought for you in the assembly hall, which they wrought at the gambling table,
the spell which they cast upon the dice— that I take back again.
That spell which they have cast upon your army, that which they have cast upon the weapons,
and the spell which they have cast upon the drum— that, I bring back again.
The spell (*kṛtyā*) which they placed for you in the well, or buried in the cemetery—whatever spell they have made in your dwelling, that I bring back again. (8)
That [evil] which men have wrought against you in the human bone, and that which they have placed in the fire and the funeral pyre—that Mroka, Nirdāha, and Kravyāda, I drive back again to them. 9.
By a pathless way we have seized her; from that path we send her forth.
The unwise man has seized her from the wise by his lack of understanding.
He who attempted but was unable to do it, and broke his foot and toe—may he bring us prosperity, for he is without fortune while we possess fortune. (AVŚ 5.31.11)
May Indra strike down with a great weapon the performer of sorcery, the practitioner of deception, the root-user, and the one subject to curses; may Agni pierce him with his missile.
Sing the *doṣa* hymn; sing it aloud; bestow splendor. O Atharvan, praise the god Savitṛ. //1//
Praise him who is within the river, the son,
the youth of Truth, whose speech is guileless and who is most gracious.
May that god Savitṛ indeed impel for us many immortal things, so that both our excellent praises may go well on their way. //3//
O officiating priests, press the Soma for Indra and wash it;
may he who hears the singer’s word and my call. //1//
Into him the drops enter, as birds into a tree, with the soma-juice.
O Virapśin, strike down the malicious ones who possess demonic power.
Press the Soma for Indra, the drinker of Soma, the wielder of the thunderbolt;
he is the youthful conqueror, the sovereign lord, praised by many.
May Aditi protect us; may Indra and Pūṣan protect us; may the Maruts protect us.
May the Son of the Waters and the Seven Rivers protect us; may Viṣṇu and the Sky protect us.
May Heaven and Earth protect us for our aid; may the pressing-stone protect us, and may Soma protect us from distress.
May the goddess Sarasvatī, the fortunate one, protect us; may Agni protect us with his auspicious guardians. 2.
May the divine Aśvins, lords of splendor, protect us; may Dawn and Night likewise grant us wide space.
O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, son of the waters, increase our household even when it is oppressed, for the sake of complete well-being.
May Tvaṣṭṛ, Parjanya, and Brahmaṇaspati grant me divine speech;
may Aditi with her sons and brothers now protect us—[grant] invincible, rescuing power.
May Aṃśa, Bhaga, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman, Aditi, and the Maruts protect us.
May his hatred depart, driven away; may he keep the enemy at a distance.
O Aśvins, further our prayer; protect us, O wide-striding one, never failing.
O Father Heaven, ward off whatever misfortune there may be. 3.
Lead him upward, O Agni, you who are invoked with clarified butter;
endow him with splendor and make him abundant with progeny. //1//
O Indra, make him superior; let him be the controller among his kinsmen.
Endow him with the increase of wealth; lead him to life and to old age.
O Agni, do you cause him to prosper in whose house we prepare the oblation; for him may Soma speak favorably, as may this Brahmaṇaspati. //3//
O Brahmaṇaspati, whoever, being godless, seeks to harm us—deliver him all to my control, for me, the sacrificer who presses the soma. //1//
O Soma, whoever, being ill-disposed toward us who are well-praising, seeks to direct his malice against us—strike him in the mouth with your thunderbolt; crushed, let him depart.
Whoever assails us, O Soma— whether he be a kinsman or a stranger—
drive away his strength, as the great heaven does by means of its thunderbolt.
By that path on which Soma, Aditi, and the guileless Mitra go, by that come to us with your protection. //1//
O Soma, with that power by which you cause the Asuras to be subdued, speak for us with that. //2//
With that by which you gods overcame the powers of the Asuras, with that grant us protection. //3//
Just as the *libujā* creeper embraces the tree on all sides, so do you embrace me, that you may be loving toward me and never turn away from me. //1//
Just as a bird, when swooping down, strikes its wings against the earth, so do I strike down your mind, so that you shall be loving toward me and never turn away from me. //2//
Just as the sun instantly traverses these two, heaven and earth, even so do I encompass your mind, so that you may be loving toward me and never turn away from me. //3//
Desire my body; desire my feet; desire my eyes; desire my thighs.
May the eyes and the hair of you who lust after me wither away through desire for me.
I make you cling to my arms,
clinging to my heart, so that you shall abide in my will and follow my mind.
Those whose navel is the place of attraction, in whose heart the act of enchantment is made—those cows, the mothers of clarified butter, let them bring her under my control. 3.
To the Earth, to the sense of hearing, to the trees, and to Agni the overlord—svāhā! 1.
To the breaths, to the intermediate space, to the birds, and to Vāyu the overlord, Svāhā!
To the sky, to the eye, to the stars, to Sūrya the sovereign lord—svāhā!
The *aśvattha* has climbed onto the *śamī*; there the rite for producing a male child was performed.
That which is indeed the means of obtaining a son, that we bring to these women. //1//
In the male indeed semen comes into being; it is poured into the female. That is the means of obtaining a son; that Prajāpati declared.
Prajāpati, Anumati, and Sinīvālī have fashioned this;
causing the female seed to be elsewhere, they place the male here.
Like the sun around the sky, I have come to the progeny of the serpents;
as the night [surrounds] all other moving things, by that I ward off your poison. 1.
That which was known of old by the Brahmans, by the seers, and by the gods—that which has been, that which is to be, and that which exists—by means of that I ward off your poison. 2.
I mix the rivers with honey; the mountains and the hills are honey.
May the Paruṣṇī and the Śīpālā be honey; may there be peace for my mouth and peace for my heart. 3.
Homage to the slayers of gods, homage to the slayers of kings;
and also to those who are the slayers of commoners—to you, O Death, let there be homage.
Homage to your favor; homage to you for your rejection.
Homage to you, O Death, for your goodwill; this homage to you for your ill-will. //2//
Homage to your sorcerers, homage to your remedies;
homage to you, O Death, to your roots; this homage to the Brahmins. //3//
The loosening of the bones, the loosening of the joints, the disease seated in the heart, the *balāsa*—destroy all of it, whether it resides in the limbs or in the joints. 1.
I destroy the consumption of the consumptive man, like one who castrates a testicular tumor;
I cut his bond, his very root, like a creeping vine.
Fly away from here, O Balāsa, swift as a young fawn; then, like a year-old calf, run away without harming the heroes.
You are the highest of plants; trees are your attendants.
May he who assails us be our attendant. //1//
Whether he be a kinsman or a stranger who assails us—
may I become the highest of them all, like the tallest among trees.
Just as Soma is made the highest among herbs and the best of oblations, so may I become the highest, like the Tālāśa tree among trees. 3.
The consuming ones, the non-consuming ones—their essence is yours, O fierce one;
we eat your *karambha* porridge. 1.
Vihahla is the name of your father; Madāvatī is the name of your mother. For you are indeed that which has caused yourself to waste away.
O Tāuvilikā, at this very moment this Ailaba has been made to tremble;
both Babhru and Babhrukarna—go away, O Āla! 3.
The *alasālā* is the first; the *silāñjalā* is the second;
the *nīlāgalasāla* is [the third]. //4//
Just as this great earth receives the germ of living beings,
so may your embryo be sustained for birth after the impelling.
Just as this great earth supports these lords of the forest,
so may your embryo be sustained for birth in due time.
Just as this great earth supports the mountains and the peaks,
so may your embryo be sustained for birth and for delivery.
Just as this great earth supports the world that stands upon it,
so may your embryo be sustained for birth, following the impulse of Savitṛ.
The first flight of envy, and that which follows it—
this heart-scorching fire, this grief of yours, we extinguish for you.
Just as the earth has a dead mind, more dead than those who have died; and just as the mind of one who has passed away is dead, so too is the mind of the enemy dead.
That which is settled in your heart, the mind that is prone to flight— from that I release your envy, like steam from a leather bag. 3.
May the divine hosts purify me; may the sages purify me with their inspired thought.
May all beings purify me; may Pavamāna purify me. 1.
May Pavamāna purify me for wisdom, for skill, and for life,
and also for safety.
O God Savitṛ, with both [means]— with the filter and with the impulse—
purify us so that we may see.
Like the fire of this impetuous one, it comes burning; like one intoxicated, he wanders away lamenting.
Let him who is without vows seek someone other than us; let there be homage to Takman for his burning destruction! 1.
Homage to Rudra; homage be to Takman; homage to King Varuṇa, the radiant one. Homage to Heaven; homage to Earth; homage to the plants. //2//
(6.20.3a) This one who causes burning, you who turn all forms yellow— (6.20.3c) to that ruddy, brown, forest-born fever, I pay homage. 3.
Of these three earths that exist, this ground is indeed the highest;
from their very skin, I have gathered together this medicine. //1//
You are the best of medicines, the most excellent of plants;
like Soma among the gods, like Bhaga in his journeys, and like Varuṇa. //2//
O wealthy ones, unassailable, desiring to win, you shall win! You are indeed those who strengthen the hair, and also those who cause the hair to grow. //3//
The tawny birds with beautiful wings fly up to heaven, clothed in the waters, along their black path.
They have returned from the seat of Cosmic Order; indeed, they have spread the earth with clarified butter.
Make the waters and the plants full of milk and auspicious, O Maruts, when you stir yourselves, you who have golden plates upon your chests.
Bestow both strength and favor there, where, O Marut heroes, you pour forth honey.
Plunged into the water, O Maruts, send forth that rain which shall fill all the hollows.
It stirs like a gambler’s stake, like a maiden who has been pierced; it moves like a wife toward her husband.
Those who have flowed, performing their work by day and by night—those who have flowed, I, whose resolve is excellent, invoke the divine waters. 1.
May the waters, ready for action, release us from here for guidance;
may they enable us to go forth immediately.
By the impulse of the god Savitṛ, let men perform their work.
May the waters and the plants be auspicious and propitious to us. 3.
From the Himavat they flow forth; their meeting place is in the Sindhu.
May the divine waters grant me that medicine which illuminates the heart.
Whatever has pained my eyes, my heels, and my forefeet—
may the waters, the most excellent of physicians, drive all that away.
O you who have the Indus as your consort, O you whose queen is the Indus, all you rivers that exist—grant us the remedy for this; through it may we enjoy your favor.
The fifty-five sinews that converge upon the neck—
let them all perish from here, like the spells of those who have lost their honor.
The seventy-seven necklaces that come together around the neck—
let them all perish from here, like the spells of those who have been humbled.
The nine and the ninety shoulder-blades that come together—
let them all perish from here like the spells of those who have been humbled.
Release me from evil, O Lord; being self-controlled, have mercy on us.
Place me, unharmed, in the world of the auspicious, O Evil One. 1.
O Evil One, you who do not leave us—now we abandon you!
At the turning point of the paths, let another evil fall upon you.
Let the immortal, thousand-eyed one designate [the curse] upon someone other than us.
Let it strike him whom we hate; indeed, slay him whom we loathe. 3.

O gods, since the dove, sent as a messenger by Nirṛti, has come here seeking [us], let us offer praise to it and perform an atonement; may there be well-being for our bipeds and well-being for our quadrupeds. //1//
May the dove sent to us be auspicious; O gods, may this bird be harmless to our home.
May Agni, the sage, accept our oblation; may the winged missile spare us. //2//
The winged missile shall not harm us; the female owl makes her dwelling in the fire-chamber.
May she be auspicious to our cattle and to our men; O gods, let not the dove injure us here. 3.
Drive away the dove with a verse; casting it forth, we lead the cow around while rejoicing in the food.
Causing it to falter at the evil steps, may it leave us strength and depart upon the paths.
These men have carried Agni around; these men have led the cow around.
They have established glory among the gods—who would dare to attack them? //2//
He who first reached the slope, finding the path for many;
he who rules over his two-footed and four-footed creatures—to that Yama, to Death, let there be homage. 3.
May that winged missile descend upon those [enemies]! What the owl hoots is in vain;
or whatever footprint the dove makes in the fire. //1//
Those two messengers of yours, O Nirṛti, who have come here to our house—whether unbidden or bidden—let that footless state belong to the dove and the owl. //2//
May this fly away for the sake of freedom from enmity; may it settle here for the sake of heroic offspring.
Turn away and speak away, following the backward-turning wind, so that in the house of Yama you may behold only saplessness, you may behold only fruitlessness.
The gods ploughed this barley, mixed with honey, upon the Sarasvatī over the gem;
Indra, the lord of a hundred powers, was the master of the plough, and the bounteous Maruts were the ploughmen. //1//
That intoxication of yours which is loose-haired and disheveled, by which you make a man laughable—far from you I cut down other woods; O Śamī tree, grow forth with a hundred branches.
O you with broad leaves, fortunate one, grown great by the rain, observer of the cosmic order;
like a mother to her sons, be gracious to my hair, O Śamī tree. 3.
This spotted bull has come; he has settled before his mother, and advancing toward heaven, he has reached his father. //1//
He moves within the luminous realms; from his out-breath and in-breath, the Great One has manifested the sun.
He shines across thirty stations; Vāk, the bird, has taken her stand, day after day at the break of dawn. //3//
Offer this into the midst of the forest with clarified butter; it is the destroyer of sorcerers.
Burn the demons far away, O Agni; do not let them scorch our homes. 1.
O Piśācas, may Rudra shatter your necks; O Yātudhānas, may he crush your backs.
May the plant of all-pervading power bring you under the sway of Yama.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, let there be fearlessness for us here; with your flame, drive away the devourers from the front.
Let them find neither a kinsman nor a firm footing; striking one another down, let them go unto death. 3.
To whom this dust belongs, whose yoke is for the sake of strength, [to him] men [offer] new light;
it is the great, delightful [power] of Indra. //1//
The bold one, daring and possessed of daring power, is not assailed by the bold; just as of old his renown was unassailable, so too is Indra’s power unassailable. //2//
May he grant us that wealth, vast and golden-hued;
may Indra, the most powerful lord among men, [bestow it]. //3//
Send forth your speech toward Agni, the bull of the peoples;
may he carry us across our enemies.
The Agni who utterly consumes the *rakṣas* with his sharp flame—
may he carry us across our enemies.
He who shines forth from the furthest distance across the desert wastes—may he carry us beyond our enemies. //3//
He who looks out upon all beings and beholds them together— may he carry us across our enemies.
That bright Agni who was born on the further shore of this region—may he carry us across our enemies. //5//
May Vaiśvānara come to us for our protection from afar;
may Agni come to our well-spoken hymns. 1.
May Vaiśvānara come to this sacrifice of ours with joy;
may Agni [come] to our hymns and to our distresses.
Vaiśvānara has fashioned for the Aṅgirases the hymn and the chant;
he has bestowed upon them splendor and the light of heaven.
We implore the eternal heat, the observer of cosmic order, Vaiśvānara, the lord of the light of truth. //1//
He has fashioned all things; the Lord releases the seasons, furthering the vigor of the sacrifice.
Agni, in the highest abodes, is the desire for what has been and what is to be;
as the sole sovereign, he shines forth. 3.
The thousand-eyed Curse has come near, having yoked its chariot;
seeking out my curser, it has gone to his house like a wolf to a sheepfold.
Avoid us, O curse, like fire burning a lake;
strike down our curser here, as lightning strikes a tree from heaven. //2//
Whoever would curse us when we do not curse, or whoever would curse us when we do curse—
him I cast back toward death, like a dog’s dregs thrown away.

The splendor that is in the lion, the tiger, and the adder, that which is in fire, in the Brahmin, and in the sun—the auspicious goddess who gave birth to Indra, may she come to us, in harmony with our luster. 1.

The splendor that is in the elephant, in the leopard, in gold, in the waters, in the cattle, and in men— that goddess, the fortunate one who gave birth to Indra, may she come to us, in harmony with our luster.

In the chariot, in the axles, in the bull, in the prize, in the wind, in Parjanya, in the strength of Varuṇa—may that fortunate goddess who gave birth to Indra come to us, endowed with splendor. //3//
When the drum resounds for the nobleman, at the prize-winning of the horse and the wondrous power of man—may that auspicious goddess who gave birth to Indra come to us, in harmony with splendor. 4.
May the glory, impelled by Indra, increase—the oblation that possesses a thousandfold power, well-sustained and created with force.
May it spread forth for far-reaching vision; O you who possess the oblation, cause me to increase for the sake of preeminence.
Toward Indra, the glorious one, we who possess glory shall pay homage with worship. May he grant us a kingdom impelled by Indra; in the bounty of you, the glorious one, may we abide. //2//
Glorious was Indra, glorious was Agni; glorious Soma was born. Glorious among all that exists, I am the most glorious. //3//

May heaven and earth grant us fearlessness here; may Soma and Savitṛ grant us fearlessness. May the intermediate space be free from fear for us, and through the oblation to the Seven Seers, may there be fearlessness for us. //1//
For this village, may Savitṛ bestow the four quarters, nourishment, prosperity, and well-being upon us. May Indra, who has no enemies, grant us fearlessness; let the wrath of kings fall elsewhere.
Make us free from enemies from below, free from enemies from above;
O Indra, make us free from enemies from behind and free from enemies from the front.
To mind, to consciousness, to thought, and to intention; to perception, to hearing, and to sight—to these we pay worship with our oblation.
For out-breath, for diffused breath, for vital breath that provides abundant sustenance—
for Sarasvatī of wide extent, may we worship with an oblation.
May the divine seers not abandon us—those who are the guardians of our bodies and those who are born from our own bodies.
O immortals, attend upon us mortals; bestow upon us further life that we may live. 3.
I loosen the fury from your heart, as one loosens the string from a bow, so that we two, becoming of one mind, may move together like two friends. //1//
Like two friends, let us stay together; I loosen your wrath. We cast down beneath you that heavy wrath of yours, as if a stone.
I trample upon your fury with my heel and my forefoot, so that you shall not speak according to your own will, but shall follow my mind. 3.
This *darbha* grass is free from anger, for oneself and for one's companion;
it is called the pacifier of wrath, the remover of the anger of the angry. //1//
This Darbha grass, which has deep roots and stands reaching toward the ocean, rising from the earth, is called the pacifier of wrath.
We remove the arrow from your jaw and we remove it from your mouth, so that you, no longer speaking as you please, shall follow my will. 3.
The sky has stood firm, the earth has stood firm, and this entire world has stood firm;
the trees have stood with their sleep upright—may this disease of yours stand still. 1.
The hundred remedies that are yours, and the thousand gathered together— this is the most excellent medicine for discharges, the best healer, the destroyer of disease.
You are the urine of Rudra, the navel of immortality. You are indeed named Viṣāṇakā; you have arisen from the root of the Fathers, the destroyer of Vātīkṛta. 3.
Go away, O evil-minded one; why do you utter ill-omened things?
Depart! I do not desire you. Roam among the trees and the forests; my mind is set upon my home and my cattle.

Whatever we have committed through our own impulse, through the impulse of others, or through the impulse of enemies—whether waking or sleeping—may Agni place all those evil deeds and unpleasant things far away from us. //2//
O Indra, O Brahmaṇaspati, whatever we do falsely, may the wise Aṅgiras protect us from misfortune and distress. //3//
(6.46.1a) You who are neither living nor dead, you are the embryo of immortality for the gods, O Sleep.
(6.46.1c) Varuṇānī is your mother, Yama is your father; your name is Arawar. //1//
We know your origin, O dream; you are the son of the sisters of the gods, the agent of Yama.
You are the Ender, you are Death. As such we know you, O dream; protect us, O dream, from evil dreaming. 2.
Just as they pay back a sixteenth part, an eighth part, or a debt,
even so do we collect all evil dreams and transfer them to our enemy.

May Agni Vaiśvānara, the maker of all, the source of all well-being, protect us at the morning libation. May he, the purifier, bestow wealth upon us; may we be long-lived and share in the draught together. 1.
May all the gods, the Maruts, and Indra not abandon us at this second libation.
Living long and speaking what is pleasing to them, may we abide in the good favor of the gods. 2.
This is the third libation of the seers, those who by means of the Eternal Law set the chalice in motion.
May those sons of Sudhanvan, having attained the light of heaven, lead us toward well-performed sacrifice and toward greater prosperity. 3.
(6.48.1a) You are a falcon, having the *gāyatrī* as your meter; I take hold of you.
(6.48.1c) Carry me safely to the conclusion of this sacrifice; *svāhā*!
(2) You are R̥bhu; the Jagatī is your meter. I take hold of you. May you carry me safely to the conclusion of this sacrifice. Svāhā!
You are the bull, having the *triṣṭubh* as your meter; I take hold of you. Carry me safely to the conclusion of this sacrifice; *svāhā*!
For no mortal has ever reached the core of your body, O Agni; the monkey devours its own whetted point, as a cow consumes her own afterbirth.
Like a ram, you move both together and apart when the upper and lower stones chew;
striking head with head and flank with flank, you consume the stalks with your golden jaws.

The fair-winged ones have made their voice heard from the sky; the black, vigorous ones have danced upon the mountain ridge. As they descend to the appointed place of the lower one, they, resting in the sun, have deposited abundant seed.
O Aśvins, slay the caterpillar, the beetle, the rat; split its head and crush its backbones!
Bind its mouth so that it does not eat the barley, and then grant safety to the grain. 1.
O Tarada, O Pataṅga, O Jabhya, O Upakvasa!
Like a Brahmin who has not yet partaken of the sacrificial oblation, you have eaten these barley grains; having done no harm, you have departed. 2.

O lords of piercing, O lords of striking, you with the sharp-jawed mouths, listen to me! Those forest-dwelling beasts of prey, and whoever else you are that are beasts of prey—all of them we crush to pieces.
Purified by the filter of Vāyu, Soma has flowed across toward us;
he is the ally and companion of Indra. //1//
May the Waters, our mothers, purify us; may those who cleanse with ghee purify us with ghee.
For the goddesses carry away every defilement; indeed, from them I emerge bright and purified. 2.
Whatever offense against the divine folk, O Varuṇa, humans commit here through thoughtlessness, if we have violated your law, O God, do not harm us for that sin. //3//
The Sun rises from the sky, utterly consuming the *rakṣas* before him;
the Āditya, visible from all mountains, is the slayer of the unseen. //1//
The cows have settled in the cow-pen; the wild beasts have entered their lairs; the waves of the rivers have subsided; and the unseen ones have been smeared away.
I have brought hither the life-giving, wise plant of Kaṇva, renowned and possessing all healing powers; may it cause those unseen [diseases] to be stilled.
May both Heaven and Earth, the wise ones, and may the bright, vast [Soma] fulfill this for me through the sacrificial gift (*dakṣiṇā*).
May *Svadhā*, Soma, Agni, Vāyu, Savitṛ, and Bhaga take notice of us and protect us. 1.
May breath return, may the self return; may sight return, and may the vital spirit return.
May Vaiśvānara, the undeceived protector of our bodies, stand between us and all misfortunes.
We have united with splendor, with nourishment, and with our bodies; we have united with a gracious mind.
May Tvaṣṭṛ grant us wide space here, and may he mend whatever in our bodies is injured. 3.
I adorn this Indra, the superior ally, for the sake of success. May his sovereignty and great glory increase like rain increasing the grass.
O Agni and Soma, maintain sovereign power for him; maintain wealth for him.
Make him superior, a companion in the attainment of the kingdom.
Whether he be a kinsman or a stranger, whoever assails us—subject all of them to me, the sacrificer who presses the soma. //3//
The many paths that lead to the gods, which travel between heaven and earth— of these,
whichever one carries me without failure, to him may all the gods entrust me here.
Summer, winter, the cool season, spring, autumn, and the rains—bestow upon us well-being. Grant us a share in cattle and progeny; may we abide in your windless shelter.
To the *idāvatsara*, to the *parivatsara*, and to the *saṃvatsara*, offer great homage!
May we abide in the benevolent favor and the auspicious goodwill of those worthy of sacrifice. 3.
O gods, let not the serpent slay us, together with our children and our men.
Let him not close what has been opened, nor open what has been closed; homage to the divine folk!
Homage be to the Black One, and homage to the one with transverse stripes!
Homage to the self-born, tawny one; homage to the hosts of gods. //2//
I crush your tooth against tooth; I crush your jaw against jaw. I crush your tongue with your tongue; I close your mouth with your mouth.
This indeed is the remedy, this is the remedy of Rudra,
by which he has warded off the single-pointed arrow with its hundred barbs.
Sprinkle us with *jālāṣa*, pour it upon us with *jālāṣa*;
*jālāṣa* is a powerful remedy—by means of that, be gracious to us so that we may live.
May there be peace for us and joy for us; may nothing whatsoever cause us distress.
May [the earth] forgive our sin; may everything be a healing medicine for us—may all things be a healing medicine for us. 3.
