May Indra Maghavan make me glorious; may both these, Heaven and Earth, make me glorious.
May the god Savitṛ make me glorious; may I be dear here to the giver of the sacrificial fee. 1.
As Indra is glorious between heaven and earth, as the waters are glorious among the plants, even so may we be glorious among all the gods. //2//
Glorious is Indra, glorious is Agni; glorious Soma was born. Glorious among all that exists, may I be the most glorious. //3//
O Arundhatī, you first [bestowed] protection for the oxen and for the milch cows; grant shelter to the barren cow, to the birds, and to the four-footed creatures.
May the herb Arundhatī, together with the goddesses, grant us protection. May she make the cow-pen full of milk and the men free from disease.
I invoke the multiform, auspicious, life-sustaining one;
may she carry away the missile of Rudra far from our cattle.
Here comes Aryaman from the east, with his top-knot loosened;
he desires a husband for this maiden, and a wife for the man who has no wife. 1.
This woman has grown weary, O Aryaman, as she goes to the gathering of others. Truly, O Aryaman, another woman now goes to her gathering.
The Ordainer has supported the earth; the Ordainer [has supported] the sky and the sun.
May the Ordainer bestow upon this maiden a husband who is desirable. 3.
May the waters pour forth sweetness for me; may the sun bring light for me.
May all the gods born of fervor grant it to me, and may the god Savitar bestow wide space upon me.
I separated the earth and the sky; I brought forth the seven seasons together.
I am the truth and the falsehood that I speak; I encompass the divine speech and the people.
I gave birth to the earth and the sky; I generated the seasons and the seven rivers.
I am the truth and the untruth that I speak, I who have delighted in Agni and Soma as friends. //3//
May Vaiśvānara purify us with his rays; may the wind, swift with its breath, purify us through the mists;
may Heaven and Earth, rich in milk, observers of cosmic order, and worthy of sacrifice, purify us with their milk. 1.
Seize upon the Vaiśvānarī Sūnṛtā, whose bodies and back are eager for our prayers.
Praising her at our shared feasts, may we become masters of riches. 2.
Take hold of the Vaiśvānarī for the sake of splendor, becoming pure, bright, and purifying.
Rejoicing here in the shared feast with this song of praise, may we long behold the rising sun. 3.

The bond which the goddess Nirṛti fastened upon your necks, that which cannot be loosened—that I untie for you, for long life, for splendor, and for strength. Being impelled, eat food that brings no distress. //1//
Homage be to you, O Nirṛti of piercing brilliance; loosen the iron bonds and fetters.
Yama shall give you back to me; homage be to that Yama, to Death. //2//
Thou art bound here to an iron pillar, summoned by the deaths that number a thousand.
In harmony with Yama and the Fathers, cause this man to ascend to the highest heaven.
O bull-like Agni, you gather for yourself all the wealth of the enemy;
kindled at the place of libation, bring us riches.
Come to an understanding; be united; let your minds be in harmony, just as the gods of old, being in accord, attend to their portion.
Common is their mantra, common their assembly, common their vow, and their thought is united.
With a common oblation I sacrifice for you; enter into a common consciousness. 2.
One and the same be your intention, one and the same your hearts; let your mind be united so that you may act in harmony.
Let wrath go down, let the two arms extended by the mind go down.
O Parāśara, crush their forward-flying vigor, and then bring wealth to us. //1//
Against those who are handless, the handless weapon which you gods hurl as an arrow— by means of this oblation, I cut off the arms of my enemies.
Indra performed the first act of hand-binding against the Asuras; may my warriors be victorious through Indra, who is steadfast and a companion. 3.
May the attacking enemy be rendered handless—those who come against us with their armies for battle.
O Indra, strike them down with your great weapon; let their destroyer, pierced through, run away. 1.
O you who stretch [the bow], who draw it, and who run while shooting—your enemies are now handless; Indra has scattered you today.
May the enemies be handless; we cause their limbs to wither away.
Then, O Indra, let us divide their possessions into hundreds.
Indra and Pūṣan have traversed the paths on every side;
let those armies of the enemies be bewildered today, far away.
Foolish enemies, moving about like headless snakes—
may Indra slay each one of you, those fools, one by one.
Bind the bull's hide upon them; strike fear into the deer.
Let the enemy flee away; let the cow come hither.
Savitar has come here with the razor; O Vāyu, come with warm water!
May the Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus, being of one mind, moisten [the hair]; O wise ones, shave [the hair] for King Soma. //1//
May Aditi shave the beard; may the waters moisten it with luster. May Prajāpati provide for its healing, so that there may be long life and sight.

With that razor with which Savitṛ, the knower, shaved the hair of King Soma and Varuṇa, with that may the Brahmans shave this [hair] of his; may he be possessed of cattle, possessed of horses, and possessed of progeny. //3//
Whatever glory is in the mountain, in the Aragaraṭas, in gold, and in cattle;
whatever sweetness is in the flowing liquor and in the sacrificial mead—may that be in me. 1.
O Aśvins, lords of splendor, anoint me with the honey of the bee,
so that I may speak words full of luster among the people.
In me be luster and fame, as well as whatever milk belongs to the sacrifice;
may Prajāpati establish that in me, as one secures the sky upon the heavens. 3.
As meat, as liquor,
as dice upon the gaming board, as a man’s mind is struck down with lust for a woman— even so, O inviolable cow, let your mind be struck down upon your calf.
Just as an elephant follows step by step the track of a female elephant,
just as a man’s mind, seeking virility, is fixed upon a woman, so, O inviolable cow, let your mind be fixed upon the calf.
Just as the felly, just as the rim, just as the nave runs along the wheel;
just as a man’s mind, when he is full of desire, is fixed upon a woman— so, O inviolable cow, let your mind be fixed upon the calf.
Whatever food I eat in many forms—gold, horse, cow, goat, or sheep—whatever I have accepted as a gift, may Agni, the Hotṛ, make that a well-offered oblation. (1)

Whatever has come to me as an offering, whether formally sacrificed or unsacrificed, given by the ancestors and approved by men—may Agni, the Hotṛ-priest, make that well-offered for me, since my mind leaps up as it were because of it. //2//

Whatever food I eat through falsehood, O gods—whether I am about to give it or not to give, or whether I praise it—I [offer it] through the greatness of the great Vaiśvānara; may my food be auspicious and sweet. 3.

Just as the black antelope spreads itself out according to its will, fashioning its forms through the magic power (*māyā*) of the Asura, even so let this hymn of yours, O *śepa*, by its own force, join limb with limb together. //1//
Just as the tail of a thief was made thick by the wind,
so may your tail grow as large as the tail of a wild ass.
As much as there is of the horse from the Pārsva region, the elephant, and the donkey; as much as there is of the vigorous stallion—so much may your penis grow. 3.
Let Varuṇa come here, let Soma, Agni, and Bṛhaspati come here with the Vasus. All you kinsmen, of one mind, approach the glory of this fierce lord. 1.
Whatever vigor is within your hearts, whatever intention has entered your minds—that I sew together with oblation and ghee. O kinsmen, may your delight be in me. 2.
Stay right here; do not go away from us. May Pūṣan make the path difficult for you from beyond.
May Vāstoṣpati call out to you repeatedly; O kinsmen, may your delight be in me. //3//
May your bodies be united, may your minds be united, and may your vows be united. May this Brahmaṇaspati, Bhaga, bring you all together. //1//
This is the appeasement of your mind, and this is the appeasement of your heart;
moreover, with that which is the exhaustion of Bhaga, I appease you.
Just as the Ādityas were united with the Vasus, and the fierce Maruts were free from malice, so do you, O Triṇāman, being free from malice, make these people here of one mind. 3.
Drive that rival away from his dwelling who attacks us;
with the *nairbādhyam* oblation, Indra has cast him down. 1.
May Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, drive her to the furthest distance, from whence she shall not return again for eternal years. //2//
Let it go beyond the three distant realms; let it pass beyond the five peoples.
Let it go beyond the three luminous spheres, from which it shall not return again for eternal years, as long as the sun remains in heaven. //3//
Those who sit around him and prepare him for sight—may Agni, fully kindled by his tongues, rise up from the heart. 1.
I take hold of the station of Agni Sāmtapana for the sake of long life—
of him whose smoke, rising from his mouth, one truly beholds.
He who knows his fuel, kindled by the Kṣatriya—he does not set foot upon the precipice for Death. //3//
The pursuers do not slay him, nor does he fall into the snare—
this wise Kṣatriya who utters the name of Agni for the sake of long life.
The sky has stood firm, the earth has stood firm, and this entire world has stood firm.
The mountains have stood upon their foundations; I have established the horses in their place.
I call upon him who is the upward breath and the ultimate goal, who is the out-breath and the path of right conduct; I call upon that guardian who is the turning back and the returning.
O Jātavedas, turn [them] back! Let there be a hundred returns for you;
let there be a thousand approaches for you. With these, bring them back to us again. //3//
By that true oblation, let this man swell again;
let him cause to increase with sap the wife whom they have brought for him. //1//
May he increase with milk; may he increase with royal power.
With wealth of a thousandfold luster, may these two be undecaying.
Tvaṣṭṛ has generated the wife; Tvaṣṭṛ [has given] you as her husband.
May Tvaṣṭṛ grant you both a thousand lifespans and long life. 3.
May this lord of the sky, the nourisher, protect us; may he grant us peerless prosperity within our homes.
O Lord of the Cloud, do you bestow vigor upon our homes;
let nourishment come, and let wealth come.
O God, O Increaser, you are the lord of thousandfold nourishment. Grant us of that; bestow that upon us; may we be partakers of that which is yours. 3.
He flies through the intermediate space, beholding all beings;
with that greatness of the divine dog, let us worship you with this oblation. //1//
Those three Kālakāñjas who dwell in heaven like gods—
I have invoked them all for aid, for this man’s safety and well-being.
In the waters is your birth, in heaven is your dwelling; within the ocean and upon the earth is your greatness.
With that splendor of the divine dog, we shall worship you with this oblation. //3//
You are a restrainer; you restrain both hands and drive away the demons.
Seizing offspring and wealth, this *parihasta* has come into being. 1.
O bracelet, hold fast the womb for the depositing of the embryo;
place the son within the boundary; do you bring him hither at our coming.
That amulet which Aditi wore on her wrist, desiring a son—
Tvaṣṭṛ fastened it upon her so that she might give birth to a son.
I take the name of you who have come from afar as you approach;
I win [the favor] of Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, the son of Vasu, the lord of a hundred powers.
By that path on which the Aśvins brought Sūryā Sāvitrī, by that same path Bhaga said to me: "Bring hither a wife. //2//
O Indra, Lord of Might, with that great golden goad of yours which bestows wealth, grant me a wife who shall bear children. 3.
O scabs, fly away like a well-winged bird from its dwelling;
may the Sun provide the remedy, and may the Moon drive you away.
One is brownish, one is falcon-colored, one is black, and two are ruddy.
I have seized the name of them all; you who do not kill heroes, depart!
The woman who has not given birth, the one afflicted by *rāmāyaṇī*, shall fall away; the *glau* disease shall fall away from here, and that *galunta* shall perish. //3//
Enjoy your own oblation, being pleased in mind; *svāhā*, that which I offer here with the mind! //4//
Into whose terrible mouth I offer this for the release of these who are bound—people call you "Earth," but I know you thoroughly from every side as Nirṛti. //1//
O Earth, be rich in oblations; this is thy portion which belongs to us. Release these and those from sin—svāhā!
Thus, O Nirṛti, may you, who are not stingy, loosen for us these iron fetters and bonds.
Yama gives you back to me; let there be homage to that Yama, to Death. 3.
Thou art bound here to an iron pillar by the deaths that number a thousand.
In harmony with Yama and the Fathers, cause this man to ascend to the highest firmament.
May this divine tree, Varaṇa, ward off [the disease]; the consumption that has entered into him, that very thing the gods have warded away.
By the word of Indra, and by that of Mitra and Varuṇa,
and by the speech of all the gods, we ward off your consumption.
Just as Vṛtra held back these waters flowing in every direction, even so do I ward off your consumption with Agni Vaiśvānara. 3.
The bull of heaven, the bull of earth—this one is the bull of all that exists; may you be the sole bull. //1//
The ocean rules over the flowing rivers; Agni is the master of the earth.
The moon rules over the constellations; may you become the sole bull. 2.
You are the sovereign of the Asuras, the leader of men;
you are the half-share of the gods—be thou the sole bull. //3//
I have brought you here; you have entered within. Stand firm, unshakable.
Let all the people desire you; let the kingdom not fall away from you. 1.
Be right here; do not fall away, remaining as immovable as a mountain.
Stand firm here like Indra; uphold the sovereignty here.
Indra has established this [pillar] as firm with a firm oblation;
may Soma and this Brahmaṇaspati speak in its favor. //3//
Firm is the sky, firm is the earth, firm is this entire moving world;
firm are these mountains, and firm is this king of the people.
Surely may King Varuṇa, surely may the god Bṛhaspati, and surely may both Indra and Agni maintain your kingdom securely. //2//
Firm and unshakable, crush the enemies; cast down those who act as foes.
May all the quarters of space be of one mind and united; may the assembly be favorable here for you, the firm one. 3.
This head of the lover which was given by Soma as virility—by that which is born from it, we cause your heart to burn. //1//
We burn your heart; we burn your mind.
Like smoke following the wind, let your mind follow after me alone. 2.
For me may Mitra and Varuṇa, for me may the goddess Sarasvatī—may both ends of the earth cast you into my midst. 3.
O Rudra, that arrow which you have aimed at your [victim’s] limbs and heart—today we pull that away from you in all directions. 1.
Those hundred vessels of yours that are distributed throughout your limbs—
from all of them we summon forth the poisons.
Homage to you, O Rudra, as you are about to shoot; homage to you when you have aimed.
Homage to you as you are releasing [the arrow]; homage to you when it has fallen. //3//
They have ploughed this barley with eight teams and six teams;
by that, drive away the affliction from your body toward the west.
Downward blows the wind; downward the sun shines; downward the cow yields her milk; let your ailment go downward. 2.
The waters indeed are healers; the waters are the drivers away of disease.
The waters are the healers of everything; may they provide healing for you. //3//
Become one with the speed of the wind, O steed, when being harnessed; go forth at Indra’s impulse, swift as thought.
Let the Maruts, possessors of all wealth, harness you; may Tvaṣṭṛ bestow swiftness in your feet.
O steed, that speed of yours which is placed in secret, whether it moves within the hawk or the wind,
or that which has been gathered together— with that, O powerful one, being strong with strength, win the race, you who are ever-victorious in the assembly.
O vigorous one, may your body, leading your body [to the goal], run for us toward what is desirable; may it bring protection to you.
Unharmed, the great god, for the sake of support, shall measure out his own light like the light in heaven. //3//
Yama, Death, Aghamāra, Nirṛtha, Babhru, Śarva the archer, Nīlaśikhaṇḍa—the divine folk who have risen with their army—may they spare our heroes. //1//

With mind, with oblations, with heat, and with ghee, I pay homage to Śarva, to the weapon, and to King Bhava—to these who are worthy of worship, I offer my salutation; let them lead the evil poisons away from us. //2//
Protect us from evil poisons and from slaughter, O All-Gods and Maruts, possessors of all wealth!
May we abide in the good favor of Agni, Soma, Varuṇa of purified skill, and of Vāta and Parjanya. 3.
We bend together your minds, your vows, and your intentions.
Those who are here with divergent vows, we cause them all to bow together before you.
I seize your minds with my mind; follow my thought with your thoughts.
I bring your hearts under my control; follow the path of my coming. 2.
Woven into me are Heaven and Earth; woven is the goddess Sarasvatī. Woven into me are Indra and Agni; may we succeed in this, O Sarasvatī. //3//
The Aśvattha tree, the abode of the gods, is in the third heaven from here; there the gods obtained Kuṣṭha, the manifestation of immortality. //1//
A golden ship with golden moorings moved through the sky;
there the gods gathered the *kuṣṭha* plant, the flower of immortality.
You are the embryo of the plants, and the embryo of the Himalayas;
you are the embryo of all that exists—make this one free from disease for me. 3.
The many herbs whose king is Soma, possessing a hundredfold insights,
impelled by Bṛhaspati— may they release us from distress.
May they release me from the curse, and also from that which pertains to Varuṇa; and from the fetter of Yama, and from every offense against the gods.
Whatever we have committed with the eye, with the mind, or with speech, whether waking or sleeping—may Soma purify those things for us by means of the *svadhā* offering. 3.
Victorious is the sacrifice, victorious is Agni, victorious is Soma, victorious is Indra.
May I overcome all hostile armies; thus may we worship with this oblation at the *agnihotra*. 1.
May there be the *svadhā* offering, O wise Mitra and Varuṇa; swell here with honey our sovereignty accompanied by progeny.
Drive far away Destruction to the distant realms, and release us from whatever sin has been committed. 2.

Rejoice after this hero; O friends, take hold together after the fierce Indra—the conqueror of villages, the winner of cattle, the thunderbolt-armed, who conquers the race and crushes with his might. //3//
May Indra conquer; may he not be conquered. May he rule as sovereign king among kings.
Worthy of praise, worthy of worship, worthy of being approached, and worthy of homage—may he be present here. 1.
O Indra, you are the sovereign king, the seeker of glory; you are the one who has become the overcomer of men.
You rule over these divine clans; may your dominion be long-lived and undecaying.

From the eastern quarter you are king, O Indra; from the northern quarter you are the slayer of Vṛtra, the destroyer of enemies. Wherever the rivers flow, that is your conquest; O Bull, you go as one to be invoked from the south. //3//
I call upon you, O Indra, from afar, even before distress; I invoke the fierce one, the perceiver, the one with many names, the uniquely born.
Whatever weapon of the army rises today, seeking to strike us down— there we place the two arms of Indra all around us.
We entrust ourselves on all sides to the arms of Indra, the protector; may he protect us.
O God Savitṛ, O King Soma, make me well-disposed for my well-being. //3//
The gods have given; Sūrya has given; Heaven has given; Earth has given.
The three Sarasvatīs, being of one mind, have given the poison-destroyer. 1.
O gods, Upajīkas, with that water which you poured upon the desert, by that which was impelled by the gods, do you now corrupt this poison.
You are the daughter of the Asuras; you are the sister of the gods. Born from heaven and earth, you have made the poison sapless. 3.
Be virile, breathe forth, grow strong, and expand.
May the penis grow according to its proper parts; with it, strike the woman. 1.
With that by which they urge the plough, with which they drive the sick man,
with that, O Brahmaṇaspati, stretch his member like a bow.
I stretch out your feet like a bowstring upon a bow;
stride forth always without weariness, like a rishi toward a red steed.
Just as this vehicle, O Aśvins, comes together and rolls along,
even so let your mind come together with me and roll along with me.
I press down your mind as a king’s horse [presses] its back;
like a blade of grass cut by the wind, let your mind coil itself around me.
Of the ointment, of the madugha, of the kuṣṭha, and of the nalada—
by the hands of Bhaga, I bring forth the Anurodhana plant with speed.
May Bṛhaspati make for you a bond; may Savitṛ make a bond.
May Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga, and the two Aśvins make a bond.
I bind together those who are highest, those who are lowest, and likewise those who are in the middle.
Indra has bound them all around with a cord; O Agni, do you bind them together.
Those who come here to battle, having made their banners in ranks—Indra has bound them with a cord; O Agni, you yourself bind them together. 3.
With seizing and with binding, we bind our enemies;
their out-breaths and their in-breaths, their life-forces—we have cut them off from life.
I have performed this taking up, sharpened by the Lord of Heat;
O Agni, drive away those enemies who are here against us.
May Indra and Agni, and King Soma, the two allies, strike them down;
may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, make us seize our possessions from our enemies. //3//
Just as the mind flies swiftly away by means of its mental intentions, even so,
O cough, fly forth along the swift course of the mind.
Just as a well-sharpened arrow flies swiftly away,
so do you, O cough, fly forth along the expanse of the earth.
Just as the rays of the sun fly away with speed,
even so, O cough, fly forth along the flow of the ocean.
On your path hither and on your path away, let flowering *dūrvā* grass grow;
or let a spring arise there, or a pond filled with lotuses.
This is the gathering place of the waters, the dwelling of the ocean;
our houses are in the middle of the lake—turn your faces away from them.
With the caul of the frost, O house, we enclose you on all sides;
for may our cold pools become [cool], and may Agni provide a remedy. 3.
O Viśvajit, entrust me to Trāyamāṇā!
O Trāyamāṇā, protect all our bipeds and whatever four-footed property belongs to us.
O Trāyamāṇa, deliver us to Viśvajit;
O Viśvajit, protect all our bipeds and whatever four-footed things are ours.
O Viśvajit, entrust me to Kalyāṇī;
O Kalyāṇī, protect all our bipeds and whatever four-footed property belongs to us.
O auspicious one, entrust us to the All-Knowing One.
O All-Knowing One, protect all our bipeds and all our quadrupeds that are our own. 4.
O Medhā, come first to us with cattle and horses;
you come with the rays of the sun; you are worthy of our sacrifice. 1.

I invoke for the protection of the gods that first intelligence, which is possessed of sacred knowledge, impelled by the Brahman, praised by the seers, and drunk in by those who lead the life of sacred study. //2//
The wisdom that the Ṛbhus know, the wisdom that the Asuras know, and the auspicious wisdom that the seers know—that we cause to enter within me. 3.
O Agni, with that wisdom which the seers, the makers of beings, and the wise know, make me wise today. 4.
Wisdom at evening, wisdom at dawn, and wisdom at midday—
through the rays of the sun and with our speech, we cause wisdom to enter us.
The long pepper is a medicine for what has been cast out, and it is a medicine for what has been pierced through;
the gods prepared it so that this [woman] would be fully capable of living.
The long pepper plants have conversed together from their birth onward:
"That man whom we shall reach while he is alive, he shall not come to harm. (AVŚ 6.109.2)
The Asuras dug you in; the gods dug you up again.
You are the remedy for one afflicted by wind, and the remedy for one who has been cast down.
For you are the ancient one, worthy of praise at the sacrifices; as the Hotṛ priest from of old, sit here, both new and ancient.
O Agni, nourish your own body and win for us prosperity through sacrifice. //1//
Born under the constellation Jyeṣṭhaghni, protect him from the loosening of Yama’s root-extraction;
may he pass beyond all misfortunes for a long life of a hundred autumns.
On a tiger-like day was the hero born; being born under a lunar mansion, he is one who brings forth brave sons.
May he, as he grows, not slay his father, nor harm his mother, his own progenitress.
O Agni, release this man of mine who is bound and tightly restrained, yet prattles on.
From this, he shall offer you a portion when he is no longer insane.
May Agni pacify your mind if it has been stirred up; being wise, I prepare the remedy so that you shall not be insane. 2.
For one who has been driven mad by the offense against the gods, or who is insane from a *rakṣas*, I, being wise, prepare the remedy so that he shall no longer be insane. 3.
May the Apsarases give you back, may Indra give you back, may Bhaga give you back;
may all the gods give you back, so that you shall no longer be insane. 4.
Let him not slay the eldest among these; O Agni, protect him from being uprooted by the root.
Knowing the way, loosen the snares of Grāhi; may all the gods acknowledge you. //1//
Unloose their bonds, O Agni; those three by which they were bound have been released by the three. Knowing well, untie the snares of Grāhi; release both father and son, and all the mother.

With those snares by which the outcaste is bound, pinned limb to limb, and cast up—let them be loosened from you, for they are meant to be released; O Pūṣan, wipe away the misfortunes of the slayer of the embryo. 3.
The gods wiped away this sin upon Trita; Trita wiped it away among human beings.
Therefore, if the Grāhi has seized you, may the gods destroy her for you by means of the sacred word (*brahman*). 1.
Enter the rays of light and the smokes, O evil one; go forth to the clouds or the mists.
Vanish along with the froth of the rivers! O Pūṣan, wipe away the misfortunes of the slayer of the embryo.
The twelve-fold [sin] deposited by Trita, the human transgressions wiped away—therefore, if the *grāhi* has seized you, may the gods destroy it for you by means of the sacred word (*brahman*). 3.
O gods, whatever offense against the gods we have committed,
O Ādityas, release us from that by means of the eternal Law.
O Ādityas, worthy of worship, by means of the Truth through Truth, release us here, since we, though striving,
have not succeeded in performing the sacrifice, O you who carry the sacrifice.
O all you gods, though we were sacrificing with fat and offering clarified butter with the ladle, we were unable to succeed, even as we strove and desired it. 3.
Whatever sins we have committed, whether knowing or unknowing—O All-Gods, acting in harmony, release us from that! 1.
Whether waking or whether sleeping, whatever sin I have committed—
may the past and the future release me from that, as if from a wooden post.
Like one released from a wooden stock, like one who has bathed and is cleansed of sweat and dirt,
like clarified butter purified by a strainer— may all purify me from mental taint.

Whatever path the cultivators, finding food but lacking knowledge, first made for themselves by digging it out—that I offer into King Vaivasvata; thus may our food be worthy of sacrifice and full of sweetness.
May Vaivasvata provide his portion; may the sharer of honey mingle us with honey.
Whatever offense sent from our mother has come upon us, or whatever wrong our father has committed that has caused him to shrink away—[may he forgive it].
Whether this mental transgression has come upon us from our mother, or from our father, or from our brother, or from our son—may the wrath of all those ancestors who accompany us be auspicious. 3.
Whatever I owe as a borrowed debt, unpaid, which I carry as an offering to Yama—O Agni, through this [offering] I become free from that debt; you know how to loosen all the bonds. //1//
Remaining right here, we give this back; while living, we deliver it to those who live.
Whatever grain I have eaten after borrowing it, O Agni, through this I become free from that debt.
Free from debt in this world, free from debt in the next, may we be free from debt in the third world;
free from debt on all paths—those leading to the gods and those leading to the fathers—may we dwell. 3.
Whatever sins we have committed with our two hands, seeking to win the throw of the dice—O Ugrapasyā and Ugrajit, may those two Apsarases today grant us that as a debt. 1.
O Ugrampaśyā, sustainer of the realm, take away our sins; that which was lost at dice, that which was given away—that is not [to be counted against us].
Like one seeking to collect a debt, the cord of Yama has been extended over us in the world of Yama. 2.

O gods, for whomsoever I approach with a debt, or to whose wife I go, or whom I approach as a suppliant—let them utter speech that is not superior to mine; let the two Apsarases, the wives of the gods, take heed. 3.
Whatever debt I incur while not gambling, or whatever I promise to give but fail to give, O Agni—may Vaiśvānara, our most excellent protector, lead us up to the world of the righteous. 1.
I announce to Vaiśvānara if there is a debt or a pledge among the gods;
he knows how to loosen all these bonds, and then may we be united with what is cooked. 2.
May Vaiśvānara, the purifier, cleanse me when I run toward a compact or a hope;
whatever sin I have committed there through ignorance, while praying with my mind, that I cast away. 3.

If we have harmed the intermediate space, the earth, or the sky, or if we have injured our mother or our father—may this Gārhapatya Agni lead us up from that [sin] to the world of the well-done. //1//
Earth is our mother, Aditi our place of birth; the atmosphere is our brother, protecting us from imprecation.
May the sky, our father, be auspicious toward us on account of our paternal kin; having approached my kinsman, may I not fall away from the world.
Where those of good heart and virtuous deeds rejoice, having cast off disease from their own bodies—
there in heaven, may we, with our limbs unimpaired and unbent, behold our parents and our sons.
O Horn, untie the snares from us—those that are highest or lowest, those belonging to Varuṇa.
Drive away from us bad dreams and misfortune; then may we go to the world of the righteous. 1.

Whatever you are bound with wood, and whatever with rope, whatever you are bound with the earth, and whatever with speech—from that [bondage], may this Gārhapatya fire lead us up to the world of the well-done. //2//
The two blessed stars named Vicṛtau have risen;
may they extend this bond of immortality. Let the release of the bound go forth.
Open wide, make room; release those who are bound.
Like an embryo falling from the womb, dwell along all the paths.
Knowing this, O Viśvakarman, first-born of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*), I bestow this portion upon you.
May we, having given it by our hands, cross over along the unbroken thread beyond old age. //1//
Some cross along the stretched-out thread, those for whom ancestral wealth has been given according to the traditional way.
Some, giving and bestowing it upon those who have no kin, if they train themselves to give, that indeed is heaven.
Take hold of each other; take hold together. Those who have faith resort to this world.
Whatever cooked food has been served for you in the fire, O husband and wife, come together for its protection. 3.
I ascend with my mind to the great sacrifice that goes forth, sharing the same womb through ascetic heat.
O Agni, invited beyond old age, may we rejoice in communal feasting in the third firmament.
Pure, cleansed, and worthy of sacrifice are these women; I set them down separately in the hands of the Brahmins.
With whatever desire I sprinkle you here, may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, grant that to me.
O you who share this common dwelling place, I entrust this treasure to you, which Jātavedas shall bring hither.
The sacrificer will follow after it in well-being; recognize him in the highest heaven. //1//
O gods who dwell together in the highest heaven, recognize him; know his place here.
The sacrificer shall follow after you with well-being; make manifest for him the merit of his sacrifices and pious works.
The gods are the fathers, the fathers are the gods;
whoever I am, that is who I am. //3//
I cook; I give; I sacrifice; I have given. Do not let me be cooked [by those things]. //4//
O King, take your stand upon the firmament; may this [offering] likewise find its place there.
Know of our meritorious deeds, O King; as a god, be well-disposed toward us.
From the great heaven, from the mid-air, a drop of water has fallen upon me with its essence;
O Agni, may I be united with sensory power, with milk, with the meters, with sacrifices, and with the merit of those who do good. 1.
If a fruit has fallen from a tree, or if it has come from the intermediate space, that indeed is the wind itself.
Wherever it has touched the body or the garment, may the waters drive away Destruction far away.
The fragrant ointment, that prosperity, gold, and luster—this indeed is most pure.
All purifiers are spread out over us; may Destruction and Malignity not cross over me. 3.
O Lord of the Forest, may you have strong limbs; be our friend, a furtherer, and a hero.
You are bound with cow-hides—be firm! May your rider conquer all that is to be won. 1.
The power drawn forth from heaven and earth, the force brought together from the lords of the forest;
the vigor of the waters, encompassed by the rays of light—worship with an oblation the chariot that is Indra’s thunderbolt.
The vigor of Indra, the vanguard of the Maruts, the offspring of Mitra, the navel of Varuṇa—O divine chariot, enjoying this our offering of oblations, accept these sacrificial gifts! 3.
Make the earth and the sky resound; let the world scattered in many places take heed of you. O drum, in harmony with Indra and the gods, drive the enemies far, even further away. //1//
Thunder forth strength; bestow vigor upon us; roar aloud, driving away misfortunes.
O drum, ward off calamity from here. You are the fist of Indra; be firm. 2.
Victory to the front! May they conquer in the terrifying battle; let the bannered drum resound loudly.
Let our horse-winged heroes fly together; O Indra, may our chariot-warriors be victorious. 3.
O Lord of the Forest, O Herb, leave nothing remaining of the abscess, the wasting disease, the blood, or the spreading sore— not even a trace of flesh.
Those two swellings of yours that remain in your armpit, the testicles that have settled there—I know the remedy for them: the *cīpudru* tree is the visible cure.

The swelling that is in the limbs, that which is in the ears, and that which is in the eyes— we pull out the swelling, the abscess, and the disease of the heart. We drive away that unknown consumption; we cast it downward. 3.
When the stars made Śakadhūma their king, they bestowed upon him an auspicious day, saying, "May he establish this kingdom. //1//
May there be a blessed day for us at midday; may there be a blessed day for us in the evening.
May there be a blessed day for us at dawn among the days; may the night be a blessed day for us.
From day and night, from the constellations, and from the sun and moon—O King Śakadhūma, grant us an auspicious day. 3.
To you who have brought us auspicious days, both by night and by day—to you, O King of the Constellations, Śakadhūma, we offer perpetual homage. //4//
Together with the Bhaga of the *śāṃśapa* tree, with Indra as my ally, I make myself fortunate; let the enemies flee away. //1//
By that fortune and splendor with which you overcame the trees, by that make me fortunate; let the enemies flee away. //2//
He who is blind, he who is one who returns again—Bhaga is placed within the trees. Through him, make me fortunate; let the enemies flee away.
This is the love-spell of the Apsarases, the Rathajitas and the Rāthajiteyīs. O gods, send forth Love; let him burn with longing for me! 1.
"May he remember me," "may my beloved remember me"—O gods, send forth the god of love; may he burn with longing for me.
Just as he remembers me, so may I never remember him. O gods, send forth the god of love; let him grieve for me. 3.
O Maruts, exhilarate me; O Atmosphere, exhilarate me!
O Agni, do you exhilarate me; may that one burn after me. 4.
I drive away your longing from your head, from your feet, and from your very heart.
O gods, send forth the memory; let that one grieve for me. 1.
O Anumati, agree to this; O Ākūti, accept this homage.
O gods, send forth the god of love; let that one burn with longing for me.
Whether you run three *yojanas* or five *yojanas*, as far as the domain of the Aśvins, from there you shall return again and be the father of our sons. 3.
That memory which the gods poured into the waters, burning with intense heat, together with their meditation— that I kindle for you by the law of Varuṇa.
That memory which all the gods poured into the waters, burning with intense heat along with their resolve— that I heat for you by the law of Varuṇa.
That passion which Indrāṇī poured into the waters, burning together with her resolve—that I heat for you by the law of Varuṇa. //3//
That memory which Indra and Agni poured into the waters, burning with intense heat along with their resolve— that I inflame for you by the law of Varuṇa.
That memory which Mitra and Varuṇa poured into the waters, burning with intense heat, together with their resolve— that I kindle for you by the law of Varuṇa.
The god who bound this girdle for me, who fastened it and who joined us together—may that god by whose command we move seek the further shore and may he release us. //1//
You are invoked and offered oblations; you are the weapon of the seers.
Consuming the first portion of the vow, O girdle, be a slayer of my enemies.
I am a student of sacred knowledge belonging to Death, when I go forth to demand a man from the living for Yama;
him I bind with the sacred word, with austerity, with toil, and with this girdle. //3//
The daughter of Faith, born from fervor, has become the sister of the seers who create all beings.
O girdle, bestow upon us intelligence and inspired wisdom; furthermore, grant us fervor and sensory power.
O girdle, whom the ancient seers, the makers of beings, have bound around—do thou embrace me for the sake of long life. 5.
May this vajra satisfy [him]; may it strike down the kingdom and the life of this one who has violated the cosmic order (*ṛta*).
May it shatter his neck-bones and crush his nape, just as the Lord of Power (*śacīpati*) [shattered] Vṛtra. //1//
Lower and lower than the higher ones, hidden within the earth, do not creep forth;
struck down by the thunderbolt, let him lie prostrate.
Seek out him who conquers; strike down him who conquers.
O Vajra, as he conquers, cause his hairline to fall following its natural direction.
Whatever I eat, I turn into strength; thus I take up the thunderbolt, lopping off the shoulders of that man, just as the Lord of Might did to Vṛtra.
What I drink, I drink up; like the ocean, I drink it all up. Having drunk up the vital breaths of that person, we drink him up completely. //2//
What I swallow, I swallow up completely, like the ocean, a great swallower; having swallowed up the breaths of that person, we swallow that one up completely. 3.
O herb, you are divine, born upon the divine earth. As such, O Nitatnī, we dig you up for the sake of strengthening the hair. 1.
Strengthen the ancient ones, give birth to those yet unborn, and make those already born more excellent.
That hair of yours which falls out, and that which is cut away with its root—this I sprinkle upon it for you with this all-healing plant. 3.
That which Jamadagni dug up for his daughter, the hair-increasing [plant]—that Vītahavya brought from the houses of Asita. //1//
They were to be measured with a rein, to be inferred by a fathom;
let your black hairs grow from your head like reeds.
Firm the root, hold fast the tip, and restrain the middle, O herb!
Let your black hairs grow all around your head like reeds.
O herb, you are renowned as the most excellent among plants.
Today, make this man of mine eunuch and shorn of his topknot. 1.
Make him impotent, yet provide him with a head-ornament; furthermore, make him wear a turban.
Then may Indra, with his two pressing-stones, split both of his testicles.
O eunuch, I have made you a eunuch; O impotent one, I have made you impotent; O sapless one, I have made you sapless.
We place a turban upon his head and a water-pot upon it.
Those two testicles of yours, fashioned by the gods, upon which virility rests—
those I split apart for you with a peg, from the scrotum of so-and-so.
Just as women split a reed with a stone for the sake of a mattress, so do I split your penis upon his testicles. 5.
You have grown as a climbing vine, O Nyastikā, making me fortunate;
you have a hundred spreading shoots and thirty-three descending roots.
With that thousand-leaved plant, I dry up your heart.
May your heart wither within me, and may your mouth wither as well;
then, wither away through desire for me, and wander about with a parched mouth.
O uniter, rich in lilies, brown and beautiful one, drive them together!
Drive her and me together; make our hearts one. //3//
Just as the mouth of one who has drunk water dries up, even so, O Māra, dry up through desire for me, and then wander about with a parched mouth. 4.
Just as a mongoose, having cut [an adder], joins it together again, so, O powerful one, join together what has been severed of desire. 5.
Those two tigers who have descended and desire to devour their father and mother—O Brahmanaspati, O Jātavedas, make them both harmless when they have been appeased. //1//
Eat the rice, eat the barley, and likewise the bean and the sesame.
This portion has been set aside for you both for the bestowal of treasure; O two teeth, do not harm the father and the mother.
Invoked are the two companions, the pleasant teeth, most auspicious.
O teeth, let the terrible power of your bodies go elsewhere; do not harm the father and the mother. //3//
May Vāyu gather them together; may Tvaṣṭṛ sustain them for prosperity.
May Indra speak in their favor; may Rudra provide for their abundance.
With a red axe, create a pair upon the two ears;
let the Aśvins fashion a mark there, and may that be multiplied through progeny.
Just as the gods and asuras did, and just as men have done, so likewise,
O Aśvins, create for us a mark for the sake of a thousandfold prosperity.
Rise up, O barley, become abundant through your own greatness;
crush all vessels, lest the divine thunderbolt strike you down. 1.
O God, where we call upon you, listen to us as you do to the barley;
therefore, rise up like the sky, and be inexhaustible like the ocean.
(6.142.3a) May your attendants be imperishable; may the heaps be imperishable.
(6.142.3c) May those who bestow be imperishable; may those who eat be imperishable. //3//
Those who by intuition brought forth the first word of speech, or those who with their mind spoke the *ṛta*s;
increasing through the third sacred formulation (*brahman*), they perceived the name of the Cow through the fourth. //1//
He knows his father, he knows his mother; he becomes a son, he becomes one who bestows wealth again.
He spread out the sky, the mid-air, and the heavens; he became this entire universe; he brought it all hither. 2.

Atharvan, the father, kinsman of the gods, the embryo of the mother, the life-breath of the father, the youth—he who has perceived this sacrifice with his mind: proclaim him for us here; speak of him here. 1.
By this manifestation, engendering mighty deeds, he is indeed the glowing one, the wide path for the seeker.
He has risen up toward the support, the summit of the honey; by his own body, he has extended his form. 1.
With one and with ten, O well-sacrificed one, with two and with twenty for the sake of the sacrifice;
with three and with thirty you carry us—O Vāyu, unyoke them here.
With sacrifice the gods sacrificed to the sacrifice; those were the first ordinances.
Those great ones attained the firmament where the ancient Sādhyas, the gods, abide. //1//
The sacrifice came into being; it has come into existence; it was born, and it has grown great again.
It became the sovereign lord of the gods; may it bestow wealth upon us. //2//
When the gods, with oblations, worshipped the immortal gods with a mortal mind, may we rejoice there in the highest heaven; may we behold that at the rising of the sun.
When the gods performed the sacrifice with man as the oblation, is there indeed anything more powerful than that, by which they sacrificed with the *vihavya* hymn? 4.
The gods were bewildered; they sacrificed even with a dog, and in many ways they sacrificed with the limbs of a cow.
He who has perceived this sacrifice with his mind—proclaim him for us here, speak of him here! 5.5
Aditi is heaven, Aditi is the mid-region; Aditi is the mother, she is the father, she is the son.
All the gods are Aditi, the five peoples are Aditi; Aditi is what has been born, Aditi is what is yet to be born. //1//

We invoke for our protection the great Mother of those who follow holy vows, the consort of *Ṛta*, Aditi— mighty in dominion, undecaying, far-reaching, providing excellent shelter, and a perfect guide.
May we ascend for our well-being the divine ship, well-oared and leakless, which has the good savior Earth and the faultless Heaven, the well-protecting Aditi, and the excellent guide. //1//
In the impulse of strength, we now celebrate with our speech the great mother named Aditi;
she whose lap is the wide mid-air—may she grant us a triple-layered protection. //2//
I have performed worship for the sons of Diti and for Aditi; I have honored the great, non-mocking gods.
For their domain is deep within the ocean; there is no one whatsoever beyond them who can surpass them with reverence. 1.
From good, go forth to what is better; let Bṛhaspati be your leader.
Then, in this choice place upon the earth, make this man free from enemies and possessed of all heroes. //1//
On the far path of paths Pūṣan was born; on the far path of heaven, on the far path of earth. To both most beloved meeting places he goes, hither and thither, knowing all.
May Pūṣan know all these regions; may he lead us by the path most free from fear.
Bestowing well-being, glowing, possessing all heroes, may he go before us, never heedless, knowing the way.
O Pūṣan, under your protection may we never come to harm;
we here are your praisers. 3.
May Pūṣan stretch forth his right hand from beyond; may he bring back to us what we have lost, and may we be reunited with that which is lost. 4.

That breast of yours which is inexhaustible, which brings delight, which seeks our favor, which is easy to invoke, and which bestows good gifts—that by which you nourish all desirable things, O Sarasvatī—bring that here for us to suck. 1.
(7.11.1) Your broad thunder, that lofty divine banner which encompasses all this—O God, do not slay our grain with lightning, nor slay it with the rays of the sun. //1//
May the Assembly and the Council protect me, the two daughters of Prajāpati, acting in harmony.
O Fathers, may he with whom I meet grant me his favor; may I speak pleasantly among those who have gathered.
We know your name, O assembly; your name is "Unharmed. May those who sit in your assembly be of one voice with me.
From these who are seated together, I take away their luster and their discernment;
O Indra, make me the fortunate one among this entire assembly. 3.
Whatever mind of yours has gone away, whether it be bound here or there, we cause that to turn back toward you; may your mind delight in me. //4//
Just as the rising sun takes away the splendor of the stars,
so do I take away the luster of both women and men who are my enemies.
As many of my rivals as you behold me approaching,
from them I take away the splendor, just as the rising sun takes the luster from those who sleep among their enemies.
I praise that god Savitṛ, who is within the two bowls, whose wisdom is that of a seer, the one whose impulse is true, the bestower of jewels, the beloved thought. 1.
He whose inspired thought, a radiant light, shone upward at his impulse— he of the golden hands, the skillful one, measured out the sun from his creative power.
For you, O God, have impelled the first father; grant him height, grant him breadth.
And so, O Savitṛ, impel for us day by day many desirable things and cattle. //3//
The domestic god Savitṛ, the most excellent, bestows treasure and long lives upon the fathers.
May he drink the Soma; may he rejoice in it at our sacrifice. Even the wanderer moves about according to his law.
O Savitṛ, I choose that most wondrous favor of yours, which is true in its impulse and possesses all boons—
the swelling, thousand-streamed [milk] which Kaṇva milked for Bhaga, like a mighty bull.
O Bṛhaspati, O Savitṛ, cause him to grow; illumine him for great good fortune. Sharpen him further, even though he is already sharpened; let all the gods rejoice after him. //1//
May Dhātṛ, the lord and master of the moving world, bestow wealth upon us;
may he grant it to us with abundance. //1//
May Dhātṛ grant to the donor an eastern, undecaying life;
may we obtain the benevolence of the god who bestows all wealth.
May Dhātṛ bestow all desirable things within the home upon the donor who desires offspring.
May all the gods, Aditi, and the Viśve Devas, acting in harmony, grant immortality to him. 3.
May Dhātṛ, Rāti, and Savitṛ enjoy this; may Prajāpati, the lord of treasures, and Agni [enjoy it]. May Tvaṣṭṛ and Viṣṇu, bestowing abundance upon our progeny, grant wealth to the sacrificer. //4//
Heave yourself up, O Earth; burst open this celestial cloud.
O Dhātṛ, as the lord, unbind for us the leather bag of celestial water.
Neither heat has scorched him nor has cold destroyed him; may the earth, the giver of life-sustaining gifts, yield to him.
Even the waters pour forth ghee for him; wherever Soma is, there is always prosperity.
Prajāpati generates these creatures; may Dhātṛ, being well-disposed, establish them. Being of one mind, of one thought, and of one womb, may the Lord of Prosperity bestow prosperity upon me. 1.
May Anumati favor our sacrifice today among the gods;
and may Agni, the bearer of oblations, be present for me, the donor. (AVŚ 7.20.1)
After this, O Anumati, you shall consider us; grant us well-being.
Accept the offered oblation, O Goddess, and bestow progeny upon us.
May he, being well-disposed, grant us wealth accompanied by progeny that shall never fail. May we not come under his wrath; may we abide in his favor and his gracious goodwill. 3.

O well-guided Anumati, whatever name of yours is easy to invoke, which is approved and bountiful—by that, O possessor of all boons, fulfill our sacrifice; O fortunate one, bestow upon us wealth accompanied by heroic sons.
Anumati has come to this sacrifice, well-born for the sake of good fields and for the sake of good heroes;
for her providence has been auspicious—may she, the guardian of the gods, protect this sacrifice. 5.
Anumati has become all this: whatever stands, whatever moves, and whatever of the universe stirs.
O Goddess Anumati, may we abide in your favor; for you, Anumati, will indeed be gracious toward us.
Gather together, all of you, with your speech toward the Lord of Heaven—the one pervasive guest of men.
May he, the ancient one, seek intimacy with the new; may his many paths turn toward him, the One alone. 1.
May this thought of the seers, a light that ordains the world, come to us for a thousandfold vision. //1//
The ruddy one has brought together the converging dawns;
they are stainless, of one mind, most full of spirit in their own dwelling, intent upon the cow.
Bad dreams, a miserable life, the demon, the monster, and the mischievous spirits—all those with evil names and evil voices, we cause them to perish from us. //1//
That which Indra did not dig, that which Agni, the All-gods, and the Maruts with their beautiful hymns [did not dig]—may Savitṛ, whose laws are true, Prajāpati, and Anumati bestow that upon us. //1//
By whose power the regions were propped up, who by their heroic deeds are most manly and most mighty;
they two who rule as irresistible through their strengths—to Viṣṇu and Varuṇa has my first invocation gone.
In whose direction this shines forth and breathes out, and whom he beholds with his powers;
before the law of the god by his might, the first invocation has gone to Viṣṇu and Varuṇa. //2//
Now I shall proclaim the heroic deeds of Viṣṇu, who measured out the earthly realms;
he who, striding thrice with wide-gaited might, propped up the highest dwelling place.
For that Viṣṇu his heroic deeds are praised: like a terrifying beast, roaming and dwelling in the mountains, may he come hither from the furthest distance.
In whose three wide strides all beings dwell;
O Viṣṇu, stride out widely, make wide room for our dwelling!
Drink the clarified butter, O you whose source is clarified butter; further and further prolong the life of the lord of the sacrifice. 3.
Vishnu strode across this [universe]; he established it in three places; his footstep was gathered in the dust.
Viṣṇu, the guardian, the undeceivable, strode forth three steps, maintaining from here the laws of righteousness. //5//
Behold the deeds of Viṣṇu, through which he has made his vows manifest;
he is the close ally and friend of Indra.
The wise ever behold that highest step of Viṣṇu,
like an eye fixed in the sky.
O Viṣṇu, from heaven and from earth, O Viṣṇu, from the great and wide mid-air—fill your hands with many riches; bestow them from the right and from the left.
May Iḍā herself clothe us with her sacred law, she in whose place those seeking the gods purify themselves;
she whose feet are dripping with ghee, the powerful one whose back is Soma, belonging to all the gods, has approached the sacrifice. 1.
The Veda is well-being, the mallet is well-being; the axe, the altar, and the axe bring us well-being.
May those gods—performers of oblations, worthy of sacrifice, and lovers of sacrifice—enjoy this sacrifice. //1//
O Agni and Viṣṇu, great is that majesty of yours; you guard the secret name of the hidden ghee.
Bestowing the seven treasures in every house, may your tongue move toward the ghee.
O Agni and Viṣṇu, your great and beloved domain is vast; you enjoy the secret portions of the clarified butter with pleasure.
Increasing through excellent praise in every house, may your tongue rise up toward the clarified butter.
May Heaven and Earth make me well-anointed; may this Mitra make me well-anointed. May Brahmaṇaspati make me well-anointed; may Savitṛ make me well-anointed. //1//
O Indra, with your many and most excellent aids today, O Maghavan, O Hero, quicken us!
May he who hates us fall low; and may our life-breath abandon him whom we hate. //1//
To the beloved, the one worthy of praise, the youthful, who increases the oblations—to him we have come, bearing homage. May he grant me long life. (AVŚ 7.32.1)
May the Maruts sprinkle me; may Pūṣan and Bṛhaspati sprinkle me;
may this Agni sprinkle me with offspring and with wealth, and grant me long life. //1//
O Agni, drive away my rivals who have already been born; O Jātavedas, push back those yet unborn.
Place beneath our feet those who attack us; may we, being sinless, belong to Aditi. //1//
Overpower with might those rivals who breathe; O Jātavedas, drive away those yet unborn.
Prosper this kingdom for its good fortune; let all the gods rejoice after him. //1//
These hundred veins of yours, and the thousand arteries—
of all of them, I have sealed the openings with a stone.
I place that which is beyond your womb below you; let neither offspring nor a child be born from you.
I make you barren and childless; I make a stone your covering. //3//
Our two eyes are like honey; our countenance is anointing.
Place me within your heart; let our minds be together. 1.
I clothe you with my garment, born of thought,
so that he may be mine alone, and not even mention the names of other women.
I dig this healing medicine: the sight of me, which causes one who is weeping to rejoice;
it is the turning back of one who is departing and the welcoming of one who is approaching.
With that by which you overturned the Asura Indra from among the gods,
with that do I now turn you down, so that I may be very dear to you.
You face toward Soma, and you face toward the Sun;
you face toward all the gods—to you we speak these words. 3.
I speak, not you; speak in the assembly, not you!
You belong to me alone; do not mention the names of other women at all. 4.
Whether you are beyond the people, or whether you are across the rivers—
this herb has indeed brought you here for me, like one who has bound you.

The divine, well-winged, milk-yielding, vast one, the embryo of the waters, the bull of the plants—who satisfies us from every side with rain—may he establish us, rich in wealth, in our cow-pen. //1//
Whose ordinance all cattle follow, in whose ordinance the waters abide, and in whose ordinance the Lord of Prosperity is established—to that Sarasvant we call for protection. //1//

To Sarasvant, who comes toward the donor as one who bestows gifts, the lord of prosperity, the abode of wealth—to him, the increase of riches, the seeker of glory, we, clothed in splendor, come to this dwelling place of treasures. 2.

He has pierced through the deserts and through the waters; the falcon, the beholder of men, who sees his dwelling place, crossing all the lower regions, may he come hither as a friend with Indra, bringing auspiciousness. //1//

The falcon, the celestial one with the gaze of a man, the well-winged, thousand-footed, hundred-sourced, bestower of vigor—may he grant us the wealth that has been carried away; may it belong to our ancestors as a *svadhā*-offering.
O Soma and Rudra, tear asunder in all directions the disease that has entered our home.
Drive far away Destruction; release us from whatever sin we have committed. 1.
O Soma and Rudra, place all these remedies within our bodies.
Untie and release from us whatever sin has been committed that remains bound within our bodies. 2.
Some of them are auspicious for you, some are inauspicious; you bear them all with a well-disposed mind.
Three voices are deposited within him; of these, one has flown away following the sound.
Both of you have conquered; you are not defeated, nor has either of these two been defeated. O Indra and Viṣṇu, when you two contended, you divided the thousandfold [booty] into three parts.
Brought hither from the man who belongs to all people, from the river;
I consider you, brought from afar, the remedy for the name of envy.
Like the fire of a forest burning separately as it consumes, quench this jealousy of his like a blazing fire. 1.
O Sinīvālī of the broad tresses, you who are the sister of the gods—be pleased with the oblation offered; O goddess, grant us progeny. //1//
She who has beautiful arms, beautiful fingers, who is well-nourished and prolific—
offer the oblation to that Sinīvālī, the mistress of the people.
O Goddess who art the mistress of the people, facing Indra, approaching with a thousand locks—O wife of Viṣṇu, for you the oblations are offered; O Goddess, impel your husband toward prosperity. 3.

I repeatedly invoke at this sacrifice Kuhū, the goddess, the well-doer, whose works are known; she who is easy to call upon. May she bestow upon us wealth containing all boons; may she grant a praiseworthy hero-son who bestows a hundredfold.
May Kuhū, the goddess and consort of the immortals, accept our oblation of this offering;
may she, longing for us, hear our sacrifice today and, being wise, bestow upon us the increase of wealth. //2//
I invoke Rākā, who is easily summoned, with a beautiful hymn; may the fortunate one hear us and take notice of us herself.
May she sew [the womb] with a needle that does not break, and may she grant a heroic son, a giver of a hundred, worthy of praise.
O Rākā, those benevolent thoughts of yours which are well-formed, by which you grant riches to the donor—
with those, come to us today with a gracious mind, O fortunate one, bestowing thousandfold prosperity.
May the longing wives of the gods protect us; may they aid us in our striving for offspring and in the winning of booty.
Those who belong to the earth and those who abide in the law of the waters—may those goddesses, who are easy to invoke, grant us protection. 1.
And may the divine ladies, the wives of the gods—Indrāṇī, Agnāyī, Aśvinī, and Rāṭ—come hither;
may Rodasī and Varuṇānī hear us; may the goddesses come, they who are the season of women.
Just as the thunderbolt strikes down a tree at all times without resistance, even so may I today bind the gamblers with dice without resistance. //1//
Of the swift and the unswift, of the tribes that do not yield—let Bhaga come from every side; let what is placed within my hand be gathered together. 2.

I praise Agni, the possessor of good wealth, with prostrations; may he, being well-disposed here, discern our offering. Like chariots seeking booty, I bring forth [the hymn]; may I successfully accomplish the praise-song of the Maruts in a clockwise direction.
May we, with you as our ally, conquer the foe; protect our share in every battle.
O Indra, make for us a wide and easy path; O Maghavan, shatter the manly strength of our enemies.
I have conquered you, who were carved out; I have conquered you, who were hemmed in.
Just as a wolf might seize a sheep, so do I seize what you have done. //5//
Moreover, he who plays beyond the stake wins; like a gambler, he gathers his winnings at the right time.
He who desires the gods does not withhold wealth; the Lord of the Self (Svadhā) pours forth riches upon him.
O Much-invoked One, may we cross over this evil-minded poverty with cattle, or hunger with barley, O All-pervading One;
may we, unhurt, be the first among kings to win riches through our communities.
Victory is placed in my right hand, and triumph is set in my left. May I be a winner of cattle, a winner of horses, a winner of wealth, and a winner of gold.
O dice, give me a fruitful day, like a cow that yields milk;
bind me with a stream of winnings, as one fastens a bowstring upon the bow.
May Bṛhaspati protect us from behind, and from above, and from below against the evildoer;
may Indra from the front and from the middle, as a friend to his friends, grant us wide space. //1//
May there be recognition for us with our own kin, and recognition with strangers.
O Aśvins, bestow upon us here that recognition.
Let us be of one mind and of one intent; let us not be parted by the divine mind.
Let no shouts arise when the vast battle is joined; let the arrow fly when the day of Indra arrives.
Since you, O Bṛhaspati, have released me from the curse of Yama regarding my existence in the world beyond,
may the Aśvins and the two physicians of the gods, O Agni, drive away death from us by their powers.
Come together; do not abandon the body. Let out-breath and in-breath remain here as your companions.
Live for a hundred autumns, growing strong; Agni is your protector and Vasiṣṭha is your supreme lord.
The life-force of yours that has been cast away in the distance—let the out-breath and the in-breath come back again.
Agni has brought that from the lap of Nirṛti; I cause that to enter back into your own self. 3.
Let not this breath depart from me, nor let the out-breath leave me and go away.
I entrust him to the Seven Seers; may they carry him safely to old age.
Enter, O out-breath and in-breath, like two oxen into their pen;
may this unharmed treasure of old age increase here.
We breathe forth your breath; I drive away your consumption.
May this Agni, the most excellent, bestow life upon us from every side. //6//
Climbing up from the darkness to the highest firmament, we have gone to Sūrya, the god among gods, the supreme light. 7.
We worship the *ṛc* and the *sāman*, by means of which they perform their rites;
these two reign in the assembly and present the sacrifice to the gods. //1//
The *ṛc*, the *sāman*, the oblation, vigor, the *yajus*, and strength—whatever I have asked about these, may this Veda, when questioned, not harm me, O Lord of Might! (AVŚ 7.54.2)
Those paths of yours that go down from heaven, by which you have set the universe in motion—
by those, O Vasu, bestow favor upon us.
The poison that was gathered from the black, cross-striped viper— that poison of the *kaṅka* joint this plant has destroyed.
This plant is born of honey; it is honey-scented, honey-sweet, and honey itself.
It is the remedy for the one who has stumbled, and moreover, it is the destroyer of mosquitoes.
From where it was bitten, from where it was sucked, from there we call it away for you—
the sapless poison of the tiny, stinging gnat.
This one who is crooked, with missing joints and deformed limbs—you make his faces crooked and twisted;
O Brahmaṇaspati, you bend them together like a reed. //4//
Of the sapless Śarkoṭa, who creeps along facing downward—his poison indeed I have sought out, and furthermore, I have crushed him. 5.
There is no strength in your arms, nor in your head, nor in your middle; then why do you carry this tiny, wretched thing on your tail?
The ants eat you; the peahens tear you apart. All of you, say this clearly: the poison of the *śārkoṭa* is sapless.
You who strike with both [your mouth] and your tail—with your mouth there is no poison; how much less could it be in your tail?
Whatever has been disturbed in my speech as I speak with hope, whatever in my begging as I move among the people,
whatever fracture there is in my own body— may Sarasvatī fill that up with clarified butter.
Seven flow for the child accompanied by the Maruts; the sons have brought the cosmic orders back to the father.
Both indeed belong to him, both are his; both strive for him, both prosper for him.

O Indra and Varuṇa, drinkers of the pressed juice, who uphold the sacred law, drink this pressed Soma, the exhilarating draught. May your chariot come toward the sacrifice for the feast of the gods, arriving at its own place to drink.

O Indra and Varuṇa, you two bulls, drink of this most honeyed, potent Soma. This juice has been poured out for you; having sat down upon this sacred grass (*barhis*), may you both rejoice in it. //2//
He who would curse us when we do not curse, or he who would curse us when we do curse—like a tree struck by lightning, let him wither away from the root. //1//
Bearing strength, a winner of wealth, and wise, with a non-terrible, friendly eye, I come to the house with a benevolent mind, offering praise: "Dwell here; do not be afraid of me. (AVŚ 7.60.1)
These houses are sources of delight, rich in vigor and rich in milk; standing full with all that is desirable, may they know us as we approach.
Those from whom one departs when traveling abroad, and in whom there is much goodwill—those houses we call upon; may they recognize us as we approach.
Summoned are the friends who possess abundant wealth and delight in sweet things;
may you be free from hunger and thirst. O houses, do not be afraid of us! 4.
Invoked here are the cows; invoked are the goats and sheep. And so, the sweet essence of food is invoked within these houses.
Rich in pleasant speech, fortunate, full of refreshment, and abounding in laughter and joy;
free from thirst and hunger—O house, do not be afraid of us. 6.
Stay right here; do not go away. Nourish all forms. I shall return with good fortune; may you become more prosperous through me. //7//
O Agni, as we perform this austerity through the heat of our penance, may we become dear to sacred learning, long-lived, and wise. //1//
O Agni, we perform fervor; we practice fervor.
Hearing what is heard, may we be long-lived and wise.
This Agni is the lord of the good, the bull of great vigor; like a charioteer, he has conquered the foot-soldiers as our domestic priest.
Established at the navel of the earth, let him flash forth his brilliance and cast beneath his feet those who seek to attack us. 1.

We invoke with hymns Agni, the conqueror of armies, the subduer, from his highest dwelling place. May he, the god Agni, carry us across all difficulties; may he, the patient one, carry us beyond all misfortunes. //1//
Whatever this black bird, flying down, has dropped—may the waters protect me from all that misfortune, from that distress. //1//
Whatever the black bird has pecked with your mouth, O Nirṛti—may Agni Gārhapatya release me from that sin. //2//
For you, O Apāmārga, have grown with fruit turned toward us;
drive all curses away from me and keep them far from here.
Whatever has been ill-done, whatever impurity, or whatever we have committed through our evil nature— that, O all-facing Apāmārga, we wipe away with you.
Whatever we have shared with one who has black teeth, one with deformed nails,
or a cripple— O Apāmārga, by means of you, we wipe all that away.
Whether it was in the intermediate space, or in the wind, or in the trees, or in the shrubs—whatever the cattle heard as it was being raised up, may that Brahman return once more to us. (1)
May power return again, may the self, wealth, and the Brahmanic luster return;
may the sacrificial fires, each according to its place, be established here once more. //1//
O divine Sarasvatī, in your sacred observances and celestial abodes, accept the oblation offered to you; O Goddess, grant us progeny. //1//
This oblation, rich in ghee, is for you; this sacrificial offering is the mouth of the ancestors. These most auspicious words are for you; through them may we be full of sweetness. 2.
Be auspicious and most peaceful for us, O Sarasvatī, be very gracious;
may we not be separated from the sight of you.
May the wind blow auspiciously for us; may the sun shine auspiciously for us.
May the days be auspicious for us; may the night be established as auspicious for us. May the dawn shine forth auspiciously for us. //1//

Whatever he offers with his mind, whatever with his speech, with sacrifices, with oblations, and with sacrificial formulas—Nirṛti, in agreement with Mṛtyu, shall destroy that offering of his before it becomes true. 1.
May the sorcerers, Nirṛti, and the Rākṣasas slay him with untruth;
may the gods, impelled by Indra, churn away his sacrificial oblation. May that which he offers not reach its completion.
Like two swift, supreme kings, like two hawks swooping down together—
let them strike down the ghee-seeking assailant and whoever seeks to harm us.
I bind both your arms behind you and I bind your mouth; with the wrath of the divine Agni, by that I have struck down your oblation. 4.
I bind your arms; I bind your mouth. With the wrath of the terrible Agni, by that [wrath] I have struck down the oblation. //5//
O Agni, O powerful one, we place you around us as a fortress— you, the inspired sage,
whose color is bold, who day by day slays the treacherous foe.
Arise and look upon Indra’s seasonal portion!
If it is cooked, offer it; if it is uncooked, wait for it to be done.
The oblation is cooked; come hither, O Indra! The sun has reached the midpoint of its path.
Your friends sit around you with their treasures, like householders surrounding a leader of the clan as he journeys abroad.
I consider it cooked in the udder, cooked on the fire; I consider that newest *ṛta* to be well-cooked.
O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, performer of many deeds, drink of the curd of the midday libation with favor.
Kindled is Agni, O Bulls; the charioteer of heaven. The heated *gharma* is milked for you both, its honey for nourishment.
For we, the singers, many times have called upon you, O Aśvins, at the shared feasts.
The fire is kindled, O Aśvins; the *gharma* vessel is heated for you; come hither!
Now indeed the cows are milked here by the bull-like ones; O wonder-workers (*dasra*), the wise ones rejoice.
Like a pure oblation offered among the gods, this is the cup of the Aśvins, the vessel for the drinking of the gods.
All the immortals, taking delight in it, lick it with the mouth of the Gandharva.
The ghee and milk offered in the cows—that is your portion, O Aśvins; come hither!
O lovers of sweetness, upholders of the assembly, lords of the virtuous, drink the heated *gharma* from heaven. 4.
May the heated oblation reach you both, with Svahotṛ as its priest; let the Adhvaryu move forward for you, bearing milk.
O Aśvins, enjoy the continuous flow of the milked honey; drink of the milk of the ruddy cow.
Run hither with milk, O milker of cows; quickly pour the milk of the cow into the heated vessel.
Savitar, the most excellent, has looked upon the firmament; he shines following the departure of the Dawn.
I invoke this well-milking cow; may the skillful milker milk her.
May Savitṛ impel for us the most excellent impulse. The Gharma has been heated; let him proclaim that clearly. //7//
Muttering the sound *hiṅ*, the mistress of treasures, seeking her calf with her mind, has come down.
May this inviolable cow yield milk for the Aśvins; may she increase for our great good fortune.
Welcome as the domestic friend and guest in our home, O wise one, come to this our sacrifice.
Having struck down all assailants, O Agni, bring hither the possessions of those who act as enemies. //9//
O Agni, be bold for great good fortune; may your splendors be most excellent. Bring together a household that is easy to govern, and trample down the powers of those who act as enemies. //10//
O blessed one, may you indeed have good pasture; and may we also be blessed.
Eat grass, O inviolable one, at all times; drink pure water as you wander. 11.
"We have heard that the mother of the red *apacits* is black;
by means of the root of the divine sage, I pierce them all. (AVŚ 7.74.1)
I pierce their first; I pierce their middle one as well;
here I cut off their last, like a lock of wool.
With a word belonging to Tvaṣṭṛ, I have made your jealousy flow away;
furthermore, O husband, that wrath of yours, we pacify it for you.
O Lord of Vows, united with the vow, shine here forever with a gracious mind.
May we all, possessing offspring, sit near you, O Jātavedas, when you are kindled. 4.
May you be rich in offspring, grazing on lush pasture, radiant, and drinking pure waters at a good watering place.
Let neither the thief nor the malevolent man have power over you; may the missile of Rudra pass you by.
You are knowers of the tracks, delighting ones, united, bearing all names.
Come to me, O goddesses, together with the gods. Sprinkle us with ghee in this cow-pen, in this dwelling place. 2.
More fragile than the fragile, more non-existent than the non-existent;
more sapless than a stalk of hemp, more prone to decay than a mere call.
Those honors that are on the neck, and those that are on the armpits;
those honors on the joints that fall away by themselves—[may they all go forth].
He who crushes the cartilages and settles upon the breastbone—
drive out all that *jāyānya* disease, whatever rests upon the hump.
The winged bird Jāyānya flies and enters into the man;
that is the remedy for both the undecaying and the badly wounded. //4//
We indeed know your origin, O Jāyānya, from whence you are born, O Jāyānya.
How then can you strike us there, in whose house we prepare the oblation for you? 1.
Drink boldly the Soma from the jar, O Indra, hero and slayer of Vṛtra, in the battle for riches. At the midday libation, pour yourself full; as one who abides in wealth, bestow wealth upon us. //2//
O Sāṃtapana Maruts, may you graciously accept this oblation; O destroyers of enemies, protect us with your aid.
O Maruts, O Vasus, whatever mortal man of evil intent seeks to strike down our thoughts from within, may the snares of his malice be cast back upon him; slay him with your most scorching heat!

The Maruts, who abide for a year, who possess beautiful songs, whose dwellings are wide, who move in troops, and who belong to men—may they release us from the snares of sin; may the Sāṃtapana gods, exhilarating and intoxicating, grant us joy.
I loosen for you the cord, I loosen the yoke-thong, I loosen the fastening.
Right here, O Agni, may you remain imperishable. 1.
O Agni, I yoke you with divine prayer, you who maintain sovereign powers for him.
Shine forth for us here with auspicious wealth; speak this word among the deities on behalf of the giver of the oblation.

Whatever portion the gods, dwelling together in greatness, have prepared for you, O Amāvāsyā, with that do you fulfill our sacrifice, O possessor of all boons; bestow upon us wealth, O fortunate one, accompanied by heroic sons. //1//
I alone am the new moon; the doers of good deeds dwell within me.
In me all the gods, both the Sadhyas and those with Indra as their chief, have come together.
Night has arrived, the gatherer of treasures, bringing strength, nourishment, and wealth.
To the New Moon we offer our oblation; milking out strength with her milk, she has come to us. 3.
On the new moon night, none other than you has brought forth all these forms as their encompasser.
Whatever desire we have in offering to you, may that be ours; may we be masters of riches. 4.
The full moon has conquered;
dwelling with the gods upon her in majesty, may we rejoice together on the back of the firmament with nourishing food.
We sacrifice to the bull, the prize-winning one, the Full Moon;
may he grant us imperishable wealth that is never-failing.
Prajāpati, none other than you has brought forth all these forms as their encompasser.
Whatever desire we have in sacrificing to you, may that be ours; may we be masters of riches. 3.
The full moon was the first to be worthy of sacrifice among the days and nights during the deepening of the darkness.
Those who honor you with sacrifices, O worthy of sacrifice, those well-doers have entered your celestial vault.
These two move one after the other by my power; like two playing children, they go around the ocean.
One beholds all beings; the other, ordaining the seasons, is born ever anew.
Being born, you become ever new; as the banner of the days, you go at the forefront of the dawns.
Coming, you distribute a portion to the gods; O Moon, you extend a long life.
O Lord of battles, you are the portion of Soma, and your name is "The Whole. O Darśa, make me whole with offspring and with wealth. //3//
(7.81.4a) You are the visible; you are the beautiful to behold; you are complete; you are all-encompassing.
(7.81.4c) May I become complete and all-encompassing through cattle, horses, progeny, livestock, houses, and wealth. //4//
He who hates us and whom we hate—swell with his life-breath!
May we swell with cattle, horses, offspring, livestock, houses, and wealth. //5//
The stalk which the gods cause to swell, which the imperishable ones consume as the imperishable—
