The Vasus shall protect you from the south, the Maruts from the north, and the Ādityas from behind; run past the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.
The gods, the ancestors, human beings, and those who are Gandharvas and Apsarases—they shall all protect you; run beyond the nightless [sacrifice]. 9.9a-c.
The intermediate space, heaven, earth, the Ādityas, the Maruts, and the quarters—
he who gives the hundred-porridge attains all these worlds.
(10) Sprinkling ghee, the fortunate goddess shall go to the gods.
O inviolable cow, do not harm the one who cooks you; go to heaven, O you of a hundred grains.
Those gods who dwell in heaven and those who dwell in the intermediate space, and those who are here upon the earth—
from them, may you always milk forth milk, clarified butter, and honey.
May that which is your head, that which is your mouth, your two ears, and your two jaws,
yield curd for the giver— milk, clarified butter, and honey.
May those two lips of yours, those two nostrils, those two horns, and those two eyes of yours—
may they yield for the giver curds, milk, clarified butter, and honey.
May your lungs, your heart, your pericardium, together with your throat—
may these yield for the giver curd, milk, ghee, and honey.
Whatever liver you have, whatever kidneys, whatever intestines and whatever bowels you have—
let them yield curd for the giver, as well as milk, clarified butter, and honey.
May that which is your gullet, your rectum, your two flanks, and your skin—
may these yield for the giver curd, milk, clarified butter, and honey.
Whatever marrow is yours, whatever bone, whatever flesh, and whatever blood—
let them yield for the giver curd, milk, clarified butter, and honey.
May your two arms, your two forearms, your two shoulders,
and your hump yield for the giver curd, milk, clarified butter, and likewise honey.
(20) Those necks of yours, those shoulders, those vertebrae, and those ribs— let them yield for the giver curdled milk,

milk, clarified butter, and honey. (21) Those two thighs of yours, the two knee-caps, those two hips, and that which is your buttock— let them yield for the giver curdled milk, milk, clarified butter, and honey.
May they yield for the giver curds, milk, ghee, and likewise honey.
That which is your tail, those which are your hairs, that which is your udder, and those which are your teats—
let them yield for the giver curds, milk, clarified butter, and likewise honey.
Those shanks of yours, those hocks, the sinews, and those hooves—
let them yield for the giver curd, milk, ghee, and likewise honey.
Whatever hide is yours in the hundredfold rice-offering, O inviolable cow, whatever hairs there are—
let them yield curd for the giver, as well as milk, clarified butter, and honey.
Let your two breasts be two sacrificial cakes (*puroḍāśa*) sprinkled with clarified butter;
having made them your two wings, O Goddess, carry the cooker to heaven. (25)
Whatever grain or husk is in the mortar, in the pestle, on the hide, or in the winnowing basket;
or whatever the purifying wind Mātariśvan has scattered—that may Agni, the Hotṛ, make into a well-offered oblation.

The divine waters, honey-sweet and dripping with clarity, I set down separately in the hands of the Brahmins. Whatever desire I have for which I sprinkle you here, may all that be fulfilled for me; may we be masters of riches.
Homage to you as you are being born, and homage to you once born.
To the young ones, to the hooved ones, to the one of beautiful form, to the inviolable one—to you, homage! //1//
He who knows the seven downward slopes, he who knows the seven distant realms—he who knows the head of the sacrifice, he shall receive the barren cow. //2//
I know the seven downward slopes; I know the seven distant regions.
I know the head of the sacrifice and the Soma that is clearly visible within it. 3.
By whom the sky was protected, by whom the earth, and by whom these waters were guarded—her, the cow of a thousand streams, we address with a sacred prayer. 4.
A hundred bronze vessels, a hundred milkers, and a hundred guardians are upon her back. Those gods who breathe within her know the cow as one. (5)
Having the sacrifice as her feet, milk as her eyes, the *svadhā* offering as her breath, and the earth as her garment—
Vaśā, the consort of Parjanya, approaches the gods with sacred prayer (*brahman*).
Agni has entered into you; Soma has entered into you by your will.
Parjanya is your udder, O blessed one; the lightnings are your breasts, [placed] by your will.
You milk the waters first; you milk the fertile fields next according to your will. Thirdly, you milk the kingdom; you milk food and milk according to your will.
When you, O observer of the cosmic order (*ṛtavarī*), approached while being offered by the Ādityas,
Indra caused you to drink a thousand vessels of Soma under his control.
Since the bull called you hither from afar to Indra,
therefore the Vṛtra-slayer, though enraged, took the milk and the fluid into his power.
Since the enraged Lord of Wealth took the milk into his power, [so be it].
Today, he protects this very heaven in three vessels. //11//
The cow, O Goddess, brought that Soma in three vessels to where Atharvan, consecrated for initiation, sat upon the golden sacrificial grass.
For she has come together with Soma, and indeed with every footed creature;
the cow has entered the ocean along with the Gandharvas and the Kali-demons.
For she has come together with the wind, and indeed with all winged creatures;
the barren cow danced upon the ocean, bearing the *ṛc* verses and the *sāman* chants.
For she has come together with the sun, together with every eye;
the cow has looked across the ocean, bearing auspicious lights. 15.
O observer of the cosmic order (*ṛtāvarī*), when you stood covered with gold,
the horse, having become the ocean, leaped upon you according to your will.
Then the auspicious ones gathered together— the Vaśā, the Deṣṭrī, and likewise the Svadhā—
where the consecrated Atharvan sat upon the golden sacrificial grass.
The barren cow is the mother of the Rājanya; O Svadhā, the barren cow is your mother.
From the sacrificial implement of the barren cow, consciousness was born. 18.
The drop rose upward from the summit of the sacred formulation (*brahman*);
from that you were born by your own will, and from that the Hotṛ-priest was produced. 19.
From your mouth the *gāthās* arose; from your lips came strength and power.
From your belly the sacrifice was born; from your breasts your rays issued forth.
{34} From your two flanks movement was born, and from your thighs, O Lord, [power] was born.
From the entrails were born the Atris; from the belly, the plants.
When you entered the belly of Varuṇa and came under his control,
from there the Brahman called out to you, for he knew your way.
All those who were in the womb trembled at her being born from the vital breaths;
for they say she has given birth to that [Vāk] as "Vaśā," for she has been fashioned by the sacred hymns (*brahman*), and she is indeed its kin.
He alone unites them through battle, he who is the sole lord of this [earth].
Sacrifices became the strengths; the cow became the eye of the strengths. 24.
The cow accepted the sacrifice; the cow sustained the sun.
Within the cow entered the rice-mash together with the sacred word (*brahman*). 25.
They call the cow immortality; they worship the cow as death.
Through the cow all this came to be: gods, humans, asuras, ancestors, and seers. //26//
He who knows thus should accept the barren cow;
for in this way the sacrifice yields all things to the giver without failing.
Three tongues flash within the mouth of Varuṇa;
of these, she who shines in the middle is the barren cow, difficult to accept as a gift.
The seed of the cow became fourfold:
one quarter is water, one quarter is immortality, one quarter is sacrifice, and one quarter is cattle.
The Sky is the Cow, the Earth is the Cow, Viṣṇu is the Cow, and Prajāpati is the Cow;
the Sādhyas and the Vasus drank the milk of the Cow.
Having drunk the milk of the barren cow, the Sādhyas and those who are the Vasus—
verily they, upon the summit of the sun, partake of her milk.
Some milk her as Soma; others attend upon her as clarified butter.
Those who have given a barren cow to one who knows thus have gone to the third heaven from the sky. 32.
Having given a cow to the Brahmins, one attains all the worlds;
for truth is established in her, as are sacred knowledge and ascetic fervor.
On the cow do the gods depend for life, and on the cow do human beings as well;
by the cow has all this come to be, as far as the sun shines.
O Agni, be born! This Aditi, seeking protection, cooks the *brahmaudana* (sacrificial rice-mess), desiring a son.
May the Seven Seers, the makers of beings, churn you here together with offspring.
Produce smoke, O bull-like friends; you who are free from guile, direct your speech toward the protector.
This Agni is the conqueror of armies and possesses heroic sons, by whom the gods overcame the Dasyus. 2.
O Agni Jātavedas, you have been born for great heroic power, to cook the *brahmaudana*.
The seven seers, the makers of beings, have brought you forth; bestow upon this woman wealth consisting of all-heroic sons. 3.
Kindled with fuel, O Agni, be well-kindled; as one who knows, bring here the gods worthy of sacrifice.
Cooking the oblation for them, O Jātavedas, cause this man to ascend to the highest firmament. 4.

The threefold portion that was formerly assigned to you—belonging to the gods, the ancestors, and mortals—know your shares; I divide them for you. That which belongs to the gods shall carry this [sacrifice] across.
O Agni, you are powerful, victorious, and triumphant; bend down the hateful rivals who are below us.
This measure, being measured and already measured, shall make your kinsmen bringers of tribute.
Together with your kinsmen, together with milk, grow strong; lift her up for great heroic power.
Rise up to the highest point of the firmament, that which they call the heavenly world.
(8a) May this great earth, the goddess Pṛthivī, receive the skin with a well-disposed mind;
(8c) then may we go to the world of the well-done. //8//
Yoke these two pressing-stones as a pair upon the hide; press out the stalks well for the sacrificer.
Striking down, destroy those who attack us here; lift up the offspring and carry it upward.
Take the two well-fashioned pressing-stones in your hand, O Hero; the gods worthy of sacrifice have come to your sacrifice.
Whatever three boons you choose, those successes of yours I shall cause to prosper here.
This is your devotion, this is your birthplace; may Aditi, mother of heroes, accept you.
Drive away those who attack her; bestow upon her wealth consisting of all heroic sons.
Breathe upon the wooden post; sit down, you who are worthy of sacrifice, separating yourselves from the husks.
Through glory may I surpass all my equals; I cast the feet of the hater beneath me.
Go away, O woman; come back quickly! The stall of the waters has mounted you for the sake of bearing [the child].
Of those [waters], seize whichever are worthy of sacrifice; having distinguished them, let the wise one abandon the others.
Here come these women, adorning themselves; arise, O woman, and take hold of the vigorous one.
With a good husband and offspring, you who are rich in progeny—the sacrifice has come to you; receive the jar.
The portion of nourishment that was deposited for you of old—bring these waters, which have been instructed by the seers.
May this sacrifice be for you a finder of passage, a finder of protection, a finder of progeny, fierce, a finder of cattle, and a finder of heroes. 15.
O Agni, the sacrificial oblation has mounted upon you—pure and most burning; burn him with your heat!
Let the seers and the gods, having come together, let those who are most burning burn him with this portion according to the seasons.
Pure, cleansed, and worthy of sacrifice are these women; may these bright waters glide down over the sacrificial porridge (*caru*).
May they grant us abundant offspring and cattle; may the one who has cooked the rice-mash go to the world of the righteous. 17.

Purified by the sacred word (*brahman*) and cleansed with clarified butter, these grains of rice are the stalks of Soma, worthy of sacrifice. Enter the waters; let the sacrificial porridge (*caru*) receive you. Having cooked this, go to the world of those who have performed good deeds.
Spread wide with great majesty, O thousand-backed one, in the world of the well-made!
Grandfathers, fathers, progeny, offspring—of these fifteen, I am the cooker. 19.

Thousand-backed, hundred-streamed, inexhaustible, the Brahman-food, the path to the gods, leading to heaven—those [enemies] I place for you; harm them with their offspring, and be gracious to me for the sake of the tribute.
Arise upon the altar; increase it with offspring; drive away the demon; bestow long life upon it.
May I surpass all those who are my equals in glory; I cast the feet of my enemies beneath my feet.
Turn back with cattle; come toward her together with the gods. Let no curse nor sorcery reach you; reign free from disease in your own field.

Fashioned by the *ṛta* and prepared with a focused mind, this altar for the *brahmaudana* was established first. O woman, place here the pure shoulder-supporting [stone]; upon it, set down the rice-offering for the gods.
This second ladle, the hand of Aditi, which the seven seers, the creators of beings, fashioned—that ladle, knowing the limbs of the rice-mess, let it place him upon the sacrificial altar. 24.
(25a) May the gods sit down beside you, the cooked oblation; having emerged from the fire, settle back among them again.
(25c) Purified by Soma, sit within the belly; may those of the seers' lineage who consume the *brahman* not suffer harm. //25//
O King Soma, bestow recognition upon these men, whoever among them sits near you as excellent Brahmins.
I repeatedly invoke the seers and those born of seers, who were born from ascetic heat, for this *brahmaudana* offering, O you who are easily invoked.
Pure, cleansed, and worthy of sacrifice are these women; I set them down separately in the hands of the Brahmins.
With whatever desire I sprinkle you here, may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, grant that to me. 27.
This is my immortal light, this gold; this cow of plenty is mine, ripened from the field.
This wealth I deposit among the Brahmins; I prepare the path to that heaven which exists among the Fathers. 28.
Scatter the husks into the fire, into Jātavedas; cast the empty stalks far away.
We have heard this to be the portion of the King of the House, and thus we know it to be the allotted share of Nirṛti.
Know him as one who exerts himself, who cooks, and who presses the Soma; lead him upward onto the path to heaven.
By that path may he ascend, reaching the highest state—that which is the supreme life-force, the firmament, the loftiest sky.
O brown Adhvaryu, cleanse this mouth; being well-acquainted with the way, prepare a space for the clarified butter.
Anoint all my limbs with clarified butter; I prepare for myself the path to heaven that leads among the ancestors.
Carry off the *rakṣas* and the strife; scatter them from these [people], whoever they may be, who sit down near you without being Brāhmaṇas.
May those who eat first, the descendants of seers (*ārṣeya*), who are full of vital essence (*purīṣin*), not come to harm.
I place you, O rice, among those of noble lineage; there is also a place here for those of various lineages.
May Agni be my protector, and all the Maruts; may all the Viśve Devas guard the cooked offering.
Milking the sacrifice that is ever swelling, the male, the cow, the abode of riches—may we sit beside you with offspring, immortality, long life, and the increase of wealth. 34.
You are a bull; go to the heavenly world and to the seers of the seer-lineage. Sit in the world of those who have performed good deeds; there let our preparation be completed.

Gather them together and follow along; O Agni, prepare the paths that lead to the gods. May we follow after these good deeds to the sacrifice standing in the vault of heaven upon the seven-rayed pole.
(37a) By that light with which the gods ascended to heaven after cooking the *brahmaudana* for the world of the well-done;
(37c) by that may we go to the world of the well-done, ascending to the heavenly light, toward the highest firmament.
//37// {4} (1a) O Bhava and Śarva, be gracious! Do not come against us! O lords of beings, lords of cattle, homage be to you both!
Do not let go of our messenger who has come from afar; do not harm us, neither our bipeds nor our quadrupeds. //1//
Do not let the dog or the jackal devour the bodies, nor the *aliklavas*, the vultures, and those black scavengers;
O Lord of Creatures, let not the flies and the birds find you for their prey.
For your roar, for your breath, and for those growths of yours, O Bhava, we pay homage to you, O Rudra, the thousand-eyed, the immortal. //3//
We offer homage to you from the front, from above, and from below;
from the expanse of heaven and from the intermediate space, homage to you! //4//
For your mouth, O Paśupati; for those eyes of yours, O Bhava; for your skin, for beauty, for the sight, and for that which faces you—homage to you! //5//
Homage to your limbs, to your belly, to your tongue, and to your mouth; homage to your teeth and to your sense of smell. //6//
With the missile of Nīlaśikhaṇḍin, with the thousand-eyed Vājin, with Rudra who strikes with half his body—may we be united with him. 7.
May Bhava spare us on every side; may Bhava spare us as fire spares the waters.
Let him not harm us; let there be homage to him. //8//
Four times homage to Bhava, eight times to Paśupati—ten times homage to you!
These five classes of animals have been distributed by you: cattle, horses, humans, goats, and sheep. //9//
(11.2.10a) The four quarters are yours; the sky is yours, the earth is yours, and this vast intermediate space, O fierce one, is yours.
(11.2.10c) This entire living world that breathes along with the earth is yours.
(11.2.11a) This wide treasury, the container of wealth, is yours, within which all these worlds are contained.
Be gracious to us, O Lord of Cattle; homage be unto you! Let the jackals, the howling dogs, and the foul-voiced, disheveled women stay far away.

You bear a golden, green bow, O crested one, that slays a thousand and kills a hundred. The arrow of Rudra, the weapon of the gods, flies forth; homage to it, wherever it may be in this direction from here. 12.
O Rudra, whoever approaches you and seeks to harm you, you shall pursue him from behind like one following the tracks of a wounded animal. 13.
Bhava and Rudra, joined together and in harmony, both fierce, move about for the sake of heroic power;
homage be to them both, whichever direction they are in from here.
Homage be to you as you approach; homage be to you as you depart. Homage to you, O Rudra, as you stand, and homage to you as you sit. //15//
Homage in the evening, homage in the morning; homage by night, homage by day.
To Bhava and to Śarva—to both of them I have paid homage.
The thousand-eyed Rudra, who sees beyond, shooting forth in many ways from the front—
may we not provoke him with our flickering tongue.
The dark, black, and tawny one, crushing [all], the terrible chariot that causes the long-haired ones to fall—may we meet him facing forward;
let there be homage to him. 18.
Do not let the divine bolt strike us, O mortal; do not be angry with us, O Lord of Cattle, homage be to you!
Shake the divine branch elsewhere than upon us.
Do not harm us; speak for us; choose us as your own; do not be angry.
May we never come into conflict with you. Do not covet our cattle, our men, nor our goats and sheep.
O fierce one, turn away elsewhere; destroy the offspring of those who are hostile.
He whose fever, the coughing weapon, comes with a single roar like that of a stallion, who advances and then retreats—homage be to him! 22.
To him who stands in the intermediate space, firmly established, crushing those who do not sacrifice and slaying the revilers of the gods—to him be homage with the ten *śakvarī* verses. //23//
To you belong the wild beasts, the deer placed in the forest, the swans, the eagles, the birds, and the winged fowl.
O Lord of Beasts, your power dwells within the waters; for your growth, the celestial waters flow. 24.

The *śiṃśumāras*, the pythons, the *purīkayas*, the *jaṣas*, the fish, and the *rajasas* to whom you cast [your weapon]—for them there is no distance, nor is there any place for them to escape; O Bhava, you behold the entire earth instantly, from the eastern ocean to the northern one.
O Rudra, do not strike us with fever, nor with poison; do not consume us with divine fire.
Let your lightning fall elsewhere than upon us. //26//
Bhava rules over heaven; Bhava rules over the earth; Bhava has filled the vast mid-air.
Homage to him from whichever direction he may be here. //27//
Be gracious, O King, to the sacrificer; for you have become the Lord of Animals.
Be merciful to his four-footed and two-footed creatures—whoever has faith that "the gods exist. (AVŚ 11.2.28)
Do not harm our great ones, nor our small ones; do not harm those who carry us, nor those who shall carry us.
Do not injure our father and mother, O Rudra; do not destroy our own bodies. //29//
To the dogs of Rudra, the Elabakāras, who swallow what has not been consecrated by hymns—
to these large-mouthed dogs, I have rendered this homage.
Homage to you, O noisy ones; homage to you, O long-haired ones! Homage to those who have been saluted; homage to those who enjoy together!
Homage to your armies, O God; may there be well-being for us and fearlessness for us. 31. {7}
Of that rice-offering, Bṛhaspati is the head; the sacred word (brahman) is the mouth. //1//
Heaven and Earth are the ears; the sun and moon are the eyes; the seven seers are the out-breath and the in-breath. //2//
The eye is the pestle, O Kāma, and the desire is the mortar. //3//
Diti is the winnowing basket; Aditi is the one who holds the basket; Vāta has winnowed it clean.
Horses are the grains, cows are the rice-grains, and gadflies are the husks. //5//
The *kabru*, the husks, the *śara* grass, and the cloud.
His flesh is black iron; his blood is red.
Tin is its ash; green is its color; the lotus is its fragrance.
The threshing floor is the sacrificial vessel; the two shoulder-blades are the two wooden spades; the two shafts are the spine.
The entrails, the collarbones, and the intestines are the leather straps. //10//
This very earth becomes the cooking-pot for the rice being prepared; the sky is the lid. //11//
The cold ribs are the sand; the undigested contents are the bladder.
The *ṛta* is the washing of the hands and the sprinkling of the water-channel. 13.
The pot was placed upon [the fire] with a *ṛc* verse; it was sent forth by means of the priestly office (*ṛtvijya*). //14//
She is embraced by the *brahman* and encompassed by the *sāman*. //15//
The Bṛhat and the Rathantara are the ladle for the prolonging of life. //16//
The seasons are the cooks; the seasonal periods kindle [the fire] together.
(18) He heats the cauldron, the five-holed vessel, as the Gharma offering.
(19) By means of the cooked rice, all the worlds of the sacrificer are to be fully satisfied.
In whom the ocean, the sky, and the earth—the three, both near and far—are supported.
From whose leavings the gods were fashioned—the eighty-six [clans]. //21//
I ask you about that rice-porridge, what its great majesty is.
Whoever should know the greatness of that rice-mess.
One should not say, "This is not a small amount," nor "It has no condiment," nor "What is this? //24//
As much as the giver intends in his mind, he should not speak more than that. //25//
The exponents of sacred knowledge say: "Did you eat the rice facing away, or facing toward [me]?"
"You ate the rice; you [ate] the rice," he says. //27//
"You have eaten him facing away; your vital breaths will desert you," he said to him.
"If you have eaten this facing backward, your vital breaths will desert you," he said to him.
Neither am I the rice, nor is the rice me.
"He ate the rice-porridge with the very same rice-porridge. "Then you ate it with a different head than the one with which the seers of old ate it;
therefore, your offspring shall die starting with the eldest," he said to him.
Neither facing this way, nor facing away, nor facing toward me—
with Bṛhaspati as my head,
with that [head] I have consumed him; with that I have sent him forth.
(32) This porridge indeed possesses all limbs, all joints, and an entire body.
He who knows this becomes possessed of all limbs, all joints, and an entire body.
(33) And from that, you ate it with other ears—those same ears with which the ancient seers ate it.
"You will become deaf," he said to him.
"Neither toward this side, nor toward that side, nor facing me—
by means of the two ears of heaven and earth."
Through these two I have caused him to eat; through these two I have brought him here.
This very rice-mess has all its limbs, all its joints, and all its body.
He who knows thus becomes possessed of all his limbs, all his joints, and all his body. 33. [2]
"Then you ate it with those other two eyes with which the ancient seers ate it;
you shall become blind," he said to him.
"Indeed, I [ate it] neither facing downward, nor facing away, nor facing toward me."
With the sun and the moon as its two eyes;
with those two I have caused him to eat, and with those two I have made him go forth.
This very rice-mess has all its limbs, all its joints, and all its body.
"He becomes one whose every limb, every joint, and every body-part is complete, he who knows thus.
"Then you ate this with another mouth, the one with which the ancient seers ate it.
'Your offspring shall die from the mouth,' he said to him."
Neither toward this side, nor toward that side, nor facing him, have I [consumed] him with the sacred word as my mouth;
with that I have consumed him, with that I have sent him forth.
(35) This very rice-mess has all its limbs, all its joints, and all its body. He who knows thus becomes possessed of all his limbs, all his joints, and all his body.
(36) And then you ate it with another tongue, with which the seers of old ate it.
"Your tongue will perish," he said to him. "Neither toward this side, nor toward that side, nor facing me— with the tongue of Agni, I [consume] it."
By that very means I have caused him to eat; by that very means I have brought him here.
This rice-mess indeed has all its limbs, all its joints, and all its body.
He who knows thus becomes possessed of all his limbs, all his joints, and his entire body. 36. [5]
"Then you ate it with other teeth than those with which the seers of old ate it;
your teeth will fall out," he said to him.
"Indeed, I [ate it] neither facing downward, nor facing away, nor facing toward me."
With the seasons as teeth, with those I have eaten him; with those I have sent him forth.
This very rice-mess has all its limbs, all its joints, and all its body.
"He becomes whole in every limb, whole in every joint, whole in every body, he who knows thus.

(AVŚ 11.3.37) "Then you have consumed him with other out-breaths and in-breaths, those with which the ancient seers consumed him. 'The out-breaths and in-breaths shall leave you,' he said to him. (AVŚ 11.3.38)
Neither toward this side, nor away from that side, nor facing toward me—
by means of the seven seers, the out-breaths and in-breaths—
with those I have eaten him; with those I have sent him forth.

(38) This very rice-mess is complete in all its limbs, complete in all its joints, and complete in its entire body. He who knows this becomes indeed complete in all his limbs, complete in all his joints, and complete in his entire body.
(39) And from that, eat it with another measure, with which the seers of old ate it.
"Consumption shall slay you," he said to him;
"I [drive it away], neither toward this side, nor toward that side, nor backward,
but through the expanse of the intermediate space."
By that I have caused him to eat; by that I have brought him here.
This very rice-mess has all its limbs, all its joints, and all its body.
He who knows thus becomes possessed of all his limbs, all his joints, and all his body. 39. [8]
Then he made him eat it with another back—that with which the ancient seers had eaten it.
He said to him, "Lightning will strike you.
But I [ate it] neither facing downward, nor facing away, nor facing toward me.
By day with the back;
by that I have eaten him, by that I have reached him.
This rice-mess indeed has all its limbs, all its joints, and all its body.
"He becomes one whose every limb, every joint, and every body-part is complete, he who knows thus.
[40] [9] "Then you ate this with another breast than that with which the ancient seers ate it.
'You shall not succeed through agriculture,' he said to him. [41] [10]ab.
Neither toward this side, nor toward that side, nor facing him directly—
with the essence of the two earths—
by that have I consumed him; by that have I sent him forth.

(41) This very rice-mess is complete in all its limbs, complete in all its joints, and complete in its entire body. He who knows thus becomes complete in all his limbs, complete in all his joints, and complete in his entire body.
(42) And therefore, you have eaten this with another belly than that with which the ancient seers ate it.
"Your belly will kill you," he said to him.
"Neither facing this way, nor facing away, nor facing toward me—
with my belly of truth— will I [kill] him."
By that I have caused him to eat; by that I have sent him forth.
This rice-mess indeed has all its limbs, all its joints, and its entire body.
He who knows thus becomes possessed of all his limbs, all his joints, and his entire body. 42. [11]
"Then he made him eat it with another bladder, the one with which the ancient seers had eaten it.
He said to him, 'You shall die in the waters.
But I [ate it] neither facing downward, nor facing away, nor facing toward me."
With the ocean as its garment, with that I have eaten him; with that I have sent him forth. This very rice-mess has all its limbs, all its joints, and all its body.
"He who knows thus becomes whole in every limb, whole in every joint, and whole in his entire body.
[43] "Then you ate this with other two thighs—those with which the ancient seers ate it.
'Your thighs shall perish,' he said to him. [44]
Neither toward this side, nor toward that side, nor facing me—
through the thighs of Mitra and Varuṇa,
with those two have I caused him to eat; with those two have I sent him forth.
(44) This very porridge has all its limbs, all its joints, and all its body. He who knows thus becomes possessed of all his limbs, all his joints, and all his body.
(45) And from that, you ate it with two other kneecaps—those same ones with which the seers of old ate it.
"You shall become lame," he said to him.
"I [shall strike] him neither from this side, nor from that side, nor from behind,
but with Tvaṣṭṛ’s two knees."
With these two I have caused him to eat; with these two I have brought him here.
This very rice-mess has all its limbs, all its joints, and its entire body.
He who knows thus becomes one who has all his limbs, all his joints, and his entire body. 45. [14]
"And then you ate it with two other feet, those with which the ancient seers ate it.
He said to him: 'You shall become one who travels much.
Indeed, I did not eat it facing downward, nor facing away, nor facing toward me."
From the two feet of the Aśvins;
with those two I have caused him to eat, with those two I have sent him forth.
This very rice-mess has all its limbs, all its joints, and all its body.
He who knows this becomes whole in every limb, whole in every joint, and whole in his entire body. 46.
Then he said to him: "Eat from these two other forefeet, those from which the ancient seers ate;
a serpent will kill you. 47.
I have not [seen] him from the front, nor from behind, nor from across;
[I have seen him] by means of the two fore-feet of Savitṛ.
By those two I have caused him to eat; by those two I have caused him to come.

(47) This very rice-mess is complete in all its limbs, complete in all its joints, and complete in its entire body. He who knows this becomes complete in all his limbs, complete in all his joints, and complete in his entire body.
(48) And thereafter, you ate it with those other two hands with which the ancient seers ate it.
"You will kill a Brahmin," he said to him.
"But I [shall strike] him neither from this side, nor from that side, nor from behind,
with the two hands of *ṛta*."
Through these two I have caused him to eat; through these two I have brought him here.
This very rice-mess has all its limbs, all its joints, and its entire body.
He who knows this becomes possessed of all his limbs, all his joints, and his entire body. 48. [17]
"And then you ate it with a different foundation than that with which the ancient seers ate it.
[Therefore] he said to him: 'Without a foundation and without a support, you shall die.
Indeed, I have not eaten it facing downward, nor facing away, nor facing toward me."

Established upon truth, by that very means I have caused him to eat; by that very means I have brought him here. This rice-mess indeed is complete in its limbs, complete in its joints, and complete in its body.
He who knows thus becomes whole in every limb, whole in every joint, and whole in his entire body. 49.
This rice-mess is indeed the summit of the sun. 50.
He who knows thus comes to be in the world of the sun; he rests upon the summit of the sun. 51.
From this very rice-mess, Prajāpati measured out the thirty-three worlds. 52.
For the sake of discerning them, he created the sacrifice. 53.
He who becomes a supervisor of one who knows thus obstructs his own vital breath. 54.
And he does not obstruct his vital breath; he is not deprived of everything.
(55) [6] He is not deprived of everything, and before old age, his vital breath does not leave him.
(56) [7] {10} Homage to the vital breath, under whose control all this exists! (1) [1]
He who has become the Lord of all, in whom everything is established. //1//
Homage to you, O Prāṇa, for your thundering; homage to you for your roaring.
Homage to you, O Prāṇa, for your lightning; homage to you, O Prāṇa, for your raining.
When the vital breath roars through the thunder, the plants are impregnated;
they conceive their embryos and then bring forth many offspring.
When the breath arrives at the appointed time and cries out to the plants,
then everything that exists upon the earth rejoices.
When the vital breath has rained down rain upon the great earth,
then the cattle rejoice, saying, "Great indeed shall our prosperity be."
The plants, drenched by the rain, have conversed together with the breath of life.
You have indeed prolonged our lifespan; you have made us all fragrant.
Homage be to you as you come; homage be to you as you go away.
Homage to you, O Prāṇa, as you stand, and homage to you as you sit. //7//
Homage to you, O Prāṇa, as you breathe out; homage be to you as you breathe in. Homage to you as you move away; homage to you as you move toward us. To you in your entirety, this homage! //8//
O Prāṇa, that body of yours which is dear, that which is most beloved to you, O Prāṇa,
and whatever healing power you possess— bestow that upon us so that we may live.
Breath clothes living beings as a father clothes his beloved son;
breath indeed is the lord of all, both that which breathes and that which does not. Breath is death, breath is fever; the gods worship breath.
For breath places the speaker of truth in the highest world.
Breath is the Virāj; breath is the Deṣṭrī; all worship breath. Breath indeed is the sun and the moon; they call breath Prajāpati. //12//
Inhalation and exhalation are rice and barley; the ox is said to be the out-breath (*prāṇa*). Indeed, the out-breath is placed in the barley, while inhalation (*apāna*) is said to be the rice. //13//
A person breathes out and breathes in while within the womb;
when you, O Prāṇa, quicken him, then he is born again. //14//
They call Mātariśvan the breath; indeed, Vāta is called the breath. In the breath is what has been and what is to be; in the breath everything is established. //15//
The plants born of Atharvan, of Aṅgiras, of the gods, and those born of men, spring forth when you, O Prāṇa, quicken them.
When the vital breath has rained down rain upon the great earth,
the herbs are born forth, as well as whatever plants there may be.
Whoever knows this breath of yours, in which you are established—for him all shall bring tribute in that highest world. 18.
Just as all these creatures here offer tribute to you, O Prāṇa, so let them bring tribute to him who hears you, O you of good fame. 19.
The embryo moves within the deities; having come into being, he is born again.
Having become the past, he enters as the father into the son who is to be and will be, by means of his powers.
As a swan rising from the water, he does not lift up one foot.
If indeed someone were to dig that up, it would exist neither today nor tomorrow;
there would be no night and no day, and it would never dawn at any time.
The eight-wheeled [chariot] rolls with a single rim; it has a thousand syllables, forward and backward.
With one half he generated the entire world; what is that sign which is his other half? //22//
To him who rules over this entire birth of all beings and over everything that moves, to him who possesses a swift bow among others—to you, O Prāṇa, let there be homage! 23.
May the tireless, wise Prāṇa, who rules over all this birth and over everything that moves, abide within me through the sacred word (brahman). 24.
Standing upright while others sleep, he does not indeed fall prone;
no one at all has ever heard him sleeping while others sleep.
O Prāṇa, do not turn away from me; you shall be none other than I.
Like the embryo of the waters, for the sake of life, O Prāṇa, I bind you to me.
The student of sacred knowledge (*brahmacārī*) moves about, pervading both worlds; in him the gods become of one mind.
He has supported both the earth and the sky; he satisfies his teacher through austerity.
The fathers, the divine folk, and all the gods individually follow after the one who lives the holy life (*brahmacārin*).
The Gandharvas followed him—thirty-three, three hundred, and six thousand; he satisfies all those gods through his ascetic heat (*tapas*).
The teacher, leading him forward, makes the student his embryo within;
for three nights he bears him in his belly; when he is born, the gods come together to behold him. //3//
This earth is the fuel, and the second is the sky; thus he fills the mid-air with fuel.
The student of sacred knowledge (*brahmacārī*), by means of fuel, his girdle, toil, and ascetic heat, fulfills the worlds. 4.

Born before Brahmā, the student of sacred knowledge (*brahmacārī*), clad in the *gharma*, stood firm through austerity. The student of sacred knowledge goes forth, kindled with fuel, clothed in black, consecrated, and long-bearded.
Having grasped the worlds, he immediately goes from the eastern ocean to the northern one, repeatedly performing his course.
The celibate student, generating the sacred word (*brahman*), [produced] the waters, the world, Prajāpati, Parameṣṭhin, and Virāj;
having become the embryo in the womb of immortality and having indeed become Indra, he struck down the Asuras. 7.
The teacher carved out both these expanses, the broad and deep earth and heaven. The student of sacred knowledge protects them through his fervor; in him the gods become of one mind. //8//
The first student of sacred knowledge (*brahmacārī*) brought forth this earth, the broad ground, and the sky as his alms.
Having made these two into fuel-sticks, he worships them; upon them all beings are established. 9.
One is near, the other is beyond the back of heaven; two treasures are deposited in secret within the Brahmin.
The student of sacred knowledge (*brahmacārī*) guards them through austerity; knowing the *brahman*, he makes that his own entirely.
One is near, the other is from here on earth; the two fires meet together within these two atmospheres.
Their firm rays rest upon those two; the student of sacred knowledge (brahmacārī) stands upon them through his ascetic heat (tapas). //11//
Crying out, thundering, ruddy, with white horns and a great tail, he has spread along the earth.
As a student of sacred knowledge (*brahmacārī*), he pours his seed upon the summit of the earth; by it the four quarters of space live.
In fire, in the sun, in the moon, in Mātariśvan, and in the waters, the student of sacred knowledge (*brahmacārī*) places the fuel-stick.
Their flames move separately within the cloud; their clarified butter is man, their rain is water. 13.
The teacher was Death, Varuṇa, Soma, and the plants were milk; the clouds were the warriors—with them, this heaven was brought down. //14//
Having become the teacher, Varuṇa makes the clarified butter his own alone;
whatever he desired from Prajāpati, that the student gave him, as a friend from his own self.
The teacher is a celibate student; the celibate student is Prajāpati.
Prajāpati shines forth as Virāj; Virāj became the sovereign Indra. 16.
Through the holy life and through austerity, the king protects his kingdom;
through the holy life, the teacher seeks a student of the holy life.
Through the practice of celibacy, a maiden finds a young husband;
through the practice of celibacy, a draft-ox and a horse seek to win fodder.
By the holy life and by austerity, the gods struck down death;
indeed, Indra brought back the light from the gods through the holy life. //19//
The plants, the past and the future, day and night, and the forest lord;
the year together with the seasons—these were born as Vedic students.
(20) The animals of the earth and the heavens, those of the wild and those of the village. (21)
And those wingless birds that have been born as practitioners of the holy life. //21//
Each of these individual beings belonging to Prajāpati bears vital breaths within themselves;
Brahman protects them all, which have been brought together in the one who practices sacred study.
This, which is consecrated by the gods, moves about unclimbed and radiant;
from it was born the Brāhmaṇa, the highest Brahman, along with all the gods and immortality. //23//
The radiant student of sacred knowledge (*brahmacārī*) bears the *brahman*; in him all the gods are gathered together.
Generating out-breath, in-breath, and diffused breath (*vyāna*), he generates speech, mind, heart, sacred knowledge (*brahman*), and wisdom (*medhā*).
Bestow upon us sight, hearing, and glory; food, seed, blood, and the belly. //25//
Fashioning them, the student of sacred knowledge stood performing austerities upon the surface of the waters in the ocean.
Having bathed there, he became tawny and reddish-brown, shining brightly upon the earth.
We praise Agni, the lords of the forest, the herbs, and the plants.
May Indra, Bṛhaspati, and Sūrya release us from distress. //1//
We invoke King Varuṇa, Mitra, Viṣṇu, and Bhaga;
we invoke Aṃśa and Vivasvant—may they release us from distress.
We invoke the god Savitṛ, Dhātṛ, and Pūṣan;
we invoke Tvaṣṭṛ, the foremost. May they release us from distress. //3//
We invoke the Gandharvas and Apsarases, the two Aśvins, and Brahmaṇaspati; may the god named Aryaman release us from distress. //4//
Day and night we address this to both the Sun and the Moon;
we address all the Ādityas: may they release us from distress.
We speak to the wind, to Parjanya, to the intermediate space, and likewise to the quarters; we speak to all the regions as well—may they release us from distress.
May Day and Night release me from the curse, and may Dawn as well;
may the god Soma release me, whom they call the Moon.
The domestic animals of the earth, those of heaven, and the wild beasts that roam the forest;
the winged birds—we speak of them: may they release us from distress.
We speak thus to Bhava and Śarva, and to Rudra who is Paśupati:
may those arrows which we know them to possess always be auspicious to us. //9//
We invoke the heavens and the stars, the earth and the yakṣas, the mountains;
may the oceans, the rivers, and the ponds release us from distress.
We invoke the seven seers, the divine waters, and Prajāpati.
We address the ancestors, of whom Yama is the chief; may they deliver us from distress. 11.
Those gods who dwell in heaven and those who dwell in the intermediate space, and those who are established upon the earth, O Śakras—may they release us from distress. //12//
The Ādityas, Rudras, Vasus, the gods in heaven, the Atharvans, the wise Aṅgirases—may they release us from distress. //13//
We speak of the sacrifice, the sacrificer, the *ṛc* verses, the *sāman* chants, and the healing remedies;
we speak of the *yajus* formulas and the priestly offices—may they deliver us from distress. //14//
We declare that there are five royal plants, of which Soma is the best: Darbha, Bhaṅga, Yava, and Sahas; may they release us from distress.
We name the *arāyas*, the *rakṣases*, the serpents, the *puṇyajanas*, and the *pitṛs*; we name the one hundred and one deaths—may they release us from distress. //16//
We invoke the seasons, the lords of the seasons, and the seasonal periods;
the years, the full years, and the months—may they release us from distress. 17.
Come hither, O gods, from the south and from behind; come forward, O Śakras, from the east and from the north! May all the gods, having assembled, release us from distress. //18//
We address all the gods, who are true to their covenant and who increase the cosmic order:
together with all their wives, may they release us from distress. //19//
We speak thus to all the gods, who are true to their covenant and who increase the cosmic order (*ṛta*):
together with all their wives, may they release us from distress.
We speak of the Real, the Lord of beings, who is the controller of all creatures;
may all beings, having come together, release us from distress. //21//
The goddesses who are the five directions, the gods who are the twelve seasons—those which are the fangs of the year, may they be ever auspicious to us. //22//
That immortal medicine which Mātali knows as "Rathakrīta," Indra caused it to enter into the waters; O Waters, give that medicine!
In the remnant (ucchiṣṭa) are name and form; in the remnant is the world established.
In the remnant are Indra and Agni; the entire universe is contained within it.
In the remnant are heaven and earth; all that has come to be is contained therein.
In the remnant are the waters and the ocean; the moon and the wind are established there.
Both the Residue and the Non-residue are Death, Vāja, and Prajāpati. The worldly powers depend upon the Residue; may both Vraś and Draś, as well as Prosperity, abide in me.
Firm, make firm; steadfast, O Nyas, the ten creators of the universe! As the hub, so are all things; upon the Ucchiṣṭa the deities are supported. //4//
The Ṛg, Sāman, and Yajus are the remnant; the Udgītha, the Prastāva, and the Stotra are the remnant.
The Hiṅkāra is in the remnant, as is the tone of the Sāman and its Meḍi; may that be in me. (5)
The Aindrāgna, the Pāvamāna, the Mahānāmnīs, and the Mahāvrata—
these limbs of the sacrifice reside within the Residue, like a fetus within its mother.
The Rājasūya, the Vājapeya, the Agniṣṭoma, and that sacrifice; the Arka and Aśvamedha are in the remnant, as is the most exhilarating Jīvabarhis. //7//
The establishment of the sacred fires, as well as the consecration, the fulfillment of desires together with the meters—
these sacrifices and sacrificial sessions, though fallen into ruin, are all contained within the remnant.
The Agnihotra sacrifice, faith, the Vaṣaṭ-call, the vow, austerity, the sacrificial fee, the offering, and the work of public utility— all these are established within the remnant.
The one-night rite, the two-night rite, the *sadyaḥkrī*, the *prakrī*, and the *ukthya*;
the woven and the deposited [oblation] remaining from the sacrifice—these minute parts [are known] through knowledge.
(10) The four-night rite, the five-night rite, and the six-night rite, both together. (11)
The *ṣoḍaśin* and the seven-night sacrifice—all those sacrifices established in immortality—were born from the Residue. //11//
The Pratihāra is the Nidhana, as are the Viśvajit and the Abhijit;
the Sāhna and the Atirātra are in the Ucchiṣṭa, and the Dvādaśāha is also contained within me. 12.
Truth, humility, security, skill, vigor, immortality, and force—all desires are directed toward the remnant; through desire they have been satisfied. 13.
The nine earths and the oceans rest upon the Residue of heaven;
the sun shines within the Residue, and day and night are likewise contained therein—may they also be in me.
The Upahavya, the Viṣūvant, and those sacrifices that are hidden in secret—the Supporter, the Residue, the Father of the progenitor, sustains them all. 15.
The father is the remnant of the progenitor; he is the grandson of the *asu* and the grandfather.
As the lord of all, that bull dwells upon the earth, surpassing all others.
Cosmic order, truth, ascetic heat, sovereignty, toil, righteousness, and action;
the past and the future, vigor, fortune, and strength are in the remnant, within strength.
Prosperity, vigor, intention, dominion, the kingdom, and the six expanses;
the year remains as the remnant, as does the sacrificial food, the commands, the cups, and the oblation.
The Caturhotṛ formulas, the Āprī hymns, the Cāturmāsya sacrifices, and the Nīvids;
the remnants of the sacrifice, the Hotṛ-offices, the animal sacrifices, and the Iṣṭi offerings—all these are contained therein. //19//

The half-months and the months, the seasons together with the seasonal periods; in the remnant [of the sacrifice] are the sounding waters, the thunder, and the great hearing. (20) Gravel, sand, stones, herbs, climbing plants, and grasses.
The clouds, lightning, and rain are dependent upon, and rest within, the leavings. //21//
Success, attainment, completion, pervasion, greatness, and growth; over-attainment, prosperity in what remains, and that which is placed, established, and beneficial—may these increase.
Whatever breathes with breath and whatever sees with the eye—all these were born from the remnant; the gods in heaven are supported in heaven.
The *ṛg*-verses, the *sāman*-chants, the meters, and the ancient *yajus* formulas—all these were born from the Residue; likewise, all the gods dwelling in heaven were born therefrom. //24//
In-breath and out-breath, sight and hearing, and both imperishability and perishability—all these were born from the remnant; all the gods in heaven are supported by heaven. 25.
The Ānandas, the Mods, the Pramudas, and those who are the Abhīmodas and Mudas—
all these gods dwelling in heaven were born from the Residue.
The gods, the ancestors, human beings, and those who are Gandharvas and Apsarases—all were born from the remnant; the gods in heaven are established in heaven.
When Manyu brought his wife from the house of Saṃkalpa.
Who were the kinsmen, who were the suitors, and who indeed became the eldest suitor? //1//
Austerity and ritual action both existed within the great ocean;
they were the suitors for her hand, and among them, Brahman became the suitor with the highest claim. //2//
Ten gods were born together in the ancient time before the [other] gods.
Whoever indeed may know them face-to-face, he alone may speak of the Great One today. (3)
Inhalation and exhalation, sight and hearing, imperishability and perishability, the diffused breath and the upward breath, speech and mind—may these bring about your intention. 4.
The seasons were unborn, as were Dhātṛ and Bṛhaspati; at that time, Indra, Agni, and the Aśvins—whom did they worship as their eldest?
Both austerity and action existed within the great ocean;
indeed, austerity was born from action, and they venerated that as the eldest.
That which was the earth in the beginning, which those who know the truth understand;
he who indeed knows it by name may consider himself a knower of antiquity.
From where was Indra born, from where Soma, and from where was Agni born? From where did Tvaṣṭṛ come into being, and from where was Dhātṛ born? //8//
From Indra was born Indra, from Soma was born Soma, from Agni was born Agni; Tvaṣṭṛ was indeed born from Tvaṣṭṛ, and from Dhātṛ was Dhātṛ born. //9//
(10a) Those ten gods who were born before the [other] gods—
having given the world to their sons, in what world do they now dwell?
(10c) When he brought together hair, bone, sinew, flesh, and marrow...
Having made his body like a foot, into which world did he enter? //11//
From where did he bring the hair, from where the sinews, and from where the bones?
From where did he bring the limbs, the joints, the marrow, and the flesh? 12.
The gods named Saṃsic were those who gathered the materials together;
having poured everything together, the gods entered the mortal person. 13.
The thighs, the feet, the kneecaps, the head, the hands, and then the face;
the spine, the breasts, and the sides—what seer put all that together? 14.14a-c.
The head, the two hands, then the mouth, the tongue, the neck, and the vertebrae—having covered all that with skin, the Great One joined it together. 15.
That great body which lay there, joined together by its joints—by what does it shine today? Who bestowed color upon it? //16//
All the gods learned this; the virtuous bride understood it. She who is the wife of the Lord of Power brought splendor to this community.
When Tvaṣṭṛ pierced [him], he who is higher than Tvaṣṭṛ’s father—having made a house for the mortal, the gods entered the Puruṣa. //18//
Sleep, lethargy, destruction, and the deities named Evil have entered into the body—old age, baldness, and graying hair. 19.

Theft, evil-doing, and transgression, truth, sacrifice, and great glory— strength, dominion, and vital force entered into the body. Prosperity and adversity, those things which are gifts and those which are not— {23}
And all forms of hunger and thirst entered into the body. //21//
Both blame and praise, and both "come" and "no," entered the body along with faith and lack of faith as sacrificial gifts.
Knowledge and ignorance, and whatever else is to be taught—the body entered into that Brahman, as did the Ṛg, Sāman, and Yajus verses. //23//
Delights, joys, pleasures, and those ecstasies and raptures—laughter, the *nariṣṭās*, and dances entered into the body. //24//
The utterances, the lamentations, and those words of distress—all these entered the body: the āyujas, the prayujas, and the yujas. //25//
In-breath and out-breath, sight and hearing, as well as imperishability and perishability, the diffused breath and the upward breath, speech and mind— they all move within the body.
The blessings, the commands, the instructions, and the distinctions— all thoughts and all volitions entered into the body.
The waters that belong to the fields and those that belong to the dwellings, those that are swift and those that are pitiable,
the secret, the bright, and the thick— those waters have settled into the loathsome.
Having made the bones the fuel, they placed the eight waters upon it;
having made the semen the clarified butter, the gods entered into Puruṣa. //29//
The waters and the deities, the Virāj together with Brahman—the body entered into Brahman; within the body is Prajāpati.
The sun and the wind have distributed the eye and the breath of the person;
then the gods bestowed his other self upon Agni. 31.
Therefore, indeed, the wise man considers this person to be Brahman;
for all the deities abide within him, like cows in a cow-pen. //32//
By the first plague, it spreads in three directions;
with one [part] it goes there, with one it goes there, and with one it settles here.

Within the swelling waters that have grown great, the body has been placed; within it is vigor, and because of that, it is called "vigor. (34) Whatever arms, whatever arrows, and whatever heroic powers belong to the bows—
The axes, the hatchets, the weapons, and whatever intention or purpose is in the heart—O Arbudi, show all that to our enemies; and reveal our noble wives to them. 1.
Arise and gird yourselves, O you divine folk, you who are our friends!
May those who are visible and those who are hidden be protected—those who are our friends, O Arbudi.
Arise, seize them with your grasp and your bond;
O Arbudi, strike down the armies of our enemies!
The god named Arbudi and Nyarbudi, who are lords—
by those two by whom the atmosphere and this great earth are encompassed,
by those two, the slayers of Indra, I follow the victory with my army. 4.
Arise, O Arbudi, you who belong to the host of gods, together with your army!
Shattering the army of our enemies, surround them with your coils.
Beholding seven *nyarbudas* of noble beings born,
rise up with your entire army when these oblations of clarified butter have been offered.
Let her strike out, with tearful face and short ears,
crying out when a man is slain— she with disheveled hair, O Arbuda, at your piercing!
Drawing together the *karūkara* with her mind, desiring a son, [she seeks] a husband, a brother, or even her own kin; O Arbudi, when you have crushed them! 8.

Let the *aliklava*s, the *jāṣkamada*s, the vultures, the hawks, the winged birds, the crows, and the fowls find satisfaction among the enemies, as they gaze upon them torn apart by you, O Arbudi. //9//
Moreover, let every beast of prey, the fly, and the worm be satisfied upon this human corpse, O Arbudi, as it is torn apart by you.
Seize them, O Nyarbudi; join together their out-breath and in-breath!
Let the rustling sounds gather against the enemies, making them look upon one another with terror at the place pierced by you, O Arbudi.
Make them tremble; let them be struck with fear; send the enemies together! O Nyarbuda, pierce the enemies with your wide-reaching, arm-like jaws.
Let their arms fail them, and whatever intention is in their hearts; let nothing remain of them once they have been struck down by you, O Arbudi.
Striking one another, they run together, beating their breasts and thighs;
with disheveled hair and weeping, they wail when a man has been slain—when he has been struck down by you, O Arbudi! 14.
The Apsarases who possess dogs, Rūpakā, and Arbudi;
the one who licks within the vessel, Riśā, who seeks out what is ill-placed—all these, O Arbudi, you must make visible to our enemies, and show them their own wives. 15.
Khaḍūra, Adhicaṅkramā, Kharvikā, and Kharvavāsinī;
those noble ones who have vanished, the Gandharvas and Apsarases, the serpents, the Itarajanas, and the Rakṣasas—[may they all be appeased]. //16//
The four-tusked ones with black teeth, those with pot-like testicles and blood-stained faces—
those who are terrifying by nature and those who inspire terror.
O Arbudi, make those enemies' garments tremble!
May Jaya and Jiṣṇu, who delight in Indra, conquer the enemies.
Completely cowed, crushed, and lying dead is the enemy, O Nyarbudi!
Let the victorious ones, with Agni as their tongue and smoke as their crest, advance with their army.
By that [spell], may Indra strike down the best of each of those driven away by Arbuda;
may the Lord of Might (*śacīpati*) slay the enemies, so that not one of them escapes.
Let their hearts burst open; let their life-breath (*prāṇa*) surge upward.
Let dryness of the mouth pursue the enemies, and not those who are our friends.
Those who are wise and those who are unwise, those who are turned away and those who are deaf,
those who are hornless from darkness and those who are clothed in rags—
O Arbudi, make all of them visible to our enemies, and show us our own noble wives.
May Arbudi and Triṣandhi pierce through our enemies,
so that, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra, lord of power, we may slaughter these enemies by the thousands.
The lords of the forest, the products of the forest, the herbs, and the climbing plants;
the Gandharvas, the Apsarases, the serpents, the gods, the holy folk, and the ancestors—all these, O Arbudi, you must make visible to our enemies, and show them their own wives. 24.
The god Maruts, Āditya, and Brahmaṇaspati have made you masters;
Indra and Agni, Dhātṛ, Mitra, and Prajāpati have made you masters.
The seers have made you masters, O Arbudi, so that you may look upon our enemies when they have been struck down by you. 25.
(26) You who are the lords of them all, arise and gird yourselves!
O you divine folk, having won this battle, go forth each to your own realm.
(27) Arise and gird yourselves, O noble ones, together with your banners!
O serpents, other folk, and demons, pursue the enemies! 1.
I know your sovereignty, O Triṣandhi, together with your ruddy banners.
Those who are in the intermediate space, those in heaven, those on earth, and those who are human—
let those of evil name wait upon the mind of Triṣandhi.
With iron mouths, needle-mouths, and likewise with *vikaṅkata*-wood mouths—
flesh-eaters, swift as the wind— let them seize the enemies with the three-jointed thunderbolt.
Place it within, O Jātavedas; O Āditya, hide this corpse well.
May this army of Triṣandhi be well-disposed and remain under my control.
Arise, O Arbudi, you who belong to the host of gods, together with your army!
This offering is presented for you; this oblation is dear to Triśandhi.
Let this four-footed arrow, white-footed, pierce through;
O Kṛtyā, become three-jointed together with your army against the enemies.
Let Dhūmākṣī fall together with Kṛdhukarṇī and let her shriek;
when conquered by the army of Triṣandhi, let the banners be crimson.
May the winged birds that move in the intermediate space and those that roam in heaven come down;
may the beasts of prey, the flies, the vultures, and the scavengers seize upon the corpse and tear at it.
The alliance which you have established with Indra and with Bṛhaspati, O Brahman—by that alliance with Indra, I summon all the gods here; let them conquer from here, not from there. //9//
Bṛhaspati Āṅgirasa and the seers sharpened by sacred knowledge took refuge in heaven with the three-jointed weapon, the destroyer of the Asuras,
by which that Aditya is protected and both Indra and [the sun] stand firm.
The gods divided the three-jointed [plant] for vigor and for strength. //11//
By means of this oblation, the gods conquered all the worlds;
Bṛhaspati Āṅgirasa poured forth that thunderbolt, the weapon that destroys the Asuras.
The thunderbolt which Bṛhaspati Āṅgirasa poured out—the weapon that destroys the Asuras—with that I smear that army; O Bṛhaspati, I slay the enemies with my might. //13//
All the gods come forth who consume that which is consecrated with the *vaṣaṭ* call;
enjoy this oblation and conquer from here, not from there.
May all the gods come hither; let the oblation be dear to Triṣandhi.
Guard the great covenant by which the Asuras were conquered in the beginning. //15//
May Vāyu bend the tips of the arrows of our enemies.
May Indra break their arms so that they cannot shoot back their arrow.
May Āditya destroy their weapon; may Candramas close the path of him who has not yet arrived.

If they have passed away from the cities of the gods and have made the *brahman* their armor, creating a protection for their bodies and a defense around them as they recited [the spells], make all that sapless.
Following the flesh-eaters and Death as your domestic priest, go forth with your army at Triṣandhi; conquer the enemies and press forward! 18.
O Triṣandhi, with darkness do thou surround our enemies;
let not one among these who have been driven away by the speckled butter escape me.
Let the white-footed one fly together against those cloaks of the enemies.
Let those armies of the enemies be bewildered today, O Nyarbuda!
O Nyarbuda, having bewildered the enemies, strike down their best man after the best man.
With this army, strike! //21//

Whether he be an enemy wearing armor or one without armor, whoever is struck down on the battlefield by the snares of the bowstring, the snares of armor, or by the path of the chariot— let him lie there dead.
Those enemies who are armored and those who are unarmored, and those who wear armor—
O Arbudi, let all of them, once slain, be devoured by dogs upon the earth.
Those who have chariots and those who are without chariots, those who are foot-soldiers and those who are horsemen—
let all those slain ones be devoured by vultures, hawks, and winged birds.
Let the enemy army, consisting of thousands of corpses, lie dead in battle,
pierced through and rendered mangled.
Let the birds devour the evil-minded one who pierces the vital organs, who cries out in pain, who lies crushed;
[devour] the enemy who desires to fight against this oblation of ours directed toward him. 26.
That which the gods uphold, that which is without failure—
that with it may Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, strike with his three-jointed thunderbolt.
Truth, the great, the formidable cosmic order, consecration, ascetic heat, sacred formulation, and sacrifice— these sustain the earth.
May she, the mistress of what has been and what is to be, the Earth, create for us a wide world. //1//
Unconfined in the midst of men, she whose heights, slopes, and level plains are many;
she who bears herbs of manifold powers—may Pṛthivī spread out for us, may she be successful for us. //2//
In whom the ocean and the Sindhu, in whom the waters and the food of the people have come together;
in whom this world breathes, stirs, and moves—may that Earth grant us the first draught. //3//
She whose four quarters are the earth, in whom the peoples have produced their food;
she who bears the many things that breathe and move—may that Earth grant us [a share] in cattle and in food. 4.
On whom the people of former times strode forth, on whom the gods overcame the Asuras—may the Earth grant us the abundance, the splendor, and the various hosts of cattle, horses, and birds. 5.
The all-sustaining, treasure-bearing foundation, gold-breasted, the dwelling place of the world;
may the Earth, bearing Vaiśvānara Agni, who has Indra as her bull, bestow wealth upon us. //6//
The earth, the broad ground, which the gods guard sleeplessly at all times with vigilance—may she yield for us her dear honey; may she also sprinkle us with splendor.
That which was upon the ocean, over the waters, in the beginning; that which the wise followed with their creative powers (*māyā*);
whose heart, in the highest heaven, is the immortal covered by truth upon the earth—may that Earth bestow upon us brilliance and strength in the supreme kingdom. (8)
In whom the waters flow together in a common course, day and night pouring forth without ceasing—
may that Earth, with her many streams, milk out nourishment for us, and may she sprinkle us with splendor.

That earth which the Aśvins measured out, upon which Viṣṇu strode forth, and which Indra, the lord of power, made for himself free from enemies—may that Mother Earth release milk for me, her son. 10. {1}
May your mountains be snowy peaks; may the forest, O Earth, be pleasant for you.
The brown, the black, the ruddy, the multiform, the firm ground—the Earth protected by Indra—I have stood upon it, unconquered, unhurt, and unharmed. (11)
Whatever is your middle, O Earth, and whatever is your navel, and those strengths that have come together as your bodies—place us within them;
flow over us. The Earth is the mother, I am the son of the Earth; Parjanya is the father; may he indeed protect us. 12.
On her they enclose the altar-ground, on her the Viśvakarman-sages perform the sacrifice;
on her the sacrificial posts are measured out upon the earth, standing upright before the bright oblations.
May that Earth, ever increasing, cause us to prosper. //13//
Whoever hates us, O Earth, whoever attacks us, whoever seeks to harm us with his mind or with a weapon—
deliver him over to us, O Earth, you who act from of old.
Born from you, mortals move about in you; you support the bipeds and the quadrupeds.
O Earth, these five classes of men belong to you, for whom the immortal light rises as the sun, spreading its rays across the mortals. 15.
May they milk for us offspring in their entirety; O Earth, bestow upon me the honey of speech.
May we always follow the auspicious and pleasant Mother of the plants, the firm Earth, the Pṛthivī, who is upheld by the cosmic order. 17.
A great dwelling place you have become, O Great One; great is your surge, your movement, and your trembling. The mighty Indra guards you vigilantly.
O Earth, cause us to shine forth like the appearance of gold; let no one at all hate us. 18.
Agni is in the earth, in the plants; the waters bear Agni; Agni is in the stones.
Agni is within men; in cows and horses, there are Agnis.
Agni burns from the sky; the vast mid-air belongs to Agni, the god. Mortals kindle Agni, the bearer of oblations, who loves clarified butter.
Clad in fire, with black knees, may the Earth make me radiant and sharpened.
Upon the earth they present to the gods the sacrifice, the well-prepared oblation;
upon the earth mortals live by means of *svadhā* and food.
May that Earth grant us breath and long life; may the broad Earth let me reach old age. //22//
(12.1.23) That fragrance which has arisen from you, O Earth, which the plants bear and which the waters hold;
that which the Gandharvas and Apsarases have shared—by means of that, make me fragrant; let no one whatsoever hate us. 23.

That fragrance of yours which entered the lotus, which they gathered together at the wedding of Sūryā—O immortal Earth, with that fragrance at the beginning, make me fragrant; let no one whatsoever hate us. 24.
That fragrance of yours which is among men, the fortune and splendor found in women and men;
that which is in horses, in heroes, and in wild beasts as well as in elephants; the luster that is in a maiden, O Earth—unite us with all that! Let no one whatsoever hate us. (25)
The earth is rock, stone, and dust; that earth is firmly established and supported.
To that Earth, whose breast is gold, I have paid homage. 26.
We call upon the Earth, the all-sustaining, who is firmly established, upon whom the trees and lords of the forest stand steadfast for all time. 27.
Whether rising up, or sitting, standing, or walking forth, may we not stumble upon the earth with our right and left feet.
I address the wide-spreading earth, the patient ground that has grown great through sacred power (*brahman*).
O Earth, may we settle upon you—you who bear strength, nourishment, and a portion of food, and who are rich in clarified butter (*ghṛta*). 29.
May pure waters flow over our bodies; him who has sat upon us unkindly, him we cast down.
With the purifier, O Earth, I cleanse myself.
(30) Those quarters of yours that face the east, those that face the north, those of yours, O Earth, that are below and those behind—(31)
May they be pleasant for me as I move about; may I not fall down while resting upon this world. //31//
Do not push us from behind, nor from the front; do not [push us] from above, nor from below.
O Earth, be auspicious for us! Let not highwaymen find us; drive away the weapon to a far distance.
As far as I behold you, O Earth, together with the sun,
so long may my sight not fail me for each succeeding year.
When lying down, I turn toward my right side upon you, O Earth; when we lie upon our backs facing you with our ribs pressed against you—do not harm us there, O Earth, you who receive all things.
Whatever of yours I dig up from the earth, may that grow back quickly; O you who are marked by lines, may I not pierce your vital organ, nor may I strike your heart.
Summer is yours, O Earth, the rains, autumn, winter, the cool season, and spring;
the seasons are ordained for you as your years. May day and night milk forth abundance for us, O Pṛthivī. //36//
She who drives away the serpent, she who is full of wild beasts, in whom dwelt the fires that are within the waters—
driving away the Dasyus, the revilers of the gods, and choosing Indra, the earth has yielded Vṛtra for the sake of Śakra, the bull, the powerful one.
In which the *sadas* and the *havirdhāna* [sheds] are located, and in which the sacrificial post is erected;
in which the Brahmins, knowers of the *yajus*, praise with *ṛc*s and *sāmans*; and in which the officiating priests are joined together for Indra to drink the *soma*—[that is this earth]. //38//
In which the ancient seers, the makers of beings, the wise ones, together with sacrifice and austerity, uttered forth the cows by means of the sevenfold sacrificial session.
May that Earth point out to us whatever wealth we desire;
may Bhaga bestow it upon us, and may Indra go before us as our leader.
(40) Upon that Earth where mortals sing and dance, free from disease—
May that earth, where they fight and where the war-cry resounds and the drum speaks, drive away our rivals; may the earth make me free from enemies. 41.
To her in whom food, rice, and barley exist, in whom these five peoples dwell—to Earth, the wife of Parjanya, whose fatness is the rain, let there be homage. 42.
She whose cities are fashioned by the gods, in whose field they transform themselves—may Prajāpati make the earth, which contains all embryos, pleasant for us in every direction. 43.
Bearing treasures in many ways within her secret depths, may the Earth grant me jewels and gold.
May the Goddess, the giver of wealth, bestow riches upon us, being well-disposed as she grants her favor.
Bearing people who speak in many ways, whose laws are diverse according to their dwellings, may the Earth yield for me a thousand streams of wealth, like a steady cow that does not kick away.
The serpent that is yours—the scorpion with its stinging sting, hibernating in its lair during winter, restless and dwelling in its hole;
the worm that stirs, O Earth, whatever moves at the onset of the rains—let none of that crawl upon us; let that which is auspicious be gracious to us. //46//
Those many paths of yours, frequented by people, the tracks for the chariot to travel;
those by which both the good and the evil pass—may we conquer that path which is free from enemies and thieves, which is auspicious; with that, be gracious to us. 47.
Bearing the impurity, supporting the heavy, enduring the destruction of both good and evil;
the Earth, in harmony with the boar, opens herself wide for the wild swine. 48.
Those wild animals and beasts dwelling in the forest that roam there—lions, tigers, and man-eaters—drive away from us the wolf, the jackal, misfortune, the *ṛkṣīkā*, and the *rakṣas*, O Earth. 49.
The Gandharvas and Apsarases, the Arāyas and Kimīdins,
all the Piśācas and Rākṣasas— drive them away from us, O Earth!
Upon which the two-footed winged creatures fly together— the swans, the eagles, the birds, the fowls.
In which the wind Mātariśvan blows, creating dust and shaking the trees;
along the wind’s outblowing and inblowing, the flame blows after.
Upon which the black and the ruddy are joined, and day and night are established over the earth;
may that Earth, the broad ground, covered and encompassed by rain, bestow upon us what is auspicious, O beloved one, at every stationing of our dwelling. 52.
May Heaven and this Earth, and the mid-air grant me spacious room;
may Agni, Sūrya, the Waters, and all the gods bestow wisdom upon me.
I am the conqueror named Uttara upon the earth;
I am the subduer of all, the overcomer of every quarter.

O Goddess, when you first moved forward from the east, having been addressed by the gods, you displayed your greatness; then well-being entered into you, and you fashioned the four quarters of space. 55.
Whatever villages, whatever wildernesses, whatever assemblies upon the earth;
whatever battles and gatherings—may we speak what is pleasing to you in those places. 56.
Like a horse, he has shaken off the dust—those people who settled upon the earth when it was born.
She moves with joyous speed, the guardian of the world, grasping the lords of the forest and the plants.
Whatever I speak, that I speak sweetly; whatever I look upon, they seek it from me.
I am radiant and full of speed; I strike down the others who are defiant.
Peaceful, fragrant, pleasant, with udders of ghee and rich in milk—
may the Earth, the broad ground, speak in my favor along with her milk.
Her whom Viśvakarman sought with oblation, who had entered into the ocean within the intermediate space;
that vessel which was hidden in secret as a servant—she became manifest for enjoyment to those who possess a mother.
You are the receptacle of people, Aditi, the cow of plenty, spreading far and wide;
may Prajāpati, the first-born of Cosmic Order, fill for you whatever in you is deficient.
May your attendants be free from disease and free from consumption, sent forth by you for our sake, O Earth. Awakening to a long life, may we be the ones who bring tribute to you.
O Mother Earth, place me down with auspiciousness, well-established.
O Sage, in harmony with the day, place me in glory and prosperity.
Climb the reed; there is no world for you here. This head is your allotted portion; come!
The consumption that is in cattle, the consumption that is in men—with that, go far away, downward.
From the one who intends evil and the one who utters curses, from the hand and the foreleg,
we drive out all consumption and death from here.
We drive death away from here, destruction away, and hostility away.
O Agni, consume him who hates us—being one who does not eat raw flesh—and him whom we hate, we cast forth to you. 3.

Whether it be the flesh-eating Agni or a tiger that has entered this cow-pen as a stranger, having made him a bean-cake with clarified butter, I send him far away; let him go even to the fires that dwell in the waters.
Whatever they, being angry, have done to you out of wrath when a man has died—O Agni, that act of yours is well-ordered; we kindle you anew.
Again may the Ādityas, the Rudras, and the Vasus restore you; again may Brahmā and Vasunīti restore you, O Agni.
Again may Brahmaṇaspati establish you for long life, for a hundred autumns.
The raw-flesh-eating Agni who has entered our house, beholding this other Jātavedas—him I carry far away for the sacrifice to the Fathers; may he kindle the heat in the highest dwelling-place.
I send the flesh-eating Agni far away; let him go to the realm of Yama, carrying off the impurities.
Here, let this other Jātavedas, the god who knows all beings, carry the oblation to the gods, for he is discerning.
Impelled, I carry away the flesh-eating Agni, who holds death firm with his thunderbolt;
I, the wise one, subdue him by means of the *gārhapatya* fire. Let there be a share for him in the world of the ancestors. 9.
I send forth the flesh-eating Agni, who is being honored with hymns, along the paths traveled by the fathers.
Let him not return again by the paths of the gods; remain right here among the fathers and be watchful.
They kindle the crumbling fire for their well-being, becoming pure, bright, and purifying.
He leaves behind his impurity; Agni, being kindled, passes beyond it and purifies him thoroughly with his cleansing power.
The divine Agni Saṃkasuka has ascended the ridges of heaven;
being released from sin, may he free us from ill-repute.
In this shifting fire we wipe away our impurities; we have become pure and worthy of sacrifice. May he prolong our lifespans. 13.
Saṃkasuka, Vikasuka, Nirṛtha, and he who is voiceless—they, sharing your affliction, have driven your consumption far, far away. 14.
