The flesh-eater who is among our horses, among our heroes, who is among our cattle, goats, and sheep—him we drive away; that fire which seeks out people. 15.
We drive away from you the flesh-eater, the fire that robs life, for the sake of other men, for the cows, and for the horses.
In that [place] where the gods cleansed themselves, and where men likewise, having cleansed yourself there, O Agni, you who are praised with oblations of ghee, ascend to heaven. 17.
Kindled and offered with oblations, O Agni, do not depart from us;
shine right here in the sky, so that we may long behold the sun.
Be gracious to our head; be gracious to the reed, to the fire, and to the crumbling ground;
and likewise to the woolly, dark-red pillow, [be gracious] to the headache.
Having laid the filth upon the head, and the headache upon the pillow;
having wiped them away in the black sheep’s wool, become pure and worthy of sacrifice.
(20) Go away, O Death, along the further path, that which is distinct from the way of the gods.
To you who have eyes and hear, I speak: may these many heroes here come to be.
These living ones have turned away from the dead; today our invocation of the gods has become auspicious.
We have gone forward for dancing and laughter; as men of noble heroes, may we address the assembly. 22.
I set up this boundary for the living, so that no other among them may now go to this goal.
Living a hundred abundant autumns, let them pass beyond death by means of this mountain.
Ascend [to life], choosing old age, striving one after another as you proceed;
may Tvaṣṭṛ, the well-born, acting in harmony with you, lead you all through your full span of life for living. 24.
Just as days follow one another in succession, and just as seasons proceed together with seasons, so,
O Ordainer, arrange their lifespans such that the later does not abandon the former.
The stony river flows; hold fast, show your heroism, and cross over, O friends!
Leave behind here those who are evil-minded; free from disease, may we cross over to the spoils of war.
Arise and cross over, O friends! This river flows with stones.
Leave behind here those who were unpropitious; may we cross over to the propitious and pleasant strengths.
Take hold of the Vaiśvadevī with splendor, becoming pure, bright, and purifying;
passing over the difficult places, may we rejoice for a hundred winters with all our heroes. 28.
Passing along the northern paths that belong to Vāyu, crossing from the lower to the higher realms,
the seers have gone forth thrice-seven times and have warded off death by means of the foot-covering.
Trampling the track of death, do you come here, securing for yourselves a longer and more extended life.
Sitting together in this place, drive away death; then, as living beings, may we proclaim our wisdom at the assembly.
May these women, not widows and having good husbands, touch themselves with collyrium and clarified butter.
Free from tears, free from disease, and possessing excellent jewels, let the women ascend first to the place of birth.
With the oblation I distinguish these two; with the sacred word (*brahman*) I arrange them.
I provide undecaying *svadhā* for the fathers; I unite these [two] with long life. //32//
O Pitṛs, that Agni who has entered into our hearts as the immortal among mortals—him, the god, I embrace within myself; may he not hate us, nor may we hate him. 33.
Turning away from the *gārhapatya* fire, go forth, O flesh-eater, toward the south;
do what is pleasing to the ancestors, to yourself, and to the *brahmans*. 34.
Taking two shares of the wealth, he squanders it through misfortune— that Agni who is the eldest son, the eater of raw flesh, who has not been properly installed.
Whatever one ploughs, whatever one gathers by hunting, and whatever one acquires through purchase—
all that belongs to a mortal ceases to exist if the flesh-eater has not been warded off.
Unfit for sacrifice and with his luster destroyed, he becomes one by whom no oblation is to be eaten;
the flesh-eater follows him and cuts him off from the fruits of plowing, cattle, and wealth.
The mortal man, led astray by greed, repeatedly utters cries of distress;
the flesh-eating fire, being fully aware, drives them away from his presence.
The houses are seized; they are joined together when the husband dies by [the hand of] a woman.
Only the one who knows the *brahman* is to be sought, he who drives away the flesh-eater. 39.
Whatever stain, impurity, or evil deed we have committed—
may the waters cleanse me from that, and from whatever [sin] comes from the fire-pit.
They have turned from the south toward the north, knowing the way, along the paths traveled by the gods.
Upon the back of the bull-like mountain, the ancient rivers flow anew.
O Agni, drive away the flesh-eater who is not a consumer of raw flesh; carry [us] to the place of sacrifice for the gods.
This flesh-eater has entered here; this one has followed after the flesh-eater.
Having made them two tigers of different kinds, I carry him away as one who is auspicious.
The secret place belongs to the gods, the enclosure to humans; Agni Gārhapatya has taken refuge between both. //44//
O Agni, extend the lifespan of the living; let those who have died go to the world of the ancestors.
As a good *gārhapatya* fire, burning away hostility, grant him a better and better dawn after every dawn. 45.
O Agni, overcoming all rivals, bestow upon us their vigor and wealth. //46//
Seize upon this Indra, the bearer, the protector; may he carry you out from misfortune and from reproach.
With him, drive away the missile that comes flying; with him, let the two protectors ward off Rudra. 47.
Seize hold of the ox as a raft; may it carry you out from misfortune and from blame.
Ascend this ship of Savitṛ; with its six broad expanses, may we cross over want.
Day and night you follow along, bearing [us], dwelling in peace, furthering us, and rich in heroes;
O bed, bearing us free from disease and of good cheer, remain for a long time indeed with the fragrance of manhood for us. 49.
They cut themselves off from the gods; they live perpetually in evil.
Like a flesh-eating fire that consumes reeds, Agni pursues them from close at hand like a horse.
Those who, lacking faith and desiring wealth, sit together as flesh-eaters— 50. {11} (AVŚ_12,2.51a) those who, lacking faith and desiring wealth, sit together as flesh-eaters.
Or they always carry a pot for others. //51//
He wishes to fly away with his mind, yet he turns back again and again;
the flesh-eating fire, knowing them well, drives them far away from his presence.

The black sheep is the portion of cattle; they say that lead is your share, O flesh-eater, even though you are bright. Ground beans are your sacrificial offering; O Forest-Dweller, frequent the depths.
Having offered up a withered blade of grass, a sesame husk, a reed-staff,
and a reed, Indra made these his fuel and extinguished the fire of Yama.
Having directed the hymn toward the west, the wise man has indeed entered upon the path;
he has sent their lives far away, and with long life I unite these people.
As a man, stand over the man’s skin; call there to those who are dear to you.
As great as you two were when you first met in the beginning, such is your common power in the realm of Yama.
So great is your vision, so great your heroic powers, so great your splendor, and so many your strengths.
When the fuel meets the body, O Agni, then you two shall become a united pair once it is cooked.
Be united in this world and likewise in the path to the gods; may you be gathered together in the realms of King Yama.
Purified by means of filters, pour forth that seed which has been produced within you both.
O Waters, sons, come together and enter this living man, you who bring life to the living.
Partake of that immortality which they call yours—the porridge which your mother cooks for you both. 4.

That rice-mash which your father cooks and that which your mother cooks for release from blemish and from the impurity of speech—that rice-mash, hundred-streamed, is heaven; by its greatness it has pervaded both worlds.
Both atmospheres and both worlds, those heavenly realms won by the sacrificers—of these, that which is foremost, luminous, and honey-sweet: in that, may you two take refuge with your sons in old age.
Grasp ever toward the eastern direction; those who have faith resort to this world.
Whatever cooked food has been served for you in the fire, O husband and wife, take refuge together for its protection.
Turning toward this vessel, turn back from the southern direction;
there Yama, in harmony with the ancestors, shall grant you both abundant protection for the cooked offering.
Of all the directions, this western quarter is indeed the best, wherein Soma is the sovereign lord and the one who bestows mercy.
Upon it may you two take refuge; may you, as doers of good deeds, dwell together there, and then, as a pair, enjoy the ripened fruits.
May the northern realm, preeminent through progeny, make the northern quarter our foremost among the directions.
May we become united with all our limbs, like the fivefold *chandas* and the person (*puruṣa*).
{13} May this Virāj be firm; let there be homage to her. May she be auspicious to my sons and to me.
O Goddess Aditi, possessor of all boons, protect our ripened [grain] like a vigilant guardian. //11//
Embrace us as a father his sons; let the auspicious winds blow for us here upon the earth.
O two deities, may that rice-mash which you cook here be known by us as heat and as truth. 12.
Whatever the black bird, having come here and flying about, has settled upon while it was stuck in the hole;
or whatever the female slave with wet hands has smeared [with it]—cleanse the mortar and pestle, O Waters! 13.
This stone, broad-based and bestowing vital strength, purified by the filters, shall drive away the demon.
Ascend the skin; grant me great protection! Let not the husband and wife fall into the evil of their offspring. 14.
The Lord of the Forest has come to us along with the gods, driving away the *rakṣases* and the *piśācas*.
May he rise up and let forth his voice; through him may we conquer all the worlds. 15.
The cattle have encompassed seven kinds of sacrificial food—both that which is luminous among them and that which has grown thin.
The thirty-three deities attend upon them; may they lead us toward the heavenly world. 16.
Lead us toward the heavenly world; may we be united with wife and sons.
I take your hand; follow me here. May Destruction and ill-will not overcome us. 17.
May we pass beyond that seizing evil; may you dispel the darkness and speak what is beautiful.
O wooden vessel, being lifted up, do not harm me, nor the grain, nor the one who seeks the gods. 18.
O all-pervading one, with ghee upon your back, becoming co-natured, go to this world;
reach out to the winnowing basket increased by rain; let it separate the chaff and the husks. 19.
The three worlds have been measured out by the Brahmin: yonder sky, this earth, and the intermediate space.
Having grasped the stalks, take hold of them; let them swell again and return to the winnowing basket.
Though the forms of cattle are manifold, you become of one form through abundance.
Push away this red skin; let the pressing-stone polish it like a washerman cleanses garments.
I cause you, O Earth, to enter into the earth; this body of yours is uniform yet transformed.
Whatever has been smeared or scratched by the instrument, may that not cause me harm; by means of this sacred prayer (*brahman*), I heal it. 22.
Like a mother, you shall welcome your son; I unite you, the earth, with the earth.
O cauldron, pot, do not tremble upon the altar, being closely joined with the sacrificial implements and the clarified butter.

May Agni, cooking [the oblation], protect you from the east; may Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, protect you from the south. May Varuṇa make you firm in the western support; may Soma join you together from the north. //24//
Purified by the filters, they flow clear; from the clouds they go to heaven and to the earth, to all the worlds.
They, the life-giving, the bringers of wealth to the living, established as supports—may Agni kindle them when poured into the vessel. 25.
They come from heaven; they attend to the earth; they attend to the earth and dwell in the intermediate space.
Being pure, they indeed adorn themselves; may they lead us toward the heavenly world. 26.
They are indeed powerful, well-proportioned, bright, pure, and immortal;
may those waters, being instructed, teach the husband and wife how to cook the rice-porridge well-protected.
Counted drops pervade the earth, equalized with the vital breaths and the plants;
uncounted, being poured out as golden and pure, they have pervaded all purity. 28.
They rise up, they leap about; heated, they cast forth foam and many drops.
Like a woman who has seen her husband at the proper time, O Waters, become united with these rice grains. 29.
Raise them up from the bottom where they sit; let them touch themselves with water.
I have filled these vessels with this water, as have these measured grains of rice and these quarters of space.
Hand over the axe; let it carry [the wood] quickly. Let the plants be cut without being harmed at their joints.
Soma has attained sovereignty over the plants; may they be free from wrath toward us. 31.
Strew fresh sacrificial grass for the rice; let it be dear to the heart and pleasing to the eye.
Upon it may the gods together with the divine hosts enter; having sat down, let them consume this according to the seasons.
O Lord of the Forest, sit upon the strewn sacrificial grass, measured out by the *agniṣṭoma* chants and the deities.
Like Tvaṣṭṛ, with a well-fashioned form and a sharp axe, we have beheld these [limbs] here within the vessel.
In the sixtieth autumn, may the guardian of the treasure desire it; may he attain heaven through the ripened [fruit].
May the living fathers and sons come to him; O Agni, lead him to this heavenly world. //34//
O Supporter, be supported upon the foundation of the earth; may the deities cause you, the immovable one, to be moved.
May the husband and wife, living with their sons still living, lift you up from the place where the fire was deposited.

Having conquered all the worlds and encountered them all, you have fully satisfied as many desires as there were; plunge into the stirring-ladle and draw this [sacrificial food] up into a single vessel. 36.
Spread it out and extend it before you; sprinkle this vessel with clarified butter.
Like lowing cows toward their young calf, O gods, utter the sound of *hiṅ* over this one. 37.
(38a) You have spread out this world; may the vast, peerless heaven expand.
(38c) Upon it let the buffalo, the fair-winged one, rest; O gods, deliver him over to the deities. 38.
Whatever the wife cooks beyond you, or whatever the husband [cooks] beyond you, O wife—let the two of you join that together; let it be yours in common, as you bring about a single world together.
As many as are upon this earth, our sons who have been born from us—invite them all to the vessel; knowing their kinship, let the young ones come together.
The streams of wealth that are swollen with honey, mixed with ghee, are the naves of immortality.
He wins all of them; in sixty autumns, the guardian of the treasure shall seek him out in heaven.
May the guardian of the treasure seek him as his own hoard; may all others who are not masters remain around him powerless.
Bestowed by us and deposited here, this treasure of heaven has ascended to the three heavens by means of its three sections.
Let the fire burn away the demonic spirit; let the flesh-eating Piśāca who seeks the gods' property be driven away from here.
We thrust him out and ward him off from us; may the Ādityas and the Aṅgirases attend to him. 43.
To the Ādityas and the Aṅgirases, I offer this honey mixed with ghee.
With pure hands, having not struck down the Brahmin, we two, the doers of good deeds, have reached this heaven. 44.
I have attained this supreme section, which Parameṣṭhin reached from that world beyond. Pour out the clarified butter; anoint it well! This is our portion here, O Aṅgiras.
For the sake of truth, for ascetic fervor, and for the deities, we entrust this treasure, this hoard, to you.
Let it not fall away from us in gambling, nor in assembly; let them never release it to another before our time.
I cook; I give. Let my wife be born for my compassionate deed.
A son has been born into the world of youth; may you two both grasp after a later age. 47.
There is no blemish here, nor is there any support; it does not go along with those who act as friends.
This vessel is set down without deficiency; once cooked, the cooked food does not enter back into the cooker. 48.
May we make him dear among those who are dear; let darkness go to those who hate you.
May the cow, the ox, and the birds drive away death and whatever belongs to human [evil]. //49//
The fires know one another, he who dwells among the plants and he who dwells among the rivers;
as many gods as blaze in heaven, gold has become their ripening light. This [gold] has come together within the skin of man; all other animals are without it.
Clothe yourselves in power; this unsewn garment is the face of the rice porridge.

Whatever falsehood I have spoken at dice, or whatever I have spoken in the assembly, or whatever I have spoken as untruth out of a desire for wealth—while weaving together the common thread, may you two deposit all that impurity therein. //52//
Rain down, go even unto the gods; from the skin, you shall rise upward as smoke.
All-pervading, with clarified butter on your back, becoming one of common origin, go to this world. 53.
The heavenly one has fashioned his body in many ways according to his knowledge, assuming a different color within himself.
Purifying himself, he has cast off the black and the white; that which is red, I offer that to you in the fire. 54.
To the eastern quarter, to Agni as overlord, to the black protector, to the Ādityas who possess the arrow—him we entrust to you;
protect him for us until he returns. May he lead us here to old age; may old age deliver us unto death, and then may we be united with the ripened [world]. 55.

To the southern quarter, to Indra as overlord, to Tiraścīrāji as protector, and to Yama who possesses the arrow—him we entrust to you. Guard him for us until he returns; lead him here to old age as our allotted destiny. May old age deliver him unto death, and then may we be united with him once more in the world of the cooked.
To the western quarter, to Varuṇa as the overlord, to the viper as the protector, who possesses food and arrows—him we entrust to you.
Guard him for us until he returns to us.
May he lead us here to old age; may old age deliver us unto death. Then may we be united with what is cooked [ripe].
To the northern quarter, to Soma as overlord, to Svajā as guardian, to the lightning-bolt armed with arrows— to these we entrust him;
protect him for us until he returns. May he lead us here to old age; may old age deliver us unto death. Then may we be united once more with what is cooked [the body]. 58.
For the fixed quarter, for Viṣṇu the overlord, for Kalmāṣagrīva the protector, for the herb-bearing plants—him we entrust to you;
protect him for us until he returns. May he lead us here to old age as ordained; may old age deliver us unto death, and then may we be united with the cooked [world]. 59.
For the upward direction, for Bṛhaspati the overlord, for Śvitra the protector, who possesses rain and arrows—him we entrust to you.
Guard him for us until he returns.
May he lead us here to old age; may old age deliver us unto death. Then may we be united with what is cooked [the ripened reward]. {18}
"I give," he should simply say, and let him acknowledge her; [he gives] a cow to the Brahmins who beg for it—[a gift] which brings offspring and progeny. //1//
He who does not wish to give the cow of the gods to those who are descendants of seers and who beg for it, he barters away his offspring and exhausts his cattle.
With a humpbacked woman his wealth is shattered; with a lame woman he tramples the straw;
with a eunuch his houses are consumed by fire; with a one-eyed woman his own property is lost. //3//
The deep-red one finds the master of cattle from his station; even so, having found the barren cow, you are indeed called "the unassailable. 4.4a-c.
From the treading upon her feet, one finds what is called "withering";
through the failure to name her, those whom she sniffs at with her mouth are utterly destroyed.
He who pierces her ears cuts himself off from the gods;
thinking "I am making a mark," he makes it smaller for himself.
When someone cuts off the hair of this [woman] for some purpose or other, then the colts die and the predatory wolf slays the calves. //7//
When the crow has pecked at the hair of this woman while her husband is away, from that [act] boys die; the wasting disease (*yakṣma*) finds him through his lack of mindfulness.
When the slave-girl throws together her cleansing of this [vessel] with dung, from that a misshapen thing is born; therefore, one should not look upon it out of sin.
As she is born, the cow gives birth to the gods together with the Brahmins;
therefore, she must be given to the Brahmins, for they say this is the protection of one's own property. Those who come to her as a prize—their cow has been created by the gods.
They say that he who treats her with hostility incurs the censure of the Brahmans. 11.
He who does not wish to give a cow to the descendants of seers when they come begging for it from the gods— he cuts himself off from the gods and incurs the wrath of the Brahmins.
If one who possesses this wealth of choice should desire another, that ungiven [wealth] harms the man, for he does not wish to give what has been asked for. 13.
Just as a treasure is deposited for the Brahmins, so is the barren cow;
they seek her out wherever she may be born. 14.
The Brahmins who attack the barren cow destroy their own; just as one might overcome them by means of another, such is the suppression of this [cow]. 15.15
Even if she has been unobserved for three years, she should indeed be treated [as such];
and one should know her as a barren cow (*vaśā*), O Nārada; then the Brahmins will come here.
To him who speaks of this hidden treasure of the gods while she is powerless,
both Bhava and Śarva shall pursue him and discharge their arrows.
He who does not know her udder, nor even her teats—
for him she yields with both [only] if he is able to grant his wish.
The one who is difficult to overcome lies upon him; he does not wish to give what has been asked for.
His desires do not succeed—that thing which he wishes to accomplish without having given it away. //19//
The gods, having made the Brahmin their mouth, begged for the cow;
to all of them, the human gave the cow, and thus he goes down into their displeasure. He goes down into the displeasure of the cattle, having given the cow to the Brahmins.
If a mortal treats with hostility the portion assigned to the gods, [he incurs their wrath]. 21.
Even if a hundred other Brahmins were to beg for the cow from the owner of cattle, the gods said of her: "She belongs indeed to one who knows thus. 22.
If one, having failed to give to such a knower, instead gives a cow to others, then the Earth, together with the gods, will stand as a difficult obstacle for him in his dwelling. 23.
The gods entreated the cow at the very beginning when she was born;
Nārada, together with the gods, brought her forth, knowing her as such. 24.
A barren cow makes a man childless and destitute of cattle;
moreover, when she is begged for by Brahmins, she causes him to lose what is dear to him.
To Agni and Soma, to Kāma, to Mitra, and to Varuṇa—the Brāhmaṇas make their requests to these; he who does not give cuts himself off from them. 26.
As long as her owner does not himself hear these verses, so long may one move among his cattle; but once he has heard them, he shall no longer dwell in his house.
The gods, being provoked to anger, cut off the life-span and prosperity of him who, having overheard this verse, then wandered among the cattle. //28//
The barren cow wanders in many ways; she is the treasure deposited for the gods.
Reveal your forms when he seeks to strike down our standing place. 29.
When she reveals her self, desiring to destroy his standing place, then indeed the cow sets her mind upon the Brahmins for the sake of being sacrificed.
(30) With her mind she plans it; that [plan] goes even to the gods.
Then the Brahmins approach the cow to beg for it. 31.
By the utterance of *svadhā* for the ancestors, by sacrifice for the deities,
and by giving for the mother cow, the Rājanya does not incur her wrath.
The cow is the mother of the kṣatriya; thus was she produced in the beginning.
They say that what is given to the brahmins is her non-delivery. 33.
Just as one might snatch the clarified butter held in the ladle for Agni,
even so does he who does not give seize the cow from the Brahmins for Agni.
In this world, a well-milking cow with a calf that eats sacrificial cake stands near him; she, the wish-granting cow, yields all desires for him who bestows gifts.
In the realm of King Yama, she yields and grants all desires to the one who has offered her;
yet they say that for the one who restrains her when she is asked, it is a world of hell.
Being impregnated, she moves about in anger like a barren cow for her owner; let him who considers her a barren cow be bound in the snares of death. 37.
But he who, thinking her barren, cooks a cow for him— Bṛhaspati makes even his sons and grandsons beg for alms.
This great cow, moving among the cattle, burns with heat;
moreover, she milks poison for the ill-disposed owner of the herd.

That which is given to the Brahmins becomes dear to the cattle; moreover, that which is an oblation for the gods is dear to the barren cow. The barren cows whom the gods fashioned, having emerged from the sacrifice—
Nārada brought forth from among them the terrifying Viliptī. 41.
The gods deliberated upon her: "Is she submissive or unsubmissive?
Nārada said to them: "She is the most submissive among the submissive. //42//
How many barren cows, O Nārada, do you know that are born of man?
I ask you, the wise one: of which may a non-Brahmin not eat? //43//
O Bṛhaspati,
one who is not a Brāhmaṇa should not eat the omentum of a cow that has miscarried or a barren cow, if he desires prosperity.
Homage be to you, O Nārada, who are well-knowing and self-controlled! Among these [powers], which is the most terrifying, by failing to give which one would suffer defeat? //45//
The cow that is smeared with [blood], O Bṛhaspati, and likewise the cow that miscarries after giving birth— the non-Brāhmaṇa who desires prosperity should not eat of her.
There are indeed three kinds of barren cows (*vaśā*): the smeared cow (*viliptī*), the cow that has recently calved (*sūtavaśā*), and the barren cow (*vaśā*).
One should bestow these upon the Brahmins; such a gift is inviolable toward Prajāpati.

"If he is asked, let him think: 'This is the sacrificial offering for you, O Brahmins,' even if they should ask him for a barren cow that was in the house of one who gave nothing to the fearsome [deity]."
The gods spoke to Vaśā, "She has not given to us," being thus provoked;
by means of these verses, Bheda indeed perished because of her. 49.
Furthermore, when requested by Indra, Bheda did not take this cow;
therefore, the gods cut away that offense from him, leaving me superior.
Those malicious revilers who speak against the giving of the barren cow— those wretches,
through their lack of understanding, cut themselves off by the wrath of Indra.
Those who, having driven away the lord of cattle, say, "Do not give him," go about with thoughtlessness, avoiding the missile of Rudra.
Whether an offering has been made or not, if one cooks a victim for oneself alone,
having offended the gods together with the Brahmins, he falls crookedly from the worlds.
Created through toil and austerity, they were discovered by Brahmā and have taken refuge in the Ṛta.
Enveloped by truth, clothed in splendor, and surrounded by glory. //2//
Enveloped by the *svadhā* offering, clothed in faith, guarded by consecration, established in the sacrifice—this world is the finale. //3//
The Brahmin is the lord who has attained the state of Brahman. //4//
For a Kṣatriya who seizes that Brahmin’s cow and defeats the Brāhmaṇa, [the following occurs]. //5//
Truthfulness departs, as do heroism, merit, and fortune.
(6) Vitality, brilliance, endurance, strength, speech, sensory power, prosperity, and righteousness. (7)
The priesthood and the nobility, the ruling power and the commoners, brilliance and renown, splendor and wealth. //8//
Life-span and form, name and fame, out-breath and in-breath, eye and ear. //9//
Milk and juice, food and the eating of food, cosmic order and truth, what is desired and what is accomplished, offspring and cattle. //10//
All these [powers] depart from the Kṣatriya who seizes the Brahman-cow and defeats the Brāhmaṇa.
(11) This very Brahman-cow is terrifying, possessing deadly poison; she is a manifest *kṛtyā* (sorcery), covered with the *kūlbaja* plant. (12)
In her are all terrors and all deaths. //13//
In her are all cruelties; in her are all murders of men. //14//
She, being seized as the Brahman-cow by the oppressor of the Brahman and the scorner of the gods, drags him into the path of death.
For that curse brings a hundredfold slaughter; for it is the destruction of the oppressor of the Brahmin.
Therefore, indeed, the cow of the Brahmins is invincible to one who understands this. 17.
The thunderbolt, Vaiśvānara, running, has been raised up. 18.
The weapon, uprooting the hooves, the great deity gazes upon it.
Sharp-edged as a razor, looking on and bellowing, she flashes forth.
Death, the fierce god, utters the *hiṅ* sound; she who tosses about the tail.
Total loss, making the ears ring; royal consumption, causing [the urine] to flow. //22//
The Meni, while being milked, has been milked as the head-ailment. //23//
Sitting down, she stands near him; having been touched, she becomes a mutual combatant.
The arrow being bound to the mouth, the misfortune being struck down. //25//
The poison of misfortune falls; darkness has fallen. //26//

Following after his vital breaths, the Brahman-cow destroys the one who injures the Brahman. (27) When she is being torn apart, it is enmity; when she is being divided, it is the portion for the grandson. (28)
The weapon of the gods being carried away, misfortune has been taken away. //29//
When evil is being imposed, it results in harshness when it is being laid down. //30//
As the poison departs, the fever has departed. //31//
May misfortune and bad dreams be cooked away as they are driven forth.
The root-destroying earth, while being prepared, has been fully prepared.
The unconscious snake, being pulled out by its scent, was drawn forth with pain. //34//
Non-existence being brought near is defeat already brought near. //35//
The enraged Śarva is being crushed; Śimidā is being crushed to pieces. //36//
Non-turning is that which is being eaten; destruction is that which has been eaten. //37//

The Brahman-cow, when eaten, cuts away from this world and from yonder world the one who treats the Brahmin with contempt. (38) Its slaughter is sorcery; its killing is a malevolent charm; its entrails are a secret spell. (39)
Unwelcome and rejected. //40//
Agni, having become a consumer of raw flesh, enters the Brahmin’s cow and devours the oppressor of Brahmins. //41//
He cuts away all her limbs, joints, and roots. 42.
He severs his paternal kin and alienates his maternal kin. //43//
The Brahman-cow, when not returned by a Kṣatriya to the one who violated the Veda, consumes all the relatives and marriage-allies of that oppressor of Brahmins. 44.
He makes him homeless, without cattle, and without offspring; he becomes one who lacks further support and is diminished. //45//
If a Kṣatriya seizes the cow of a Brāhmaṇa who knows thus, (46) vultures will quickly make a feast of his body upon its slaughter. (47)
Swiftly indeed they dance around his funeral pyre—the long-haired women, beating their breasts with their hands and committing the Ailaba sin.
Indeed, quickly will wolves make a howling in his dwellings. 49.
They quickly ask him about that which was there: "Is this now that very thing? //50//
Cut it! Cut it down! Cut it apart! Burn it up! Burn it away!
O daughter of Aṅgiras, subdue the oppressor of the Brahmin who seizes [the property].
For you are called Vaiśvadevī, a magical spell (*kṛtyā*) enveloped in a *kūlbaja* [incantation]. //53//
Burning, fiercely burning, it is the thunderbolt of the Brahman. //54//
Becoming death with razor-sharp edges, run forth! 55.
You bestow upon the victors splendor, the merit of sacrifices and charitable works, and the fulfillment of their aspirations.
Having taken what was won from this world, you bestow it upon that world beyond. //57//
O inviolable one, become a tracker of the path for the Brahmin’s curse.
Become an arrow-shaft, become a missile; become one whose poison is sin. //59//
O inviolable one, strike off the head of the oppressor of the Brahmin, the evildoer, the scorner of the gods, and the one who offers no gifts.
May Agni burn the ill-minded one who has been crushed and trampled by you. {29} Tear him apart, tear him asunder, tear him to pieces! Burn him, burn him up, burn him completely! {62}
O divine cow, burn up the oppressor of Brahmins from the very root.
As if one were to depart from the abode of Yama, from the worlds of evil, to the far distance.
Thus, O inviolable goddess, [deal with] him who is a violator of sacred knowledge, a committer of offense, a scorner of the gods, and one who bestows no gifts.
With the hundred-jointed thunderbolt, sharp and with a razor-edged tip.
Strike down the shoulders; strike down the head! 67.
Cut his body hairs; strip away his skin.
Cut away his flesh; tear out his sinews.
Crush his bones; extract his marrow.
Relax all her limbs and joints.
May Agni, the consumer of raw flesh, drive him away from the earth; may Vāyu burn him up from the great expanse of the intermediate space.
May Sūrya drive him away from heaven; may he burn him down.
Arise, O vigorous one who art within the waters; enter this kingdom, which is full of prosperity.
May he who is the Red One, who has generated all this, sustain you well for the sake of the kingdom.
Upward has Vāja come, who is within the waters; ascend to the clans that have their origin in you.
Holding Soma, establish here the waters, the plants, the cattle—both four-footed and two-footed.
O you fierce Maruts, sons of Pṛśni, with Indra as your ally, crush the enemies.
O bounteous Maruts, may your ruddy steed hear us; you who are thrice-seven in number, you who delight in sweet pleasures. 3.
The red one has ascended; the embryo has ascended to the lap of the women, the source of births.
With them, firmly grasped, he found the six expanses; beholding a path, he brought the kingdom here.
(5a) Rohita has brought your kingdom here; the adversaries have been scattered; fearlessness has come to you.
(5c) For you, may Heaven and Earth, with their rich and powerful hymns, milk out your desire here.
Rohita generated heaven and earth; there Parameṣṭhin stretched out the thread. There the one-footed goat took his stand; he made heaven and earth firm by his strength.
Rohita has made firm heaven and earth; by him the sky was propped up, by him the vault of heaven.
By him the intermediate space and the regions were measured out; through him the gods found immortality.
The ruddy one has touched the multiform world, fashioning both the ascending and the descending growths.
Having ascended to heaven with great majesty, may your kingdom be anointed with milk and ghee. 8.
(9) Those shoots of yours, those sprouts, those upward-growths by which you fill the sky and the intermediate space—
with the sacred word (*brahman*) and the milk of those, increasing in strength, remain watchful for the clan and the kingdom of the Red One.
Those clans of yours that arose from fervor (*tapas*), following the calf, the *gāyatrī*—they have come here.
Let them enter you with a gracious mind; let the mother come together with the red calf.
The youthful seer (*kavi*), the red one, has stood erect upon the firmament, generating all forms.
With his sharp radiance Agni shines forth; in the third realm of space he manifests his beloved splendors.

The thousand-horned bull, Jātavedas, invoked with clarified butter, whose back is laden with Soma, the possessor of excellent heroes—may he not abandon me, for I am your suppliant; may I not forsake you. Bestow upon me the nourishment of cattle and the nourishment of heroes. 12.
Rohita is the progenitor of the sacrifice and its mouth; for Rohita I offer with speech, with hearing, and with mind.
The gods go toward Rohita with well-disposed minds; may he cause me to ascend through ascents to the assembly. 13.13
Rohita distributed the sacrifice for Viśvakarman; from him these splendors have come to us.
I would proclaim your origin within the expanse of the world. //14//
The Bṛhatī and the Paṅkti have ascended unto thee with splendor, O Jātavedas; the Kakubh has ascended unto thee;
the Uṣṇih and the syllable Vaṣaṭ have ascended unto thee; Rohita has ascended unto thee together with seed. 15.
This one clothes himself in the womb of the earth; this one clothes himself in heaven and this one in the intermediate space.
This one has pervaded the worlds of light upon the summit of the sun.
O Lord of Speech, may the earth be gentle for us; may our womb and our bed be gentle and most auspicious.
May our vital breath remain right here in this friendship. O Supreme Lord, may Agni endow you with long life and splendor. 17.

O Lord of Speech, the five seasons which belong to Viśvakarman and have come together around us—let our vital breath remain right here in this friendship. May that Parameṣṭhin, O Rohita, endow you with long life and splendor. 18.
O Lord of Speech, grant us goodwill and a gracious mind; produce cattle for us in our stalls and offspring in our wombs.
Let vital breath remain right here in this friendship of ours; may you, O Parameṣṭhin, endow me with long life and splendor. 19.19
May the god Savitṛ encompass you, may Agni, and may Mitra and Varuṇa endow you with splendor.
Treading upon all enemies, come hither; you have made this kingdom full of prosperity. O red horse, whom the spotted deer draws as a side-horse at your chariot—
Beautiful, you go forth, letting the waters flow. //21//
The ruddy Rohiṇī, devoted to her vow, the golden-hued, lofty, and full of splendor, is the patroness of the Red One.
Through her may we win spoils of every form; through her may we overcome all hostile armies. 22.
This is the seat of Rohiṇī, the red one; that is the path of the red steed by which the speckled one goes.
The Gandharvas, the Kaśyapas, lead her up; the seers guard her with vigilance. 23.
The immortal, radiant bay horses of the Sun always draw his easy-moving chariot with its banners.
The god Rohita, the drinker of clarified butter, shining brightly, has entered the spotted cow of heaven.
The ruddy bull with sharp horns who has encompassed both Agni and Sūrya—he who supports the earth and the sky: from him the gods release their creations. //25//
Rohita has ascended to heaven from the great ocean;
Rohita has climbed every climbing plant.
Measure out the milk-laden, ghee-dripping cow, this one that belongs to the gods and is never-failing.
Let Indra drink the Soma; let there be peace; let Agni offer praise; drive away the adversaries. 27.
Enkindled by fuel, increasing with fuel, strengthened by ghee, and offered ghee—may Agni, the overcomer, the all-conquering one, slay my rivals who are my enemies. 28.
Let him strike them down, let the enemy burn up him who attacks us;
with the flesh-eating fire, we utterly consume our rivals. 29.
O Indra, wielder of the arm, strike down those who face downward with your thunderbolt!
Then, by the splendors of Agni, I consume my rivals.
(30) O Agni, cast our rivals beneath us; O Bṛhaspati, cause our kinsman who seeks to rise up to falter. (31)
May Indra and Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa, fall low, no longer showing defiance. //31//
Rising, O divine Sūrya, strike down my rivals;
strike them down with this stone! Let them go to the lowest darkness.
The calf of Virāj, the bull of hymns, with a bright back, has ascended the intermediate space.
With clarified butter they sing praise to the Sun; the calf, being the sacred word (*brahman*), they cause to grow by means of the sacred word. 33.
Ascend to heaven and ascend to earth; ascend to sovereignty and ascend to wealth.
Ascend to progeny and ascend to immortality; with the Rohita, touch thy body. 34.
The gods who, as upholders of the kingdom, go forth around the sun—with them, may this Rohita, being in harmony with you and well-disposed, bestow sovereignty upon you. //35//
The sacrifices, purified by prayer, carry you upward; the bay steeds carry you along the path.
You shine across the ocean, over the surging flood.
Upon the ruddy ones, heaven and earth are established—the winners of wealth, the winners of cattle, the winners of spoils.
He whose births are a thousand and seven; may I proclaim your navel upon the expanse of the world. 37.
Glorious you go to the intermediate directions and the cardinal directions; glorious among cattle and among the people;
glorious in the lap of Aditi, the earth—may I be as beautiful as Savitṛ. //38//
Being there, you perceive these things here;
from here they behold the radiant sun in heaven, the wise one.
As a god, you cause the gods to flourish; you move within the ocean.
They kindle the same fire; the supreme sages know it.
Beneath the farther shore and beyond this nearer one, the cow has risen up, bearing her calf with her foot.
Whither has she gone, turning away? To which side has she departed? Where indeed does she bring forth, for she is not in this herd?
She has become one-footed, two-footed, four-footed, eight-footed, and nine-footed;
she is the thousand-syllabled row of the world, and from her the oceans flow forth.
Ascending to heaven, the immortal one has favored my speech;
the sacrifices purified by prayer carry you upward, and the bay steeds carry you along the path.
I know that immortality of yours, O Deathless One, which is your ascent into heaven;
I know that dwelling place of yours in the highest firmament.
The Sun looks beyond the sky; the Sun looks beyond the earth; the Sun looks beyond the waters.
The Sun, the sole eye of all that exists, has ascended to the great heaven. 45.
The wide expanses became the enclosing sticks; the earth was fashioned as the sacrificial altar. Thereupon Rohita established these two fires: the cold and the heat.

Having established frost and heat, having fashioned the sacrificial posts as mountains, the two fires, Agni and Varuṇa, sacrificed with the rain and the clarified butter of the ruddy, light-finding [soma]. 47.
By the sacred formulation (*brahman*) of the light-finding, ruddy [horse], Agni is kindled;
from him came the heat, from him the cold, and from him the sacrifice was born. 48.

The two fires, increased by the sacred word (*brahman*), grown by the sacred word, and offered to with the sacred word; kindled by the sacred word, the two fires have sacrificed for Rohita, the finder of heaven. 49.
One is concentrated in truth; another is kindled in the waters. These two fires, kindled by the *brahman*, perform sacrifice for the ruddy one who finds the light of heaven.
He whom the wind fans, whom Indra and Brahmaṇaspati [fan]—
The two fires, kindled by Brahmā, perform the sacrifice for the ruddy one who finds the light of heaven.
Having fashioned the earth as the sacrificial altar and made heaven the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*),
having made the sun that fire, Rohita performed the sacrifice with rain as the clarified butter (*ājya*), making everything possessed of a self.
The rain was the sacrificial butter, Agni the heat; the earth became the altar.
There, with his songs, Agni fashioned these mountains upright.
Having fashioned the heights with hymns, Rohita spoke to the earth:
"In you let all this be born—whatever has been and whatever is yet to be."
That sacrifice, the first to exist, was born as that which is yet to be; from it indeed was born all this, whatever shines here, brought forth by the seer Rohita. //55//
And he who kicks a cow with his foot and urinates toward the sun—for him I cut off your root; I shall not create another shadow for you.
(57) You who pass me by, between my shadow and the fire— I cut off your root; you shall cast no further shadow.
O divine Sūrya, whatever bad dream, impurity, or misfortunes lie between you and me today—those we wipe away. //58//
May we not stray from the path, nor from the sacrifice, O Indra, we who possess the Soma;
may no enemies stand before us.
May we partake of that oblation which is the thread that accomplishes the sacrifice, stretched out among the gods.
His bright rays rise up, shining in the sky.
Of Āditya, who beholds men, whose laws are great, and who is bounteous. //1//
We praise Sūrya, the guardian of the world, who makes the quarters known with his light, who flies swiftly with beautiful wings across the ocean, he who illuminates all the directions with his rays.
When you go swiftly eastward and westward by your own power, you fashion the two days of different forms through your creative might.
That, O Āditya, is your greatness; that is your great glory, that as the one you are born encompassing the entire world.
The many tawny mares carry him, the wise one, the deliverer, the radiant;
he whom Atri drew up from the stream to heaven—you, such as you are, they see as you come to the race. //4//
May they not deceive you as you go around the racecourse; cross over the difficult passage swiftly for your well-being.
O Sūrya, as you travel, measuring out heaven and the goddess earth, and day and night. //5//
May there be well-being for your chariot, O Sūrya, as you travel, by which you swiftly encompass both ends [of heaven and earth].
Those bay horses of yours that carry you—the swiftest—whether they be a hundred steeds or many sevenfold.
Mount, O Sūrya, the comfortable chariot—radiant, pleasant, a good bearer, and swift;
that which your bay horses, the best at drawing, carry: whether they be a hundred steeds or many seven.

The sun has yoked seven bay mares to his chariot to travel—the great ones with golden skins. The bright one has been released from beyond the region; having shaken off the darkness, the god has ascended to heaven. 8.
With his lofty banner the god has come; he has dispelled the darkness and turned toward the light.
That divine eagle, the hero, son of Aditi, has looked out upon all beings. 9.
Rising, you stretch out your rays; you nourish all forms.
With your power (*kratunā*), you shine across both oceans, encompassing all worlds as you blaze.
These two move one after the other by means of their creative power (*māyā*); like two playing children, they go around the ocean.
One beholds all beings; the other, golden-hued mares carry him away.
Tvaṣṭṛ has established you in heaven so that Sūryā may be made into a month. Thus, well-sustained, you go forth, heating and looking down upon all beings. 12.
You flow toward both ends as a calf toward its two mothers;
surely those gods have known this sacred formulation (*brahman*) from of old.
That which rests along the ocean, the Sun desires to win it; his path is stretched out vast, both the eastern and the western.
He attains him by means of his impulses; from there, he does not depart. By that, they do not fail to obtain a portion of the nectar of the gods. //15//
Upwards his rays bear aloft that god who knows all beings,
the Sun, so that everyone may behold him.
Those stars go away with the nights like thieves,
before the Sun who beholds all things.
His banners have been seen; his rays extend across the people, shining like blazing fires. //18//
O Sūrya, you are the one who carries us across, visible to all, the maker of light; you illuminate the entire radiant realm.
Facing the clans of the gods, facing the human races, you rise up;
facing all, you look upon the light of heaven.
O Purifier, with that eye wherewith you look upon the active people...
O Varuṇa, you behold it. //21//
O Sūrya, you rise up toward the sky, across the broad expanse, measuring out the days with your rays, beholding all living beings.
Seven bay mares carry you in your chariot, O divine Sūrya, you whose hair is flame, the far-seeing one. //23//
The Sun has yoked the seven bright mares, the daughters of his chariot;
with them, as his own team, he goes forth.
The ruddy one, performing asceticism, ascended to heaven by means of his austerity. He returns to his source and is born again; he has become the sovereign lord of the gods. //25//
He who is the observer of all people and whose face is turned everywhere, whose hands are on every side and whose reach extends in all directions—
he, the one God, generating heaven and earth, brings them together with his arms and his wings.
The one-footed has stepped out further than the two-footed; the two-footed follows behind the three-footed.
Indeed, the two-footed has stepped out further than the six-footed; they rest their bodies upon the one-footed.
When the tireless one, moving, has mounted his bay steeds, he assumes two forms as he shines.
Rising with a banner, overcoming the regions, O Āditya, you illuminate all the slopes.
Truly great art thou, O Sūrya; truly great art thou, O Āditya.
Great is the majesty of thee who art great; thou, O Āditya, art great. //29//
You shine in heaven, you shine in the intermediate space; O Bird, you shine upon the earth, you shine within the waters.
You have pervaded both oceans with your radiance; you are a god among gods, a mighty bull, the winner of the light of heaven.
Moving hither from afar, traversing the middle of the path, the swift and wise Bird flies on.
Viṣṇu, discerning through his power and standing firm, overcomes with his signal all that moves. //31//
Variegated, observant, the buffalo, the fair-winged one, illuminating both worlds and the mid-air;
the sun, clothed in day and night, surpasses all heroic powers as he moves around them.
Sharp, gleaming, sharpening his body, hastening along the downward slopes, bestowing gifts;
luminous, winged, mighty, bestowing vital strength, he has pervaded all the quarters as he ordains them. //33//
The wondrous banner of the gods, the radiant face, the sun rises toward the quarters of space;
the maker of day, with his splendors, has overcome the darkness—the bright one has crossed over all misfortunes.
The brilliant face of the gods has risen, the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni.
Sūrya has filled heaven, earth, and the intermediate space; he is the soul of all that moves and stands. 35.
We behold you, the ruddy, fair-winged bird flying aloft, crossing through the midst of heaven, shining brightly—whom they call Savitṛ, the eternal light which Atri discovered. 36.
On the back of heaven, I, fearing and seeking protection, approach the fair-winged one, the son of Aditi, as he flies.
O Sūrya, extend long life for us; may we not come to harm, but abide in your favor. 37.
The two wings of this golden swan, flying to heaven, extend over a thousand days’ journey.
Laying all the gods upon his breast, he goes beholding all the worlds. 38.
Rohita became Time; Rohita was Prajāpati in the beginning. Rohita is the mouth of sacrifices; Rohita brought down the light of heaven.
The world became ruddy; the ruddy one heated the sky intensely.
The ruddy one traverses the earth and the ocean with his rays. 40.
The ruddy one, the sovereign lord of heaven, traversed all the quarters.
He guards the sky, the ocean, and the earth—indeed, every living being. //41//
Ascending the lofty heights, the bright and tireless one assumes two forms as he shines;
wonderful, observant, and mighty, possessing the speed of the wind, he blazes over as many worlds as there are.
One [part] of him goes forward, the other is cast around, as the buffalo adjusts himself to day and night.
Seeking aid, we invoke Sūrya, who dwells in the mid-air and knows the way. 43.
The Earth-supporting Buffalo, the unerring-eyed path for the supplicant, has encompassed all.
Seeing all, the benevolent and worshipful one—may he hear this which I speak. 44.
His greatness encompasses the earth and the ocean, shining forth with light around the sky and the intermediate space.
Seeing all things, he who is benevolent and worthy of sacrifice—may he hear this which I speak. 45.
Agni has been awakened by the fuel of the people, facing the Dawn as she approaches like a milch-cow.
Like young birds flying up toward a branch, his rays stream forth toward the firmament.
He who brought these two, heaven and earth, into being—he who, having made them a garment, clothes himself in the worlds.
In whom the six wide quarters abide, whom the bird surveys from afar—
this is the offense against that god when one oppresses a Brahmin who knows thus.
From whom the winds blow in due season, from whom the oceans flow forth.
This is the offense against that enraged god, who oppresses a Brahmin possessing such knowledge.
O Rohita, cause him to tremble; destroy him; cast your snares upon the oppressor of Brahmins! 2.
He who slays and yet gives life, from whom all beings draw their breath—against that god, when he is enraged, is this offense: he who oppresses a Brahmin who possesses such knowledge.
O Rohita, make him tremble, destroy him; cast your snares upon the oppressor of the sacred word (*brahmajyasa*). 3.

He who satisfies heaven and earth with his out-breath (*prāṇa*), and fills the belly of the ocean with his in-breath (*apāna*)—this is the offense against that god when one, knowing him thus, oppresses a Brahmin. O Rohita, cause him to tremble, destroy him, and cast your snares upon the oppressor of Brahmins! 4.
In whom Virāj, Parameṣṭhin, Prajāpati, and Agni Vaiśvānara together with Paṅkti are established; he who seizes the breath of the highest and the splendor of the supreme—
this is the offense against that enraged deity when one oppresses a Brahmin who knows thus.
In whom the six expanses and the five directions are established, the four waters, and the three syllables of the sacrifice;
he who, enraged, looked between the two worlds with his eye—
this is the offense against that angry god, whoever oppresses a Brahmin who knows thus.
He who is the eater of food, the lord of food, and who is Brahmanaspati;
he who is the past, the future, and the lord of the world—
this is the offense against that enraged god when one oppresses a Brahmin who knows thus.
He who fashions the thirteenth month, measured by days and nights and consisting of thirty parts—for that god, when enraged, this is the offense: he who oppresses a Brahmin who knows thus.
O Rohita, cause him to tremble, destroy him; cast your snares upon the oppressor of the sacred word (*brahmajyasya*). 8.
The black path, the bay birds with beautiful wings, clothed in the waters, fly up to heaven;
they have returned from the seat of *ṛta*.
This is the offense against that enraged god, who oppresses a Brahmin possessing such knowledge.
That which is your radiant, bright realm, O Kaśyapa, that which is well-joined, abundant, and of wondrous luster, wherein the seven suns are placed together—

all this belongs to that god when he is provoked to anger by one who oppresses a Brahmin who knows thus. O Rohita, cause him to tremble, destroy him, and cast your snares upon the oppressor of the sacred word!

The *Bṛhat* hymn clothes him from the front, and the *Rathantara* receives him from behind; he is ever clothed in light and remains vigilant. This is the offense against that god when one, being angry, oppresses a Brahmin who possesses such knowledge.

The *Bṛhat* was on one wing, the *Rathantara* on the other; together they were strong when the gods brought forth the Red One (*rohit*). This is the offense against that angry god, who oppresses a Brahmin possessing such knowledge.

He becomes Varuṇa in the evening; he becomes Agni; rising in the morning, he becomes Mitra. Having become Savitṛ, he moves through the mid-air; having become Indra, he burns from the middle of the sky.
This is the offense against that god when one oppresses a Brahmin who knows thus.
The two wings of this golden swan, flying to heaven, extend across a thousand leagues.
Laying all the gods upon his breast, he goes beholding all the worlds.
This is the offense against that god when one oppresses a Brahmin who knows thus.
This is that god within the waters, thousand-rooted, jointed, the devourer;
he who brought forth this entire world.
This is the offense against that god when one in anger oppresses a Brahmin who knows thus.
The bay steeds, swift-gliding, carry the bright one— the god blazing with splendor in heaven—
whose upward bodies heat the sky and who shines hitherward with golden wings.
This is the offense against that enraged god, when one oppresses a Brahmin who knows thus.
By which the bay horses carry the Ādityas, by which many go forth knowing the sacrifice;
that single light which shines manifoldly—
this is the offense against that god when one oppresses a Brahmin who knows thus.
Seven harness the one-wheeled chariot; a single horse draws it, having seven names.
The wheel has three naves, is undecaying and invincible, upon which all these worlds stand.
This is the offense against that enraged god, who oppresses a Brahmin possessing such knowledge.
Yoked in eight ways, the fierce bearer draws [the chariot]; he is the father of the gods, the progenitor of inspired thoughts.
Measuring out the thread of cosmic order (*ṛta*) with his mind, Mātariśvan blows through all the quarters.
This is the offense against that god when one in anger oppresses a Brahmin who knows thus.
Woven together along all directions, within the *gāyatrī* as the embryo of immortality—this is the offense against that god when one, knowing this, harms a Brahmin.
O Rohita, make him tremble, consume him; cast your snares upon the oppressor of Brahmins! 20. {13}

Three sunsets, three dawns, the three realms, and the three parts of heaven—O Agni, we know your triple birth; we know the triple origins of the gods. This is the offense against that god when one oppresses a Brahmin who knows thus.
He who, at his birth, spread out the earth and established the ocean in the mid-air—this is the offense against that god when one in anger oppresses a Brahmin who knows thus.
O Rohita, cause him to tremble, destroy him; cast your snares upon the oppressor of Brahmins! 22.
O Agni, established by rites and signs, you, the hymn, kindled, have shone forth in heaven.
Why did the Maruts, sons of Pṛśni, sing toward [you] when the gods generated the ruddy one?
This is the offense against that god when one oppresses a Brahmin who knows thus.
He who gives self and gives strength, whose command all the gods revere— he who rules over these two-footed beings and those four-footed;
against that god, when he is enraged, is this offense committed by one who oppresses a Brahmin who knows thus.
The one-footed has stepped out further than the two-footed; the two-footed follows after the three-footed.
The four-footed, listening to the call of the two-footed, stands waiting while beholding their row.
This is the offense against that angry god, who oppresses a Brahmin possessing such knowledge.
Arjuna, the son of Kṛṣṇā, was born as the calf of the Night.
He indeed ascends to heaven; the ruddy one has climbed the heights.
He goes forth, Savitṛ, from the back of heaven, looking down upon the sun.
Brought by its rays from the sky, Mahendra comes, encompassed.
He is the Ordainer, he is the Sustainer; he is Vāyu and the exalted sky.
He is Aryaman, he is Varuṇa, he is Rudra, he is Mahādeva. //4//
He is Agni, he is Sūrya, and he indeed is Mahāyama. //5//
The calves, ten in number, stand near him, joined together with a single head.
From behind they stretch it forward, that which rises and shines forth. //7//
This host of Maruts belongs to him; he goes along fashioned like a sling.
Brought by its rays, the sky is filled; Mahendra comes, encompassed.
Of this [body], these nine sheaths are established as supports, arranged in a ninefold manner.
He looks out upon his offspring, both that which breathes and that which does not.
This very power has arrived; he is that one, the sole increaser, truly alone. //12//
In him these deities become unified.
(13) Fame, glory, water, the firmament, the splendor of the Brahman, food, and the eating of food. (14)
He who knows this god as the one-and-only. //15//
A second is not spoken of, nor a third, nor even a fourth.
It is not called the fifth, nor the sixth, nor even the seventh.
He is not called the eighth, nor the ninth, nor even the tenth. //18//
He sees everything: both that which breathes and that which does not. 19.
This very power has come hither; he is that one, the sole increaser, truly alone.
In him all the gods become unified.

(21) The sacred word (*brahman*) and ascetic heat (*tapas*), renown (*kīrti*) and glory (*yaśas*), the waters (*ambhas*) and the sky (*nabhas*), the splendor of the Brahmin (*brāhmaṇavarcasa*) and food (*anna*) and the eating of food (*annādya*). (2)
The past and the future, faith and inclination, heaven and the ancestral offering. //23//
He who knows this god as the one-and-only. //24//
He alone is death; he is immortality; he is the vast; he is the Rakṣas. //25//
That Rudra is the bestower of wealth; he is joined with the invocation of "namas" at the giving of wealth and with the exclamation "vaṣaṭ."
All these sorcerers sit waiting for his command.
All those constellations, together with the moon, are under his control.
He was indeed born from the day; therefore, the day was born from him.
He was indeed born from the night; therefore, the night was born. //30//
He was indeed born from the intermediate space; from him the intermediate space was born. //31//
He was indeed born from Vāyu; therefore, Vāyu was born from him. //32//
He was indeed born from heaven; from him heaven was born. //33//
He was indeed born from the quarters; therefore, the quarters were born from him. //34//
He was indeed born from the earth; therefore, the earth was born from him. //35//
He indeed was born from Agni; therefore Agni was born from him. //36//
He was indeed born from the waters; from him the waters were born.
He was indeed born from the Ṛg-verses; therefore, the Ṛg-verses were born from him.
He was indeed born from the sacrifice; from him the sacrifice was born. //39//
That is his sacrifice, that is his sacrifice; that has been made the head of the sacrifice.
He thunders, he flashes forth lightning, and he hurls the thunderbolt.
Whether for an evil man or a noble one, for a human or for an asura. //42//
Whether you perform your work upon the plants, or whether you rain down with blessing, or whether you have strengthened the people. //43//
So great, O Maghavan, is your majesty; even a hundred of your bodies are yours.
(45) Untie those bonds of thine, whether they be bound fast or even a hundred million.
(46) Greater art thou than Namuci, O Indra; greater art thou than deaths, O Indra.
"Greater than the Lord of malice is your power; O Indra, you are all-pervading and sovereign"—thus do we worship you. 47.
Homage be to you! Look, look at me; look!
With food, with fame, with splendor, and with the luster of a brahmin. //49//
O Ambhas, O Ama, O Mahas, O Sahas—we worship you thus. //50//
"O Ambhas, Aruṇa, Rajata, and Sahas, as such we worship you.
(51) "O Uru, Pṛthu, Subhū, and Bhū, as such we worship you. (52)
We worship you as the wide expanse, the opening, and the world. //53//
We worship you as Bhavadvasu, Idadvasu, Saṃyadvasu, and Āyadvasu. //54//
Homage be to you! Look, look at me; look! //55//
With food, with glory, with splendor, and with the luster of a Brahmin.
The earth is supported by truth; the sky is supported by the sun.
By the cosmic order (*ṛta*), the Ādityas stand firm; Soma is established in heaven.
By Soma the Ādityas are strong; by Soma the earth is great;
moreover, Soma is placed within the lap of these constellations. //2//
One thinks he has drunk Soma when they grind the plant;
but that which the Brahmans know as Soma, the earthly king does not eat of that. //3//
When they drink you, O Soma, from that you swell again;
Vāyu is the guardian of the Soma, and the month is the form of the year.
Guarded by various coverings and protected by the Bṛhatī verses, O Soma, you stand listening to the pressing-stones; no earthly being eats of you.
Thought was her cushion, sight was her ointment;
heaven and earth were the chariot-box when Sūryā went to her husband.
Raibhī was the female companion; Nārāśaṃsī was the one who settled her down. Sūryā’s auspicious garment has been adorned by Gāthā. //7//
The hymns were the cross-pieces, the *kurīra* was the head-ornament, the meter was the crest;
for Sūryā, the Aśvins were the suitors, and Agni was the leader of the procession. //8//
Soma became the suitor for the bride; both Aśvins were the groomsmen, when Savitṛ gave Sūryā to her husband with his mind as she was being praised.
The mind was her chariot-pole, and the sky was the canopy;
the two bright ones were the draft-oxen when Sūryā went to her husband.
Your two oxen, harnessed with the *Ṛg* and *Sāman*, came together in harmony.
The two ears were your wheels; your path was in heaven, moving and unmoving. //11//
Pure are your two wheels as you go; the vital breath (*vyāna*) is the axle fastened thereon.
Sūryā, ascending her mind-made chariot, has gone forth to her husband.
The bridal procession of Sūryā has set forth, which Savitṛ sent away;
under the Maghās the cows are slaughtered, and under the Phalgunīs she is led away in marriage. 13.
When you two Aśvins, being questioned, came with a three-wheeled vehicle as the bridal conveyance for Sūryā—where was one wheel of yours? Where did you stand for the sake of the director? //14//
When you two, O Lords of Splendor, came to Sūryā for her choice, all the gods recognized that deed of yours; Pūṣan, as a son, chose you as his father. //15//
O Sūryā, two of your wheels the Brahmins know according to the seasons;
but that one wheel which is hidden, only those who possess direct knowledge know it.
We worship Aryaman, the kind kinsman who finds a husband for the woman.
Like a gourd from its stem, I release her from here, but not from there.
I release her from yonder, not from here; I have bound her fast from there. O bounteous Indra, so that she may be well-favored and possessed of good sons.
I release you from the noose of Varuṇa, with which Savitṛ, the most gracious, has bound you.
In the womb of Cosmic Order, in the world of good deeds, may there be comfort for you and for your husband. 19.19
(20) May Bhaga lead you from here, taking you by the hand; may the Aśvins carry you away on their chariot.

Go to the house so that you may be the mistress of the household; as one who has power, may you speak at the assembly. (21) Here, may what is dear to your offspring prosper; be watchful in this house for the sake of the domestic fire.
With this husband, unite your body; then, full of vigor, you shall proclaim the sacred assembly.
Stay right here; do not be separated. May you both attain a full span of life, playing with sons and grandsons, rejoicing, and established in well-being.
Moving one after the other by means of their creative power (*māyā*), these two children play as they go around the ocean.
One beholds all beings; the other, ordaining the seasons, is born anew. 23.
Becoming ever new as you are born, you come as the banner of the days at the forefront of the dawns.
Arriving, you distribute the portion to the gods; O Moon, you extend a long life.
Give away the woolen garment; distribute wealth among the Brahmins.
Having become a footed sorcery, this wife enters her husband.
It becomes blue and red; the attachment of the *kṛtyā* is revealed.
Her kinsmen prosper, while her husband is bound in fetters.
The body becomes unseemly and pale-red through that evil act,
when the husband covers his own limb with the garment of the bride.
The carving, the cutting up, and furthermore the slicing—behold these forms of Sūryā; the Brahman indeed adorns them.
This is harsh, pungent, and like a poison with a jagged edge; it is not for eating.
Only that Brahmin who knows Sūryā is worthy of this bride-price.
He, the Brahman priest, brings that auspicious, pleasant garment,
he who knows the expiation by which the wife is not harmed.
You two, speaking the Truth at the rites of Truth, bring together abundant fortune.
O Brahmanaspati, make him pleasing to her as a husband; let the matchmaker speak these words.
Stay right here; do not go elsewhere. O cows, increase this [place] with progeny.
Moving toward beauty, the cows resplendent with Soma—O All-Gods, may you set your minds upon this place. 32.
O cows, enter into this man with his offspring; he does not diminish the portion of the gods.
For him, may Pūṣan and all you Maruts, for him may Dhātṛ and Savitṛ impel you. 33.
May the paths be thornless and straight by which our friends go to choose a bridegroom;
may Bhaga, Aryaman, and Dhātṛ unite her with splendor.
Whatever luster is in the dice and whatever is placed in the *surā* liquor, whatever luster is in the cattle, O Aśvins—with that luster, protect this woman. 35.
With that by which the great inviolable cow was struck on the haunch, O Aśvins, or with that by which the Soma was [prepared],
or with that by which the dice were anointed— thereby endow this woman with splendor.
He who shines within the waters without fuel, whom the sages praise during the sacrifices—O Son of the Waters, grant us the honeyed waters by which the heroic Indra was strengthened. 37.
Here I cast away this glowing grasp that corrupts the body; I draw up that which is auspicious and radiant.
Let the Brahmins bring the waters for her bathing; let the waters rise up, not slaying heroes. Let Pūṣan lead the fire around from Aryaman; the father-in-law and the brother-in-law await her.
May the gold be auspicious for you, and may the waters be auspicious; may the wedge be auspicious, and may the hole of the yoke be auspicious.
May the waters with their hundred purifiers be auspicious for you; and in peace with your husband, touch your body.
(40) O Śatakratu, [be present] in the socket of the chariot, in the socket of the cart, and in the socket of the yoke.
O Indra, having purified Apālā three times, you made her skin like that of the sun.
Desiring goodwill, offspring, good fortune, and wealth,
being devoted to your husband, gird yourself for the sake of immortality.
Just as the Sindhu, the bull among rivers, has brought forth sovereignty,
so may you become the sovereign queen, having gone to your husband's home.
Be a sovereign queen among your fathers-in-law, and a sovereign queen among your brothers-in-law;
be a sovereign queen among your husband’s sisters, and a sovereign queen among your mother-in-law.
Those goddesses who cut [the cloth], those who wove it, and those who stretched it out, who placed the borders all around—may they clothe you for old age; put on this garment, O long-lived one.
They weep for the living; they lead him away to the sacrifice. The men have gazed along the long path of his departure.
May they bring what is auspicious for the fathers who have sent him here; may they bring joy for the husbands as they embrace their wife.
I place this pleasant and firm stone for you in the lap of the goddess Earth, for the sake of offspring.
Ascend it, O radiant one, with approval; may Savitṛ grant you a long life. 47.
By that same [power] with which Agni took this earth’s right hand, by that I take your hand; do not falter, together with me, with offspring, and with wealth. 48.
May the god Savitṛ take your hand; may King Soma make you rich in offspring. May Agni Jātavedas make you a fortunate wife for your husband, reaching old age. //49//

I take your hand for the sake of good fortune, so that you may reach old age with me as your husband. Bhaga, Aryaman, Savitṛ, and Purandhi—the gods have given you to me for the state of a householder.
Bhaga has taken your hand; Savitṛ has taken your hand.
By the sacred law you are my wife; I am your householder.
May she be my one to be nourished; Bṛhaspati has given her to me. With me as your husband, O mother of offspring, live a hundred autumns.
Tvaṣṭṛ has fashioned a garment for splendor, by the command of Bṛhaspati, the seers;
with that, may Savitṛ and Bhaga clothe this woman around with offspring, even as they did Sūryā.
May Indra and Agni, Heaven and Earth, Mātariśvan, Mitra and Varuṇa, Bhaga, both Aśvins, Bṛhaspati, the Maruts, Brahma, and Soma cause this woman to increase with progeny. //54//
Bṛhaspati was the first to fashion the hair upon the head of Sūryā;
with that, O Aśvins, we adorn this woman for her husband. 55.
This is that form which the maiden has assumed; I shall seek with my mind the wife who wanders about.
I will pursue her with the Navagva companions; who, knowing this, has untied these bonds?
I shall unbind her form within me; seeing it, may he know it as the nest of the mind.
I do not consume the theft with my mind; I have been released, loosening by myself the bonds of Varuṇa.
I release you from the noose of Varuṇa, with which Savitṛ, the most gracious, bound you.
I make for you, O bride, along with your husband, a wide space and an easy path here. 58.
Lift her up! Drive away the demon! Place this woman in a state of well-being.
The wise Dhātṛ has found a husband for her; may King Bhaga go before her, knowing the way.
Bhaga fashioned the four feet; Bhaga fashioned the four hooves.
Tvaṣṭṛ shaped the fetlocks along the middle; may she be auspicious for us. 60.
Mount this well-fashioned, well-wheeled chariot, adorned with *kiṃśuka* flowers, multiform, golden-hued, and beautiful;
O Sūryā, ascend to the world of immortality, and make this pleasant vehicle for your husbands.
O Bṛhaspati, bring to us from Varuṇa a woman who does not kill her brothers, nor cattle; O Savitṛ, bring one who does not kill her husband and who possesses sons.
Do not harm the young bride, O two pillars, on this path prepared by the gods;
we make the door of the divine hall a pleasant way for the bride.
Let the sacred word (*brahman*) be joined as the highest, the sacred word as the first; let the sacred word be at the end, in the middle, and on all sides.
Having entered the invulnerable city of the gods, may you shine auspiciously and pleasantly in the world of your husband.
For you, they first led Sūryā around with her bridal procession.
O Agni, grant this wife to our husbands, together with offspring. //1//
Agni has given back the wife together with life and splendor;
may he who is her husband live a hundred autumns, possessing long life.
Soma was your first husband; the Gandharva was your next husband;
Agni was your third husband; your fourth husband is born of man.
Soma gave [her] to the Gandharva; the Gandharva gave [her] to Agni.
And Agni has given me wealth and sons, and also this woman. 4.

(5a) O Aśvins, lords of ample wealth, may your benevolence come to us; desires have settled within our hearts. (5c) You have become our guardians, a pair, lords of splendor; may we reach the dear dwellings of Aryaman. //5//
Rejoicing with a gracious mind, bestow upon us wealth consisting of all-heroic sons and eloquence.
O Lords of Splendor, provide a good path, a good ford, and a good watering place; strike down the obstacle on the road and destroy evil intent.

The herbs that there are, the rivers that there are, the fields that there are, and the forests that there are— may they, O bride, protect you, who are rich in offspring, from demons for the sake of your husband.
We have ascended this path, easy to traverse and carrying one to well-being,
upon which a hero is not harmed and acquires wealth from others.
Hear this well from me, O men: the blessing by which a husband and wife obtain what is desirable.
Those Gandharvas and divine Apsarases who dwell upon these trees—may they be gracious to this bride; may they not harm the wedding procession as it is being carried away. 9.
The consumption-diseases that follow people along with the bride’s radiant bridal procession—
may the worshipful gods lead them back to the place from which they came.
(10) May the highwaymen who lie in wait not find the couple.
Having crossed over the difficult path by means of the easy way, let the enemies flee away. //11//
With the sacred word (*brahman*) and with friendship, I cause the bridal procession to appear with a non-terrible eye.
May Savitṛ make that which is bound around, multiform, and pleasant for her husbands. 12.
Auspicious is this woman; she has come to her home. The Creator has assigned this world to her.
May Aryaman, Bhaga, both Aśvins, and Prajāpati increase her with progeny. 13.
This woman has come, a fertile field endowed with life-force; sow your seed in her!
May she, bearing the seed of the bull, produce offspring for you from her wombs, yielding milk.
Stand firm; you are the Virāj. Like Viṣṇu, O Sarasvatī, be present here. O Sinīvālī, let him be procreated; may he abide in the favor of Bhaga.
May your wave rise up; let the pins strike it down. O Waters, release the thongs!
Let the two inviolable bulls, free from malice and guiltless, go forth to pasture.
With eyes that are not terrible, not slaying her husband, pleasant, helpful, very kind, and easy to manage for the household;
a mother of heroes, desiring her brothers-in-law—may we prosper with you, being well-disposed toward one another. 17.
Be one who harms neither husband nor brother-in-law; be auspicious toward the cattle, easy to manage, and full of luster.
Bearing offspring, a mother of heroes, and desiring your brothers-in-law, serve this pleasant Gārhapatya fire. 18.
Arise from here! Desiring what have you come hither? I, the conqueror, call upon you from my own house.
O Nirṛti, seeker of emptiness, since you have come, arise; O Arāti, fly away! Do not remain here. 19.
When this bride has worshipped the former Gārhapatya fire,
then, O woman, pay homage to Sarasvatī and to the Fathers.
(20) Bring this protection and armor for this woman to spread beneath her.
O Sinīvālī, let him be born; may he abide in the favor of Bhaga.
The *balbaja* grass that you lay down and the skin that you spread out—may she who is well-procreated ascend it, the maiden who finds a husband. 22.
Spread the *balbaja* grass upon the red hide;
having sat down there, may she of good offspring worship this fire. //23//
Ascend the skin; sit down near the fire. This god slays all the demons.
Here, procreate offspring for this husband; may this son of yours be preeminent among his brothers. //24//
Let the animals of various forms, being born, emerge from the lap of this mother. O auspicious one, sit down near this Agni; together with your husband, worship the gods here.
Highly auspicious, a deliverer of the household, most gracious to her husband and bringing well-being to her father-in-law;
pleasant to her mother-in-law—may we enter these houses. 26.
Be pleasant to your fathers-in-law, pleasant to your husband, and pleasant to the household; be pleasant to this entire people, and be pleasant for their prosperity. 27.
