Auspicious is this bride; come together and behold her!
Having bestowed good fortune upon her, depart with your misfortunes.
Those young women who are ill-disposed, and those here who are even aged—
bestow upon her now your splendor, and then go away to your resting place.
Sūryā Sāvitrī has mounted the litter, which is spread with gold and bears all forms, for the sake of great good fortune.
(30) Mount the couch with a well-disposed mind; here, procreate offspring for this husband.
Like Indrāṇī, well-awakened and awakening, you watch over the dawns that have light as their vanguard. //31//
In the beginning, the gods descended; they united their bodies with their wives.
Like the sun, O woman of every form, through thy greatness, be thou here united with a husband, bearing offspring.
Arise from here, O Viśvāvasu; we pay homage to you with reverence.
Seek a kinswoman who dwells among the ancestors and is well-disposed; that is your portion by birth—recognize it as such.
The Apsarases rejoice in their shared revelry between the sun and the oblation-holder;
they are your source of birth—go toward them! I pay homage to you, O Gandharva, according to the season. //34//
Homage to the Gandharva Namasi; homage we pay to Bhāma and to Cakṣus.
O Viśvāvasu, with this prayer we offer homage to you; go forth to the Apsarases as your wives. 35.
May we be well-disposed through wealth; let us now bring the Gandharva hither from there.
That god has gone to the highest dwelling place; we have gone to where they prolong their life-span.
O Father and Mother, at the proper season, unite; may you both become the source of seed. Like a youth mounting a maiden, mount her; create offspring here and prosper in wealth.
O Pūṣan, send forth that most auspicious woman upon whom men sow their seed— she who, longing for us, shall spread her thighs apart, so that we, longing for her, may strike our member within her.
Place your hand upon her thigh; embrace your wife with a well-disposed mind.
May you two create offspring here, rejoicing; may Savitṛ grant you both a long life. 39.
May Prajāpati produce offspring for you two; may Aryaman unite you with day and night.
Free from ill fortune, enter this world of the husband; be auspicious to our bipeds and auspicious to our quadrupeds.
This bridal garment and the cloth of the bride have been given by the gods together with Manu.
He who gives to the wise Brahmin indeed strikes down the demons and their dwellings. //41//

That portion of the sacred word which Datta gave me, the bridal garment for the two brides, and the cloth for the bride—O Bṛhaspati and Indra, you two, granting your consent to the sacred word, have given this together. 42.
Being bound from a pleasant womb, laughing and exulting with great joy—
you two, having good cattle, good sons, and a good house, cross over the shining dawns while still alive.
Clothed in new, fragrant, and beautiful raiment, I, living, have emerged from the shining dawns;
like a bird from its egg, I have emerged free from every sin.
Adorning heaven and earth, who are near with their benevolence and possess great ordinances—the seven divine waters have flowed forth; may they release us from distress.
To Sūryā, to the gods, to Mitra and to Varuṇa—to those who are conscious of all that has come into being—to them I have paid this homage. //46//
He who, even without a binding, before the joints are pierced, is the restorer of the fracture, Maghavan, the possessor of many riches; he shall mend again what was dislocated.
May the darkness depart from us—the dark blue, the tawny, and the red.
That consuming *pṛṣātakī* plant, I fasten it upon this sacrificial post.
As many spells as there are upon the sacrificial grass, as many snares as King Varuṇa has, whatever failures and whatever misfortunes there are—those I place upon this post. 49.
That body of mine which is most dear has become afraid of my garment;
O Lord of the Forest, place its hem at the front so that we may not come to harm.
Whatever are the ends, as many as there are fringes, whatever are the warp-threads and the woof-threads—
May that garment which has been woven by the wives touch us pleasantly.
These longing maidens, going from the world of the fathers to their husband, have released the consecration; Svāhā!
Released by Bṛhaspati, the All-Gods have sustained it;
that splendor which has entered into the cows—with that we unite this [woman]. //53//
Released by Bṛhaspati, the All-Gods sustained it;
that brilliance which has entered into the cows—with that we unite this [earth]. //54//
Released by Bṛhaspati, the All-Gods have sustained it;
that portion which has entered into the cattle—with that we unite this [earth]. //55//
Released by Bṛhaspati, the Viśve Devās have sustained it;
that glory which has entered into the cows—with that we unite this [earth]. //56//
Released by Bṛhaspati, the Viśve Devas sustained it; that milk which has entered into the cows—with that we unite this [earth]. //57//
Released by Bṛhaspati, the All-Gods have sustained it;
that essence which has entered the cows—with that we unite this [earth]. //58//
If these long-haired people have danced together in your house, creating evil with their weeping—
may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin.

If this daughter of yours, with disheveled hair, has wept in the house, bringing evil by her weeping—may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin. (60) If the female relatives, the young women, have danced together in your house, bringing evil by their weeping—[may Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin]. (61)
May Agni and Savitṛ release you from that sin. //61//
Whatever evil has been committed against you by evildoers— whether it be established in your offspring, in your cattle, or in your houses—
may Agni and Savitar release you from that sin.
This woman speaks thus as she scatters grains of parched rice:
"May my husband live a long life; may he live for a hundred autumns."
O Indra, drive these two together here like a pair of cakravāka birds;
may they, blessed with offspring, enjoy a full lifespan throughout their entire lives.
Whatever has been done upon the throne, or upon the pillow, or on the seat;
whatever sorcery they have performed at the wedding—we deposit that in the washing-basin.
Whatever is ill-done, whatever is impure, and whatever [fault] exists in the wedding and the bridal procession—
on the blanket of Saṃbhala we wipe away that misfortune.
Having deposited our impurity in the *saṃbhala* and our misfortune in the *kambala*, we have become worthy of sacrifice and purified; may he prolong our lives.
This artificial thorn, which causes a hundred pains—
may it scratch away the impurity from her hair and the impurity from her head.
From limb by limb we drive the consumption from her away.
Let it not reach the earth nor the gods; let it not reach the sky nor the wide atmosphere.
Let it not reach the waters, O Agni, nor this impurity; let it not reach Yama nor any of the ancestors.
I bind you together with the milk of the earth; I bind you together with the milk of the plants.
I bind you together with offspring and wealth; thus bound, win this prize. I am he, you are she.
I am the *sāman*, you are the *ṛc*. I am heaven, you are the earth.
Let us two come together here; let us procreate offspring.
The noble ones desire to have daughters; the liberal givers desire sons. May we, unharmed, be united for the sake of great acquisition of booty.
Those ancestors who have come to this bridal procession as beholders of the bride— may they grant protection, rich in progeny, to this bride who has a husband.

Having given offspring and wealth here to her, that which was acting like a tethering rope in the east—let them carry it back along the path of the non-returner; this Virāj, possessing good offspring, has won through.
Awaken, O well-awakened one, awakening for long life lasting a hundred autumns!
Go to the house so that you may be the mistress of the house; may Savitṛ grant you a long life.
The Vrātya was indeed moving along; he set Prajāpati in motion.
That Prajāpati saw gold within himself; he brought it forth. 2.
That became one; that became a mark; that became great; that became the eldest; that became Brahman; that became austerity; that became truth;
by it he was procreated. //3//
He grew; he became great; he became Mahādeva.
He went around the lords of the gods; he became the Lord.
He became the sole Vratya; he took up a bow, which was indeed the bow of Indra.
Her belly is blue and her back is red.
"By means of the dark-blue [wool] he covers over his unpleasant rival, and by means of the red [wool] he pierces him who hates him," so say the exponents of sacred knowledge.
He arose; he moved forth toward the eastern direction.
Bṛhat and Rathantara, and the Ādityas and the Viśve Devas, followed after him.
He who, knowing this, reviles a Vrātya, cuts himself off from Bṛhat and Rathantara, and from the Ādityas and the Viśve Devas.
He who knows this becomes the beloved abode of the *bṛhat* and the *rathantara*, of the Ādityas, and of all the gods.

(4) In his eastern direction is Śraddhā the courtesan; Mitra is the bard, discernment is the garment, day is the turban, night is the hair, the two green ones are the earrings, and the *kalmali* plant is the jewel. (5)

The past and the future are his two attendants; the mind is the byway; Mātariśvan and Pavamāna are the two who drive along the byway; Vāta is the charioteer; Reṣman is the whip; fame and glory are the two precursors.
Fame goes to him and glory goes to him who knows thus. (1)
He rose up; he moved forth toward the southern direction.
After him followed the Yajñāyajñīya and the Vāmadevya [Sāmans], as well as the sacrifice, the sacrificer, and the cattle.
He who reviles a Vrātya knowing this cuts himself off from the Yajñāyajñīya and the Vāmadevya, from the sacrifice, the sacrificer, and the cattle.
He who knows this becomes the beloved abode of the Yajñāyajñiya chant, the Vāmadevya chant, the sacrifice, the sacrificer, and the sacrificial animals.

[12] In its southern direction, Dawn is the harlot; the mantra is the Magadhan bard; discernment is the garment; the day is the turban; the night is the hair; the two green ones are the earrings; and the *kalmali* plant is the jewel. [13]
The new moon and the full moon are the two attendants; the mind and Mātariśvan are the two byways; Pavamāna is the driver of the byways; the wind is the charioteer; the whirlwind is the whip;
and fame and glory are the two precursors.
Fame goes to him and glory goes to him who knows this. //2// [14]
He rose up; he moved forth toward the western direction.
Vairūpa and Vairāja, the waters and King Varuṇa followed after him.
He who, knowing this, speaks ill of a Vrātya who knows thus, cuts himself off from Vairūpa and Vairāja, from the waters and from King Varuṇa.
He who knows this becomes the beloved abode of Vairūpa, Vairāja, the waters, and King Varuṇa.
[18] In his western direction, there is a courtesan named Īrā; laughter is his garment, knowledge is his turban, day is his hair, night is his locks, and the emerald is his jewel. [19]
Day and night are the two attendants; Mind and Mātariśvan are the two who drive on the wrong path; Pavamāna is the driver of the wrong path; Vāta is the charioteer; and the whirlwind is the whip.
Renown and glory are the two precursors.
Renown comes to him and glory comes to him who knows thus. 3. [20]
He rose up; he moved forth toward the northern direction.
After him Śyaita and Naudhasa, the Seven Seers, and King Soma moved forth.
He who, knowing this, reviles a Vrātya who knows thus, cuts himself off from Śyaita, from Naudhasa, from the Seven Seers, and from King Soma.
He who knows this attains the beloved abode of the Śyaita and the Naudhasa, of the Seven Seers, and of King Soma.
[24] In his northern direction are lightning as his courtesan, thunder as his bard, discernment as his garment, day as his turban, night as his hair, two green ear-rings, and a glittering gem. [25]
Fame and renown are the two attendants; the mind is the uneven path; Mātariśvan and Pavamāna are the two who travel the uneven path; Vāta is the charioteer; Reṣman is the whip;
and Kīrti and Yaśas are the two precursors.
[26–27] Fame comes to him and renown comes to him who knows thus. [28]
He stood upright for a year. The gods said to him, "O Vrātya, why do you stand? 1.
He said, "Let them prepare a throne for me."
For that Vrātya, they brought together a throne-seat.
Of her, summer and spring were the two feet, and autumn and the rainy season were the other two. 4.
The Bṛhat and the Rathantara were on the two longitudinal beams; the Yajñāyajñīya and the Vāmadevya were on the two cross-beams.
The *ṛc* verses are the longitudinal threads; the *yajus* formulas are the transverse threads.
The Veda is the carpet; the Brahman is the cushion.
The *udgītha* has the *sāman* as its seat and the *apaśraya*.
The Vrātya ascended that throne.
The divine folk were his attendants; his intentions were his messengers, and all beings were his followers.
All beings indeed become his attendants for one who knows thus. //11//
For him, they made the two months of spring the guardians from the eastern quarter, and the *Bṛhat* and *Rathantara* [Sāmans] the attendants.
The two months of spring guard him from the eastern quarter and the *Bṛhat* and *Rathantara* attend him, for one who knows thus. //1//
For him, they made the two summer months the guardians from the southern direction; they made the *yajñāyajñīya* and the *vāmadevya* the attendants.
For him, they made the two months of the rainy season the guardians from the western quarter, and the *vairūpa* and *vairāja* [sāmans] the attendants.
The two months of the rainy season guard him from the western quarter and the *vairūpa* and *vairāja* attend upon him, for one who knows thus. 3.3.9.

For him, from the northern direction, they made the two autumn months the guardians, and the Śyaita and Naudhasa [sāmans] the attendants. The two autumn months guard him from the northern direction and the Śyaita and Naudhasa attend upon him, for one who knows thus. 4.4.4–12c.
For him, they made the two winter months the guardians of the fixed quarter; the earth and Agni were the attendants.
The two winter months guard him from the fixed quarter, and the earth and Agni attend upon him, for one who knows thus. 5.15.5–15.4.5(4.13–15) c–d.
For him, from the upward direction, they made the two months of the dewy season the guardians, and the sky and the sun the attendants.
The two months of the dewy season guard him from the upward direction, and the sky and the sun attend him, for one who knows thus. 6.18.
For him, from the intermediate region of the eastern quarter, they made Bhava the archer, the follower.

[1] Bhava, the archer, follows as a follower from the intermediate region of the eastern quarter; neither Śarva, nor Bhava, nor Īśāna harms him, nor his cattle, nor his kinsmen—provided he knows thus. [2–3]
For him, they made Śarva, the archer, the follower from the intermediate region of the southern quarter.
Śarva, the archer, stands as a follower from the intermediate region of the southern quarter; Śarva, nor Bhava, nor Īśāna harms him, his cattle, or his kinsmen—he who knows thus. //2// [5]
For him, from the intermediate region of the western quarter, they made Paśupati the archer the follower.

[6] Paśupati the archer, as a follower, stands behind him from the intermediate region of the western quarter; neither Śarva, nor Bhava, nor Īśāna harms him, nor his cattle, nor his kinsmen, for one who knows thus. [7] 3.
From the intermediate region of the northern quarter, they made the fierce god, the archer, the follower.

[8] The fierce god, the archer, as a follower stands behind him from the intermediate region of the northern quarter; neither Śarva, nor Bhava, nor Īśāna harms his cattle or his kinsmen—he who knows thus. [4] [9]
(5.5) For him, from the intermediate region of the fixed quarter, they made Rudra the archer the rear-guard.

(5.11) Rudra the archer, as the rear-guard, stands behind him from the intermediate region of the fixed quarter; neither Śarva, nor Bhava, nor Īśāna harms him, his cattle, or his kinsmen—provided he knows this.
From that intermediate region of the upward direction, they made Mahādeva the archer their follower.

[12] Mahādeva the archer, as a follower, stands behind him from that intermediate region of the upward direction; neither Śarva, nor Bhava, nor Īśāna harms him, nor his cattle, nor his kinsmen, who knows thus. [13] 6.

For him, they made Īśāna the archer their follower from all the intermediate regions. [14] Īśāna, the archer, stands as a follower after him from all the intermediate regions. Neither Śarva, nor Bhava, nor Īśāna harms his cattle or his kinsmen, who knows thus. [15–16]
He moved out toward the fixed quarter.
After him the earth, Agni, the plants, the trees, the products of trees, and the creepers moved out.
He moved out toward the upward direction.
After him, *ṛta* and *satya*, Sūrya, Candra, and the constellations moved out.
He moved out toward the northern direction.

And he indeed becomes the beloved abode of all the *virāj*s, of all the gods (*deva*), and of all the deities (*devatā*), for whoever knows thus. He moved forth through all the intermediate regions. Prajāpati, Parameṣṭhin, the father, and the grandfather moved forth after him.

Faith, sacrifice, the world, food, and the eating of food, having become these, turned back toward him. //4//

Therefore, if a Vrātya who knows this should come as a guest to one's house... (1)
Having gone out to meet him himself, he should say: "O Vrātya, where have you stayed? O Vrātya, [here is] water; O Vrātya, let them satisfy you!
O Vrātya, may it be as is dear to you! O Vrātya, may it be as is your will! O Vrātya, may it be as is your desire! 2.
When he says to him, "O Vrātya, where have you stayed?", he thereby secures for himself the paths traveled by the gods. 3.
When he says to him, "O Vrātya, water," he thereby secures the waters.
When he says to him, "O Vrātya, may they satisfy you," he thereby makes his vital breath more abundant. //5//
When he says to him, "O Vrātya, may it be as is dear to you," he thereby secures what is indeed dear.
The beloved comes to him, and he becomes beloved of the beloved, who knows thus. //7//
When he says to him, "O Vrātya, let it be as you desire," he thereby secures his very will.
Desire comes to him; he becomes a master among masters, who knows thus. //9//
When he says to him, "O Vrātya, as is your desire, so let it be," by that very means he secures his desire.
Desire comes to him; he attains his desire at will, who knows thus. //11//
Now, if a Vrātya who knows this should come as a guest to the house of someone whose fires have been taken out and the Agnihotra has been set down, [he should be treated accordingly]. //1//
Having risen toward him himself, he should say: "O Vrātya, release me; I shall sacrifice."
If he should grant permission, he should offer the oblation; if he does not grant permission, he should not offer the oblation. //3//
He who, being thus authorized by a Vrātya who knows this, offers the oblation.

He does not cut himself off from the gods; his offering becomes effective.
A dwelling place remains for him in this world who, permitted by a Vrātya who knows thus, offers the oblation.
Now, if one who does not know this offers the oblation without being authorized by the Vrātya who knows thus— //8//
He knows neither the path of the ancestors nor the path of the gods. //9//
Among the gods he is cut off; his offering becomes as if unoffered. //10//
No abode remains for him in this world who offers oblations without being authorized by a Vrātya who knows thus. //11//

Thus, when a Vrātya who knows this stays as a guest for one night in someone’s house, he thereby wins those worlds on earth that are auspicious. (1) Thus, when a Vrātya who knows this stays as a guest for a second night in someone’s house, he thereby wins those worlds in the atmosphere that are auspicious. (2)
(2) Those worlds in the intermediate space that are meritorious— those he wins by that very act.
(3) Thus, when a Vrātya who knows this stays as a guest in one's house on the third night,
those worlds in heaven that are meritorious— those he wins by that very act.
Thus, when a Vrātya who knows this dwells as a guest in one's house for the fourth night,
he thereby wins those worlds which are the most meritorious among the meritorious.
(4) Thus, when a Vrātya who knows this dwells as a guest in one's house for an unlimited number of nights—
(5) He thereby wins those very same immeasurable, meritorious worlds.
(6) Now, if a non-Vrātya who calls himself a Vrātya should come as a guest to one’s house under that name— (7) One should either entertain him or not entertain him.
(8) “Let us ask water from this deity; let us clothe this deity; I envelop this deity”—with these words, he should envelop it.
(9) For him who knows thus, that offering becomes made in that very deity.
(1) When they moved forth toward the eastern direction, they moved forth having become the host of Maruts, having made the mind their eater of food.
He who knows thus eats food with the mind-eater; 1.
When he moved toward the southern quarter, he moved having become Indra, having made himself strength that eats food. He who knows thus eats food with strength that eats food; 2.
When he moved toward the western quarter, he moved having become King Varuṇa, making the waters the eaters of food. He who knows thus eats food with the waters as the eaters of food.
When he moved toward the northern quarter, he moved having become King Soma, made into an oblation by the Seven Seers, making the oblation the eater of food.
He who knows thus eats food through the oblation as the eater of food.
When he moved forth toward the fixed quarter, having become Viṣṇu, he moved forth having made the Virāj the eater of food.
He who knows thus eats food through the Virāj as the eater of food.
When he moved among the cattle, he moved having become Rudra, making the plants eaters of food.
He who knows thus eats food by means of the plants that are eaters of food.
When he moved among the ancestors, he moved having become King Yama, making the utterance *svadhā* an eater of food.
He who knows thus eats food with the utterance *svadhā*, which is the eater of food.
When he moved among men, he moved having become Agni, making the utterance *svāhā* the eater of food.
He who knows thus eats food with the utterance *svāhā*, which is the eater of food.
When he moved out toward the upward direction, he moved out having become Bṛhaspati, having made the *vaṣaṭ*-call the eater of food.
He who knows thus eats food by means of the *vaṣaṭ*-call as the eater of food.
When he moved out toward the gods, he moved out having become Īśāna, having made wrath the eater of food.
10. He who knows thus eats food with fury as the eater of food.
11. When he moved forth after his offspring, having become Prajāpati, he moved forth having made breath the eater of food.
He who knows thus eats food with breath as the eater of food.
When he traversed all the intermediate regions, having become the Supreme Lord (*parameṣṭhin*), he traversed them having made the *brahman* his eater of food.
He who knows thus eats food by means of the *brahman* as the eater of food. Of that Vratya... [1]
Seven are the out-breaths, seven the in-breaths, and seven the diffused breaths. //2//
That which is his first vital breath, named "Upward," is this Agni. //3//
That which is his second vital breath, named Prauḍha, is that Āditya.
That third vital breath of his which was drawn upward is that which is named the moon. //5//
That which is his fourth breath, named Vibhu—this is Pavamāna.
That which is his fifth vital breath, named the Womb—that is these waters.
That which is his sixth vital breath, named "the dear," these are the domestic animals.
That which is his seventh vital breath, named "Immeasurable," these are all these creatures. //9//
That which is his first out-breathing is the full moon day. 1.
That which is his second downward breath is the Aṣṭakā.
That which is his third downward breath is the Sāman and the New Moon.
That which is his fourth downward breath is faith. 4.
That which is his fifth downward breath is the consecration (*dīkṣā*). //5//
That which is his sixth downward breath is the sacrifice.
That which is his seventh downward breath—these are the sacrificial gifts.
That which is its first diffused breath (*vyāna*) is this earth. //1//
That which is his second, the vyāna, is the intermediate space.
That which is his third diffused breath (*vyāna*) is the sky.
That which is his fourth diffusion, those are the lunar mansions. //4//
That which is his fifth out-breath is the seasons. //5//
That which is his sixth vital air, that consists of the seasonal periods.
That which is its seventh diffused breath (*vyāna*) is the year.
The gods go around a common goal; indeed, the seasons go around the year and the Vrātya.

Of that Vrātya. //1//

Victory is ours; our [strength] has burst forth. Truth is ours; splendor is ours; the sacred word (*brahman*) is ours; heaven is ours; sacrifice is ours; cattle are ours; offspring are ours; heroes are ours.
Therefore, we exclude that one—him, the son of such-and-such a lineage, the son of such-and-such a woman—whoever he may be.
May he not be released from the snares of King Varuṇa. //26//

Victory is ours; our [victory] has burst forth. Truth is ours; splendor is ours; the sacred word (*brahman*) is ours; heaven is ours; sacrifice is ours; cattle are ours; offspring are ours; heroes are ours. //27//
Victory is ours; the breakthrough is ours; I have overcome all hostile armies.
This Agni has said, and Soma too has said it: "May Pūṣan place me in the world of the righteous."
We have gone to heaven; we have gone to the light of heaven; we have come together with the light of the sun. 3.
For the sake of greater prosperity, may the sacrifice be rich in wealth; may I win wealth; may I become wealthy; bestow wealth upon me. //4//

I invoke by name Indra, the subduer, the overcomer, the most powerful, the one who conquers, the winner of strength, the winner of heaven, the winner of cattle, the winner of wealth—the one worthy of praise. May I be long-lived. 1.1.1–e.

I invoke by name Indra, the overcomer, the one who conquers, the victorious, the most powerful; the one who overcomes, the winner of strength, the winner of heaven, the winner of cattle, the winner of wealth—the one worthy of praise. May I become dear to the gods. 2.

I invoke by name Indra, the overcomer, the one who conquers, the victorious, the most powerful; the one who overcomes, the winner of strength, the winner of heaven, the winner of cattle, the winner of wealth—the one worthy of praise. May I be dear to all creatures. 3.

I invoke by name Indra, the overcomer, the enduring, the victorious, the most powerful; the one who endures, the winner of strength, the winner of heaven, the winner of cattle, the winner of wealth—the one worthy of praise. May I be dear to the animals. //4//

I invoke Indra by his name, the one who overcomes the unsubduable, the subduer, the most powerful, the conqueror, the one born of strength, the winner of heaven, the winner of cattle, and the winner of wealth. May I be dear among my peers. //5//
Arise, arise, O Sūrya; rise up toward me with your splendor!
May he who hates me be subdued, and may I not be subdued by him who hates me. O Viṣṇu, yours are manifold heroic powers.
Do you fill us with cattle of every form; place me in the secure realm, in the highest heaven.
Rise up, rise up, O Sūrya; shine upon me with your splendor!
Grant your favor to those whom I see and those whom I do not see. O Viṣṇu, yours are many heroic powers;
fill us with cattle of every form, and place me in the nourishment in the highest heaven.

Let not those snarers who stand here within the waters and the depths deceive you. Having cast off all ill-will, you have ascended to this heaven; be gracious to us, and may we abide in your favor. O Viṣṇu, your heroic deeds are manifold;
fill us with cattle of every form, and place us in the blissful highest heaven. 8.
O Indra, protect us for great good fortune with your unfailing protections throughout the nights; O Viṣṇu, your heroic powers are manifold.
You, provide us with cattle of every form; place me in the nourishment in the highest heaven. 9.

O Indra, through your auspicious aids, be most propitious to us. Ascending to the third heaven from the sky, being praised for the drinking of Soma—O Viṣṇu, whose abode is dear, for our well-being, your heroic deeds are manifold.
Do you fill us with cattle of every form; place me in the nourishment in the highest firmament. 10. {1}

O Indra, you are the all-conquering, the all-knowing, the much-invoked; O Indra, you are he. O Indra, bring forth this well-invoked hymn of praise; be gracious to us, and may we abide in your favor. O Viṣṇu, yours are many heroic deeds;
with cattle of every form, satisfy us, and place me in the nourishment of the highest heaven. 11.
Unassailable in heaven and on earth, your greatness has not been reached even in the intermediate space.
Increasing through the unassailable *brahman*, do you, O Indra, grant us protection in heaven. O Viṣṇu, yours are many heroic deeds;
satisfy us with cattle of every form, and place me in the nourishment of the highest firmament. 12.

That body of yours, O Indra, which is in the waters, which is on the earth, which is within the fire, and that body of yours, O Indra, which is in the purifying [sun] that finds the light—heaven—(AVŚ_17,1.13c) with that body by which, O Indra, you have pervaded the mid-air, with that body, O Indra, grant us protection. O Viṣṇu, your heroic powers are manifold;
(AVŚ_17,1.13e) do you fill us with cattle of every form; place me in the nourishment in the highest heaven. //13//
O Indra, the Ṛṣis, magnifying you with sacred hymns and imploring you, have performed their sacrificial session. O Viṣṇu, yours are many heroic deeds.
Fill us with cattle of every form; establish me in the world of nourishment, in the highest heaven. 14.
Thou art the third; thou shalt encompass the fountain that flows in a thousand streams, the assembly that finds the light of heaven. O Viṣṇu, thine heroic deeds are manifold.
Do thou fill us with cattle of every form, and place me in the blissful highest heaven. 15.
You guard the four quarters; you shine through both worlds with your flame.

You stand over all these beings; as one who knows, you follow the path of *ṛta*. O Viṣṇu, yours are many heroic deeds. Fill us with cattle of every form; place me in the nourishment in the highest heaven. 16.
With five [steps] you move away, with one toward us; you go forth warding off the curse on this auspicious day. O Viṣṇu, yours are many heroic deeds.
Fill us with cattle of every form; place me in the nourishing highest heaven. 17.
You are Indra, you are Mahendra; you are the world, you are Prajāpati. For you the sacrifice is spread out; to you they offer as they sacrifice. O Viṣṇu, yours are many heroic powers.
Do you fill us with cattle of every form; place me in the secure nourishment in the highest heaven. 18.
In the non-existent, the existent is established; in the existent, the being is established.
The being is placed within the future; the future is established in the being. O Viṣṇu, manifold are your heroic powers.
Grant us wealth in the form of cattle of every kind; place me in the nourishing highest heaven. 19.
(17.1.20a) You are bright; you are radiant.
(17.1.20c) Just as you are radiant with radiance, so may I be radiant with radiance. (17.1.21a) You are luster; you are light.
Just as you shine with splendor, so may I also shine with cattle and the luster of a Brahmin. 21.
Homage to the one being raised up, homage to the one being raised up further, homage to the one already raised up;
homage to the one shining forth, homage to the self-radiant one, homage to the sovereign ruler. //22//
Homage to him who is setting, homage to him who is about to set, homage to him who has set;
homage to the Virāj, homage to the Svarāj, homage to the Samrāj. //23//
This Āditya has risen up together with all-consuming heat.
Subduing my rivals, may I not be subdued by the one who hates me. O Viṣṇu, yours are many heroic deeds;
do you provide us with cattle of every form, and place me in the nourishment in the highest heaven. 24.
O Āditya, you have ascended the ship with a hundred oars for our well-being;
you have carried me across the day, so carry me safely across the night as well. 25.
O Sūrya, you have mounted the ship with a hundred oars for our well-being; you have carried me across the night; carry me safely across the day.

By the turning of Prajāpati, by the Brahman as armor, and by the light and splendor of Kaśyapa—may I, reaching old age, having achieved valor, being expansive, and possessing a thousand-year lifespan, move about as one who has performed good deeds. 27.
Enveloped by the Brahman as my armor, and by the light and splendor of Kaśyapa,
may the divine arrows and those discharged by men for the sake of slaughter not reach me.
Guarded by *ṛta* and by all the seasons, guarded by what has been and what is to be—let no evil reach me, nor death; I interpose myself with the waters of speech. 29.
May Agni, my protector, guard me on every side; may the rising sun drive away the snares of death.
May the dawning dawns and the steadfast mountains [be my support]; may a thousand vital breaths be gathered within me.
I would indeed turn my friend toward me through our friendship, having traveled even across the vast ocean.
May the wise one, meditating upon the furtherance [of the sacrifice], establish the grandson of the father upon the earth. //1//
Your friend does not desire this friendship, since she who shares the same mark becomes of different form.
The sons of the great Asura, the heroes, the upholders of heaven, look out widely around.
The immortals indeed desire this from you alone: the abandonment of even one mortal.
May your mind be fixed upon our mind; as a husband, may you enter into the body of your wife.
What we have never done before, how could we now speak untruth while proclaiming the *ṛta*?
The Gandharva who is in the waters and the watery maiden—they are our kin; that is our highest bond of relationship.
In the womb, the progenitor, the god Tvaṣṭṛ, Savitṛ of all forms, made us a husband and wife.
No one violates his ordinances; both Earth and Heaven know this of us. (AVŚ 18.1.5)
Who today yokes to the pole of the Cosmic Order (*ṛta*) the impetuous, fierce, and ill-disposed bulls?
Those who are near-at-hand with arrows, heart-piercing, yet life-bestowing—whoever provides for their maintenance shall live.
Who knows of this first day? Who has seen it? Who here can declare it?
Great is the ordinance of Mitra and Varuṇa; what indeed will you say, O reviler, to deceive men?
O Yamī, let not the desire for Yama come upon me, that we might lie together in the same womb.
Like a wife to her husband, I would yield my body; let us move apart like two chariot wheels.
They do not stand still, nor do they close their eyes—these spies of the gods who move here.
O you who incite me, go quickly by another way; with that, tear us apart like the two wheels of a chariot.
May she honor him with nights and days; may she repeatedly measure out the eye of the sun.
Yamī, the twin sister, would tear asunder the forbidden act with Yama—she who is kin to heaven and earth, a fellow kinswoman.
(10) Surely those later ages will come when kinsmen shall commit the forbidden act.
Press your arm close to the bull; seek another husband than me, O fortunate one.
What is a brother, if he leaves one without protection? What is a sister, if Destruction (Nirṛti) approaches?
Driven by desire, I murmur this much; unite my body with your body. 12.
I am not here to be your protector, O Yamī; I will not unite my body with your body. Arrange your pleasures with another than me; your brother does not desire this, O fortunate one.
(14a) Indeed, I would not wish to unite my body with your body; they call it an evil thing when one approaches his own sister.
(14c) This is not a union for my mind or my heart, that as a brother I should lie upon the bed of my sister. 14.
Alas, O Yama, you are indeed pitiable; for neither your mind nor your heart have I found.
Surely another woman has embraced you, as a girth-belt clasps a yoked horse, or as a creeper embraces a tree.
(16a) Now one [of you] shall embrace another, O Yamī, as a creeper embraces a tree. (16c) Either you shall seek his heart, or he yours; thus, establish a most auspicious bond of harmony between you.
The poets have separated the three meters, which are manifold in form, beautiful to behold, and all-seeing;
the waters, the winds, and the plants—these are fixed together in a single world.

The bull has yielded for the bull the milks of heaven by means of the milking; the mighty one, the undeceivable son of Aditi, knows all through his insight. He, the worthy of sacrifice, performs the sacrificial seasons that are worthy of sacrifice. //18//
May the Gandharva woman Rapad and the watery maiden protect our mind amidst the roar of the river. May Aditi place us in the midst of what is desired; may our eldest brother speak first for us.
Even she, the auspicious, rich in food, glorious, and radiant with light, Dawn has shone forth for mankind,
since they have brought forth Agni as the invoker for the assembly, according to the will of those who desire him.
Then the swift falcon brought that far-reaching, all-seeing drop to the sacrifice.
When the Aryan tribes choose the wondrous Agni as their Hotṛ-priest, then indeed has inspired thought been born.
(18.1.22a) You are always delightful, like a well-tended pasture for one who thrives, O Agni, you who make the sacrifice of man successful through his invocations.
(18.1.22c) Or when, having exerted yourself as the praiser of the inspired singer, you come with many [attendants] after winning the prize.
Raise up your two parents; the lover seeks fortune. The beloved one desires from the heart and sends forth his impulse.
The bearer speaks; the sacrificer performs his work well; the lord of power displays his strength; the inspired one trembles with thought.
O Agni, son of strength, that mortal who has proclaimed your favor becomes far-famed;
bestowing nourishment and borne by his horses, he, radiant and powerful, prospers through the days.
Hear us, O Agni, in our common dwelling-place; yoke your swift chariot of immortality.
Bring hither to us the two worlds, the parents of the gods; let none of the gods be absent here; may you remain present. 25.
O Agni, when this divine assembly occurs among the gods, O worshipful one worthy of sacrifice;
and when you, O self-dependent lord, distribute treasures, grant us here our share of wealth.
Agni has looked along the vanguard of the dawns; the first Jātavedas has looked along the days.
Along the dawns and along the rays of the sun, he has entered heaven and earth. 27.
Agni has looked back upon the vanguard of the dawns; Jātavedas, as the first, has looked back upon the days.
He has looked back toward the many rays of the sun; he has stretched across heaven and earth. 28.
Heaven and Earth, first by the cosmic order (*ṛta*), become listeners with true speech, when the god,
making mortals ready for sacrifice, sits down as the *hotṛ* priest, turning toward his own vital breath.
The God who encompasses the gods by the Eternal Law, bring our oblation, you who are foremost and wise;
whose banner is smoke, who is kindled with fuel, the radiant one, the delightful and eternal Hotṛ-priest, most skilled in sacrifice through speech.
I praise you both for your increase—O Waters, dripping with clarity! O Heaven and Earth, O two worlds, hear me.
When the gods went to the path of the departed, O Fathers, sharpen us here with honey.
The cow’s own portion is the immortal nectar of the god; born from that, they uphold the two wide worlds.
All the gods follow that sacrificial formula of yours, whereby the dappled cow milks forth the heavenly ghee and water.
What has the king seized from us? When have we transgressed his decree? Who knows?
For even Mitra, when he goes astray, is like a cry of reproach among the gods; even the prize of victory does not remain with those who wander.

(34a) Here, the name of immortality is difficult to perceive, when she who shares the same mark becomes manifold in form. (34c) O lofty Agni, protect without fail that one who thinks well of Yama’s name.
In which sacrificial session the gods rejoice, and which they maintain in the seat of Vivasvat;
in the sun they have placed the light, and the two unwearied ones move around the moon and the nights as a radiant glow.
That secret counsel in which the gods move together, we do not know it;
may Mitra, Aditi, and the god Savitṛ proclaim us sinless here to Varuṇa.
O friends, we instruct a sacred prayer for Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt;
let us offer praise to him who is most heroic and bold.
For you are renowned by your might as the slayer of Vṛtra through the slaying of Vṛtra;
O hero, you bestow gifts upon the generous patron.
Like a chariot, you traverse the broad earth; may the winds blow here upon our great ground.
May Mitra and Varuṇa, joined with us here, and Agni, like fire in the forest, release his heat.
Praise the renowned one who sits upon the chariot-seat of men, the king, the terrible, the smiter, the fierce!
Being praised, O Rudra, be gracious to the singer; let them cast down your army elsewhere than upon us.
Those seeking the gods invoke Sarasvatī; they invoke Sarasvatī while the sacrifice is being performed.
The doers of good deeds invoke Sarasvatī; Sarasvatī shall grant desirable wealth to the donor.
The ancestors invoke Sarasvatī, approaching the sacrifice with sacrificial fees.
Having sat down upon this sacred grass, rejoice; bestow upon us food free from disease. 42.

O Sarasvatī, you who have come on the same chariot with the Pitṛs, O Goddess, rejoicing with the hymns and the *svadhā* offerings—bestow here upon the sacrificer a portion of the *iḍā* worth a thousand, and an abundance of wealth. 43.

May the lower, the higher, and the middle Soma-loving Fathers rise up—those who have gone to the life-breath, who are harmless and knowers of the *ṛta*. May those Fathers protect us in our invocations. //44//

I have found the benevolent fathers, and the descendant, and the wide stride of Viṣṇu. Those who sit upon the sacrificial grass and partake of the pressed food with their own portion—may they be most eager to come here.

Let this homage be offered today to the fathers, those who departed in former times and those who went later; those who are settled in the earthly realm, or those who are now in the well-favored regions.
Mātali [is strengthened] by the Kavyas, Yama by the Aṅgirases, and Bṛhaspati by the Ṛkvans;
may those whom the gods have strengthened and those who are gods protect us, O Fathers, at our invocations. //47//
Truly, this is sweet and indeed honeyed; truly, this is strong and indeed flavorful.
And now, no one at all can withstand Indra when he has drunk of this in battles.
With the verse, "He who has gone forth along the great slopes," honoring with an oblation Yama, the son of Vivasvat, the king and gathering place of men, who has spied out the path for many— 49.

Yama was the first to find our path; this pasture-land is not to be taken away from us, where our ancient fathers have passed away, having been born along their own paths. O Fathers who sit upon the sacrificial grass, come hither with your aid; we have prepared these offerings for you—be pleased with them.
Having come hither with most peaceful aid, establish for us well-being, health, and freedom from harm.
Bending the knee and sitting down to the south, may all of you accept this our oblation.
O Fathers, do not harm us for anything, whatever offense we may have committed against you through human frailty.
Tvaṣṭṛ prepares the bridal procession for his daughter; because of this, all this world comes together.
The mother of Yama, being carried away as the wife of the great Vivasvat, has vanished.
Go forth, go forth by the ancient paths, by which your ancestors of old have departed.
You shall see both kings rejoicing in the *svadhā* offering—Yama and the god Varuṇa. 54.
Depart, go away, and creep far from here; the fathers have prepared this world for him.
Yama grants him a dwelling clearly distinguished by days, waters, and nights.
Desiring you, we kindle you; desiring you, we enkindle you. Desiring them, bring the desiring ancestors here to eat the oblation.
Radiant indeed may we meditate; radiant may we kindle [thee].
O radiant one, bring the radiant ancestors here to eat the oblation.
The Aṅgirases are our fathers, the Navagvas, the Atharvans, and the Bhṛgus, who are worthy of the Soma;
may we abide in the good-will of those worthy of sacrifice, and likewise in their auspicious benevolence. 58.
Come here with the Angirases, worthy of sacrifice; O Yama, rejoice here with the Vairūpas. I invoke Vivasvant, who is your father, to sit down upon this sacred grass (barhis).
O Yama, ascend this sacrificial seat in harmony with the Aṅgiras fathers;
let the mantras recited by the seers carry you here, O King, and rejoice in this oblation.
From here they have come up; they have ascended to the backs of heaven.
Like the Bhṛgus, the Aṅgirases went forth to heaven along the path.
For Yama the Soma is purified; for Yama the oblation is prepared.
The well-prepared sacrifice goes to Yama, with Agni as its messenger. //1//
Offer to Yama the most honey-sweet oblation and step forward; this homage is to the seers, the first-born, the ancient makers of the path. //2//
Offer to Yama, the king, oblations of ghee-rich milk;
may he grant us long life among the living, so that we may live on.
Do not burn him up, O Agni; do not consume him with heat; do not scorch his skin or his body.
When you have made him cooked, O Jātavedas, then send him forth unto the Fathers. //4//
When you have cooked it, O Jātavedas, then deliver this one to the ancestors;
when he goes to this guidance of the life-force (asu), then he shall become a follower of the will of the gods. //5//
Through the *trikadruka* vessels he purifies; the six wide ones and the one great [heaven].
The *triṣṭubh*, the *gāyatrī*, and all the meters—these are all established in Yama.
Go to the sun with your eye, to the wind with your breath; go to heaven and to earth according to your natures.
Or go to the waters, if that is where your welfare lies; take your stand among the plants with your bodies.
The goat is the portion of your heat; burn that, let your flame burn that, let your radiance burn that.
With those bodies of yours which are auspicious, O Jātavedas, carry him to the world of the righteous.

O Jātavedas, let those flames of yours, your swift ones, by which you fill the sky and the mid-air, follow the goat as it goes and encompass it; then, with your other most auspicious ones, make it cooked.
Release him again, O Agni, to the Fathers—he who, offered as an oblation unto thee, wanders as one possessing his own portion (*svadhā*).
Clothed in life, let the remnant approach; may he be united with a body, full of luster.
Run past the two dogs, the sons of Saramā, the four-eyed and brindled, by the straight path.
Then go to the benevolent fathers who rejoice in the company of Yama.
O Yama, those two dogs of yours who are guardians, four-eyed, dwelling on the paths, with the gaze of men—to them, O King, entrust this man; grant him well-being and freedom from disease. (12)
The two broad-nosed, honey-colored messengers of Yama, who delight in the life-force of others, wander among the people.
May they today restore to us here a favorable life-force, so that we may behold the sun. 13.
Soma purifies itself for some; others attend to the clarified butter.
May he go even to those for whom the honey flows forth. 14.
O Yama, may you go to those ancient seers who were winners of the *ṛta*, born of *ṛta*, and increasers of *ṛta*, the ascetic ones born of austerity. 15.
Those who are unassailable through austerity, those who have gone to heaven by means of austerity,
and those who have performed great austerity— may he go even to them.
Those who fight in the great battles, the heroes who sacrifice their own bodies for heaven,
or those who give away a thousandfold sacrificial fees— may he go even to them.
O Yama, go unto the seers who perform penance, those born of austerity, the poets with a thousand paths who guard the sun.
Be pleasant to him, O Earth, thornless and providing a dwelling;
grant him wide-spreading protection.
(20a) Be established in the unconfined, broad world of earth.
(20c) Those *svadhā* offerings which you made while living—may they be dripping with sweetness for you. {8} (21a) I call your mind with my mind; come here, enjoying these houses. Come!
Unite with the ancestors, unite with Yama; may gentle, strengthening breezes blow upon you.
May the Maruts, the water-carriers who move upon the waters, lift you up;
making cold with the goat, let them sprinkle [the world] with rain—*bāl*. 22.
I have called forth life for the sake of long life, for wisdom, for skill, and for living.
Let your mind go to its own kin; then hasten toward the ancestors. 23.
Let not your mind, nor your flesh, nor your limbs, nor your essence be lost; let nothing of your body perish here.
May the tree not press against you, nor may the great goddess Earth;
having found a place among the fathers who have Yama as their king, burn there.

Whatever limb of yours has been cast away, or your out-breath and in-breath that have departed—let the Fathers, dwelling together in one nest, having gathered there, lead you back again from pasture to pasture. 26.
The living have driven him away from his home; carry him out from here, beyond the village.
Death was the wise messenger of Yama; he sent the vital breaths to the fathers.
Those Dasyus who have entered among the fathers, who move about in the guise of kinsmen, consuming what is not offered;
those who carry away *parāpur*s and *nipur*s—may Agni blow them away from this sacrifice.
May the fathers enter here, making our home pleasant for us and prolonging our lives;
may we be able to serve them with oblations, reaching toward them, living many autumns. //29//
The cow which I bestow upon you, and the milk-rice meal—by means of that, may he become the sustainer of the people who here were without livelihood.
Cross over to the one rich in horses, she who is most gracious; cross further toward the newest descendant of Ṛkṣaka.
(31c) May he who struck you deserve to be slain; may he not find any other portion [of sacrificial food]. //31//
Yama is the higher, Vivasvān the lower; beyond that, I see nothing at all.
Upon Yama my sacrifice is established; Vivasvān has spread himself out along it. 32.
They concealed the immortal [portion] from mortals; having made it of like appearance, they bestowed it upon Vivasvat.
And she brought forth the two Aśvins when that occurred; Saraṇyū abandoned the two pairs. 33.
Those who were buried, those who were scattered, those who were cremated, and those who were raised up—
bring all those ancestors here, O Agni, to eat the oblation.

Those who have been consumed by fire and those who have not been consumed by fire, who rejoice in the midst of heaven through their own inherent power (*svadhā*),—you know them, O Jātavedas; may they enjoy the sacrifice and the sacrificial blade through their own inherent power. 35.
Be auspicious in your heat; do not burn me, O Agni; do not scorch my body with your heat.
Let your fury be in the forests, let that which you sustain be upon the earth.
I grant this dwelling to him who has come here and has become mine;
Yama, the wise one, has declared this in reply: "Let him abide here with my riches."
We measure out this measure so that it may not be exceeded for another hundred autumns before us. //38//
We measure out this measure of affection so that it may not diminish for us until a hundred autumns have passed.
(18.2.40a) We measure out this measure so that it may not be exhausted for another [year].
(18.2.40c) Before a hundred autumns have passed. (18.2.41a) We measure out this measure so that it may not be exhausted for another [year].
Before a hundred autumns have passed for us. //41//
We measure out this measure so that it may not be exhausted for another hundred autumns before us. //42//
Let us measure out this span so that it may not be exhausted for another hundred autumns before us. //43//
We measure out this measure so that it may not be exhausted for another hundred autumns. //44//
I have measured myself; I have gone to the light. May I be long-lived, so that I may not die before another hundred autumns have passed.
Inhalation, exhalation, and the pervasive breath; life-force, sight for beholding the sun—go by the path that is not narrow to the fathers of King Yama. 46.
Those who, being leaders and striving, have passed away, leaving behind their enmities and being childless—
they, having ascended to heaven, have found a world, meditating upon the back of the firmament.
"The lowest heaven is watery; the middle one is full of mist;
the third is indeed the radiant heaven, wherein the ancestors dwell. (AVŚ 18.2.48)
Those who are the fathers of our father, those who are our grandfathers, who have entered the wide mid-air;
those who dwell upon the earth and in the sky—to those ancestors we pay homage with reverence. 49.
(50) Indeed, this is it, and not another; you see the sun in the sky. Cover him with earth as a mother covers her son with the hem of her garment.
(51) Indeed, this is it, and not another; there is no other state of aging beyond this.
As a wife covers her husband with a garment, so do you, O Earth, cover him.
I envelop you with the auspicious garment of the earth, the mother;
may there be prosperity among the living, and may that *svadhā* which belongs to the ancestors be yours.
O Agni and Soma, you who prepare the way, bestow a pleasant dwelling and a treasure upon the gods, creating wide space;
go there where Pūṣan goes forth, he who carries [the offerings] by straight paths. //53//
May Pūṣan, the guardian of the world whose cattle are never lost, lead you forth from here, he who is wise.
May he deliver you over to these ancestors, and may Agni deliver you to the gods who are easy to find.
May Viśvāyu protect your life; may Pūṣan protect you on the distant path ahead.
Where the doers of good deeds dwell, where they have gone—there may the god Savitṛ place you. //55//
I yoke these two carriers for you, to carry you away to the world of the departed;
by means of them, may you go to the abode and the assembly of Yama.
This garment has now first come to you; cast off that which you wore here before.
O wise one, pass over to your meritorious deeds and pious works, where what was given by you in many ways among your kinsmen awaits you.

Envelop yourself with the cow-hides as a shield against Agni; cover yourself completely with fat and marrow, so that the bold one, exulting in his heat and seeking to seize you, may not, though intent on burning, leap around you.

Taking the staff from the hand of the one whose life has departed, along with his hearing, luster, and strength—right here you [remain], while we here, possessing brave heroes, shall conquer all insults and adversaries. 59.
Taking from the hand of the dead man his bow, along with dominion, splendor, and strength—seize for yourself abundant and flourishing wealth; come hither toward the world of the living!
This woman, choosing the world of her husband, has descended to you, O mortal, who have passed away.
Preserving the ancient Dharma, bestow upon her offspring and wealth here in this world. //1//
Arise, O noble lady, toward the world of the living; come to this one whose life has departed.
You have entered into this state of wifehood for your husband, who took your hand and desired you.
I saw a young woman being led away, the living one being led around from among the dead.
Since she was shrouded in blind darkness, I have led her from the east toward the west.
O inviolable cow, you who move along the path of the gods, you understand the world of the living.
This is your lord; be pleased with him, and cause him to ascend to the heavenly world. 4.
Near the sky, near the reed, you are the most excellent among the rivers;
O Agni, you are the bile of the waters.
O Agni, that which you have completely burnt, cause that to sprout again;
let the *kyāmbū*, the *śāṇḍadūrvā*, and the *vyalkaśā* grow here.
This is one [form] of yours; before this, there was another. Unite with the third light.
In this union, be beautiful in body and dear to the gods in the highest dwelling place.
Arise, go forth, run forward, and make your dwelling in the watery realm!
There, in harmony with the ancestors, rejoice with Soma and with the *svadhā* offerings. //8//
Move forward, gather yourself together; let not your limbs be scattered, nor your body.
Enter into the settled mind; go to that place where you take pleasure in the earth. 9.

May the Soma-loving Fathers anoint me with splendor; may the gods anoint me with honey and ghee. May they, leading me further for the sake of sight, increase me so that I may reach old age with my faculties intact.
May Agni anoint me thoroughly with splendor; may Viṣṇu anoint my wisdom within my mouth.
May all the gods bestow wealth upon me; may the pleasant waters purify me with their cleansing streams. 11.
May Mitra and Varuṇa encompass me; may the Ādityas, the sun-pillars, cause me to grow. May Indra anoint me with splendor upon my hands; may Savitṛ grant me long life. 12.
He who was the first of mortals to die, who was the first to depart for this world—to Yama, the son of Vivasvat, the gathering place of men, the king, do you pay honor with an oblation. 13.
Depart, O Fathers, and come back again; this sacrifice of yours is anointed with honey.
Grant us here wealth and prosperity, and bestow upon us riches accompanied by all heroic sons. //14//
Kaṇva, Kakṣīvat, Purumīḍha, Agastya, Śyāvāśva, Sobhari, Arcanānas, Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni, Atri, Kaśyapa, and Vāmadeva—may they protect us. 15.
Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni, Vasiṣṭha, Bharadvāja, Gotama, Vāmadeva—Atri has grasped our protection with his homages; O well-advising fathers, have mercy on us! 16.
Whose impurity do they pass over while being cleansed, bestowing upon us a newer and longer life? May we, increasing in progeny and wealth, be fragrant within our homes.
They anoint him, they anoint him apart, they anoint him together; they lick his creative power, they anoint him with honey.
At the swelling of the river, those who purify with gold seize the bull as he flies, the sacrificial animal, within these [waters]. //18//
O Fathers, with that which is your seal and that which is pleasing to Soma, come together with us, for you have become self-glorious.
Listen, O sages who move hitherward, you who are well-disposed, being invoked at the sacrifice.

The Atris, the Aṅgirases, the Navagvas, who were seekers of the sacrifice, bestowers of gifts, and performers of good deeds; O you who possess sacrificial fees, may you who are here rejoice upon this sacred grass.
And just as our ancient fathers of old, O Agni, aspiring toward *ṛta*, [attained their goal]...
Coming from the pure ones, they, the reciters of hymns, meditating, have broken through the earth and uncovered the ruddy dawns.
Performing good deeds, radiant, seeking the gods, like smiths blowing upon their births, O gods;
purifying Agni and strengthening Indra, they have prepared for us a vast assembly of cattle. 22.
Like a herdsman among cattle in a rich pasture, the Mighty One has beheld the final generations of the gods;
even mortals have yearned for the Urvaśīs, so that the noble one might increase the prosperity of the future man.
(18.3.24a) We have performed service for you, O skillful ones; we have let flow the truth as the dawns shine forth.
(18.3.24c) All that which the gods favor is auspicious; may we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly. //24//
May Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, protect me from the eastern quarter; may the earth, shaken by his arms, hold me aloft as the sky does.
We worship those world-makers and path-makers who are here present as the recipients of the oblations among the gods. 25.
May Dhātṛ protect me from Nirṛti, from the southern quarter; may the earth, shaken by the arms [of the gods], guard me as the sky above.
We worship the creators of the worlds, the makers of paths, who here are the recipients of the oblations among the gods. 26.
May Aditi, together with the Ādityas, protect me from the western quarter; may she, who is moved by her arms, uphold the earth as the sky is above.
We worship those world-makers and path-makers who abide here as the recipients of the oblations of the gods. 27.
May Soma protect me from the northern quarter along with all the gods; may the earth, shaken by the arms [of the gods], be as high above as heaven.
We worship those world-makers and path-makers who are here present as the recipients of the oblations of the gods. 28.
May the supporter, the sustainer, hold you up, as Savitṛ holds the sun aloft above the sky.
We sacrifice to those world-makers and path-makers who are here present as the recipients of the oblations among the gods. 29.
In the eastern direction, before it was enclosed, I place you in the *svadhā* offering, as the earth moved by the arms [of the gods] is above the sky.
We worship those world-makers and path-makers who are here present as the recipients of the oblations among the gods.
In the southern direction, before it was enclosed, I place you in the *svadhā* offering, as the earth moved by the arms [of the gods] is above the sky.
We worship those who created the world and made the paths, you who are here as the recipients of the oblations among the gods. 31.
In the western direction, before it is closed, I place you within the *svadhā* offering, as far-reaching as the earth is from the sky above.
We sacrifice to the world-makers and path-makers who are here present as the recipients of the oblations of the gods. 32.
In the northern quarter, before it was enclosed, I place you within the *svadhā* offering, as far-reaching as the earth and the sky above.
We worship those world-makers and path-makers who are here present as the recipients of the oblations among the gods. 33.
In the firm quarter, before the world was closed in, I place you within the *svadhā* offering, as the earth, shaken by arms, is placed above the sky.
We sacrifice to those world-makers and path-makers who are here present as the recipients of the oblations of the gods. 34.
In the upward direction, before it is closed, I place you within the *svadhā* offering, as far-reaching as the earth is from the sky above.
We worship those world-makers and path-makers who are here present as the recipients of the oblation among the gods. 35.
You are the upholder; you are the sustainer; you are the bull. //36//
You are full of water, you are full of honey, you are full of wind. //37//
From here and from there, protect me, as you two went striving together like Yama and Yamī.
Men seeking the gods brought you forward; sit down, you who know your own place.
Be a comfortable seat for our Soma; with prostrations, we join you with ancient prayer.
Like a patron on a path, the hymn goes forth; may all the immortals hear this. 39.
He has ascended after the three steps; he has followed this four-footed [path] by means of his vow.
By means of the syllable, he measures out the hymn; at the navel of Cosmic Order, he purifies it thoroughly.
For the sake of the gods, he chose death; for the sake of progeny, why did he not choose immortality?
Bṛhaspati, the seer, extended the sacrifice; Yama relinquished his dear body.
O Agni Jātavedas, being praised, you have carried the oblations after making them fragrant;
you have presented them to the ancestors, and they have eaten them with the *svadhā* call. O God, eat the offered oblations. 42.
Sitting in the lap of the ruddy ones, bestow wealth upon the mortal who offers oblations.
O fathers, grant a portion of that treasure to your sons; bestow strength here upon them.

O Agniṣvātta fathers, come here; sit each upon his seat, O excellent leaders. Having eaten the oblations presented upon the sacrificial grass, bestow upon us wealth consisting of all heroic sons. //44//
The Soma-loving fathers have been invited to our dear offerings placed upon the sacrificial grass;
may they come hither, may they hear us here, may they speak for us, and may they protect us. 45.

Those who were our father’s fathers, those grandfathers, the most excellent ones who followed after the drinking of Soma—may Yama, rejoicing with them, desiring [the offerings], eat the oblations according to his desire along with those who desire them. 46.

Those who have thirsted among the gods, panting, knowing the invocations, fashioning hymns with their chants—O Agni, come with the thousand god-praising, truthful sages, the seers who sit by the heated offering. 47.

O Agni, come hither with those who are true, who eat the oblation and drink the oblation, who are on the same chariot with Indra and the swift gods—with the ancient, far-reaching seers who sit by the heated milk-offering, O you of easy discernment. 48.
Crawl near to this mother earth, the wide-extending, the very gracious Pṛthivī.
Soft as wool to those who give sacrificial gifts—may she protect you from the front on your journey.
Open wide, O Earth; do not press down. Be easy of access to him, easy of approach. Cover him, O Earth, as a mother covers her son with the hem of her garment.
(50) May the Earth, opening wide, stand firm. Let a thousand columns support her.
May those houses drip with clarified butter; may they be pleasant and provide shelter for him here at all times.
I prop up the earth for you; placing this world around you, may I not come to harm.
O Fathers, you uphold this pillar; there Yama shall prepare a dwelling place for you. //52//
O Agni, do not overturn this cup; it is dear to the gods and to those who offer Soma.
This cup from which the gods drink—let the immortal gods rejoice therein. //53//
The Atharvan brought a full cup for Indra, the possessor of vigor;
therein he provides a portion of the well-performed rite, therein the drop flows at all times. 54.
Whatever the black bird has pecked at you, or the ant, the snake, or even a wild beast—
may Agni make all that free from disease, and Soma, who has entered into the Brahmins.
The plants are full of milk; my milk is full of milk.
Whatever milk belongs to the milk of the waters, may it purify me along with that.
May these women, non-widows with good husbands, touch themselves with collyrium and clarified butter.
Tearless, free from disease, and possessing fine jewels, may these women first ascend to their place of origin.
Unite with the ancestors, unite with Yama and with the merit of your sacrifices and pious works in the highest heaven.
Leaving behind all that is blameworthy, return to your home; reunited with a body, may you be full of splendor.

Those who are the fathers of our father, those who are our grandfathers, who have entered the wide mid-air—to them [belongs] the breath of life from the light; may it today fashion our bodies according to our desire. //59//
May the mist be auspicious for you; may the spray cool you with peace. O cool one, O possessor of coolness! O refreshing one, O possessor of refreshment!
O female frog, be auspicious in the waters; pacify this fire for us.
May Vivasvat grant us fearlessness—he who is the good protector, the swift-giver, the bounteous giver.
May these many heroes be ours here; may there be abundance for me in cattle and horses.
May Vivasvat establish us in immortality; may death depart and immortality come to us. May he protect these men until old age; let not their vital breaths go to Yama.

He who has established himself in the mid-air by his greatness, the seer of the fathers, the guardian of thoughts—to him, O friends of all, offer worship with oblations; may that Yama grant us further life.
Ascend to the highest heaven, O seers; do not be afraid.
O drinkers of Soma, you who drink the Soma, this oblation is prepared for you; we have gone to the highest light. 64.
With his lofty banner Agni shines; the bull bellows across the two worlds.
From the very end of heaven he has brought the highest [light]; the buffalo has grown great in the lap of the waters. 65.
When they beheld you with longing hearts as you flew toward the vault of heaven like a fair-winged bird—
golden-winged, the messenger of Varuṇa, a restless bird in the womb of Yama.
O Indra, bring us wisdom, just as a father provides for his sons. Teach us, O much-invoked one, on this path; living, may we attain the light.
Those jars which the gods held for you, covered with cakes—
may they be yours, full of *svadhā*, honeyed, and dripping with ghee.
Those parched grains mixed with sesame seeds that I scatter for you, accompanied by the *svadhā* offering—may they be abundant and powerful for you; may King Yama grant his approval for them.
Give back again, O Lord of the Forest, that which has been placed within you,
so that he may sit at the dwelling of Yama and speak the sacred ordinances.
Take hold, O Jātavedas; let your flame be brilliant.
Completely burn his body and deliver him to the world of those who have performed good deeds. //71//
Those ancestors of yours who have passed away before, and those who came later—
to them let this stream of clarified butter flow, a hundredfold, overflowing.
Ascend this, wiping away old age; here your own [lights] shine forth loftily.
Go forward; do not leave us from the midst, you who are the first among the fathers in this world.
Ascend the mother, O Jātavedas; with the paths of the fathers, I cause you all to ascend together.
Sent forth as the bearer of oblations, you have carried the offerings; may you, being yoked, place the sacrificer in the world of the righteous.
The gods, the seasons, prepare the sacrifice: the oblation, the sacrificial cake, the ladles, and the implements of the sacrifice.
Go by those paths traveled by the gods, by which those who have sacrificed go to the heavenly world. //2//
Behold well the path of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*), along which the virtuous Aṅgirases travel;
go by those paths to heaven where the Ādityas consume the honey, and take your station upon the third firmament.
Three birds with beautiful wings, peacocks of the highest realm, rest upon the back, the summit of the firmament.
May the heavenly worlds, established through immortality, yield nourishment and vigor for the sacrificer.
The *juhū* has supported the sky, the *upabhṛt* the intermediate space, and the *dhruvā* has supported the earth as its foundation.
May these worlds, whose backs are dripping with ghee and which lead to heaven, yield every desire for the sacrificer.
Ascend the firm earth, which provides nourishment for all; stride toward the intermediate space with the *upabhṛt* ladle.
Go to heaven with the *juhū* ladle together with the sacrificer; with the *sruva* as your calf, milk all the swelling quarters, being free from anger.
"By means of fords they cross over the great slopes"—thus [it is said] of those who perform sacrifice and do good deeds, by which path they go.
Therein they have established a world for the sacrificer, when the quarters and the beings were fashioned. (AVŚ 18.4.7)
The eastern fire is the path of the Aṅgirases; the Gārhapatya fire is the path of the Ādityas; the Dakṣiṇāgni fire is the path of the sacrificial gifts.
With all your limbs intact, come hither as a powerful one, united with the greatness of Agni established by the sacred word.

(9) May the eastern fire warm you; may it be auspicious before you. May the Gārhapatya fire warm you from behind; may it be auspicious. May the Dakṣiṇāgni fire warm you; may it be a refuge and a shield from the north, from the middle, and from the intermediate space. O Agni, protect us from the terrible in every direction.
O Agni, with your most auspicious bodies, carry the sacrificer to the heavenly world;
becoming horses that bear you on their backs, convey him to where they revel in communal feasting with the gods.
O Agni, burn him peacefully from behind, peacefully from the front, peacefully from above, and peacefully from below. Burn him!
Jātavedas, you who are one and yet divided threefold, place him rightly in the world of those who have performed good deeds.
May the fires, well-kindled, take hold of the sacrificial portion belonging to Prajāpati, O Jātavedas;
making it cooked, do not cast it away from here.
The sacrifice goes forth, spread out and being prepared, toward the world of heaven for the sacrificer.
May the fires take pleasure in it—this offering made with all oblations, the sacrificial portion belonging to Prajāpati, O Jātavedas. 13.
Having sacrificed, he has ascended the piled fire, about to fly up from the back of the firmament to heaven.
For him, the luminous, heavenly path leading to the gods shines forth from the sky for his well-performed deed. 14.
Agni is your Hotṛ, Bṛhaspati your Adhvaryu; may Indra be your Brahman priest on the right.
This sacrifice, offered and completed, goes where the former path of those who have sacrificed lies.
May the sacrificial porridge, rich in cakes and milk, settle here.
We worship the world-makers and the path-makers who are present here as the recipients of the oblations among the gods. 16.
May the sacrificial porridge, accompanied by cakes and curds, settle here.
We worship those world-makers and path-makers who are present here as the recipients of the oblation among the gods. 17.
May the sacrificial porridge, rich in cakes and rich in drops, settle here.
We worship those world-makers and path-makers who are present here as the recipients of the oblations of the gods. 18.
May the sacrificial porridge, rich in cakes and rich in ghee, settle here.
We worship those world-makers and path-makers who are present here as the recipients of the oblations among the gods. 19.
May the sacrificial porridge, containing cakes and meat, settle here.
We worship those world-makers and path-makers who are present here as the recipients of the oblations among the gods.
May the sacrificial porridge, containing cakes and food, settle here.
We worship those who made the worlds, who made the paths, you who are here as the recipients of the oblations among the gods. 21.
May the rice-porridge, rich in cakes and honey, settle here.
We worship those world-makers and path-makers who are present here as the recipients of the oblations of the gods. 22.
May the sacrificial porridge, rich in cakes and flavorful, settle here.
We worship those world-makers and path-makers who are present here as the recipients of the oblations of the gods. 23.
May the sacrificial porridge, containing cakes and free from husks, settle here.
We worship those world-makers and path-makers who are present here as the recipients of the oblations among the gods. 24.
The jars which the gods supported for you, covered with cakes—may they be yours, possessing the *svadhā* call, full of sweetness, and dripping with ghee. //25//
These parched grains mixed with sesame seeds, accompanied by the *svadhā* offering, which I scatter for you—may they be abundant and powerful for you; may King Yama grant his approval of them.
The most abundant imperishability. //27//

The drop has fallen upon the earth, upon the sky, upon this womb and that which was before; following the drop as it moves along toward the common womb, I offer it according to the seven priestly offices.
They who behold the hundred-streamed Vāyu, the light, the finder of heaven—their wealth is visible to those who look upon men;
they who satisfy and bestow at all times, they milk the sacrificial gift whose mother is sevenfold.
They milk the treasure-chest, the four-holed jar, the *iḍā*-cow, the honey-sweet, for well-being;
the strengthening, exhilarating Aditi among the people—O Agni, do not harm her in the highest heaven. 30.
This garment, O God Savitṛ, you give to him to wear.
Therefore, dwelling in the kingdom of Yama, move about wearing a garment of silk.
The parched grain became a cow; its calf was sesame.
Indeed, one lives upon that inexhaustible [cow] in the realm of King Yama. 32.
May these cows of yours, O [Name], be milch-cows that yield all desires;
may the dark ones, the tawny ones, those of uniform appearance and those of diverse forms, standing with sesame-seed calves, attend upon you here.
His grains are brindled, tawny, and falcon-colored; his grains are black and ruddy cows.
May they, with sesame for their calves, yielding nourishment for him, be ever-present and never-failing.
In Vaiśvānara I offer this oblation, a thousandfold fountain with a hundred streams;
swelling up, it sustains the father, the grandfather, and the great-grandfather.

The ancestors, with their *svadhā* offerings, attend upon that inexhaustible fountain which has a thousand streams and a hundred currents, spreading itself out upon the surface of the waters, yielding nourishment and never failing.
This water of the Kasa has been piled up by piling; O kinsmen, look upon it! This mortal attains immortality; build him a home as long as he has kin. 37.
Right here be a winner of wealth; right here be your thought, right here your resolve.
Right here be more heroic, a bestower of vitality, unassailable.
May these honey-sweet waters, satisfying sons and grandsons, yielding *svadhā* and nectar to the ancestors—may the divine waters satisfy both [the living and the dead]. (AVŚ 18.4.39)
O Waters, send forth Agni toward the Fathers; may my Fathers enjoy this sacrifice.
May those who attend upon the seated strength bestow upon us wealth consisting of all heroic sons.
{23} They kindle the immortal bearer of oblations, the lover of clarified butter.
He knows the hidden treasures and the ancestors who have gone to the far distance. //41//
The mash which I offer you, the rice, and the meat—
may these be yours, accompanied by the *svadhā* call, sweet as honey, and dripping with ghee.
These parched grains mixed with sesame seeds, accompanied by the *svadhā* offering, which I scatter for you—may they be abundant and powerful for you; may King Yama grant his approval of them. 43.
This is the former and this the latter path by which your ancestors have departed;
those who are the leaders and followers of this [path] carry you to the world of the righteous.
Those seeking the gods invoke Sarasvatī; they invoke Sarasvatī while the sacrifice is being performed.
The doers of good deeds invoke Sarasvatī; may Sarasvatī grant what is desirable to the donor.
The fathers invoke Sarasvatī as they approach the sacrifice from the south;
having seated yourselves upon this sacred grass, rejoice! Bestow upon us food free from disease. 46.

O Sarasvatī, you who have come on the same chariot with the Pitṛs, O Goddess, rejoicing with the hymns and the *svadhā* offerings—bestow here upon the sacrificer a portion of the *iḍā* worth a thousand, and the increase of wealth. 47.
I cause you to enter the earth upon the earth; may the divine Ordainer extend our lifespan.
May he who finds wealth depart for you; then, having died, may they be united with the Fathers. 48.
