Come forth together and wipe away that which they have spoken against you here.
O inviolable ones, let this be more agreeable to the giver than to me, who am to enjoy it among my ancestors.
(50a) This auspicious sacrificial fee has come hither; by this [gift] a well-milking, strength-bestowing cow has been given.
(50c) May she, while clinging to the living in their youth, deliver these [ancestors] over to the fathers in old age.
(51a) I bring forth this sacred grass for the fathers; I spread it out, higher [than before], for the living gods.
So ascend, O man, becoming worthy of sacrifice; may the fathers recognize you as you depart.
Sit upon this sacrificial grass; you have become fit for the sacrifice. May the fathers recognize you as you depart.
Assemble your body limb by limb; I restore your members with a sacred prayer (*brahman*).
The Parṇa tree is the king, the covering of the sacrificial vessels; may it come to us with vigor, strength, power, and vital energy.
Bestowing life upon those who live, grant long-lived existence for a hundred autumns.
The portion of vigor that begot this [world] has attained sovereignty over foods;
worship him with oblations, O Viśvāmitras! May that Yama grant us further life. 54.
Just as the five young men scattered the dwelling for Yama, so do I scatter this dwelling, so that there may be many for me.
Bear this gold which your father bore of old;
cleanse the right hand of your father as he goes to heaven.
Those who are living and those who have died, those who are born and those worthy of sacrifice—
let a stream of clarified butter, a flowing wave of honey, go forth for them.
The bull of hymns, far-seeing, flows clear; the sun of days, the prolonger of the dawns from heaven.
The breath of the rivers has bellowed toward the jars, entering the heart of Indra with inspired thought. //58//
May your brilliant smoke envelop the sky; may your bright [light] be spread abroad. For like the sun with its radiance, you shine with beauty, O Purifier.
The drop (indu) goes forward to the appointed place of Indra; as a friend, he does not fail the promise of his friend.
Like a youth [to] maidens, Soma flows together into the jar by a path of a hundred ways.
They have eaten and they have rejoiced; they have shaken off their dear [enemies].
The self-luminous sages have offered praise; we implore the youngest one.
Come hither, O Soma-loving Fathers, by the deep paths traveled by the ancestors;
bestowing upon us long life and progeny, attend us with the increase of wealth.
Depart, O Soma-loving Fathers, by the deep, ancient paths;
then, having enjoyed our oblation, return again to our homes in the month, blessed with good offspring and heroic sons.
Whatever single limb of yours Agni Jātavedas left behind when leading you to the world of the fathers, that I now replenish for you once more; O fathers, being whole in limb, rejoice in heaven.
Jātavedas has become the messenger sent forth; at evening, at the close of day, he is to be praised by men.
You have given to the fathers; they have eaten with the *svadhā* offering. Eat, O God, the presented oblations.
O earth, draw this mind of his toward you here, just as kinsmen draw one another to their bosom. Cover him with your breast.
May the worlds, the seats of the fathers, be beautified; I set you down in the world that is the seat of the fathers.
You are the sacrificial grass for those who are our fathers.
O Varuṇa, loosen the uppermost bond from us; untie the lowest.
Then, O Āditya, may we be sinless before you and before Aditi within your sacred law.
O Varuṇa, release from us all those snares with which one is bound in the encounter, whether in close range or at a distance.
Then may we live for a hundred autumns, protected and guarded by you, O King.
To Agni Kavyavāhana, the bearer of the *svadhā* offering, be *svadhā* and homage!
To Soma accompanied by the ancestors, Svadhā! Homage!
To the fathers who partake of Soma, Svadhā! Adoration! //73//
To Yama, who possesses the ancestors, Svadhā! Homage! //74//
This, O great-grandfather, is for you, svadhā, and for those who follow you. //75//
This, O grandfather, is for you as *svadhā*, and for those who follow you. //76//
This is for you, father; svadhā!
Svadhā to the ancestors who dwell upon the earth! //78//
Svadhā to the fathers who dwell in the intermediate space! //79//
Svadhā to the fathers who dwell in heaven!
(80) Homage to you, O fathers, for strength; homage to you, O fathers, for sap! (81)
Homage to you, O fathers, for your radiance; homage to you, O fathers, for your wrath. //82//
Homage to you, O fathers, for that which is terrible; homage to you, O fathers, for that which is cruel. //83//
Homage to you, O fathers, for that which is auspicious; homage to you, O fathers, for that which is pleasant. //84//
Homage to you, O fathers; the *svadhā* offering is yours, O fathers. //85//
O ancestors who are here, you who are the ancestors here—you follow them; may you become the most excellent among them. //86//
Those who are the living fathers here, and we who are here—may we follow after them, and may we be the best among them. //87//
O Agni, let us kindle you, the radiant, the unaging god, so that this most praiseworthy fuel of yours may shine in the sky;
bring nourishment to those who offer praise. 88.
The moon runs within the waters; the fair-winged bird speeds through the sky.
O you whose rims are gold, the lightnings find not your track. O Heaven and Earth, take note of this for me!
May the rivers flow together; may the winds and the winged birds come together.
Prosper this sacrifice through our songs; I offer it with the flowing oblation. 1.1c–d.
O Homas, protect this sacrifice; O Saṃsrāvaṇās, protect this sacrifice as well! Increase these songs of praise; I offer with the oblation of the Saṃsrāvya.
Taking hold of every form and every age, I embrace him.
May the four quarters increase this sacrifice; I offer it with the flowing oblation. 3.
May the waters from the Himalayas be auspicious for you, and may the waters from the springs be auspicious for you.
May the flowing waters be auspicious for you, and may the waters of the rain be auspicious for you. (AVŚ 19.2.1)
May the waters of the desert be auspicious for you; may the waters of the marshes be auspicious for you.
May the waters dug from the earth be auspicious for you, and those brought in jars be auspicious for you.
The cloudless ones, digging, the inspired singers, the workers in the deep;
we speak toward the waters, the physicians more skilled than physicians. 3.
Of the waters of heaven, of the waters flowing in streams—of those waters, indeed, in their cleansing, you become swift horses, O possessors of vigor. //4//
Those waters are auspicious, those waters which bring freedom from disease;
just as there is delight for one who is satisfied, so may they grant you healing remedies.
From heaven, from earth, from the intermediate space, from the trees, and from the plants—whithersoever Jātavedas has been distributed, from there, being praised, come to us with favor. 1.

(19.3.2) That majesty of yours which is in the waters, which is in the forests, which is in the plants, and within the cattle and the waters—O Agni, grasp all those bodies; with them come to us, O eternal giver of wealth. 2.

(19.3.3) That majesty of yours which is among the gods, that heavenly realm; that body of yours which has entered into the fathers; that prosperity of yours which has spread among men—O Agni, with that, bestow wealth upon us. (3)
To the one with attentive ears, the seer worthy of being known, I approach for a gift with words and hymns.
May that from which there is fear become for us freedom from fear; O Agni, through sacrifice, appease the wrath of the gods. 4.

The oblation which Atharvan offered first, that which was born when Jātavedas made the offering—that very one I invoke for you as the first. May Agni, being satisfied by these, carry the oblation to Agni; *svāhā*! 1.

I place before me the goddess Ākūti, the fortunate one; may she, the mother of thought, be easy for us to invoke. Whatever hope I pursue, may that be mine alone; may I find her entered into my mind. //2//
O Bṛhaspati, come to us with intention; come to us with intention. Furthermore, bestow fortune upon us, and furthermore, be one who is easy for us to invoke. 3.
May Bṛhaspati, the descendant of Aṅgiras, acknowledge my intention and this speech.
May he, from whom the gods have come into being as deities, follow after us with excellent guidance according to our desire. 4.4a-c.
Indra is the king of the moving world and of the peoples upon the earth, over all that exists in its various forms.
From there he bestows riches upon the donor; may he, being praised, send forth bounty hitherward.
The Puruṣa has a thousand arms, a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet;
having pervaded the earth on all sides, he stood beyond it by the measure of ten fingers. //1//
With three steps he ascended to heaven; one step of his remained here again.
Thus he strode out in all directions across both the hungry and the hungerless.
So great is his majesty, and yet the Puruṣa is even greater than that. All beings constitute one quarter of him; his three quarters are the immortal in heaven.
The Person alone is all this, whatever has been and whatever is to be;
moreover, he is the lord of immortality, since he came into being together with what is other than himself.
When they divided the Puruṣa, into how many parts did they arrange him?
What was his mouth, what were his arms, and what are his thighs and feet called?
The Brāhmaṇa was his mouth; the Rājanya became his arms; that which was his waist became the Vaiśya; from his feet the Śūdra was born. //6//
The moon was born from the mind; from the eye the sun was born; from the mouth Indra and Agni were born; from the breath Vāyu was born.
From his navel the intermediate space arose; from his head the sky evolved;
from his feet the earth and from his hearing the quarters—thus they fashioned the worlds. //8//
In the beginning, Virāj came into being; from Virāj, Puruṣa was born.
Once born, he extended beyond the earth, both behind and before.
When the gods performed the sacrifice with man as the oblation,
spring was its clarified butter, summer the fuel, and autumn the offering.
They sprinkled that sacrifice with the rainy season, the Puruṣa born in the beginning;
with him the gods sacrificed—the Sādhyas and those who are the Vasus.
From him were born horses, and whatever animals have two rows of teeth;
from him indeed were born cows, and from him were born goats and sheep.
From that sacrifice in which everything was offered, the Ṛg-verses and the Sāman-chants were born;
from it the meters were born, and from it the Yajus-formula was produced. 13.
From that sacrifice in which everything was offered, the speckled butter was gathered;
he made those animals—the ones belonging to Vāyu, those of the forest, and those of the village.
Seven were its enclosing sticks, thrice seven were the fuel-sticks prepared;
when the gods, performing the sacrifice, bound Puruṣa as the victim. 15.
From the head of the great god, seventy-seven stalks were born from King Soma, once he had been produced from Puruṣa.
The variegated lights together in heaven, the crawling things, the swift ones in the world—desiring Turmiṣa’s favor, I honor the days and the firmament with songs of praise. //1//
O Agni, may Kṛttikā and Rohiṇī be easy to invoke for me; may Mṛgaśiras be auspicious and Ārdrā bring peace.
May Punarvasū and Sūnṛtā be dear to me, Puṣya be radiant, Āśleṣā my path, and Maghā my course.
May Puṣya, Pūrvaphalgunī, and here Hasta, Citrā, Śivā, and Svāti be auspicious and bring me happiness;
may Rādha, Viśākhā, the easily invoked Anurādhā, Jyeṣṭhā, and the excellent constellation Mūla be free from harm. //3//
May the Pūrvāṣāḍhās grant me food; may the divine Uttarāṣāḍhās bring me strength.
May Abhijit grant me merit; may Śravaṇa and the Śraviṣṭhās provide me with excellent nourishment.
May the great Śatabhiṣaj come to me with wide space; may the two Proṣṭhapadas grant me good protection.
May Revatī and the two Aśvayujas bring me fortune; may they bring me wealth and prosperity. //5//

Those constellations which are in heaven, in the intermediate space, in the waters, on the earth, and those which are among the mountains and in the directions—may all these, as the moon moves along fashioning them, be auspicious for me. //1//
May the twenty-eight auspicious and beneficial [days] grant me success in my endeavors.
I resort to effort and peace; I resort to peace and effort. Let there be homage to day and night. //2//
May there be well-being for me; may my morning be auspicious, my evening auspicious, my day auspicious; may I have good game and good omens.
O Agni, having gone to the immortal realm for well-being, may you return again with joy, easy to invoke. 3.
O Savitṛ, drive away all those who seek to revile me, those who seek to humiliate me, those who speak against me, and those who sneer at me— drive them away like empty jars.
May we consume the auspicious snot that is free from evil; may the auspicious snot flow away.
O Evil One, may your nose be propitious, and may the one who goes toward merit urinate upon it. 5.
O Brahmanaspati, those [streams] which blow forth in all directions like the wind—
O Indra, having made them flow together, make them most auspicious for me.
May there be well-being for us; may there be fearlessness for us; homage be to Day and Night! //7//
Peaceful is the sky, peaceful is the earth, and peaceful is this wide intermediate space.
Peaceful are the waters rich in moisture; may the plants be peaceful for us. //1//
The omens of the past have been stilled; may all that we have done and left undone be stilled for us.
May what has been and what is to be stilled; may everything indeed be peace for us. (2)
This goddess of speech who is supreme, sharpened by the sacred word (*brahman*), by which she created that which was terrible—by that very [speech], may there be peace for us. 3.
This mind of yours which is supreme, sharpened by sacred knowledge (*brahman*), by which you created that which is terrible—by that very [mind], may there be peace for us. 4.

These five sense-faculties, with the mind as the sixth, which have been sharpened within my heart by Brahmā—by those very same [powers] with which he created the terrible, may there be peace for us. 5.
May Mitra be auspicious to us, may Varuṇa be auspicious, may Viṣṇu be auspicious, and may Prajāpati be auspicious;
may Indra and Bṛhaspati be auspicious to us, and may Aryaman be auspicious to us.
May Mitra be auspicious to us, may Varuṇa be auspicious, may Vivasvat be auspicious, and may Antaka be auspicious.
May terrestrial and atmospheric portents be auspicious to us, and may the planets that move through the heavens be auspicious to us.
May the earth, though trembling, be auspicious to us; may the meteor that has been cast out be auspicious.
May the cows with red milk be auspicious, and may the earth as it flows downward be auspicious.
May the star struck by meteors bring us peace; may malevolent spells and sorceries be peaceful for us, and may magical rites be peaceful.
May the buried *valgā* plants be peaceful for us, and may meteors and regional calamities likewise be peaceful for us. 9.
May the lunar grahas be auspicious to us, and may the Āditya together with Rāhu be auspicious;
may Death, whose banner is smoke, be auspicious to us, and may the Rudras of sharp splendor be auspicious. 10.
May the Rudras be auspicious, may the Vasus be auspicious, may the Ādityas be auspicious, and may the Agnis be auspicious.
May the great seers and gods be auspicious to us; may the gods be auspicious and Bṛhaspati be auspicious. //11//

Brahman, Prajāpati, Dhātṛ, the worlds, the Vedas, the seven seers, and the fires—by them has this auspicious rite been performed for me. May Indra grant me protection; may Brahman grant me protection.
May all the gods grant me protection; may every god grant me protection. 12.
Whatever peaceful things the Seven Seers know in this world—may they all be auspicious for me; may there be auspiciousness for me, may there be fearlessness for me. 13.
The earth is peace, the mid-air is peace, the sky is peace, the waters are peace, the herbs are peace, the trees are peace, all the gods are peace for me;
all the gods are peace for me—peace, peace, peace with [all] peaces!
Whatever here is terrible, whatever here is cruel, whatever here is evil—that is stilled, that is auspicious; may everything indeed be tranquility for us. 14.
May Indra and Agni be auspicious to us with their protections; may Indra and Varuṇa, to whom oblations are offered, be auspicious to us.
May Indra and Soma be auspicious for our well-being and for health; may Indra and Pūṣan be auspicious to us in the winning of booty. //1//
May Bhaga be auspicious to us, and may our praise be auspicious; may Puraṃdhi be auspicious to us, and may riches be auspicious.
May the praise of the true and well-governed be auspicious to us, and may Aryaman, born of many, be auspicious to us. //2//
May the Ordainer be auspicious to us, and may the Sustainer be auspicious to us; may the far-reaching one be auspicious to us with her self-sustaining powers.
May the two great worlds be auspicious, may the mountain be auspicious to us, and may the auspicious invocations of the gods be favorable to us. 3.
May Agni, with his face of light, be auspicious to us; may Mitra and Varuṇa and the Aśvins be auspicious to us.
May the good deeds of the doers of good be auspicious to us; may the swift wind blow auspiciously upon us. 4.

May Heaven and Earth be auspicious to us at our first invocation; may the intermediate space be auspicious for us to behold. May the plants and the trees be auspicious to us; may the victorious Lord of the Atmosphere be auspicious to us. //5//
May the god Indra with the Vasus be auspicious to us; may Varuṇa, the one of fair praise, with the Ādityas be auspicious.
May the cooling Rudra with the Rudras be auspicious to us; may Tvaṣṭṛ with the divine dames hear us here for our welfare.
May Soma be auspicious for us; may the sacred formulation (*brahman*) be auspicious for us; may the pressing-stones be auspicious for us, and may the sacrifices be auspicious.
May the measurements of the sacrificial posts be auspicious for us; may the plants be auspicious for us, and may the altar be auspicious. //7//
May the far-seeing Sūrya rise for our welfare; may the four quarters be auspicious for us.
May the firm mountains be auspicious for us; may the rivers and the waters be auspicious for us. //8//
May Aditi be auspicious to us through her sacred laws; may the Maruts, the singers of beautiful hymns, be auspicious to us.
May Viṣṇu be auspicious to us, and may Pūṣan be auspicious to us; may the means of protection be auspicious to us, and may Vāyu be auspicious. //9//
May the divine Savitṛ, our protector, be auspicious to us; may the dawns as they shine forth be auspicious to us.
May Parjanya be auspicious to our offspring; may the Lord of the Field be auspicious and a source of well-being to us.
May the lords of truth be auspicious to us; may our coursers be auspicious and our cattle be auspicious.
May the Ṛbhus, the skillful-handed doers of good deeds, be auspicious to us; may the ancestors be auspicious to us in our invocations. //1//

May the All-Gods be auspicious to us; may Sarasvatī, together with our prayers, be auspicious. May those who attack us be auspicious, and may those who bestow gifts be auspicious; may the divine ones and the earthly ones be auspicious to us, and may the waters be auspicious to us.
May the god Aja Ekapād be auspicious to us; may Ahi Budhnya be auspicious, and the ocean be auspicious.
May Apāṃ Napāt, the protector, be auspicious to us; may Pṛśni, the guardian of the gods, be auspicious to us. 3.
May the Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus take pleasure in this newly performed prayer;
may the celestial ones, the terrestrial ones, those born of the cow, and those worthy of sacrifice hear us.

Those who are the sacrificial priests of the gods, worthy of worship, the venerable ones of Manu, the immortal knowers of the cosmic order—may they grant us wide-striding space today. And do you all protect us always with your blessings. //5//
May that be so, O Mitra and Varuṇa; may that be so, O Agni. May this recitation be auspicious and healing for us.
May we attain a firm footing and a secure standing. Homage to the great Heaven, the dwelling place!
Dawn rolls away the darkness of her sister by her noble birth along the path.
Through this, may we win the strength ordained by the gods; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with heroic sons. //1//
Indra’s arms are strong and bull-like; these two wonderful bulls are victorious.
I shall yoke them first when the time for action arrives—those two by which the light of the Asuras was won.
Swift, sharpening his horns like a terrifying bull, the striker, the agitator of the people;
the roaring, unblinking, sole hero, Indra, conquered a hundred armies at once. //2//
With the roaring, unblinking, victorious, invincible, immovable, and bold Indra—
with that bull who holds arrows in his hand— conquer, O men, and prevail in battle!
He, the controller, with his arrow-handed [followers] and those bearing quivers; he, Indra, the uniter in battle with his host;
the conqueror of the united, the drinker of Soma, strong of arm, with his formidable bow, the shooter with well-aimed arrows. 4.

Recognized for his strength, the elder, the preeminent hero, the powerful, the vigorous, the conqueror, the fierce one— O Indra, mount your victorious, cattle-winning chariot, you who are a hero beyond heroes, an assailant, and the winner of power.

Rejoice after this hero; O friends, take hold together after the fierce Indra—him who conquers the village, who wins the cattle, whose arm wields the thunderbolt, who is victorious in the race, and who crushes with his might.
Plunging with force into the herds, the fierce Indra, the giver, possessed of a hundredfold wrath—
unshakable, the subduer of armies, invincible— may he protect our troops in the battles.
O Bṛhaspati, fly around with your chariot, slaying the Rākṣasas and driving away our enemies;
shattering the foes and crushing the adversaries, be the protector of our bodies. 8.
May Indra be their leader; may Bṛhaspati, the sacrificial fee, the sacrifice, and Soma go before them.
May the Maruts march in the midst of the divine armies as they shatter and conquer. //9//

The fierce roar of the gods has arisen—the host of Indra the bull, of King Varuṇa, of the Ādityas, and of the Maruts; the roar of the high-minded ones who cause the worlds to tremble as they conquer. 10.
May Indra be with us when our banners meet; may those arrows which are ours be victorious.
May our heroes be superior; O gods, protect us in our invocations. 11.
I have come to this most excellent dwelling; may Heaven and Earth be auspicious for me.
May the quarters be free from rivals for me; we truly do not hate you; may there be safety for us. 1.
O Indra, from whatever we fear, from that grant us freedom from fear. O Maghavan, help us; with your protections, strike down our enemies and our adversaries. //1//
We invoke Indra, the one who grants success; may we prosper with our two-footed and four-footed creatures.
Let not hostile armies press upon us; O Indra, scatter the treacherous enemies in all directions.
Indra is the protector, the slayer of Vṛtra, the far-expanding, the most excellent;
may he be our guardian from the furthest point, from the middle, from behind, and from the front. 3.
Lead us to a wide world, O Knower; lead us to the light of heaven, to fearlessness, and to well-being.
O Indra, we would dwell under the protection of your two mighty, firm, and great arms.
May the intermediate space grant us fearlessness; may both these, heaven and earth, grant us fearlessness.
May there be fearlessness for us from behind, fearlessness from the front, and fearlessness from above and below. 5.

Fearlessness from friend and fearlessness from foe; fearlessness from kinsman and fearlessness from the one before us; fearlessness by night and fearlessness by day—may all directions become my friends. (6)
Free from rivals in the east, let there be safety for us from behind;
may Savitṛ protect me from the south, and the Lord of Might from the north.
May the Ādityas protect me from heaven; may the fires protect me from the earth.

May Indra and Agni protect me from the front; may the Aśvins grant me shelter on both sides. May the inviolable Jātavedas protect me from the transverse direction; may the creators of beings be my armor on all sides. 2.
May Agni protect me with the Vasus from the east; in that stride, in that refuge, I enter that fortress.
May he guard me, may he protect me; to him I entrust myself. Svāhā! //1//
May Vāyu protect me from this direction along with the intermediate space; in that stride, in that refuge, I enter that fortress. May he protect me, may he guard me; to him I entrust myself. Svāhā!
May Soma protect me from the southern direction along with the Rudras. In that stride, in that refuge, I enter that fortress.
May he guard me; may he protect me. To him I entrust myself. Svāhā!
May Varuṇa, together with the Ādityas, protect me from this direction. In that stride, in that refuge, I go toward that fortress.
May he protect me; may he guard me. To him I entrust myself. Svāhā!
May Sūrya protect me from heaven and earth, from the western quarter. Upon that step, upon that support, I enter that fortress.
May he guard me; may he protect me. To him I entrust myself. Svāhā!

May the waters, rich in medicinal herbs, protect me from this direction. In them I step; in them I take refuge; to that city I go. May they protect me; may they guard me; to them I entrust myself. Svāhā!
May Viśvakarman with the Seven Seers protect me from the northern quarter; in that stride, in that refuge, I enter that city. May he guard me, may he protect me; to him I entrust myself. Svāhā!
May Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, protect me from this direction. In that stride, in that refuge, I enter that fortress.
May he guard me; may he protect me. To him I entrust myself. Svāhā!
May Prajāpati, the possessor of procreative power, protect me together with the firm foundation from the direction of the fixed quarter. In that step, in that refuge, I enter that citadel.
May he protect me; may he guard me. To him I entrust myself. Svāhā!

May Bṛhaspati, together with all the gods, protect me from the upward direction. In that stride, in that refuge, I enter that fortress. May he guard me; may he protect me. To him I entrust myself. Svāhā!
Let those who would harm me from the eastern direction, being malicious, encounter Agni accompanied by the Vasus. 1.
Let the winds, accompanied by the intermediate space, strike those malicious ones who would attack me from this direction. 2.
Let those who would harm me from the southern direction encounter Soma accompanied by Rudra. //3//
Let Varuṇa, accompanied by the Ādityas, seize those malevolent ones who from this direction seek to harm me.
Let the sun reach you, together with heaven and earth—
those malicious ones who would attack me from the western quarter.
Let the waters rich in herbs strike those malevolent ones who would harm me from this direction.
Let them encounter Viśvakarman, who is accompanied by the seven seers—
those malevolent ones from the northern direction who seek to harm me.
May Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, strike down those malicious ones from this direction who seek to harm me.
May they encounter Prajāpati, the prolific one—
those malicious ones who seek to harm me from the fixed quarter.
Let those who are malevolent and seek to harm me from the upward direction encounter Bṛhaspati, who is accompanied by the Viśvedevas.
Mitra has stepped forth from the earth; I lead you toward that stronghold.
Enter it, enter it fully; may it grant you both shelter and protection. //1//
Vāyu ascended by means of the intermediate space; I lead you toward that fortress. Enter it, enter it thoroughly; may it grant you both protection and armor. //2//
The Sun has ascended from heaven; I lead you toward that fortress.
Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you both shelter and protection.
The moon rose up together with the constellations; I lead you toward that city.
Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you both shelter and protection.
Soma has ascended up with the plants; I lead you forward to that fortress.
Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you shelter and protection.
The sacrifice, together with the sacrificial fees, ascended upward; I lead that stronghold forward for you.
Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you both shelter and protection.
The ocean has emerged from the rivers; I lead you toward that stronghold.
Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you both shelter and protection.
The sacred word (*brahman*) ascended with the students of sacred knowledge (*brahmacārin*); I lead you forward to that stronghold.
Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you both protection and armor. 8.
Indra ascended by means of his heroism; I lead you forward into that stronghold.
Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you both shelter and protection. 9.
The gods ascended by means of the immortal; I lead you toward that fortress.
Enter it, enter into it; may it grant you both shelter and protection.
Prajāpati ascended together with his offspring; I lead you forward into that stronghold.
Enter it, enter it thoroughly; may it grant you both shelter and protection. //11//
They have cast away the human weapon which Indra, Agni, Dhātṛ, Savitṛ, Bṛhaspati, King Soma, Varuṇa, the Aśvins, Yama, and Pūṣan [have warded off]. May they protect us from death. //1//

Whatever [protections] Prajāpati, the lord of the world, and Mātariśvan created for the sake of living beings—those which clothe the intermediate directions and the cardinal quarters—may those many protections be mine. 2.
That armor which the gods, the radiant rulers of heaven, the embodied ones, bound upon their bodies—that armor which Indra fashioned, may it protect us from every side. //3//
May Heaven and Earth be my armor; may the Day be my armor, and the Sun my armor.
May all the gods provide me with armor; let no returning missile reach me. 4.
The Gāyatrī, the Uṣṇih, the Anuṣṭubh, the Bṛhatī, the Paṅkti, the Triṣṭubh, and the Jagatī. //1//
To the first five sections of the Āṅgirases, svāhā! 1.
Hail to the sixth! //2//
To the seventh and eighth, svāhā! //3//
Hail to those with blue nails! //4//
Hail to the green ones! //5//
Hail to the minor ones! //6//
To those who are recurrent, svāhā!
Hail to the first conch shells! //8//
To the second conch shells, svāhā!
Hail to the third conch shells! 10.
To those preceding the final ones, svāhā! //11//
To the highest ones, svāhā! //12//
To the northern ones, svāhā! //13//
To the seers, svāhā! //14//
To the crested ones, svāhā! //15//
Hail to the hosts! //16//
To the great assemblies, svāhā! //17//
To all the Aṅgirases, the hosts of the wise, svāhā!
To the two separate thousands, svāhā! //19//
To Brahman, svāhā! //20//
The powers were gathered with the Brahman as the eldest; at the beginning, the Brahman stretched out the highest heaven.
The Brahman was born first among all beings; who then is worthy to rival that Brahman? (21)
Hail to the four-verse hymns of the Atharvans! 1.
Hail to those who possess five ṛc-verses! //2//
Hail to the six-verse hymns! 3.
Hail to the seven-versed hymns! 4.
Hail to those who possess eight verses! //5//
Hail to those consisting of nine verses! 6.
Hail to those who possess ten verses! 7.
Svāhā to those consisting of eleven verses! //8//
Hail to those consisting of twelve verses! 9.
Hail to those consisting of thirteen verses! 10.
Hail to those consisting of fourteen verses! 11.
Hail to those consisting of fifteen verses! 12.
Svāhā to those who possess sixteen verses! 13.
Svāhā to those consisting of seventeen verses! 14.
Hail to those consisting of eighteen verses! 15.
Nineteen, svāhā! //16//
Twenty, svāhā! //17//
Hail to the great stalk! 18.18a
Hail to the triple-verse hymns! 19.19a
Hail to those who consist of single verses! 20.
Hail to the minor ones! //21//
Hail to those who possess but one Ṛc! //22//
Hail to the ruddy ones! 23.23a.
To the two suns, svāhā! //24//
To the two Vrātyas, svāhā! //25//
To the two belonging to Prajāpati, svāhā! //26//
To Viṣāsahya, svāhā! //27//
To those who bring auspiciousness, svāhā! //28//
To Brahman, svāhā! //29//
The heroic powers were gathered with Brahman as the eldest; at the beginning, Brahman stretched out the highest heaven.
Brahman was born first among all beings; who then is worthy to rival that Brahman? (30)
With that by which the gods encompassed the god Savitṛ, with that, O Brahmaṇaspati, do you encompass this man for the sake of the kingdom. //1//
Place this Indra around for long life and for great sovereignty, so that you may lead him to old age and he may remain awake for a long time over his dominion.
Place this Indra around for long life and for great hearing, so that you may lead him to old age and he may remain awake for a long time upon his hearing.
Clothe him, clothe him with splendor; make him one who dies of old age, grant him long life.
Bṛhaspati has bestowed this garment for King Soma to put on.
Go well to old age; put on the garment. Become a protector against curses for the young cows.
Live a hundred abundant autumns, and clothe yourself in the increase of wealth. 5.
You have put on this garment for well-being; you have become the protector of the waters and the warder-off of curses.
Live for a hundred abundant autumns, and as a living man, may you distribute riches beautifully.
In every endeavor, in every contest, we call upon the most powerful Indra as our friend for protection. //7//
Golden-hued, undecaying, and possessing excellent heroes, enter into union with your offspring, whose death is old age.
This Agni has said, and Soma has said this; Bṛhaspati, Savitṛ, and Indra have said this.
I yoke you with unwearied thought, as the first and foremost.
Be a carrier up the slope; having carried up, run back again.
The gold that was born from Agni, which is immortal, has been placed among mortals;
he who knows this is indeed worthy of it. He who wears it becomes one whose death is only old age. //1//

The gold that was fashioned by the sun as a fine ornament, which the ancient men possessed of progeny desired— that [gold], O radiant one, unites thee with splendor; he who wears it becomes long-lived. //2//
For long life, for splendor, for vigor, and for strength;
so that by the brilliance of gold you may shine forth among the people.
That which King Varuṇa knows, that which the god Bṛhaspati knows, and that which Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, knows—may that be long life for you; may that be vigor for you. //4//
May the bull protect you with cattle; may the stallion protect you with vigorous steeds.
May Vāyu protect you with the sacred word (*brahman*); may Indra protect you with his powers.
May Soma protect you with the plants; may the Sun protect you with the constellations. May the Moon, the slayer of Vṛtra, protect you from the months; may Vāta protect you with his breath. //2//
Three heavens, three earths, three midspaces, and four oceans;
they call the threefold Stoma and the threefold waters—may these protect you with the threefold and by means of the threefold.
I fashion for you three heavens, three oceans, three radiances, three firmaments,
three Mātariśvans, and three suns as your guardians.
I sprinkle you with ghee, O Agni, increasing you with clarified butter.
May the deceivers not harm the breath of Agni, of the Moon, and of the Sun. 5.
Let not the deceivers harm your out-breath, nor your in-breath, nor your vigor; O radiant gods, possessors of all wealth, run forth with your divine power!
Through breath he unites with Agni; Vāta is joined with breath.
Through breath the gods generated the sun, which faces every direction. 7.
Live with life, O living one, created by the life-givers; live long-lived, do not die!
Live with the breath of those who possess the self; do not fall under the power of death. 8.

The treasure deposited by the gods, which Indra discovered by means of the paths traveled by the gods—the waters have guarded that gold with their triple-folded powers; may they protect you with their triple-folded, triple-folded protections.
The thirty-three deities and the three heroic powers, acting with affection, have guarded [it] within the waters.
Whatever gold is upon this moon, with that may he perform heroic deeds. //10//
O gods who are eleven in heaven, you gods, may you enjoy this oblation. //11//
O gods who are eleven in the intermediate space, you gods, may you graciously accept this oblation. 12.
O gods who are eleven upon the earth, you gods, may you graciously accept this oblation. 13.
May there be freedom from rivals before us; may fearlessness be established behind us.
May Savitṛ protect me from the south, and Śacīpati from the north.
May the Ādityas protect me from heaven; may the fires protect me from the earth.
May Indra and Agni protect me from the front; may the Aśvins grant me shelter on both sides.
May the inviolable Jātavedas protect me from the transverse direction; may the creators of beings be my armor on all sides. 15.
I bind this amulet for you, for long life and for splendor—
this *darbha* grass, the subduer of rivals, the burner of the heart of the enemy.
Scorching the hearts of those who hate you, scorching the minds of your enemies—
you, O Darbha grass, burn all the evil-hearted like a heated cauldron.
Like a cauldron heating intensely, O Darbha, burning down those who hate us, O amulet, shatter the hearts of our rivals; like Indra, break their strength asunder.
O Darbha, O amulet, split open the hearts of our rivals and those who hate us;
as the rising sun [strips] the skin from the earth, so cause their heads to fall apart.
Split my rivals, O Darbha; split those who array themselves against me.
Split all the evil-hearted ones for me; split my enemies, O amulet! 5.
Cut through my rivals, O Darbha; cut through those who attack me in battle.
Cut through all those of evil heart; cut through my enemies, O amulet!
Cut down my rivals, O Darbha; cut down those who attack me. Cut down all the evil-hearted ones, O amulet; cut down those who hate me.
Cut down my rivals, O Darbha; cut down those who array themselves against me.
Cut down all those of evil heart; cut down my enemies, O amulet! 8.
O Darbha, crush my rivals; crush those who attack me in battle.
Crush all those of evil heart toward me; crush my enemies, O amulet!
Pierce my rivals, O Darbha; pierce those who array themselves against me.
Pierce all who are ill-disposed toward me; pierce those who hate me, O amulet!
O Darbha, pierce my rivals; pierce those who attack me.
O Amulet, pierce all those of evil heart; pierce those who hate me.
Pierce my rivals, O Darbha; pierce those who array themselves against me.
Pierce all those of evil heart toward me; pierce those who hate me, O amulet! 2.
(19.29.3) O Darbha, hold back my rivals; hold back those who attack me in battle. Hold back all those of evil heart; hold back my enemies, O Amulet! (3)
Crush my rivals, O Darbha; crush those who attack me.
Crush all the evil-hearted ones, O amulet; crush those who hate me.
Churn up my rivals, O Darbha; churn up those who attack me in battle!
Churn up all the evil-hearted ones, O Amulet; churn up those who hate me! 5.
O Darbha, crush my rivals; crush those who attack me. Crush all the ill-intentioned ones; crush those who hate me, O amulet!
Burn up my rivals, O Darbha; burn up those who attack me. Burn up all who are ill-intentioned toward me; burn up my enemies, O amulet!
Burn my rivals, O Darbha; burn those who attack me. Burn all who are ill-disposed toward me; burn my enemies, O amulet! 8.
Slay my rivals, O Darbha; slay those who array themselves against me as an army.
Slay all those of evil heart toward me; slay those who hate me, O amulet!
O Darbha, that armor of yours which is a hundredfold against old age and death—having made this man armored with it, slay his rivals by your heroic powers. //1//
A hundred are your *darbha* defenses, a thousand are your heroic powers;
all the gods have given you over to him to sustain for his old age.
They call you the divine armor; O Darbha, they call you the Lord of Prayer (Brahmaṇaspati).
They call you the armor of Indra; you protect the kingdoms. //3//
O Darbha, I fashion for you this amulet, which destroys rivals, burns the heart of the enemy, increases dominion, and protects the body. 4.
When the ocean roared together with Parjanya and the lightning, from that a golden drop arose; from that, Darbha was born. //5//
With an amulet made of udumbara wood, by the Ordainer who desires prosperity, may Savitṛ bring increase of all cattle for me in my cow-pen. 1.
May this Agni, our domestic fire, who is the lord of cattle—may this male amulet of Udumbara wood unite me with prosperity. 2.
May Dhātṛ bestow upon me prosperity through the splendor of the Udumbara tree—[prosperity] that is manure-rich, fruit-bearing, self-sustaining, and refreshing in our home. 3.
Whatever there is of two-footed and four-footed creatures, whatever foods and whatever juices—
of these I take the abundance, wearing the amulet made of udumbara wood.
I have grasped the prosperity of cattle—of those that are four-footed and two-footed, and whatever grain there is.
May Bṛhaspati and Savitṛ bestow upon me the milk of cattle and the essence of plants. 5.
May I be the lord of cattle; may the Lord of Prosperity bestow nourishment upon me.
May the amulet of Udumbara wood grant wealth to me.
May the amulet made of udumbara wood come to me with progeny and wealth;
may the amulet, impelled by Indra, come to me together with splendor.
The divine amulet is the slayer of rivals, the winner of wealth;
may it bestow abundance of cattle and food, and grant an increase of kine.
Just as you, O Lord of the Forest, were born at the beginning together with nourishment, so may Sarasvatī bestow upon me an abundance of wealth. 9.
May Sarasvatī bring me wealth, abundance of milk, and grain;
may Sinīvālī bring them hither, as does this amulet of udumbara wood.
You are the bull, the sovereign lord of jewels; in you the Lord of Prosperity has produced abundance.
In you are these strengths and all riches, O you who are made of udumbara wood. As such, drive away from us—far, far away—hostility, lack of intelligence, and hunger.

You are a village-leader; having arisen as a village-leader, you who have been consecrated, sprinkle me with splendor! You are brilliance; bestow brilliance upon me. You are wealth; grant me wealth. //12//
You are nourishment; anoint me with nourishment. As a house-sacrificer, make me a lord of the household.
You, who are made of udumbara wood, bestow that wealth upon us; grant us riches consisting of all heroic sons. For the increase of wealth, I fasten you on. 13.
This amulet of udumbara wood, a hero, is bound upon a hero.
May it provide us with a honey-sweet gain and bestow upon us wealth consisting of all-heroic sons. 14.
The hundred-jointed, unshakable, thousand-leaved, and victorious Darbha grass— this formidable herb I bind upon you for the sake of long life.
They do not shave his hair, nor do they strike him on the chest—
[he] for whom one provides protection with darbha grass whose leaves are uncut.
O herb, your downy fiber is in heaven; you are firmly established upon the earth.
Through you, who possess a thousand stalks, we cause our lifespan to increase.
He has pierced through the three heavens and these three earths.
With you, I crush the tongue and the words of the ill-hearted one.
(5a) You are the overcomer; I am the overcomer. (5c) Having both become possessors of overcoming power, may we overcome our rivals.
Overcome our adversary; overcome those who attack us. Overcome all the evil-hearted ones, and make many for me those who are well-disposed.
With the *darbha* grass, born of the gods, which constantly supports the heavens, with that I have won and shall win people forever. (AVŚ 19.32.7)
O Darbha grass, make me dear to the Brahmin and the Kṣatriya, and to the Śūdra and the Ārya;
and to whomever we desire, and to every one who perceives clearly.
He who, being born, made the earth firm, who propped up the mid-air and the sky—he whom no evil found while he was bearing [the world], may this Darbha grass be that Varuṇa for us by day. 9.
The slayer of rivals, hundred-stemmed and powerful, he has become the first among plants.
May this *darbha* protect us on every side; with it may I overcome the armies of those who attack us. 10.
Worth a thousand, with a hundred joints, full of sap—the fire of the waters, the royal consecration of plants—may this Darbha protect us on every side; may the divine amulet unite us with long life.
Drawn forth from clarified butter, honeyed, full of milk, a firm support of the earth, unshakable yet causing others to shake;
driving away rivals and casting them down, O Darbha grass, grow with the power of the great! 2.
By your might you shall transcend the earth; you sit upon the sacrificial altar, beautiful at the rite.
The seers brought you as a purifier; do you cleanse away our misdeeds. 3.
Sharp is the king, the unconquerable, the slayer of demons, the one who watches over all people;
he is the fierce vigor and strength of the gods. That I bind upon you for old age and for well-being. //4//
With darbha grass you shall perform heroic deeds; bearing darbha within yourself, do not falter.
Standing firm with splendor, surpass all others; shine forth like the sun toward the four quarters.
You are Jaṅgiḍa, you are the protector Jaṅgiḍa;
may Jaṅgiḍa protect all of us—both bipeds and quadrupeds. //1//
May the Gṛtsya, the Tripañcāśī, and those who are the hundred makers of sorcery—may he separate them all from their splendor; may Jaṅgida render them sapless.
The tasteless, artificial roar; the seven tasteless decays—drive away the overweening pride of the jaṅgiḍa plant, as an archer shoots away an arrow.
This very Jaṅgiḍa is the destroyer of sorcery and likewise the destroyer of malice; moreover, being powerful, may it prolong our lifespans. 4.
Such is the greatness of Jaṅgiḍa; may it protect us on every side, by which it overcomes Viṣkandha and Saṃskandha with its own vital power.
The gods thrice generated you, established upon the earth;
the ancient Brahmins know you as Aṅgiras.
Neither the ancient plants nor those that are new surpass you;
the formidable Jaṅgiḍa is a dispeller of affliction, a protection on all sides, and most auspicious.
Then, O Blessed One, Jāṅgiḍa of immeasurable heroism—
before the fierce ones could devour you, Upendra bestowed his heroic power upon you.
O Lord of the Forest, Indra has bestowed his fierce vigor upon you;
O Herb, drive away all diseases and slay the demons.
The Āśarīka, the Viśarīka, the balāsa, and the disease of the back—
let Jaṅgiḍa render the Takman, which lasts through all autumns, sapless.
Uttering the name of Indra, the seers gave the Jaṅgida;
that which the gods made into a medicine in the beginning, the destroyer of Viṣkandha.
May that Jaṅgiḍa protect us, like a guardian of wealth over riches—
he whom the gods and the brahmins made into a protective amulet against the stingy enemy.
The evil-hearted have come against the doer of evil with a most terrible eye;
O thousand-eyed one, destroy them with your watchfulness! You, Jaṅgiḍa, are our complete protection.
From heaven protect me, from the earth protect me, from the intermediate space protect me, and from the plants protect me;
from what has been and from what is to be, from every direction, may Jaṅgiḍa protect us. //4//
Whatever [poisons] are produced by seers, whatever are made by gods, and whatever others have been transformed—may Jaṅgiḍa, the possessor of all remedies, render them all sapless. 5.5.5a-c.
Śatavāra has destroyed the wasting diseases and the demons by his splendor; ascending with luster, the amulet drives away those of evil name.
With its two horns it pushes away the *rakṣas*, with its root the sorceresses; with its middle it drives away consumption; no evil shall overcome it. //2//
Whatever wasting diseases there are— those small, those great, and those that are noisy—
all those with evil names has the amulet Śatavāra destroyed.
She has given birth to a hundred heroes; she has cast away a hundred consumptions. Having slain all those of evil name, she shakes off the *rakṣases*.
The bull with golden horns, the victorious one—this amulet, having trampled all those of evil name, has stepped over the *rakṣas* demons. 5.
A hundred of the ill-named ones, a hundred of the Gandharvas and Apsarases, a hundred of those who follow the hare— these I ward off with the hundred-fold filter.
This splendor given by Agni has come to me—glory, fame, power, vigor, and strength;
may Agni bestow upon me those thirty-three heroic powers.
Bestow splendor upon my body, along with vigor, vitality, and strength.
I receive you for the sake of sensory power, for ritual action, and for heroic might, for a hundred autumns.
For nourishment, for strength, for vigor, for power, for supremacy, and for the sustenance of the kingdom— for a hundred autumns— I carry you around.
For you, from the seasons, from the seasonal periods, from the months, and from the years;
for Dhātṛ, Vidhātṛ, Samṛdh, and the Lord of Being, I sacrifice. //4//
Consumptions do not hold him back, nor does a curse reach him,
whom the fragrant scent of the healing *gulgulu* pervades.
Therefore, the consumptive diseases flee in all directions like deer or horses,
whether you be *gulgulu* from the Indus region or that which comes from the ocean.
I have grasped the names of both for his safety. //3//
May the divine *kuṣṭha*, the protector, come from the Himalayas;
destroy every *takman* and all sorceresses.

Three are your names, *kuṣṭha*: you are the one who overcomes the river, the foe of the river. May this man not suffer harm from the river, for whom I invoke you in the evening, in the morning, and by day.
Jīvalā is the name of your mother; Jīvanta is the name of your father.
May this man not come to harm for the sake of the river, to whom I address you in the evening, in the morning, and by day.

You are the highest of plants, as the ox is among moving creatures, as the tiger is among beasts of prey. May this man not come to harm, for whom I invoke you evening and morning, and likewise by day.
Three times from the Śambus and the Aṅgirases, three times from the Ādityas,
and three times born from the Viśvedevas—
this Kuṣṭha, the universal healer, stands together with Soma.

The aśvattha tree is the abode of the gods in the third heaven from here; there is the manifestation of immortality, and from that the kuṣṭha was born. That kuṣṭha, the universal healer, stands together with Soma.
A golden ship with golden moorings moved through the sky;
there was the manifestation of immortality, and from that Kuṣṭha was born.
That Kuṣṭha, the universal healer, stands together with Soma.
Where there is no falling away, where the head of the Himavat is, there is the manifestation of immortality; from that the Kuṣṭha was born.
That Kuṣṭha, the universal remedy, stands together with Soma.
O Kuṣṭha, that which the ancient Ikṣvāku knew of you, or that which the beloved one knew of you, O Vasu—that which you have consumed, by that you are the possessor of all medicines. //9//
The headache, the tertian fever, the constant one, and that which returns every year—drive Takman away downward with your all-powerful strength. 10.
Whatever flaw there is in my mind and whatever in my speech, and whatever has gone to the wrathful Sarasvatī—may Bṛhaspati, in agreement with all the gods, restore that whole together. //1//
O Waters, do not destroy our wisdom nor our sacred formulation (*brahman*).
Flow forth with easy passage; I have been invoked, wise and full of splendor.
Do not harm our wisdom, nor our consecration, nor our ascetic heat.
May they be auspicious for us, bringing peace for our life; may the Mothers be gracious to us. 3.
May that luminous power which has carried us across the darkness, O Aśvins, grant us that nourishment. //4//
Desiring what is auspicious, the seers who have found the light of heaven sat down in the beginning for austerity and consecration.
From that, sovereignty, strength, and vital power were born; may the gods bow down before this for him. 1.
The Brahman is the Hotṛ; the sacrifice is the Brahman; by the Brahman the sacrificial posts are measured.
The Adhvaryu is born from the Brahman; from the Brahman comes the hidden oblation.
The ladles are sacred prayer, filled with ghee; by sacred prayer the altar is raised up.
Sacred prayer is the essence of the sacrifice, as are the officiating priests who prepare the oblation.
To the immolator, Svāhā! 2.
To him who releases from distress, I offer this inspired hymn; seeking his favor, I choose the benevolence of the good protector.
O Indra, accept this oblation; may the desires of the sacrificer come true. 3.

I invoke the Son of the Waters, the deliverer from distress, the bull among those worthy of sacrifice, the first to shine forth at the rites. O Aśvins, with my inspired thought, I call upon your power; grant us sensory vigor and strength. //4//
Where those who know Brahman go by means of initiation together with austerity—may Agni lead me there; may Agni bestow wisdom upon me. Svāhā to Agni! 1.
Where those who know the Brahman go, together with consecration and austerity—may Vāyu lead me there; may Vāyu bestow vital breaths upon me. Svāhā to Vāyu! //2//
Where those who know Brahman go by means of initiation and austerity—may Sūrya lead me there; may Sūrya bestow sight upon me. Svāhā to Sūrya! //3//
Where those who know Brahman go by means of consecration and austerity—may Candra lead me there; may Candra bestow his mind upon me. Svāhā to Candra! //4//
Where those who know Brahman go, by means of initiation and austerity—may Soma lead me there; may Soma bestow milk upon me.
Svāhā to Soma! //5//
Where those who know Brahman go by means of initiation and austerity—may Indra lead me there; may Indra bestow strength upon me. Svāhā to Indra!
Where those who know Brahman go, together with consecration and austerity—may the Waters lead me there; may immortality attend me! Svāhā to the waters! 7.
Where those who know Brahman go by means of initiation and austerity—may Brahmā lead me there; may Brahmā bestow Brahman upon me. Svāhā to Brahman!
You are the prolonger of life; you are called the wise remedy.
Therefore, O ointment, grant us well-being; may the waters bring peace and fearlessness. 1.
The jaundice, the wasting disease, the breaking of the limbs, and the piercing pain— may this ointment drive all that consumption out from your limbs.
The collyrium born upon the earth, auspicious and sustaining life for men— may it make [the person] free from premature death, swift as a chariot, and sinless.
O Prāṇa, protect my life-breath; be gracious to my vital force.
O Nirṛti, release us from the snares of destruction. //4//
You are the embryo of the ocean, the flower of the lightnings;
you are the breath of the wind, the eye of the sun, the milk of heaven.
O divine collyrium from the Trikakud mountain, protect me from every side!
Neither the plants of the plains nor those of the mountains surpass you.
This slayer of demons and dispeller of disease has descended into the midst; driving away all maladies, he has destroyed and banished all afflictions from here.
O King Varuṇa, man has spoken much falsehood here;
therefore, O you of thousandfold power, release us from this distress.
Whatever we have said, "O waters, O inviolable ones," or "O Varuṇa," from that,
O thousandfold-powerful one, release us from distress.
May Mitra and Varuṇa both follow after you, O collyrium!
Having followed you for a long distance, may they bring you back again for enjoyment.
Like debt from a debtor, bring back the spell (*kṛtyā*) to the house of the spell-maker;
crush even the ribs of the evil-hearted one who wields the eye-spell.
Whatever evil dream is among us, whatever is among our cattle, and whatever is in our house—
let that which is nameless and ill-intentioned be cast back upon him who is dear [to us].
Increasing through the strength and vigor of the waters, born from Agni Jātavedas—
may that mountain-born collyrium, which provides four heroes, make the quarters and intermediate directions auspicious for you.
This collyrium is bound for you, O fourfold hero; may all the quarters be free from fear for you.
Stand firm like Savitṛ, O noble one; let these subjects bring tribute to you. //4//
Wear one jewel, make one for yourself; bathe with one, drink from one of these.
May she protect us from the fourfold bonds of Grāhī, from the four Nirṛtis that bind heroes.
May Agni protect me with Agni for out-breath, for in-breath, for life, for luster,
for vigor, for splendor, for well-being, and for prosperity— svāhā!
May Indra protect me with his virile power for out-breath and in-breath, for life, for luster,
for strength, for splendor, for well-being, and for prosperity— svāhā!
May Soma protect me with his Soma-nature for out-breath, for in-breath, for life, for splendor, for vigor, for brilliance, for well-being, and for prosperity— svāhā!
May Bhaga protect me with fortune for the sake of out-breath, in-breath, long life, luster, vigor, splendor, well-being, and prosperity; svāhā!
May the Maruts protect me with their hosts for the sake of out-breath, in-breath, and life-span, for luster, vigor, and splendor.
Svāhā! For well-being and prosperity! 10.
Prajāpati bound you first, the invincible, for the sake of heroic power. That I bind upon you for long life, for luster, for vigor, and for strength; may the invincible protect you. //1//
Let him stand upright, guarding with vigilance; let not the Paṇis or the Yātudhānas deceive him.
Like Indra, shake off the Dasyus who attack; overcome all enemies; let the one who is spread out protect you.
Though they struck and smote him by the hundreds, they could not prevail.
Upon him Indra bestowed sight, breath, and strength. May he, the unsubdued, protect you from all sides.
We clothe you with the armor of Indra, who became the sovereign ruler over the gods.
May all the gods lead you forth again; may the invincible one protect you. //4//
In this amulet there are a hundred and one powers; in this invincible [amulet] there are a thousand vital breaths.
As a tiger, trample all enemies. Let him who assails you fall low; may the invincible protect you. //5//
Drawn from clarified butter, honeyed, full of milk, possessing a thousand breaths and a hundred origins,
bestowing vital strength— may he who is auspicious, who brings delight, who is full of vigor and full of milk, and who is invincible, protect you.
Just as you are superior, without rivals, a slayer of rivals, and may you be the controller of your kinsmen—so may Savitṛ make you; may the invincible one protect you.
O Night, the earthly realm has been filled by you through the domains of your father;
great one, you spread across the seats of heaven, and the brilliant darkness rolls forth.
Whose further shore is not seen, and into whom everything that moves enters and unites—O vast, dark Night, may we reach your end unharmed; O auspicious one, may we reach your end.
Those watchers of yours, O Night, who have the eyes of men—ninety-nine of them;
there are eighty-eight, and indeed seven times seven.
Sixty and six, O wealthy one; fifty and five, O gracious one; forty and four, and thirty and three, O vigorous one. //4//
Two and twenty nights, with eleven as the shortest;
with those protections, O Daughter of Heaven, protect us now this day.
(6a) Let no malevolent one have power over us; let no ill-wisher have power over us. (6c) Let not the thief of our cattle, nor the wolf of our sheep, have power over us today.
O auspicious lady, let no thief seize our horses, nor let sorceresses seize our men.
Let the thief and the robber run away by the most distant paths. Beyond lies the biting rope; beyond let the malevolent one flee.
Now, O Night, make the serpent headless and of pungent smoke;
crush the jaws of the wolf; strike the thief upon the wooden post.
In you, O Night, we dwell; we shall sleep; do you remain awake. Grant protection to our cattle, our horses, and our men.
And furthermore, whatever [is] from you and whatever is within your circumference—that we entrust to you. 1.
O Night, our Mother, entrust us to the Dawn;
may the Dawn entrust us to the Day, and the Day to you, O Radiant One.
Whatever flies here, whatever creeps here, and whatever moves upon the mountains—from all that, O Night, protect us. 3.
Do thou protect us from behind, from the front, from above, and from below;
guard us, O radiant one! We here are thy praisers.
Those who attend to the night, and those who are watchful among living beings;
those who protect all cattle—they are watchful for our selves, they are watchful for our cattle. //5//
O Night, I truly know your name; you are indeed named Ghṛtācī.
Bharadvāja knows you as such; may you, being thus known, watch over our wealth.

The vigorous maiden, the youthful mistress of the house, Night, the wife of the god Savitar and of Bhaga—she who is swift as a horse, easily invoked, and possessed of gathered splendor—has filled heaven and earth with her greatness. //1//
The deep one has risen above all; the most excellent ones have ascended to the highest.
The longing Night follows after that auspicious one, as if with Mitra, through her own inherent powers.
O Varī, O blessed and well-born one, I salute you; O Night, having come here, may we be well-disposed.
Protect us, O you who are born for men, and also those things belonging to cattle through your nourishment.
I take the luster of the lion, of the longing night, of the tiger, and of the leopard.
Of the horse you take the ruddy glow, of the man the cry; shining forth, you assume many forms. 4.
May the auspicious Night, the mother of the snow, be well-disposed toward us along with the Sun;
O fortunate one, take heed of this hymn of praise with which I laud you in all directions. //5//
O radiant Night, you take pleasure in our hymn like a queen. May we be masters of all heroes; may we possess all wealth, following after the dawns as they shine forth.
You have indeed established the name "Peace" for me; those who wish to harm my wealth—by means of nights, O drinker of breath, may they not exist as thieves, nor may they be found again. //7//
(8) You are auspicious, O Night; like a cup set down, you bear a youthful, all-encompassing form of a cow.
Possessing eyes, longing for my beauty, you have looked upon me as a celestial one gazes upon the earth. //8//
Whatever thief comes today, the mortal enemy who seeks to do harm— may Night, having encountered him, strike off his necks and his head.
As one would step forward with his feet, as one would stretch forth his hands to receive;
he who approaches as a plunderer departs crushed.
He departs, he departs badly; he departs upon a withered stump.
Now, O Night, make the serpent smoke-mouthed and headless;
strike out both eyes of the wolf; with that, slay him upon the wooden post.
O Night, those oxen of yours that have sharp horns and swift paces—with them may you carry us safely across all difficulties today. 2.
Night after night, may we cross over unharmed in our own bodies;
may our enemies not cross over, like those without a boat in the deep.
Just as a grain of millet, falling away from the wind, is not found again,
even so, O Night, cause him who seeks to harm us to fall away.
Drive away the thief who hides among our cattle and goats, as well as the robber;
and also him who, having seized the head of a horse, seeks to carry it off.
O fortunate one, when you today at night distribute wealth among the living,
may you cause us to enjoy this very thing as you approach others.
O Night, deliver us all to Dawn as those who are sinless.
May Dawn bestow our day upon us, and may the day, O radiant one, belong to you.
I am unbounded; my self is unbounded; unbounded is my eye, unbounded is my ear.
Unbounded is my out-breath, unbounded is my in-breath, unbounded is my diffused breath; unbounded am I in every way. //1//
At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, being impelled, I take hold of you.
In the beginning, desire arose, which was the first seed of the mind.
O Desire, being of one womb with the Great One through desire, bestow upon the sacrificer an increase of wealth. //1//
O Kāma, you are established by force; you are the pervasive, radiant friend to the one who seeks friendship.
You are the fierce conqueror in battles; bestow power and vigor upon the sacrificer.
For him who desired from afar a matchless counter-stake, the quarters of space listened; through desire, they generated the sun.
(19.52.4a) Let desire not come to me through desire, from heart to heart. (19.52.4c) Whatever mind they have there, let that come here to me. 4.
O Kāma, whatever desire we have while making this oblation for you, may all that be fulfilled for us; then, partake of this oblation, Svāhā! //5//
Time, a horse with seven reins, thousand-eyed, undecaying, and rich in seed, carries [all things].
Upon him mount the seers, the wise; his wheels are all the worlds. 1.
This Time carries seven wheels; its nave is sevenfold, and its axle is indeed immortality. Anointing all these worlds, Time moves on as the first god.
The full jar was placed upon Time; indeed, we see it existing in many forms. It faces toward all these worlds; they call that Time in the highest heaven.
He alone brought together all the worlds; he alone went around all the worlds.
Being their father, he became their son; therefore, indeed, there is no other brilliance higher than him.
Time generated this heaven; Time [generated] these earths as well.
In Time, indeed, both what has been and what is to be abide, impelled by him. //5//
Time created prosperity; in Time the sun shines;
in Time indeed all beings exist; in Time the eye sees clearly.
In the proper time the mind [is established], in the proper time the vital breath, and in the proper time the name is composed.
At the proper time, all these creatures rejoice when it has arrived. (AVŚ 19.53.7)
In the proper time is austerity, in the proper time the highest [state], and in the proper time the *brahman* is concentrated;
for Time is indeed the lord of all, who was the father of Prajāpati.
Impelled by him, born from him,
and established in him, Time, having become the Brahman, sustains Parameṣṭhin.
Time created progeny; in the beginning, Time created Prajāpati.
Kaśyapa was self-existent from Time; austerity was born from Time. //10//
From Time the waters came into being; from Time, sacred knowledge, austerity, and the quarters of space.
By Time the sun rises, and by Time it sets again.
In due season the wind blows; in due season the great earth [remains]; the vast heaven is established in due season.
Time indeed brought forth the past and the future as his son in the beginning;
from Time the *ṛc*s came into being, and from Time the *yajus* was born. (AVŚ 19.54.3)
Time has impelled the sacrifice for the gods, an imperishable portion.
In Time the Gandharvas and Apsarases [dwell], and in Time the worlds are established. //4//

In due time, this god Kāla, along with Aṅgiras and Atharvan, presides over this world and the highest world, the meritorious worlds, and the holy ordinances. Having conquered all worlds through the Brahman, that supreme god Kāla moves on. //5//
Night after night bringing what has not been offered, we provide for him fodder as if for a standing horse;
rejoicing in the increase of wealth and in nourishment, may we, O Agni, your neighbors, not come to harm. 1.
O Vāta, that arrow of yours which belongs to Vasu—that is this very one; with it, be gracious to us.
Rejoicing in the increase of wealth and in nourishment, may we, O Agni, as your neighbors, suffer no harm.
Every evening our householder Agni, every morning the giver of goodwill; O giver of wealth, be the bestower of wealth upon us! Kindling you, may we nourish our own bodies. 3.
Every morning may Agni, our householder, and every evening may he be the giver of goodwill. O giver of wealth, prosper us with every kind of wealth; kindling you, may we thrive for a hundred winters.
May I never be one who eats food from behind. Homage to Rudra, the eater of food, the lord of food, and to Agni.
O member of the assembly, protect my assembly, as well as those members who sit in the assembly.
O Indra, much-invoked, throughout their entire lives they have attained you;
day after day bringing tribute to you, O Agni, as fodder to a standing horse.
From the world of Yama you have come hither; O wise one, you join mortal women with passion.
Knowing all, you travel in a single chariot alone, measuring out the dream within the womb of the Asura.
Bandha saw you first, in your all-encompassing form, before the birth of night, on a certain day; then you came into this world through sleep, hiding your true form from the physicians.
Seeking greatness, Bṛhadgāva turned toward the gods from among the Asuras;
to him, that dream, the thirty-three [gods], having attained the light of heaven, granted sovereignty.
Neither the fathers nor the gods know this [speech] which wanders as chatter within these people;
the men, instructed by Varuṇa, the Ādityas, placed sleep in Trita Āptya.
Upon whom the evildoers have laid their cruelty, while the doers of good have gained merit and long life through sleeplessness;
you revel in heaven with your supreme kinsman, for you were born from the mind as it was being heated. 5.
We know all your origins from of old; we know you, O Sleep, as the sovereign lord here. Protect us here for the sake of glory; go far away, out of reach of our enemies.
Just as they pay back a sixteenth part, just as an eighth part, just as a debt, so do we transfer all evil dreams onto the one who is unfriendly. 1.
Together have the kings come; together have the debts come; together have the kuṣṭhas come; together have the kalās come.
Whatever evil dream is among us, we drive that evil dream away from our enemy.
O embryo of the wives of the gods, born of Yama, auspicious dream: let that which is mine be good; let us send what is evil to my enemy.
You are not the mouth of the harsh ones, nor of the black bird.

O Sleep, we know you as such; like a horse that has swallowed its own body, like a horse that has swallowed its bridle, sweep away from us the one who hates the gods and the hater, whatever evil dream is among us, whatever is among our cattle, and whatever is in our house.
Let that hater of the gods, the one who seeks to harm us, cast off his malice like a necklace.
Let him cast away our ninefold treasures from there.
We drive all evil dreams away upon our enemy. //5//

The impulse of ghee, seated together with the gods, increasing the year by means of the oblation—may our hearing, sight, and breath remain unimpaired; may we ourselves remain unimpaired in life and luster. //1//
May breath summon us; we summon breath.
The earth has taken up splendor, as has the mid-air; may Soma and Bṛhaspati bestow splendor upon us.
Heaven and Earth have become the gatherers of splendor; taking hold of splendor, may we move along the earth.
As cows approach their master with glory, taking hold of glory, may we move along the earth. 3.
Make a pen for yourselves, for he is your leader; sew many wide shields.
Make iron forts, unassailable; let not your cup leak—make it firm.
The eye and the beginning of the sacrifice, and its mouth—through speech, hearing, and mind, I offer this.
May the gods, being well-disposed, come to this sacrifice spread out by Viśvakarman. //5//

Those who are the officiating priests of the gods and those who are worthy of sacrifice, to whom the oblation is made as their allotted portion— let all the powerful gods, having come to this sacrifice together with their wives, rejoice.
O Agni, you are the guardian of vows, a god among mortals;
you are to be praised at the sacrifices. //1//
O gods, whatever vows of yours we, being more ignorant than the wise, have violated—that may Agni, the knowing one who has entered into the Brāhmaṇas, fulfill for us through Soma. //2//
We have come to the path of the gods, that we may carry out what we are able to do.
May Agni, the wise one, sacrifice; he indeed is the Hotṛ, he shall perform the rites, and he shall arrange the seasons.
May speech be in my mouth, breath in my nostrils, sight in my eyes, and hearing in my ears;
may my hair be free from grayness, my teeth free from blemish, and may there be great strength in my arms.
May there be vigor in my thighs, speed in my shanks, and stability in my feet; may all my limbs be uninjured and firm.
May my body be joined with my body; may I, through the teeth, attain the full span of life.
Sit comfortably for me; fill me abundantly, O Pavamāna, in the heavenly world. //1//
Make me dear among the gods; make me dear among the kings;
make me dear to everyone who beholds me, whether he be a Śūdra or an Ārya.
Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati; awaken the gods with the sacrifice.
Increase the lifespan, the vital breath, offspring, cattle, fame, and the sacrificer. //1//
O Agni, I have brought fuel for the great Jātavedas;
may that Jātavedas bestow upon me faith and wisdom. 1.
O Jātavedas, we cause you to grow with fuel and with kindling;
likewise, do you cause us to grow with progeny and with wealth. 2.
Whatever logs of wood we place upon you, O Agni—may all that be auspicious for me; accept it, O youngest one. //3//
(19.64.4a) These are your fuel-sticks, O Agni; being kindled, become the fuel itself.
(19.64.4c) Bestow long life upon us, and immortality upon our teacher. //4//

The golden-winged bird has ascended to heaven with his radiance. O Jātavedas, strike down with your heat those who seek to harm you as you fly up to heaven. Unafraid and fierce, ascend to heaven with your radiance, O Sūrya.

The illusory Asuras with iron nets, who wander about marked with iron fetters—those I subject to you by your heat, O Jātavedas; as a thousand-pointed thunderbolt, crush the rivals and protect us. //1//
May we see a hundred autumns. (1)
May we live for a hundred autumns. //2//
May we awaken for a hundred autumns. //3//
May we flourish for a hundred autumns.
May we, O Pūṣan, live for a hundred autumns. //5//
May we live for a hundred autumns.
May we adorn ourselves for a hundred autumns.
May there be many more autumns, even a hundred.
I open the aperture of both the narrow and the wide by means of creative power (*māyā*).
Having extracted the Veda from those two, we then perform our ritual acts. 1.
(1) You are living beings; may I live; may I live out my full span of life.
You are those upon whom we depend; may I live depending on you; may I live out the full span of life.
(You are) the Reviving Ones; may I revive; may I live out the full span of life. //3//
You are life-giving; may I live, may I live out the full span of life. //4//
O Indra, live; O Sūrya, live; O gods, live! May I live;
may I live out the full span of life. //1//
Praised by me, may the Giver of Boons, the Mother of the Vedas, and the Pāvamānī verses impel the twice-born.
Having bestowed upon me long life, vital breath, progeny, cattle, fame, wealth, and spiritual luster, depart for the world of Brahman. //1//
From whatever treasury we have drawn forth this Veda, within that very place we deposit it again.
This has been accomplished through the power of the Brahman; with that, O gods, protect me here by means of your fervor.
O Indra, bull, we invoke you when the Soma is pressed;
as such, drink of the sweet juice. //1//
O Maruts, of great majesty from heaven, that person in whose dwelling you drink—verily, he is the one best protected by guardians. //2//
To Agni, the ordainer, whose food is the bull and the cow, whose back is the Soma—we shall pay worship with hymns of praise. //3//
(20.2.1a) Let the Maruts, well-praising with beautiful chants, drink the Soma from the Potar’s cup according to the season. //1//
May Agni, from the Āgnīdhra fire, drink the Soma with the Ṛtu-formula, accompanied by the Suṣṭubh and Svarka chants. //2//
May Indra, the Brahman, drink the Soma with the Ṛtu-rite from the well-praising, well-singing Brāhmaṇa. //3//
May the god Draviṇodas drink the Soma with the Ṛtu from the Potṛ’s cup, accompanied by the well-praised and well-sung hymn. 4.
Come hither, for we have pressed it for you; O Indra, drink this Soma! Sit upon this sacred grass of mine. 1.
O Indra, may your two long-maned bay horses, yoked by prayer, bring you hither;
hear our sacred invocations.
O Indra, drinker of Soma, we who possess the Soma and have pressed it, we Brahmans, call upon you as our ally. //3//
Come to us who have pressed the juice, come to our fair hymns of praise;
O fair-cheeked one, drink of the soma-plant.
I pour [it] into your two flanks; let it flow through your limbs. Seize the honey with your tongue.
May it be sweet for your enjoyment, honeyed for your body;
may Soma be auspicious for your heart. //3//
O thou who art beheld by all, like a woman surrounded by her kinswomen, let this Soma flow forth toward thee, O Indra. //1//
Thick-necked, pot-bellied, strong-armed, seated upon the soma, Indra smites down the Vritras. //2//
O Indra, go forth at the head; you are the lord of all by your might.
O slayer of Vṛtra, strike down the obstacles.
Long be your hook, with which you bestow wealth upon the sacrificer who presses the soma. //4//
This Soma of yours, O Indra, has been purified upon the sacred grass; come hither, hasten to it, and drink! 5.5a, 5c.
O Śācigu, for you who are honored for your power, this [Soma] is pressed for your delight;
O Ākhaṇḍala, you are invoked.
O grandson, great-grandson of the bull-horned one, you who are worthy of the *kuṇḍapāyya* draught—
let him fix his mind upon this [sacrifice].
O Indra, we invoke you, the bull, when the Soma is pressed;
as such, drink of the sweet juice.
O Indra, praised by many, take pleasure in this pressed Soma that finds the power of the mind;
drink and pour it down until you are fully satisfied.
O Indra, together with all the gods, further our sacrifice that is accompanied by devotion;
being praised, O Lord of the People. 3.
O Indra, lord of the virtuous, these pressed Soma juices go forth to you; the bright drops seek your dwelling.
Place within your belly the pressed Soma, O Indra, the most excellent;
yours are the celestial drops. //5//
O lover of songs, drink our pressed juice; you are anointed with streams of honey.
O Indra, glory is indeed won through you alone.
The imperishable splendors of the trees attend upon Indra;
having drunk of the Soma, he has grown strong. //7//
Come to us from nearby and from afar, O slayer of Vṛtra;
graciously accept these songs of ours.
When you are invoked between the far distance and the near,
O Indra, come here from there.
Up indeed you rise, O Sūrya, toward the bull of renowned bounty, the performer of manly deeds, the archer. 1.
He who by the strength of his arms shattered ninety-nine fortresses, he,
the slayer of Vṛtra, slew the serpent.
May that Indra, our auspicious friend, [bestow wealth] consisting of horses, cattle, and barley; he milks it forth like a wide-streaming cow. //3//
