O Indra, praised by many, take pleasure in this pressed Soma that finds the power of the mind;
drink and pour it down until you are fully satisfied.
Thus protect us as in the ancient days; let [the Soma] exhilarate you. Hear our prayer and grow strong through our songs.
Make the sun manifest, cause the nourishments to swell; slay the enemies, O Indra, and burst open the cattle-pens.
Come hither; they say you desire Soma—here it is pressed, drink of it for exhilaration.
O wide-extending one, pour it into your belly; hearing us as we call, listen to us like a father.
His jar is full; *svāhā*! Like a pourer, he has filled the vessel for drinking.
The dear Soma drops have turned together toward Indra from the right, for his exhilaration.
We celebrate that wondrous Indra with our songs—he who overcomes the attackers, who rejoices in the exhilarating soma-juice—just as cows low toward their calf in the stalls. //1//
We quickly implore the celestial one, the bountiful giver, who is encompassed by powers and is like a mountain rich in many enjoyments;
we seek foodful booty, hundredfold and thousandfold, swiftly accompanied by cattle.

I beg of you that heroic power, that sacred prayer (*brahman*) for the sake of first thought—that by which you helped the *yatis* and Bhr̥gu when the prize was staked, and by which you protected Praskaṇva. //3//
That by which you released the great waters unto the ocean—that, O Indra, is your manly might.
That greatness of his is not to be attained at once, he whom the worlds have cried out after.
Upward rise your most honey-sweet songs and hymns of praise—victorious, winners of wealth, with inexhaustible aid, like chariots seeking booty. //1//
Like the Kaṇvas, like the Bhṛgus, like the suns, they have attained every desire;
magnifying Indra with hymns, the Āyus and Priyamedhas have raised their voices. //2//
Indra, the breaker of forts, has overcome the Dāsa with his hymns; the finder of wealth, bestowing gifts, he has scattered his enemies.
Urged by prayer and increasing in body, the giver of much has filled both heaven and earth.
I send forth my speech to stimulate you, the bountiful and powerful one, adorning it for the sake of the immortal.
O Indra, you are the first to go among the human settlements and the divine tribes as well. 2.
Indra, whose purpose is to provide protection, encompassed Vṛtra; he, whose purpose is to assume various forms, outwitted the wiles of the guileful.
He struck down Vyansa, burning fiercely among the woods, and made manifest the lowing of the cows during the nights.
Indra, the winner of light, generating the days, has conquered the hostile armies with his helpers, being the one who overcomes.
He made the banner of the days shine for Manu; he found the light for the great battle.
Indra has entered into the impetus with his might, bestowing many manly deeds like a hero; for he has inspired these prayers for the singer, and he has heightened this bright color of theirs. //5//
They praise his great and many well-performed deeds;
with his host he crushed the crooked ones, and by his wondrous powers, he of surpassing might, overcame the Dasyus.
Through his greatness, Indra, the lord of the people and protector of the good, created wide space for the gods by means of battle.
At the seat of Vivasvat, the inspired poets and sages praise those deeds of his with hymns.
The ever-conquering one, the most excellent, the giver of strength, who has won the light of heaven and the goddesses;
he who has won both this earth and yonder sky—after Indra, the wise ones rejoice.
Indra has won the steeds and he has won the sun; Indra has won the cow that provides much nourishment.
He has won golden wealth and possessions; having slain the Dasyus, he protected the Aryan race.
Indra won the plants and the days; he won the forest trees and the mid-air.
He shattered the strength [of the enemy] and drove away the disputants; then he became the tamer of those with overweening pride.

We invoke the auspicious Maghavan Indra, the most heroic in this battle for the acquisition of booty; the fierce one who hears us, for our protection in conflicts, who slays the Vṛtras and wins riches. //11//
The sacred hymns have risen up, seeking glory; O Vasiṣṭha, magnify Indra in the battle.
He who has spread out all things with his might—may he listen to the words of one such as me.
The cry has gone forth, O Indra, born of the gods, as the bounties are being distributed in the contest of voices.
For one's own life-span is not known among men; carry us across these very straits.
I harness the booty-seeking chariot with the two bay steeds; my prayers have reached him who accepts them with favor.
With his greatness, Indra forced asunder the two worlds, slaying the Vṛtras without a foe to withstand him.

Even the waters have swelled like barren cows; your singers, O Indra, have reached the eternal Law (*ṛta*). Come toward us as Vāyu with his teams of horses, for through our prayers you distribute spoils of war. //4//
May those exhilarating draughts, O Indra, gladden you—the mighty one who bestows abundant wealth—upon the singer.
For alone among the gods you take pity on mortals; O hero, rejoice at this libation!

Thus do the Vasiṣṭhas praise with hymns Indra, the bull whose arms wield the thunderbolt. May he, being lauded, bestow upon us wealth consisting of heroes and cattle; and may you all protect us always with blessings. //6//

The possessor of the *ṛjīṣa*, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the bull, the subduer of the swift, the impetuous king, the slayer of Vṛtra, the drinker of Soma—having yoked his two bay steeds, may Indra come hither; may he exhilarate himself at the midday libation.

O Indra and Bṛhaspati, drink the Soma, rejoicing at this sacrifice, O you who possess bull-like wealth! May the self-sustaining drops enter into you both; bestow upon us wealth consisting of all heroic sons. //1//
(2) May your swift-gliding, rapid-flying coursers carry you hither; come forward with your arms.
Sit upon the sacrificial grass; a wide seat has been prepared for you. O Maruts, rejoice in the sweet soma-juice.
(20.13.3) Let us fashion this hymn with our intellect for Jātavedas, who is worthy of it, as one fashions a chariot.
For his providence is auspicious for us in the assembly; O Agni, in your friendship may we never suffer harm. (3)
Come hither with these, O Agni, on one chariot or on various chariots, for thy horses are powerful;
bring the thirty-three gods accompanied by their wives according to thy wont, and rejoice! 4.
O matchless one, we, seeking your aid, call upon you—the wonderful one—for strength, as if bearing up something massive. //1//
Approach us for aid in this rite, O fierce one, you who have come to us as our bold protector;
for we, your friends, have chosen you alone, O Indra, as our victorious helper.
Him who brought this and that wealth to us in the past—I praise him for you;
O friends, [praise] Indra for our protection. //3//
The lord of the virtuous, master of bay horses, subduer of the people—he indeed has rejoiced;
may that Maghavan bestow upon us, his worshippers, hundreds of cattle and horses.
I offer a hymn to the most generous, the lofty one of vast wealth, whose strength is true and who is powerful—
to him whose bounty, like waters on a slope, is irresistible and whose all-encompassing power is ever-unveiled for the sake of might.
Then let all follow after your sacrifice; the libations of the one who offers oblations flow like waters down a slope.
When it has settled upon the mountain like a beloved thing, Indra’s golden thunderbolt is the shatterer.
To this formidable one, bring [oblations] with reverence at the sacrifice, like the radiant Dawn, for his great glory;
he whose domain, his name, and his Indra-power have been made into light, like a bay horse for the sake of leading.
(20.15.4) These we are, O Indra, praised by many, who move about having taken hold of you, O Lord of abundant wealth.
For there is none other than you, O lover of songs, who can sustain our hymns; as the two worlds [sustain all], so take pleasure in this our speech.
Great indeed is your heroic power, O Indra; we belong to you. O Maghavan, fulfill the desire of this singer.
The vast sky yields to your heroism, and this earth, too, bows before your might. //5//
O Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, you shattered that great and wide mountain into pieces with your bolt.
You released the obstructed waters so they might flow; truly, you possess all conquering power as your own alone.
Like birds plunging into water, guarding themselves, like the clamorous sounds of a thundercloud;
like waves breaking from the mountains, exulting, the hymns have resounded toward Bṛhaspati. //1//
Approaching with the cattle, like Bhaga he has led Aryaman, O Aṅgiras;
like Mitra among the people, he anoints the husband and wife, as Bṛhaspati anoints the swift horses in the race for booty.
The cows— obedient, hospitable, vigorous, desirable, golden-hued, and of faultless form— Bṛhaspati, having driven them forth from the mountains, brought out like barley from the granaries.
Sprinkling the womb of Order with honey, casting down the sun like a torch from heaven,
Bṛhaspati, lifting the cattle from the stone, split open the skin of the earth as if it were water.
With light, he has driven away the darkness from the mid-air, as the wind drives away the foam from the water.
Having seized Vala, Bṛhaspati brought forth the cows, as the wind scatters the cloud.

When Bṛhaspati shattered the strength of the reviling Vala with fires and fervent hymns, he seized that which was encompassed by his teeth as if by tongues; he made manifest the hidden hoards of the ruddy cows.
Bṛhaspati indeed discovered that secret name of these lowing cows which was hidden in the cave in their dwelling;
like a bird breaking open its egg, he himself brought forth the ruddy cows from the mountain.
They beheld the honey bound by a stone, like a fish dwelling in shallow water;
Bṛhaspati, having split it apart with a roar, drew it out like a cup from a tree.
He found the Soma, he found the sun, he found Agni; with his song of praise, he drove away the darkness.
Bṛhaspati tore out the marrow of Vala, who was embodied as cattle, as one might extract it from a joint.
As if the forests had been robbed of their leaves by winter, Vala, through Bṛhaspati, lamented for the cattle;
he performed an act that could not be imitated nor undone, since the sun and moon rise from each other. 10.
Like a dark horse with its white spots, the fathers adorned the sky with the stars; they placed darkness in the night and light in the day. Bṛhaspati split the mountain and found the cows. 11.
We have performed this homage to the rain-cloud which thunders repeatedly over the many [streams].
For he is Bṛhaspati; may he bestow upon us vigor through cattle, through horses, through heroes, and through men. 12.
Toward Indra, my thoughts—seeking the light of heaven, all yearning and united—have cried out.
They embrace him as wives embrace a husband, as they would a handsome youth, for the sake of the bounteous one’s protection.

(2) Indeed, my mind does not turn away from you; O much-invoked one, I have fixed my desire upon you alone. Like a king, O wondrous one, sit down upon the sacrificial grass (*barhis*); let there be a place for you to drink at this excellent Soma.
Indra is the overcomer of distress and of hunger; he alone, the bounteous Maghavan, rules over wealth and treasure.
These seven rivers flow down his slope, increasing the vigor of that impetuous bull.
Like birds alighting upon a tree with lush foliage, the exhilarating Soma drops, seated in the vessels, have settled within Indra.
Their vanguard, flashing with power, has found the light of heaven, the Aryan light for mankind.
The gambler does not recover his winnings at the game of dice as Maghavan won the sun, the prize of the contest;
no other than you, O Maghavan, neither one of old nor one of recent times, has been able to equal that heroic deed of yours.
At every settlement Maghavan has taken his stand; the Bull gazes upon the lowing of the people.
He at whose libations Śakra takes delight conquers his assailants with the potent Soma juices. //6//
As waters flow together toward the ocean, as streams flow into a lake, so the Soma juices have flowed toward Indra.
At his great dwelling, the inspired singers increase his power, just as rain nourishes the barley with its divine bounty.
Like a bull enraged, he rushed through the mists of air—he who made these waters the wives of the noble one.
That Maghavan found light for the man who presses the juice, for the swift-giving one who offers oblations. 8.
Let the axe be born forth together with light; may it be as easily milked as the ancient Order.
Let the ruddy one shine brightly with his radiance, pure as the bright sky; let the Lord of the True be resplendent.
O Much-invoked One, may we cross over ill-will with cattle, and all hunger with barley;
may we, as the first among kings, win riches through our own heroic band.
May Bṛhaspati protect us from behind, and from above, and from below, from the one who intends evil.
May Indra from the front and from the middle, as a friend to his friends, grant us wide space. 11.
O Bṛhaspati and you, Indra, you two are the lords of celestial wealth as well as that of the earth.
Bestow riches even upon the lowly singer who praises you; protect us always with your blessings. 12.
O Indra, we, your friends seeking you, yearn for you with this intent; the Kaṇvas praise you with hymns.
O Wielder of the Thunderbolt, I have thought of nothing else at this newest work of the skillful; indeed, I have conceived this hymn for you alone.
The gods desire one who presses the soma; they do not long for sleep.
Unwearied, they go toward his heedlessness. 3.
O Indra, O bull, we who long for you cry out to you;
know this of us, O Vasu.
Do not deliver us to reproach or to the words of the enemy; O Noble One, let my mental power abide in you.
(20.18.6a) You are a wide-spreading armor and a front-line warrior, O slayer of Vṛtra; (20.18.6c) with you as my ally, I speak in opposition.
For the slaying of Vṛtra, for strength, and for victory in battle—
O Indra, we turn you hither.
O Śatakratu, may the worshippers turn your mind and your eye toward us, O Indra. //2//
We invoke all your names, O Śatakratu, with every song, O Indra, for the overcoming of our adversaries. //3//
With a hundred powers of the one praised by many, we magnify Indra, the sustainer of the people.
I invoke Indra, who is invoked by many, for the slaying of Vṛtra, and for the winning of booty in battles. //5//
Be victorious in the contests for booty; we implore you, O Śatakratu. O Indra, [we call] upon you to slay Vṛtra.
In glories, in the winning of battles, in the overcoming of hosts,
and in renown— O Indra, be victorious over those who seek to harm us.
O Indra, Lord of a hundred powers, drink the most vigorous, brilliant, and watchful Soma for our protection.
O Śatakratu, those senses of yours which are among the five peoples—
O Indra, I choose them for you.
O Indra, come; win great renown and invincible splendor.
We cause your strength to increase.
Come to us from nearby, O Śakra, and also from afar;
O wielder of the stone, come here from whatever world is yours, O Indra.
Indra shall surely drive away the great fear that assails the limb;
for he is steadfast and all-seeing.
May Indra be gracious to us; may no evil reach us from behind;
may there be auspiciousness before us.
May Indra grant freedom from fear from all directions;
he is the conqueror of enemies, the one who observes all people.
(20.21.1) We bring forth this speech as a song for the Great One, for Indra at the dwelling-place of Vivasvat.
For never indeed have they found treasure like those who sleep; a poor hymn of praise is not commended among the givers of wealth. (1)
Thou art the opener of the stall for horses, O Indra, the opener of the stall for cattle, the opener of the stall for barley; thou art the powerful lord of wealth.
Thou who aidest men from of old, who art never wearied by those who desire nothing, a friend to thy friends—for him we sing this hymn. //2//
O powerful Indra, doer of many deeds, most radiant one, this wealth all around you is known to be yours alone.
Therefore, seizing it, bring it hither as the conqueror; do not let the desire of the singer who loves you go unfulfilled. //3//
With these days, with these drops, being well-disposed, warding off want with cattle and horses;
with Indra, rending the Dasyu with the drops, may we, with our enmities dispelled, seize upon nourishment.
O Indra, may we grasp wealth and food; may we grasp booty, many-glittering and reaching unto heaven.
May we grasp divine providence, which is rich in heroic strength, preeminent in cattle, and abundant in horses. 5.
Those exhilarations have gladdened you, those manly powers, O Lord of the Good, those Soma-draughts in the slayings of Vṛtra—
when for the singer who spreads the sacrificial grass, you, irresistible, struck down ten thousand Vṛtras.
With boldness you indeed go from battle to battle; you destroy stronghold after stronghold with your might.
When, O Indra, through your friendship with Nami, you struck down in the distance the sorcerer named Namuci.
You slew Karañja and Parṇaya with the most piercing path of Atithigva;
you shattered the hundred forts of Vaṅgr̥da, which were besieged by R̥jiśvan, O you who do not yield.
Of these [men] who approached you from Janarāja, accompanied by the kinsman Suśravas—
the sixty thousand, the ninety-nine— you, O renowned one, crushed with your chariot wheel so that they could not stand.

(20.21.10a) You protected Suśravas with your aids; O Indra, you protected Tūrvayāṇ with your rescuing powers. (20.21.10c) You made Kutsa, Atithigva, and Āyu subject to this great, youthful king for his subjugation. //10//
O Indra, may we, protected by the gods, be your most auspicious friends at the end;
we shall praise you, possessing excellent heroes through you, extending our life-span further and longer. //11//
O Bull, at the pressing, I pour out the pressed juice for you to drink;
satisfy yourself and enjoy the exhilaration.
Let not the foolish, seeking to harm you, nor those who mock you, deceive you;
do not favor those who hate sacred knowledge.
(20.22.3a) Here let these [soma juices], rich in milk, exhilarate you for great bounty; (20.22.3c) drink like a wild ox at a lake. 3.
Sing forth with song to Indra, the lord of cattle, as he is known—
to the son of truth, the protector of the righteous.
The bay steeds have been let loose upon the ruddy [mares] on the sacrificial grass,
where we shall raise our voices together in song.
For Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the cows have yielded the milk-mixture, the honey,
when he found it in the secret place.
Come then to us, O Indra, being invoked toward me for the drinking of the Soma;
come with your two bay horses, O wielder of the stone.
The Hotṛ has been seated, not according to the ritual order; the sacrificial grass has been strewn in succession; the pressing-stones have been yoked at dawn.
(20.23.3a) These prayers are being offered, O you who are borne by prayer; sit upon the sacrificial grass.
(20.23.3c) O Hero, partake of the sacrificial cake.
Delight yourself at these libations of ours, O slayer of Vṛtra, at these hymns and at our recitations, O Indra, lover of songs! //4//
The prayers lick the wide one who drinks the Soma, the Lord of Might—Indra—as mother cows lick their calf. //5//
So do you rejoice in the soma-juice for the sake of great bounty through your own body;
do not deliver your worshiper to reproach.
O Indra, we, seeking you and bearing oblations, sing your praises; and may you, O Vasu, be well-disposed toward us.
O Māra, release us; come hither, you who are dear to the tawny steeds. O Indra, self-sustained one, rejoice here! 8.
O Indra, may the two long-maned horses, dripping with clarity, carry you hither on a comfortable chariot to sit upon the sacrificial grass.
Come to our pressed soma, O Indra, which is mixed with milk— the one that, together with your two bay steeds, seeks you out.
O Indra, come to this exhilarating drink, pressed by the stones upon the sacrificial grass; will you not indeed satisfy yourself with it?
Thus have my songs gone forth from here, sent toward Indra,
to turn him hither for the drinking of the Soma.
We invoke Indra here with hymns for the drinking of the soma; will he not surely come through our songs of praise?
O Indra, these Soma juices have been pressed; accept them, O Śatakratu, within your belly, O possessor of wealth and horses.
For we know you, O Sage, as the winner of wealth, bold in battles;
therefore, we seek your favor.
O Indra, come with your bulls and drink this pressed juice of ours, mixed with milk and mixed with barley.
For you alone, O Indra, in your own dwelling, I urge the Soma for your drinking;
may this delight you in your heart.
We, the Kuśikas, seeking your aid, invoke you, O Indra, the ancient one, for the drinking of the pressed soma.
(20.25.1) First among mortals, O Indra, he goes forth with horses and cattle, well-protected by your aids.
You indeed fill him with even greater wealth, as the conscious waters flow from all sides toward the sea. //1//
The divine waters approach the Hotṛ’s station; they look down as if upon the vast expanse of space.
The gods lead the god-seeking man forward; like suitors, they take pleasure in him who loves the sacred word.
You have bestowed praiseworthy speech upon the two who, with uplifted ladles, worship as a pair.
Unrestrained, he dwells and prospers within your ordinance; auspicious is the power for the sacrificer who presses the soma.

Then the Aṅgirases first attained vital strength, they who kindled the fires through their skillful work with the sacrificial post. All the Panis' provisions for enjoyment the heroes found together: cattle and horses.
Atharvan first extended the paths with sacrifices; from that, Sūrya, the guardian of the vow, was born as the beloved one.
Uśanas Kāvya drove forth the cows together; we sacrifice to the immortal birth of Yama. (AVŚ 20.25.5)
Whether the sacrificial grass is trimmed for the sake of good offspring, or the hymn proclaims its verse in heaven,
where the pressing-stone speaks as a pious singer of praise— at that very moment, Indra delights in the arrivals [of the offerings].
I offer a true, forward-moving draught to the bull, for thee, O Lord of Bay Steeds, of the pressed juice, as thou goest forth.
O Indra, rejoice here with the milch-cows, being praised by all our prayers and with power.
In every endeavor, in every contest, we call upon the most powerful Indra as our friend for protection. //1//
May he indeed come if he hears us, with his thousandfold aids,
with strengths, to our invocation.
I invoke the man of many defenses from his ancient dwelling, whom your father invoked of old. (3)
They harness the ruddy, red-hued steed as he moves around those who stand still; the luminous realms shine in heaven.
They yoke to his chariot the two beloved bay horses, on either side of the poles—
red, bold, and carrying the hero.
Making a signal for the signal-less, O men, making a form for the formless,
you were born together with the dawns.
O Indra, if I alone were the lord of wealth as you are, my praiser would be a possessor of cattle. //1//
O Lord of Might, I would train myself for this wise man, I would wish to give to him, were I the master of cattle. //2//
O Indra, your bounty is like a cow for the sacrificer who presses the soma;
swelling with milk, she yields cattle and horses.
O Indra, there is no restrainer of your bounty, neither god nor mortal,
when you, being praised, desire to bestow wealth.
The sacrifice strengthened Indra when he spread out the earth,
making for himself a head-ornament in heaven.
We choose for ourselves, O Indra, the protection of you who have grown great and who have conquered all riches.
In the exhilaration of Soma, Indra extended across the mid-air and the luminous realms when he split Vala asunder. //1//
He drove the cows out for the Aṅgirases, making manifest those that were hidden;
he pushed Vala downward.
By Indra, the luminous realms of heaven were made firm and strengthened; they are steadfast and shall not be driven away. //3//
Like a wave of water exulting, the hymn speeds swiftly toward Indra;
your exhilarations have shone forth.
For you indeed, O Indra, are the increaser of the *stoma* and the increaser of the *uktha*; you are the bringer of prosperity to those who offer praise. //1//
May the two long-maned bay horses carry Indra to the drinking of the Soma,
to the sacrifice of the bounteous giver.
With the foam of the waters, O Indra, you struck off the head of Namuci,
when you conquered all rival hosts.
With your magical powers, O Indra, you shook down the Dasyus who sought to escape by leaping up and desired to climb to heaven.
O Indra, you who are the superior drinker of Soma, you have scattered in all directions the assembly of those who do not press the juice.
I shall proclaim your two bay steeds at the great assembly; I win for you, the conqueror, the desirable exhilaration.
Like beautiful clarified butter, he who pours it forth with his bay steeds—may our songs enter you, whose form is golden-bay.
For those who have sung together toward the golden source, urging on the two bay steeds as if to the celestial seat;
him whom they satisfy with bay steeds like milch-cows—sing a strengthening hymn to Indra, the lord of the bays.
His is that golden thunderbolt, made of iron, golden, desirable, and golden in his two hands;
radiant, with beautiful jaws, its fury and arrow golden—it is upon Indra that golden forms have been infused.
Like a beloved banner in the sky, the golden thunderbolt has been set aloft; it has expanded with speed like a rushing steed.
The iron one, with its golden jaws, struck the serpent; bearing the golden weight, it became possessed of a thousand flames.

O Indra, golden-haired one, you have been delighted by the ancient sacrificers who praised you; you take delight [in the sacrifice]. O you born of the golden ones, all that is yours is worthy of praise—your perfect and desirable bounty.
The two beloved bay horses carry Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the exhilarating one worthy of praise, to the intoxication in his chariot.
For him, for Indra, who delights in many libations, the golden Soma drops have flowed forth.
The bay steeds have brought [the chariot] sufficiently for the desire; the bay steeds, urging on the two swift bay horses, hasten toward the steadfast one.
He who proceeds at his pleasure with his bay coursers—he has attained his desire for the bay steeds.
Tawny-bearded, tawny-haired, made of iron, he who grew strong at the drinking of the *haris*;
he, the possessor of wealth, who with his tawny coursers shall carry us across all difficulties—he is the one who drinks the *haris*.
Whose two golden jaws, like two ladles, fly apart as he shakes them for the sake of strength;
when, having drunk of the exhilarating, desirable soma-juice, he polishes his two golden jaws over the prepared cup.
And indeed, from the seat of the beloved one between the two worlds, the Lord of the Bay Steeds has neighed like a courser for the prize;
for even the great Dhiṣaṇā was won by his might, and you have bestowed upon him great vital strength, even though he is already beloved. //5//
Desiring both worlds with your greatness, you take pleasure in every new hymn that is dear to you.
O Asura, make the beloved dwelling of the cow manifest for the golden Sun.
(2) Let the impulses of men bring you, the longing one, O Indra with golden jaws, upon your chariot.
Drink of the offered mead as you please, delighting in the sacrifice at the communal feast where the ten fingers [serve]. 2.
O Lord of the Bay Steeds, you have drunk of the pressed juices of former times; now this libation is yours alone.
Rejoice in the honeyed Soma, O Indra; pour it all at once, like a bull, into your belly.
Drink here, O Lord of the Bay Steeds, of the juice shaken in the waters and pressed by men; fill your belly.
O Indra, you for whom the pressing-stones have poured it out—you, who are borne by hymns—grow strong with these for your exhilaration.
I offer a true, forward-striding draught to the bull for you, O Lord of the Bay Horses, from the pressed juice for your journey.
Indra, rejoice here with the milch-cows, being praised with all our prayers and with power.

Through your aid, O possessor of power, and through your heroic might, the *uśij* who know the *ṛta*, bestowing vitality, have stood in the house with offspring, O Indra, praising you as those who share the feast. //3//
He who, as soon as born, was the first wise god and surpassed the gods by his creative power;
he at whose breath the two worlds trembled through the greatness of his manly might—he, O people, is Indra. //1//
He who steadied the trembling earth, who brought rest to the agitated mountains, who measured out the wide mid-air, and who propped up the sky—he, O people, is Indra. 2.

He who, having slain the serpent, set the seven rivers flowing; he who drove forth the cattle by stripping away Vala; he who generated fire between the two stones; he who is the destroyer in battles—he, O people, is Indra. 3.
He by whom all these things were made to fall, who cast the Dāsa race down into the depths;
he who, like a victorious gambler seizing his stake, took away the prosperity of the enemy—he, O people, is Indra. //4//

When they ask of that terrible one, "Where is he?", and people say of him, "He does not exist," he destroys the prosperity of the noble like a gambler's stakes; have faith in him, O people—he is Indra. //5//
He who is the impeller of the weary, he who is [the helper] of the emaciated, he who is [the protector] of the Brahmin who implores, of the singer;
he who is the protector of the one who has yoked the pressing-stones, the fair-cheeked one for the one who has pressed the Soma—he, O people, is Indra.
He under whose command are the horses, under whose are the cattle, under whose are the villages, and under whose are all the chariots;
he who begot the sun and the dawn, he who is the leader of the waters—he, O people, is Indra.
He whom the two contending armies invoke, the higher and the lower, both enemies alike; he whom two men mounted upon the very same chariot invoke separately—he, O people, is Indra. //8//
He without whom people do not conquer, whom they invoke for aid when fighting;
he who has become the counterpart of the universe, who shakes the unshakable—he, O people, is Indra. //9//
He who with his bolt struck down those who repeatedly committed sins against me while they were unaware;
he who does not grant boldness to the arrogant, he who is the slayer of the Dasyu—he, O people, is Indra. //10//
He who discovered Śambhara dwelling in the mountains in the fortieth autumn;
he who slew the dragon Ahi as he was displaying his power, the Dānu lying there—he, O people, is Indra. //11//
He who overthrew Śambhara with his arrows, he who drank the pressed juice from the beautiful vessel;
he in whom the many people sacrificing in the midst of the mountain fainted—he, O men, is Indra. 12.
He who, the bull with seven rays, the mighty one, released the seven rivers to flow;
he who, with the thunderbolt in his arm, struck down Rauhiṇa as he was scaling heaven—he, O people, is Indra. 13.

Even heaven and earth bow down before him; even the mountains tremble before his might—he who is the Soma-drinker, whose arms are bristling with the thunderbolt, who holds the thunderbolt in his hand: he, O people, is Indra. //14//
He who aids with his protection the one who presses the soma, the one who cooks it, the one who recites, and the one who exerts himself;
he for whom prayer is a source of strength, for whom the soma is intended, and for whom this gift is meant—he, O people, is Indra. 15.
Born, he has looked out from the lap of his parents; he knows not of a progenitor higher than his own.
He who, being praised by us, observes the laws of the gods—he, O people, is Indra.
He who desires Soma, the lord of bay horses, the patron from whom all beings tremble;
he who slew Śambara and Śuṣṇa, he who is the sole hero—he, O people, is Indra. 17.
O you who, even for the one who presses and cooks [the oblation], break open the prize of strength—truly, you are such a one;
O Indra, may we, ever dear to you and possessing heroic sons, proclaim our wisdom at the assembly.

To him indeed, the very powerful and swift one, I offer this hymn like a refreshing draught, to the magnificent Indra, who is equal to the *ṛc* verses; to him, the irresistible one, I present these most excellent prayers.

To him indeed I extend this like an offering; I bring forth a hymn of praise with skillful composition for the sake of relief. For Indra, the ancient lord, they polish their prayers with the heart, the mind, and inspired thought.
To him indeed I bring this highest praise with my mouth, a hymn that wins the light; with most liberal invocations and well-fashioned thoughts, I would magnify the patron who bestows wealth.
To him indeed I fashion this hymn, as a carpenter fashions a chariot for its master;
and songs well-recited for Indra, the bearer of songs, the all-impelling one, the wise.
For this Indra, with my tongue I anoint the hymn like a prize-horse seeking glory;
I shall praise the hero who dwells in the gift, the shatterer of forts whose fame is celebrated. //5//
For him indeed Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned the thunderbolt, most skillfully wrought and resounding for the battle;
with it, the lordly one, striking, found the vital spot even of Vṛtra—how great was his power! //6//
At the libations of his mother, he has immediately drunk the great draught and the choice foods;
the more powerful Viṣṇu stole the cooked meal, pierced the boar, and shot through the mountain like an archer.
For this Indra, even the divine wives, the consorts of the gods, wove a song of praise for his slaying of the dragon.
He has encompassed the two wide worlds, heaven and earth; they have not reached the limit of his greatness.
His greatness indeed has overflowed beyond heaven, earth, and the intermediate space.
Indra, praised by all, the self-radiant lord of the house, the self-shining and measureless, has grown strong for the battle.
By his very might, Indra shattered Vṛtra, who was roaring with fury, with his thunderbolt;
like cows released from their pen, he set free the flowing rivers, being intent on bestowing glory upon them.
At his fierce impetus the rivers were stayed when he hemmed them in with his thunderbolt.
Acting as a lord, bestowing gifts upon the worshipper, the victorious one made a ford for Turvīti.
For this Vṛtra, bring forth the thunderbolt with haste, O Lord of manifold power! Split him asunder like the joints of a cow, piercing through him so that the floods of waters may flow.
Proclaim now with new hymns the ancient deeds of this swift one,
when, brandishing his weapons for battle, he, roaring in his fury, destroys the enemies.
Out of fear of him, even the firm mountains and heaven and earth tremble at his birth.
Approaching the dwelling of the longing one, Nodhas has instantly become ready for heroic deeds.
To him indeed was this granted among them, since he alone, as lord of abundance, won it;
Indra aided the Sūṣi in the contest for the prize of horses, as he strove against Pretaśa at the sun.
Thus have the Gotamas fashioned these well-crafted prayers for you, O Indra, for your yoking of the bay steeds.
Bestow upon them a thought adorned with every beauty; may he who is enriched by prayer come swiftly at dawn.
(20.36.1) Him who alone is the one to be invoked by the people—that Indra, I shall celebrate with these songs;
him who rules as the bull, possessing manly vigor, the true hero, possessed of many wondrous powers, and victorious.

Him our ancient fathers, the Navagvas, the seven sages, incited with their prayers— the one who reaches the giver, the overcomer, who stands upon the mountains, whose speech is guileless, and who is most powerful through his thoughts.
We beg that Indra for this wealth—abounding in heroes, rich in men, and full of food—which is unfailing, undecaying, and heavenly; O possessor of bay horses, bring that to us so that we may rejoice.
Tell us that, O Indra: have your singers of old indeed attained your favor?
What is your portion, what is your food, O fierce one, you who cause distress, you who are invoked by many and possess much wealth, O slayer of the Asuras?
Seeking him, the trembling, eloquent song reaches toward Indra, who stands upon his chariot with the thunderbolt in his hand—
he who is the mighty grasper, the doer of great deeds, the giver of strength, the powerful one— so that it may find its way to him for nourishment.

O self-strong one, with this very magic power, with the mountain swift as thought, you shattered even the unshakable, the firmly fixed, and the solid strongholds by your own might, O exuberant one, with boldness.
With a new prayer, may we bring him near—the most powerful one, the ancient one—as of old;
may that Indra, the faultless and excellent bearer, carry us across all difficult passages.
For the person who acts with malice, you have set ablaze the earthly, celestial, and intermediate spaces.
O Bull, burn them from every side with your flame; for the hater of sacred prayer (*brahmadviṣ*), cause the earth and the waters to blaze.
You are the king of the heavenly folk and of the earthly world, O you of brilliant aspect.
Take the thunderbolt, O Indra, in your right hand; ageless one, you destroy all magical illusions.
O Indra, bestow upon us well-restrained, great, and unyielding prosperity for the overcoming of enemies—
that prosperity by which you, O wielder of the thunderbolt, made the Dāsa and Ārya Vṛtras, and the Nahuṣa tribes, easy to overcome.
O much-invoked one, wise ordainer, worthy of sacrifice, come to us with your teams of horses that bring all boons;
come quickly toward me with those which neither the godless nor the god can restrain.
He who, like a terrible bull with sharpened horns, alone causes all the peoples to tremble;
he who is the bestower of wealth upon every non-sacrificer, yet grants his own treasure to the one who presses the soma well. //1//
O Indra, you indeed protected Kutsa there, listening with your own body in the battle;
when you, bestowing favor upon the son of Arjuni, subdued the Dāsa Śuṣṇa and Kuyava for him.
O bold one, with your boldness you have protected Sudās, whose oblations were accepted, with all your aids;
you protected Trasadasyu, the son of Purukutsa, and Pūru in the winning of land and in the slaying of Vṛtra.
O you of heroic mind, with your bay horses, you slay many Vṛtras at the banquet of the gods when invoked by men;
you sent the Dasyus Cumuri and Dhuni to sleep for the sake of Dabhīti, so that he might easily slay them.
O wielder of the thunderbolt, these were your mighty deeds when you instantly [overthrew] ninety-nine fortresses;
you entered the hundredth for your dwelling, and you slew Vṛtra and Namuci.
Ancient indeed are those enjoyments of yours, O Indra, bestowed upon the liberal Sudās who offers oblations.
For you, the bull, I yoke the two vigorous bay steeds; may our prayers reach you, O you of many powers, and win us strength.
O powerful Lord of the bay horses, let us not fall into misfortune through you in this assembly;
protect us with your safe protections, and may we remain dear to you among the patrons.
O Maghavan, may we, your dear friends, rejoice under your protection in your favor. Subdue Turvaśa and Yadu; you who intend to perform a praiseworthy deed for Atithigva, sharpen your weapons!
Even now, O Maghavan, in your favor, men who recite hymns proclaim their songs of praise.
You who, through our invocations, have scattered the Paṇis—choose us for that very alliance.
(10a) These hymns of men, O most heroic one, are directed toward you as they bestow riches upon us;
(10c) for them, O Indra, be auspicious in the slaying of Vṛtra—be the friend, the hero, and the protector of these men. //10//
Now, O heroic Indra, being praised for your aid, strengthened by our prayer, increase yourself in body!
Bestow upon us strength and progeny; do you all protect us ever with your blessings. //11//
Come hither, for we have pressed it for you; O Indra, drink this Soma! Sit upon this sacred grass of mine. 1.
O Indra, let the two long-maned bay horses, yoked by prayer, bring you hither;
listen to our sacred invocations.
O Indra, we who possess the *soma*, being priests and possessing the *soma*, call upon you—the drinker of *soma*—as our ally, having pressed the juice. 3.
To Indra alone the singers have sung aloud; to Indra with hymns the chanters;
Indra the voices have celebrated. //4//
Indra indeed is joined with the two bay steeds, mingled with them, yoked by a word;
Indra is the wielder of the thunderbolt, the golden one.
Indra raised the sun high in the sky for far-reaching vision; he split the mountain open with his rays of light.
We invoke Indra for you from all sides, away from other people;
may he belong exclusively to us. //1//
In the exhilaration of Soma, Indra extended across the mid-air and the luminous realms when he split Vala asunder.
He drove forth the cows for the Aṅgirases, making manifest those that were hidden in the cave;
he pushed Vala headlong down.
By Indra, the luminous realms of heaven have been made firm and strengthened; they are steadfast and shall not be driven away.
Like a wave of water, O Indra, the exhilarating hymn speeds toward you; your intoxications have shone forth.
For you are seen united with Indra, having come together with him who is fearless— both of you joyful, possessing equal splendor.
With blameless, radiant [songs], the sacrifice honors the powerful one with the beloved hosts of Indra. //2//
Then indeed, according to their own nature, they have again assumed the state of embryos,
assuming names worthy of sacrifice.
With the bones of Dadhyanc, Indra, irresistible, struck down ninety-nine Vṛtras. //1//
Seeking the horse's head which was hidden away among the mountains, he found it at Śaryaṇāvatī.
Here they recognized the secret name of Tvaṣṭṛ’s cow,
thus, in the dwelling of the moon.
I have measured out my body from Indra— the eight-footed speech, nine-cornered, touching the eternal Order.
Both heaven and earth cried out after you as you roared,
O Indra, when you became the slayer of the Dasyus.
Rising up with vigor, having drunk, you shook your jaws;
O Indra, [you drank] the Soma pressed in the ladle.
Shatter all enemies; drive away oppressors and strike down those who seek to harm us.
Bring to us that desirable wealth.
O Indra, whatever desirable wealth has been cast away upon the rugged ground, upon firm earth, or upon the mountain slope— that bring hither to us!
Of that abundant gift of yours which all mankind shall know, bring hither that desirable wealth.
Let the singer praise with new songs Indra, the sovereign lord of the peoples, the hero who conquers men, the most bountiful. //1//
In whom all hymns of praise and all glories delight,
as the favor of the waters does in the ocean.
I seek to win him over with excellent praise— the eldest king, the doer of deeds in battle, the possessor of great strength— for the sake of gaining prizes.
This very thing you are gathering together; like a pigeon to its nest, you do not even heed that word.
O Hero, Lord of bounties, you who are borne by songs, may there be for you an abundance of true and pleasant speech as our hymn of praise. //2//
Stand up for our protection in this contest, O Śatakratu;
let us two speak together concerning other matters.
To the leader toward greater wealth, the maker of light in battles, the one who overcomes enemies in combat. //1//
May he, the much-invoked Indra, our deliverer, carry us across to safety by boat, beyond all enemies.
As such, O Indra, favor us with strengths; grant us both a path and guidance, and lead us toward happiness. //3//
We incite that Indra for the slaying of the great Vṛtra;
may he become the bull, the showerer of blessings. //1//
Indra is he who has been made for the act of giving; he is the most powerful, established in the exhilaration of the soma.
He is glorious, worthy of praise, and beloved by Soma.
Like a thunderbolt fashioned by song, he is powerful and unshakable; the lofty one has grown great, invincible.
To Indra alone the singers have sung aloud; to Indra with hymns the chanters;
to Indra the voices have cried out. //4//
Indra indeed is joined with the two bay steeds, mingled with them, yoked by a word;
Indra is the wielder of the thunderbolt, the golden one. //5//
Indra raised the sun high in heaven for far-reaching vision; he split the mountain open with his rays of light.
Come, O Indra, for we have pressed the Soma for you; drink this Soma!
Sit upon this sacred grass (*barhis*) of mine. 7.
O Indra, let the two long-maned bay horses, yoked by prayer, bring you hither;
listen to our sacred invocations.
O Indra, we who possess the Soma, being Brahmins ourselves, call upon you—the drinker of Soma—with our companions as we have pressed the juice. 9.
They harness the ruddy, bright one as he moves around those who stand still; the luminous realms shine in heaven.
They yoke his two beloved bay horses to the chariot on either side—
red, bold, and carrying the hero.
Making a signal for the signal-less, O men, making a form for the formless,
you were born together with the dawns.
Upward his rays bear aloft that god Jātavedas,
the Sun, so that everyone may behold him.
Those stars go away with the nights like thieves,
before the Sun who beholds all things.
His banners have been seen, his rays extending across the people,
shining like blazing fires.
O Sūrya, you are the one who carries us across, visible to all, the maker of light; you illuminate the entire radiant realm.
Facing the clans of the gods, facing the human races, you rise up;
facing all, so that the light may be seen.
O Purifier, with that eye wherewith you behold the people as they stir about,
you, O Varuṇa, look upon them.
You rise toward the sky, across the broad expanse, measuring out the day with your beams;
O Sūrya, you behold all living beings. 19.
Seven bay mares carry you in your chariot, O divine Sūrya,
you whose hair is flame, the far-seeing one.
The Sun has yoked the seven bright mares, the daughters of his chariot;
with them, his own team, he goes forth.
The longing songs pour forth splendor upon you, as milch-cows low toward their calf. //1//
These beautiful ones flow forth, mingling their milk with splendor,
like a mother toward her newborn, as if with her heart.
O purifier of the thunderbolt, bringing fame to the dying man,
bring to me long life, clarified butter, and milk.
This spotted bull has come; he has settled before his mother, and advancing toward heaven, he has approached his father. //4//
He moves within the luminous realms; from his out-breath and in-breath, the Great One has manifested the sun.
He shines across thirty stations; the bird has taken flight.
Day after day, at the break of dawn, he has established himself through the days.
When the Śakras have mounted their speech, you two seek to win the mid-air;
the bull has gladdened the gods.
Śakra has spoken an invincible word; be invincible!
O most bountiful one, rejoice in the highest heaven.
O Śakra, speak boldly; you who uphold the sacred law, you shine forth as sovereign, spreading the sacrificial grass while exhilarated.
We praise with songs that Indra of yours, the wondrous one who overcomes the assailants, who rejoices in the exhilarating juice of wealth—just as cows low toward their calf in the stalls. //4//

We quickly implore the celestial one, the bountiful giver, who is encompassed by powers, who is like a mountain rich in many enjoyments—granting us food, booty in hundreds and thousands, and swift possession of cattle. //5//
I beg you for that heroic power, that sacred prayer, for the sake of first awareness—
that by which you helped the *yatins* and Bhṛgu when the prize was staked, and by which you protected Praskaṇva.
That by which you released the great waters unto the ocean—that, O Indra, is your manly might.
That greatness of his is not to be attained at once, he whom the worlds have cried out after.
What newest song shall the mortal sing for the swift one of the flaxen plants?
For those who sing his greatness and his sovereign power have not yet attained the light of heaven.
When do those praising you strive toward the gods? Who among the seers is considered a sage?
When, O Indra, Maghavan, will you come to the call of the one who presses the juice, and when to the one who praises you? //2//
Sing forth to Indra, the bounteous giver, as he is known to you— he who, as Maghavan, rich in many treasures, bestows gifts upon his singers as if by the thousands.
Like Śatānīka, he advances boldly; he slays the Vṛtras for the sake of the donor. Like the streams from a mountain, the gifts of him who provides much nourishment overflow.
Sing forth for our assistance to the renowned Śakra, the bounteous giver,
who bestows desirable wealth upon the one who presses the soma and praises him, as if with a thousandfold gift.
His weapons are hundredfold and invincible; the great impetuous forces of Indra swell like a mountain rich in nourishment when the pressed juices have exhilarated him among the bounteous patrons.
We, having pressed the soma and spread the sacrificial grass like waters,
O slayer of Vṛtra, sit around you as your praisers at the outpourings of the filter.
When the Soma is pressed, O Vasu, the men who offer hymns sing out to you alone;
when, O Indra, will you come thirsting to the pressed juice as to your home, like a bellowing bull?
O bold one, with the Kaṇvas as your companions, bestow upon us thousandfold booty; O Maghavan, you who move among the people, we quickly implore you for that which is tawny-hued and rich in cattle.
Who knows him as he drinks at the pressed juice? What vital strength does he bestow?
It is this one who, exhilarated by the soma-plant, shatters the fortresses with his might, O fair-cheeked one.
Like a wild elephant in rut, you have established your course in many places;
no one can restrain you. Come to the pressed juice; you move as a great one through your might.
He who is fierce, unsubdued, firm, and prepared for battle—if Maghavan Indra hears the call of the singer, he will not stay away but shall come. //3//
In unison, they have fashioned and begotten Indra, the hero who overcomes all hostile armies,
for the sake of sovereignty— the most excellent in wisdom, the filler of the wide space, the fierce, the strongest, the powerful, and the swift.
The singers have raised their voices together for Indra, that he may drink the Soma;
for he is the lord of heaven, who increases [the world] through his power, being firm in his vows, and with his aids.
With their vision, the inspired poets bend the rim [of the chariot] toward the ram, chanting their songs;
well-shining, guileless, and impetuous, you are close to our ears along with those who sing hymns.
I call upon that Indra, the bounteous and fierce one, who ever possesses irresistible powers;
may he, the most generous and worthy of sacrifice, turn toward us with his songs, and may the wielder of the thunderbolt make all paths easy for our wealth.
O Indra, Lord of Light, those enjoyments which you brought from the Asuras—
O Maghavan, increase the one who praises this [deed] and those who have spread the sacred grass for you.
O Indra, that horse and cow, the imperishable portion which you hold, bestow it upon the sacrificer who presses the soma and gives the sacrificial fee; do not place it with the miser.
Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, has been strengthened by men for exhilaration and for power.
Him indeed we invoke in great battles and in small; may he protect us in the contests for booty. //1//
For you, O hero, are worthy of armies; you are the one who bestows much.
You are the increaser even of the small; you grant wealth in abundance to the sacrificer who presses the soma for you. //2//

When the battles arise and wealth is staked for the bold, yoke your two bay steeds that flow with exhilaration; whom will you slay, and whom will you establish in wealth? O Indra, establish us in wealth.
For at every exhilaration, he of upright intent has given us herds of cattle.
Seize for yourself much wealth with both hands; sharpen it and bring riches hither! 4.
Rejoice in the pressed juice for strength and for bounty, O Hero!
For we know you as the possessor of many riches; we have poured forth our desires toward you—therefore, be our protector. //5//
These people of yours, O Indra, nourish every desirable thing. For you, as the noble one, look upon the wealth of those people who do not give; bring that wealth to us.
For our protection, we invoke day by day him who fashions beautiful forms, like a well-milking cow for the milker.
Come to our libations; O drinker of Soma, drink of the Soma! O wealthy one, your exhilaration indeed bestows cattle. //2//
Then may we find your most intimate favors;
do not overlook us, but come to us.
Drink the most powerful, brilliant, and watchful Soma for our protection, O Indra, Lord of a hundred powers.
O Śatakratu, those senses of yours which are among the five peoples—O Indra, I choose them for you. //5//
O Indra, you have attained great renown; bestow upon us invincible splendor.
We cause your vital strength to swell upward.
Come to us from nearby, O Śakra, and also from afar;
O wielder of the stone, come here from whatever world is yours, O Indra.
Indra indeed shall drive away even great fear;
for he is steadfast and all-seeing.
May Indra be gracious to us; may no evil reach us from behind;
may there be prosperity for us from the front. //9//
May Indra grant us freedom from fear from all directions;
he is the conqueror of enemies, the one who observes all people.
Who knows him as he drinks at the pressed juice? What vital strength does he bestow?
It is this very one, the fair-cheeked, who, exhilarated by the soma-plant, shatters the fortresses with his might.
Like a wild elephant, he has established his course in many places through his gifts; no one can hold you back. Come to the pressed juice; you move as a great one with your might.
He who is fierce, unsubdued, firm, and prepared for battle—
if Maghavan Indra hears the call of the singer, he will not stay away but will come.
We, having pressed the soma and trimmed the sacrificial grass, like waters— O Vṛtra-slayer, we your praisers sit around you at the outpourings of the filter.
When the pressed juice is offered, O Vasu, the men who recite hymns sing to you alone;
when, O Indra, will you come thirsting to the pressed juice as our home, like a bellowing bull?
O bold one, with the Kaṇvas, do thou boldly strike out thousandfold booty;
O Maghavan, far-seeing one, we quickly implore thee for that which is tawny-hued and rich in cattle. 16.
Like people stretching toward the sun, may all partake of Indra’s wealth; as he is born and being born with power, we look toward our portion as if for our share.
Praise him who gives unimpaired bounty, the giver of wealth; auspicious are the gifts of Indra.
He does not frustrate the desire of the one who serves him, but impels his mind toward giving.
Truly great art thou, O Sūrya; truly great art thou, O Āditya. The majesty of thee who art great is celebrated; indeed, O God, thou art great. //3//
Truly, O Sūrya, you are great in fame; indeed, O God, you are great.
By your greatness, you are the divine Asura, the appointed priest of the gods, the pervasive and invincible light. //4//
Upward rise these most honey-sweet songs, these hymns of praise;
they are ever-conquering, winners of wealth, with inexhaustible aid, like chariots seeking booty. //1//
Like the Kaṇvas and the Bhr̥gus, like the sun, they have attained every desire;
magnifying Indra with hymns, the Āyus and the Priyamedhas have raised their voices.
Now his portion overflows like the wealth of a victor;
him whom Indra, the lord of bay horses, protects, no enemies can harm—he bestows skill upon the Soma-presser.
Place within those worthy of sacrifice a mantra that is not deficient, well-established, and beautiful;
even many snares do not overcome him who stands by Indra through his ritual action. 4.
For thus indeed you are one who possesses heroes, thus a hero and firm; thus may your mind be successful.
Thus has this gift been established by all the ordainers, O possessor of abundant wealth;
even evil things, O Indra, are with me.
O Lord of spoils, do not be sluggish like a weary priest; exhilarate yourself with the pressed juice mixed with milk.
For thus indeed is his generous bounty— overflowing, rich in cattle, and great—
like a ripe branch for the donor.
For thus indeed are thy manifestations and thy aids, O Indra, for one such as I;
they are instantly present for the donor.
For thus indeed are his desirable things: the hymn and the recitation must be chanted for Indra, for the drinking of the Soma.
We celebrate that exhilarating drink of yours— the bull-like, victorious one in battles,
the world-maker, O wielder of the stone, who possesses the splendor of gold.
By which you have found the lights for Āyu and for Manu;
rejoicing in this sacred grass (*barhis*), you shine forth.
Even now, those who offer hymns praise you as they did of old;
win for us the waters, whose lord is the bull, day after day.
Sing forth to him who is invoked by many and praised by many;
with songs, seek to win over the powerful Indra.
He whose great, twofold power sustains the two worlds— he, by his virile strength, [sustains] the mountains, the plains, the waters, and the sky.
As such, O King, much-praised one, you alone strike down the Vṛtras;
O Indra, so that we may attain victory and glory.
O peerless one, we, seeking your aid, call upon you—the wondrous one—for strength, as if bearing up a solid pillar. //1//
Come near to us for aid in this rite, O fierce one, who hast come to us as our ally, being bold;
for we, as friends, have chosen you alone, O Indra, as our victorious protector.
Him who brought this and that wealth to us in the past—him, Indra, I praise for you, O friends, for our protection. //3//
The lord of the good, master of bay horses, subduer of the peoples— for he indeed has rejoiced—
may that Maghavan bestow upon us, his worshippers, hundreds of cattle and horses.
Sing a *sāman* for Indra, for the inspired singer, the great one—the great [song]—for the upholder of the Law, the wise, the one worthy of praise. //5//
O Indra, you are the conqueror; you caused the sun to shine.
You are the maker of all, the god of all; you are great. //6//
Radiant with light, you went to the sun, to the luminous realm of heaven;
O Indra, the gods strove for your friendship.
Sing forth to him who is invoked by many, who is praised by many;
with songs, seek to win over the powerful Indra.
He whose great might is twofold has supported the two worlds— heaven and earth—
along with the mountains, the plains, the waters, and the sun by means of his virile power.
As such, you are the king, O much-praised one; alone you strike down the Vṛtras, O Indra, for victory and for the attainment of glory.
(20.63.1a) Now, whom among these beings shall we bring to fulfillment—Indra and all the gods?
(20.63.1c) May Indra, together with the Ādityas, fashion for us the sacrifice, our own bodies, and our progeny. //1//
May Indra, together with his troop, the Ādityas, and the Maruts, be the protector of our bodies;
having slain the Asuras, when the gods went forth, guarding their godhead. //2//
With our powers we have brought the sun hitherward; then indeed they beheld his vigorous self-power.
Through this may we win the strength ordained by the gods; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with heroic sons.
He who alone bestows wealth upon the mortal who offers oblations—the sovereign, the irresistible Indra—verily he is so. 4.
When will he trample with his foot the ungenerous mortal like a mushroom?
When indeed, O Indra, will you listen to our songs? //5//
For whoever, having pressed the soma, seeks to win you over from among many—
Indra alone possesses that fierce power.
O most powerful Indra, that exhilaration which is the greatest drinker of Soma and which is conscious—
that by which you strike down the devourer, for that we pray.
With that [power] by which you protected Daśagva, Adhrigu, Svarṇara, and Vepayan;
with which you protected the ocean—that we implore. 8.
By which you impelled the Sindhu and the great waters like chariots—
him we entreat so that he may travel the path of *ṛta*.
O Indra, come to us as our beloved, the ever-conquering, the unconcealable;
broad on every side like a mountain, the lord of heaven.
For you, O true drinker of Soma, have encompassed both worlds;
O Indra, you are the strengthener of the one who presses the juice, the lord of heaven. //2//
For you, O Indra, are the shatterer of eternal fortresses; you are the slayer of the Dasyu, the prosperer of Manu, and the Lord of Heaven. //3//
O Adhvaryu, pour forth of this sweet, most intoxicating juice;
for thus is the hero praised, he who ever prospers.
O Indra, driver of the bay steeds, no one has ever attained your ancient praise through power, nor through song. //5//
We, seeking glory, have invoked for you that Lord of spoils,
who is to be magnified by sacrifices that do not fail in their vitality.
Come now, O friends, let us praise Indra, the hero worthy of hymns, who alone surpasses all the tribes. //1//
To him who does not withhold the cow, who seeks cattle, the celestial one— to him speak a wondrous word sweeter than clarified butter and honey.
Whose heroic powers are immeasurable, and whose bounty cannot be encompassed—the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) surpasses everything like light. 3.
Praise Indra like Vyaśva— him who is waveless, the prize-winning steed, the controller,
who bestows the wealth of the noble upon the donor.
Thus now, O son of Vyaśva, praise the tenth and the ninth [Agni],
the one who is well-knowing and worthy of celebration among those who move.
For you, O wielder of the thunderbolt, know how to avoid the snares of Destruction;
day by day, you are pure like one who has stepped out from the footprints.
For the one who presses [the Soma] wins a dwelling from the abundance; for the one who presses indeed sacrifices away his enemies—the enemies of the gods, away his enemies.
The one who presses, a prize-winner unobstructed, desires to win thousands.
To the one who presses, Indra gives enduring wealth; he gives enduring wealth. //1//
May those manly deeds of yours never turn away from us; may your ancient glories not decay, nor may our strongholds decay.
Whatever wondrous, immortal sound of yours is ever new in age after age—O Maruts, bestow that upon us, and whatever is difficult to overcome, grant that which is difficult to overcome.
I honor Agni as the Hotṛ priest, the bountiful, the Vasu, the Son of Strength, Jātavedas— the wise one like Jātavedas— who, a god with a straight sacrifice, with a form directed toward the gods,
desires the radiant glow of clarified butter, of the offered fatness accompanied by his flame. 3.
Blended with sacrifices, with spotted deer and spears, the bright ones, dear to us, have set out on their journey while adorned with ointments.
Having sat upon the sacrificial grass, O sons of Bharata, O heroes of heaven, drink the Soma from the Potar’s cup.
O sage, bring the gods here; sacrifice and sit down, O Hotṛ, upon the three seats.
Accept the Soma-sweetness that has been set forth; drink from the Āgnīdhra and satisfy yourself with your portion. 5.
This [Soma] is for you, the increaser of the body’s manly strength; from of old, power has been placed within your arms.
Pressed for you, O Maghavan, brought for you—drink of this to your heart's content from the Brahmin.
Him whom I called upon before, him I call now; he indeed is to be invoked, he who is master of the name "Giver.
O Giver of Wealth, drink with the seasons the Soma-mead set forth by the Adhvaryus from the Potṛ’s cup. //7//
For our protection, we invoke day by day the one who fashions beautiful forms, like a well-milking cow for the milker.
Come to our libations; O drinker of Soma, drink of the Soma! O giver of cattle, the exhilaration of the wealthy one is indeed yours. //2//
Then may we find your most intimate favors;
do not overlook us, but come to us.
Go to the wise Indra, the invincible warrior, and ask him who is better than your friends. 4.
And let our revilers say, "We have turned away from others," while they offer worship only to Indra.
And may the people, O Wondrous One, call us fortunate;
may we abide in the protection of Indra.
Bring this swift one to the swift one, the glory of sacrifice, the delight of men, who flies on and gladdens his friend.
Having drunk of this, O Śatakratu, you became the slayer of the Vṛtras; you protected the prize-winner in the contests for booty.
We urge you on, the prize-winner in battles for booty, O Śatakratu;
O Indra, for the winning of riches.
To him who is a great source of wealth, easy to cross over, and the friend of the one who presses the soma—
sing to that Indra!
Come hither and sit down; sing forth to Indra, O friends who bring hymns of praise! 11
To Indra, the most frequent among the many, the lord of desirable things, when the Soma is pressed.
May he indeed come to our union; may he come for wealth and for inspired wisdom.
May he come to us with spoils of war. 1.
To him at whose conclusion of battle the enemies do not restrain his two bay steeds in the fray—
to that Indra, sing!
For the drinker of the pressed juice, these pure pressed juices go forth for his enjoyment— the Soma drops mixed with curds.
O Indra of noble power, you were born suddenly grown great for the drinking of the pressed juice, for the sake of preeminence.
O Indra, lover of songs, may the swift Soma juices enter you;
may they be a blessing for you, the wise one.
The hymns of praise have magnified you; the recitations have magnified you, O Lord of a hundred powers.
May our songs of praise magnify you.
May Indra, whose protection is imperishable, win this thousandfold prize,
in which all manly powers reside.
O Indra, lover of songs, let not mortals do harm to our bodies; as the sovereign lord, ward off the weapon of death.
They harness the ruddy, red-hued steed as he moves around those who stand still; the luminous realms shine in the sky.
They yoke his two beloved bay horses to the chariot on either side—
red, bold, and carrying the hero.
Making a signal for the signalless, O men, making a form for the formless, you were born together with the dawns. 11.
Then indeed, according to their own nature, they have brought forth the state of being embryos again,
assuming a name worthy of sacrifice.
O Indra, with those who shatter even what is firm and with those who carry you as their vehicle, you found the ruddy cows even in the cave. 1.
Seeking the gods, they have raised their songs toward the one who bestows wealth, according to their thought; they have praised the great, the renowned.
For you shall be seen united with Indra, having come together with him who is fearless— both of you joyous and equal in splendor.
With blameless, heaven-reaching [songs], the sacrifice shines with power, accompanied by the beloved hosts of Indra. //4//
From there, O all-pervading one, come hither, or from the luminous realm of heaven;
our songs of praise strive toward him together. //5//
From here we seek the gift, or from heaven, or from the earth,
or from the great mid-air— Indra.
To Indra alone have the singers sung aloud; to Indra have the chanters chanted with hymns;
to Indra have the voices cried out. //7//
Indra indeed is with the two bay steeds, mingled with them, yoked by a word;
Indra is the wielder of the thunderbolt, golden-hued. //8//
Indra raised the sun high in heaven for far-reaching vision;
he impelled Indra forth with the rays of light.
O Indra, protect us in battles for booty and in contests for a thousandfold prizes, you,
the fierce one, with your fierce aids.
We invoke Indra in the great contest, Indra in the small; we call upon the wielder of the thunderbolt as our ally against the Vṛtras.
O Bull, O Ever-Conquering One, open up for us that vessel of oblation;
be irresistible unto us.
At every clash of the thunderbolt, the hymns of Indra, the wielder of the vajra, rise higher;
yet I find no adequate praise for him.
Like a bull among the herds, he drives the people with his might;
he is the sovereign lord, unopposed.
He who alone rules over the people, over the treasures—Indra, over the five tribes. //15//
We invoke Indra for you from all sides, away from other people;
may he belong to us alone.
O Indra, bring for our protection that most excellent wealth which is winning, ever-conquering, and victorious. 17.
By means of which we may, aided by you, strike down with our fists and hold back the Vṛtras with our swift horse.
O Indra, protected by you, may we take up the thunderbolt as a weapon;
may we completely conquer our rivals in battle. 19.
With brave archers and with you as our ally, O Indra, may we overcome those who attack us.
Great is Indra, and let his greatness extend even further to the wielder of the thunderbolt; in breadth, his power is like the sky. //1//
Or those men who have attained a state of delusion regarding the winning of offspring, or the inspired poets who are intent upon their meditations. //2//
That belly which drinks most Soma, swelling like the ocean, is like the vast waters from the palate of heaven. //3//
For thus indeed is his abundant, great, and cattle-bestowing bounty;
like a ripe branch, it is for the donor.
For thus indeed are thy powers and aids, O Indra, for one such as I;
they are instantly available for the donor.
For thus indeed are his desirable things: the hymn and the recitation must be chanted for Indra, for the drinking of the Soma.
O Indra, exhilarate yourself with the soma-juice through all the Soma-offerings;
you are great, a helper by your might.
Release him upon the pressed juice— for Indra who delights in it— the exhilarating one,
the doer of all deeds for the doer.
Rejoice, O fair-cheeked one, with our gladdening hymns, O you who belong to all people;
be present at these libations.
O Indra, songs have been poured forth for you; they have risen up toward you—the unsatisfied [songs] toward the bull, the lord. //10//
O Indra, impel toward us a wonderful and choice gift; may it be abundant and sufficient for you.
O Indra, impel us there toward wealth, making us zealous,
O you of many glories and great fame.
O Indra, bestow upon us wide and lofty fame, accompanied by cattle and strength;
grant us all-encompassing, imperishable life.
Bestow upon us high renown and splendor that wins a thousandfold;
O Indra, grant us those nourishments borne on chariots.
Praising with songs Indra, the lord of wealth, the one worthy of praise,
who comes to our aid— may we offer oblations for his protection.
At every pressing, for him who dwells within, the noble one sings forth a lofty hymn of strength for the great Indra.
For at all libations they urge you on—the seekers of the bull, each separately, desiring to win the light of heaven, each separately.
We set you, like a ship that carries us across, at the pole of our strength.
With sacrifices, men discern Indra; with hymns of praise, men discern Indra. //1//
Couples seeking your aid have spread themselves out for you, O Indra, as they strive to win the stall of cattle; may they overcome the obstacles, O Indra, as they strive to win them.
When you bring together two people seeking cattle or seeking heaven, you, O Indra, manifest the bull-like thunderbolt that accompanies you, the companion that accompanies you.
And may he be pleased with us at this dawn; indeed, take notice of our hymn and our oblations with our invocations, in the winning of the light with our invocations.
O Indra, when you, the bull armed with the thunderbolt, intend to slay the enemy, listen to this prayer of mine, the most recent of the worshipper, listen to the prayer of the most recent one. (3)
For you alone, O Hero, are all these libations; for you I fashion these strengthening prayers.
You are to be invoked by men at all times. 1.
O fierce Dasyu-slayer, never indeed do they attain the greatness of you who are so esteemed;
neither your heroism, O Indra, nor your bounty.
Bring forth [hymns] to the great one who increases the great; offer your devotion to the wise one. Go forth to the many clans, O filler of the people! //3//
When the golden thunderbolt and then the chariot that the two bay steeds of Yama draw, Maghavan, renowned from of old, mounts it with the patrons—Indra, the lord of far-famed booty. //4//
He indeed, Indra, the lord of the herd, together with his own rain, sprinkles his golden beard.
He seeks the well-dwelling place when the honey is pressed; he shakes it like the wind shakes the forest. //5//
He who with his word struck down many thousands of ill-omened, discordant, and foolish speakers—
that very manly deed of his we celebrate, he who, like a father, increased his power and his might.
For even though we are, O truthful Soma-drinker,
as if unpraised, O Indra, most wealthy one, do you indeed grant us a share of beautiful cattle and horses by the thousands.
O Siprin, Lord of spoils, possessor of power, through your wondrous deed,
O Indra, most wealthy one, do you indeed grant us a share of thousands of beautiful cattle and horses.
Lull them to sleep, you two of opposite appearance; let them lie down without waking.
O Indra, most wealthy one, grant us a share of a thousand beautiful cattle and horses! 3.
Let those enemies sleep; let the generous ones wake, O Hero!
O Indra, most wealthy one, grant us a share now in cattle, in beautiful horses, and in thousands.
O Indra, crush the braying donkey who bellows with that [same] cry.
O Indra, most wealthy one, grant us a share of a thousand beautiful cattle and horses! 5.
Let the wind blow far away from the forest with the *kuṇḍṛṇācī* plant;
O Indra, most wealthy one, grant us a share of a thousand beautiful cattle and horses!
Destroy every cry of reproach; crush Kṛkadāśva!
O Indra, most wealthy one, grant us a share of a thousand beautiful cattle and horses.
Couples seeking your aid have spread themselves out for you, O Indra, at the winning of the stall of cattle, releasing their efforts— releasing them, O Indra. When two tribes,

seeking cattle and seeking the light of heaven, clash together, you, O Indra, manifesting your presence, brandish the bull-like thunderbolt that accompanies you— the thunderbolt that is your constant companion.
The Pūrus have witnessed this heroic deed of yours, O Indra, when you overthrew the autumnal fortresses—you overthrew them, prevailing in battle.
Punish that mortal who offers no sacrifice, O Indra, Lord of Might!
You stole away the vast earth and these waters; rejoicing, you took these waters.
Then indeed they celebrated this heroic deed of yours in the exhilarations, O Bull, when you helped those who desired [you], when you helped those who were your friends.
You performed a great deed for them so that they might prevail in battles.
Desiring glory, they won one river after another; desiring glory, they won them.
Like a wheel set upon a tree, your pure hymn has awakened you two, O swift ones—
he whose Hotar-priest is Indra through many days, he who is the most heroic leader of men, the protector of the people.
May we be foremost at the dancing of this Dawn and of the future one; O most heroic of heroes, may we be so. May Triśoka bring a hundred men after him, and may the chariot that has won be with Kutsa.
What exhilarating draught has been for you, O Indra, that shall be pleasing? O fierce one, pour forth your songs toward the doors.
Or rather, what thought of yours comes hitherward to me? May I be able to bring you near with gifts and food, even unto the highest bounty.
(20.76.4a) What indeed is the glory of one like you, O Indra, among men? With what thought will you act? Why have you come to us?
(20.76.4c) Like Mitra, you are true, O wide-striding one; for the sake of sustenance, let the inspired thoughts of everyone be centered upon food. //4//
O Hero, drive forward like one seeking wealth to the further shore those who have come to fulfill his desire like wives to their husbands;
and those men, O Indra born of many powers, who honor your many songs with offerings of food. //5//
O Indra, your two mothers are well-measured: the vast heaven by your majesty and the earth by your wisdom.
For your choice, let the pressed juices mixed with ghee be sweet, and let the honeyed draughts be pleasant for your drinking.
They have poured out the vessel full of honey for this Indra, for he is truly bountiful;
he has grown great across the breadth of the earth, preeminent through his wisdom and manly deeds.
Indra, self-strong, has shattered the armies; many [people] strive for his friendship.
Mount him upon your chariot as in battles, whom you shall urge on with auspicious favor.
May the true Maghavan, the drinker of the dregs, come hither; may his bay steeds run toward us.
For him we have pressed the most skillful soma-juice; being praised, may he make his arrival here.
Descend, O Hero, as one does at the end of a journey; today, at this libation, may you take delight in us.
Like Uśanas, the wise ordainer shall recite a hymn—a prayer—for the conscious Asura.
Like a sage accomplishing secret insights, when the bull, drinking deeply, shall sing his outpouring;
thus from heaven he brought forth the seven singers, who by day, chanting, performed their sacred works. //3//

When the beautiful heaven was made visible with hymns, they caused the great light to shine at the break of dawn; the most heroic one, in his desire to help, has dispelled the blinding and turbid darkness so that men may see.
Indra, impetuous in his course, has grown to immeasurable strength; with his greatness he has filled both worlds, heaven and earth.
Even beyond that his majesty extends, for he has surpassed all existing beings. //5//
Śakra, knowing all manly deeds, released the waters with his eager friends;
those Uśij who split even the rock with their words threw open the stall filled with cattle.

You struck down Vṛtra who had enclosed the waters; the earth, being of one mind, favored your thunderbolt. You sent forth the oceanic floods; O hero, O bold one, you became their lord through your might.
When you, O much-invoked one, shattered the rock for the waters, Saramā appeared before you;
as such, being praised by the Aṅgirases, may you, our leader, burst open the cow-pens and bring us abundant booty. //8//
Sing that for you at the pressing, for the one invoked by many,
the warrior, which is as auspicious for him as it is for a powerful bull.
The Vasu indeed does not withhold the gift of wealth consisting of cattle,
when he has heard our songs.
May the slayer of the Dasyus indeed go to Kuvitsa’s cow-pen;
by his powers, may he open it for us.
O Indra, bring us wisdom, just as a father provides for his sons. Teach us, O Much-invoked One, on this path; living, may we attain the light. //1//
Let not unknown, malevolent, or unpropitious powers step upon us.
With you, O Hero, may we cross over the many flowing waters.
O Indra, bring us that most excellent, most powerful, and fulfilling glory,
