O fair-cheeked one, by which you, O wondrous wielder of the thunderbolt, have filled both these worlds, heaven and earth.
We invoke you, O King, the fierce one who subdues the peoples among the gods, for our protection.
O Vasu, make all our wavering things firm; make our enemies easy to overcome. //2//
If there were a hundred heavens, O Indra, and a hundred earths for you,
O wielder of the thunderbolt, even a thousand suns could not equal you at your birth, nor could the two worlds.
O Bull, Most Powerful One, you have filled all things with your greatness, your blackness, and your might.
O Maghavan, wielder of the thunderbolt, protect us with your wondrous aids in the cattle-pen.
O Indra, if I were the lord of as much wealth as you possess, I would surely provide for my singer; O dispenser of riches, I would grant him gifts and not leave him to misery.
Day after day may I train myself to bestow wealth upon the one who magnifies me, so that he may find it wherever it may be.
For there is no kinship better than yours, O Maghavan, not even a father.
O Indra, grant a triple-layered, threefold-protecting, and auspicious refuge; bestow a shield upon the patrons and upon me, and ward off the missile from them.
Those who, with minds intent on cattle, have deceived the enemy and strike him down boldly—
O Maghavan Indra, lover of songs, be our closest protector of the body against evil.
O Indra of wondrous luster, come! These pressed juices long for you, purified through the fine strainer in a continuous stream.
O Indra, come, impelled by our prayer and urged by the inspired singer,
to the sacred formulations of the worshiper who has pressed the soma.
O Indra, Lord of the Bay Horses, come swiftly to our sacred hymns;
take pleasure in our pressed soma.
Do not praise anything else, O friends; do not suffer harm.
Praise only Indra, the bull, when the soma is pressed; recite your hymns repeatedly.
Like a bull that does not grow old, who strikes down and overcomes the people like a cow;
the one who causes both hatred and reconciliation, the most bountiful, who possesses both [powers]. //2//
For although these people here invoke you in various ways for aid,
O Indra, let this our prayer be your strengthener through all the days.
The wise ones, O Maghavan, surpass the inspired songs of the noble folk.
Approach him who has many forms; bring us the most immediate strength for our protection.
With a sacred prayer, I yoke for you the two bay steeds, yoked by prayer, your swift companions who revel together;
mounting your firm and easy chariot, O Indra, come to the Soma as one who is steadfast and wise. //1//
O Adhvaryus, offer the ruddy, milked stalk to the bull of the people.
From the cow, Indra goes seeking the drinking place more familiar than any other; day by day he goes seeking the pressed Soma.
The lovely food which you have held from of old, you desire its drinking day after day;
O Indra, enjoying it with heart and mind, desiring it, drink the offered Soma juices. //2//
As soon as you were born, you drank Soma for the sake of victory; your mother proclaimed your greatness.
O Indra, you have filled the wide mid-air; through battle, you have created space for the gods.

When we fight against those who think themselves great, challenging them with our arms; or when, surrounded by men, O Indra, you shall fight against them—we would win that glorious battle through you.
I shall proclaim the first deeds of the Bountiful One, and those new ones which he has performed.
When he overcame the godless illusions, then Soma became his own alone. //5//
All this wealth of cattle all around belongs to you, whatever you behold with the eye of the sun;
O Indra, you alone are the lord of the cows. May we enjoy the wealth that you have extended to us.
O Bṛhaspati and you, Indra, you two are the lords of celestial and earthly wealth.
Bestow riches upon the one who praises you, even upon the humble singer. Do you all protect us always with your blessings. //7//
Bṛhaspati, who by his might suddenly propped apart the ends of the earth, he who dwells in the three abodes with his roar—
him, the sweet-tongued one, the ancient seers, the inspired sages, meditating, have placed before them.

Shaking off those who assail us with their ill-omens, O Bṛhaspati, while rejoicing in your excellent wisdom—those who have attacked us, protect the speckled, flowing, inviolable enclosure and its womb, O Bṛhaspati. //2//
O Bṛhaspati, from that which is the furthest distance, those who touch the cosmic order have sat down near you.
For you, the wells dug out and milked by the stones drip honey on every side toward the overflowing abundance.
Bṛhaspati, being born first from the great light in the highest heaven, seven-mouthed and many-born, blew away the darkness with his roar by means of his seven rays. //4//
With his well-praising, chanting host, Bṛhaspati shattered the enclosure and the firm rock with a roar; bellowing aloud, he drove out the lowing, milk-yielding cows.

Thus let us worship the Father, the possessor of all gods, the Bull, with sacrifices, with homage, and with oblations. O Bṛhaspati, may we, possessing good offspring and heroic sons, be masters of riches.
Like one who shoots a well-aimed arrow at a distant mark, bring forth a hymn for him as if adorning it.
O sages, cross over the speech of the enemy with your own voice; O singer, cause Indra to settle down upon the Soma.
Win over the cow with milking; O singer, awaken your friend Indra, the lover. Like a full vessel overflowing with wealth, bring down the hero for the granting of riches.
(20.89.3a) Why indeed, O Maghavan, do they call you a liberal giver? Sharpen me; I hear that you are the one who sharpens.
(20.89.3c) Let my inspired thought be fruitful, O Śakra! O Indra, bring us Bhaga, the finder of wealth. 3.
O Indra, people standing together in battle call upon you in their desire for possessions.
In this matter, the hero makes him his ally who brings oblations; he does not desire friendship with one who presses no soma.

For him who, providing sacrificial food, presses out for him abundant and surging Soma juices of intense flavor—early in the day, he strikes down his enemies with swift weapons; he slays Vṛtra along with his followers. //5//
In whomsoever we place our hope in Indra—that Maghavan who has directed his desire toward us—let his enemy, even though he be far away, tremble; let all human glories bow down before him.
Drive the enemy far away with that fierce *śamba* weapon, O you who are invoked by many!
Bestow upon us wealth consisting of barley and cattle, O Indra; grant the singer a prayer rich in prizes.
Into whom the strong-pressing, sharp Somas with abundant ends have entered during the race—that Maghavan, the giver, does not fail to bestow;
he brings much wealth to the one who presses the juice. 8.
Moreover, he who plays beyond the stake wins; like a gambler, he gathers his winnings in due time.
He who desires the gods does not withhold wealth; the god pours riches upon him with his own powers.
O Much-invoked One, may we cross over ill-will with cattle, or hunger with barley, O All-pervading One.
May we, remaining unharmed, be the first among kings to win riches through our communities.
May Bṛhaspati protect us from behind, and from above, and from below against the evildoer;
may Indra from the front and from the middle, as a friend to his friends, grant us wide space. //11//
He who is the mountain-shatterer, the first-born, the upholder of cosmic order, Bṛhaspati Āṅgirasa, rich in oblations;
he of the double stride, the father who sits at the *pragharma* sacrifice, the bull, roars aloud to the two worlds for us. 1.
Bṛhaspati has indeed created a wide space for the person who thus invokes the gods;
slaying the Vṛtras, he shatters the fortresses, conquering the enemies and subduing the adversaries in battles.
Bṛhaspati has won all treasures; this god has conquered the great pens full of cattle.
Desiring to win the waters and the light, the irresistible Bṛhaspati slays the enemy with his hymns.
Our father discovered this seven-headed, lofty hymn, born of the Eternal Order (*ṛta*). Indeed, the son of all people, Ayāsya, brought it forth while reciting the liturgy for Indra. 1.

Proclaiming the *ṛta*, meditating on the straight path, the sons of Heaven, the heroes of the Asura, the Aṅgirases, establishing the inspired word, conceived the first foundation of the sacrifice. //2//
Like swans, his shouting companions, Bṛhaspati cast off the stone-made bonds; he bellowed toward the cows, and being wise, he sang them forth and raised his voice in song. 3.

With two [steps] he helped, with one [step] beyond; the cows standing in the cave at the bridge of falsehood—Bṛhaspati, seeking light in the darkness, drove out the ruddy kine; indeed, he uncovered the three [worlds]. 4.
Having shattered the western stronghold, he cut open the three [treasures] together from the ocean.
Bṛhaspati found the dawn, the sun, the cow, and the light, like the thundering sky. //5//
Indra, with a roar, split Vala—the guardian of the milch-cows—as if with his hand;
seeking the milk-mixture with those whose limbs were anointed with sweat, he made Paṇi weep and stole away the cows.
With his true, radiant companions who win the wealth of cattle, he has shattered the enclosure of the cow-stall.
Brahmaṇaspati, with his bull-like boars that sweat from the heat of the ritual vessel, has distributed the treasure.
With truthful minds, seeking the kine, they impelled the Lord of Cattle with their prayers;
Bṛhaspati, with those who avert mutual reproach and who yoke themselves, released the ruddy cows.
Exalting him with auspicious hymns, like a lion roaring in its lair—may we rejoice in Bṛhaspati, the bull, the victorious one, in every battle for booty. //9//
When he won the prize of every form and ascended to the sky and the highest dwellings, we, being many and bearing light in our mouths, magnified Bṛhaspati the bull. //10//
Make our prayer come true, O Giver of Life; for you protect even the humble singer with your own ways.
Let all enemies fall behind us; hear this, O Heaven and Earth, you who encompass all.
Indra, by his greatness, split asunder the head of the great, surging Arbuda; he slew the serpent and released the seven rivers. O Heaven and Earth, together with the gods, protect us! 12.
Sing forth with song to Indra, the lord of cattle, as he is known—
to the begetter of truth, the protector of the good.
The bay steeds have been let loose upon the ruddy [mares] on the sacrificial grass,
where we shall raise our voices together in song.
For Indra, for the wielder of the thunderbolt, the cows have yielded the milk-mixture, the honey,
when he found them in his secret hiding place.
When we two, Indra and I, go up to the summit, the dwelling-place of the ruddy sun, having drunk of the honeyed mead, let us stay together in the thrice-seven places of our friend.
Worship him, worship him fully; O Priyamedhas, worship him!
Let the sons also worship him; worship him boldly, as if against a fortress.
The gargara resounds; the iguana has cried out all around.
Piṅgā has tinkled all around for Indra; the sacred formulation (*brahman*) has been raised up.
When the dappled cows, easy to milk and never-shaking, come flying hither—
seize the Soma, shaking it forth, for Indra to drink.
Indra has drunk; Agni has drunk; all the gods have become exhilarated.
Varuṇa indeed dwells here; to him the waters have cried out in response, like mother cows lowing toward their calf.
(20.92.9a) You are a good god, O Varuṇa, you whose seven rivers (20.92.9c) flow along the palate like [water through] a hollow reed-pipe. //9//
He who made the well-yoked horses leap forward for the donor— he, the leader, the swift one, was released as that very wondrous form.
Truly, O Śakra, Indra has overcome all enemies;
he split apart the young boy’s porridge as it was cooking beyond the mountain with his song.
Like a small child, a little boy, he has mounted the chariot;
he has brought the buffalo, the wild beast of great power, for his father and mother.
Come, O fair-cheeked lord of the house, and mount the golden chariot!
Then let us two go together toward the heavenly, thousand-footed, ruddy one who brings well-being and is free from harm.
To him indeed, the self-radiant one, the worshipful ones sit down nearby;
for his purpose is well-established, so that they may turn him toward them for the sake of giving.

The Priyamedhas have followed the ancient dwelling-place of these [gods]; following the former impulse, those who have spread the sacrificial grass and prepared the offerings have attained their goal.
The king of the people, who advances with his chariots irresistible,
the overcomer of all hostile armies, the eldest, who is praised as the slayer of Vṛtra— him I extol.
O Puruhanman, glorify that Indra for his protection, he whose thunderbolt was placed in his hand from of old by the Ordainer, beautiful to behold like the great sun in the sky. //17//
No one shall reach him with ritual action, he who has made [himself] ever-increasing—
Indra, who is praised by all, skillful, unassailable, and possessed of daring might, like [Indra] through sacrifices.
Invincible, fierce, victorious in battles, at whose birth the great, far-reaching ones lowed together— the milch-cows lowed, the heavens and the earths lowed.
O Indra, even if there were a hundred heavens and a hundred earths belonging to you,
O wielder of the thunderbolt, neither a thousand suns nor the two worlds could equal you at your birth.
O Bull, most powerful one, you have filled all things with your greatness, your virility, and your might.
O Maghavan, wielder of the thunderbolt, protect us with your wondrous aids in the cattle-pen.
(20.93.1a) May the hymns of praise gladden you; bestow bounty, O wielder of the stone!
(20.93.1c) Strike down those who hate the sacred word! 1.
With your foot, trample down the stingy ones who offer no gifts; you are great, for there is no one at all who can withstand you.
(20.93.3a) You, O Indra, are the lord of the pressed juices; you, O Indra, are the lord of the unpressed.
(20.93.3c) You are the king of all people. //3//
Moving to and fro, the active ones wait upon Indra at his birth,
having obtained great heroic power.
O Indra, you are born from strength, from power, and from might; O bull, you are indeed preeminent as a bull.
O Indra, you are the slayer of Vṛtra; you have extended across the mid-air; with your might, you have propped up the sky.
O Indra, you bear in your arms the hymn that is in harmony with you,
whetting the thunderbolt with your might.
O Indra, you are the conqueror of all beings by your might;
as such, you have pervaded all the worlds.
May Indra, the self-ruling lord, come for exhilaration— he who, impetuous by his own nature, is mighty, all-pervading,
and surpasses all powers with his boundless, great virility.
(2) Well-supported is your chariot; well-governed are your two bay steeds. O Lord of Men, the thunderbolt has been firmly grasped in your hand.
O King, come hither quickly by a fair path; we shall increase your manly powers through our nourishment.

May the powerful and mighty ones, borne by Indra, bring hither to us this fierce king with the thunderbolt in his arm, the bull who is most active and whose strength is true— the companions in revelry.
Thus you, the bull, desire for yourself as a lord one who dwells in the wooden vat, who is conscious, the pillar of strength, and the support;
exert your power, gather it within yourself, so that you may be the master for the increase of those who drink from the buckets.

May he come to us with riches, for I have praised him; bring the fulfillment of our own prayer! Come to the one who offers Soma! You are the master; sit upon this sacred grass (*barhis*). By your law, your vessels are inviolable.
The first invocations of the gods went forth separately; they performed deeds for glory that were difficult to surpass.
Those who were unable to board the sacrificial ship settled down like moths upon this very spot.
Let those others who are ill-disposed go away; let those whose ill-yoked horses have been harnessed depart.
Thus indeed are those others present for the giving, wherein there are many provisions and means of enjoyment.
He has held firm the mountains and the plains as they trembled; heaven roared and the mid-air regions shook.
He props apart the two converging bowls; having drunk of the bull, he proclaims hymns in his exhilaration.
I carry this well-fashioned goad of yours, O Maghavan, with which you shall break those who strike with their hooves.
May there be a welcome for you at this libation; O Maghavan, be present as a sharer in the pressed juice and the sacrifice.
O Much-invoked One, may we cross over ill-will with cattle, and all hunger with barley;
may we, as the first, win riches through the kings and by our own vigorous band.
May Bṛhaspati protect us from behind, and from above, and from below against the evildoer;
may Indra from the front and from the middle, as a friend to his friends, grant us wide space. //11//

At the Trikadruka festivals, the mighty buffalo, possessing great strength, drank his fill of the barley-mixed Soma pressed by Viṣṇu, according to his desire. It exhilarated him for the sake of performing a great deed; it followed him—the great and wide one. Thus the true drop attended upon the true god Indra. 1.

Sing forth this strengthening hymn for this Indra, whose chariot is foremost; even in close combat, he is the maker of space, the slayer of Vṛtra in the clash of battles. Be our inspirer! May the bowstrings of our enemies snap upon their bows! 2.

You released the rivers to flow downward; you slew the serpent. O Indra, you were born without an enemy; you nourish every desirable thing. We embrace you; let the bowstrings of our adversaries snap upon their bows. 3.
May all hostilities be utterly dispersed; may the prayers of our noble patron reach us.
O Indra, you are the hurler of the weapon at the enemy who seeks to slay us; let that gift of yours which bestows wealth be ours.
May the bowstrings of our adversaries snap upon their bows! 4.
Drink of this intense, highly potent [soma]; unyoke your two bay horses here along with all your chariot.
O Indra, let not other sacrificers detain you; these pressed juices are for you alone. //1//
For you the juices have been pressed, and for you they shall be pressed; the strengthening songs call upon you.
O Indra, taking pleasure today in this libation, you who know all things, drink the Soma here.
Whosoever, desiring the gods, presses Soma for him with a longing mind and with his whole heart—for him Indra does not give up his cattle; he makes that [Soma] praised and pleasing for him. //3//

He is clearly marked out by this [deity] who, though wealthy, does not press Soma for him. Maghavan casts him down into the pit; he slays the haters of the sacred word (*brahman*) without being commanded. //4//
Desiring horses, desiring cattle, and desiring booty, we call upon you to come to us.
Abiding in your new favor, O Indra, may we invoke you for our welfare.
I release you with this oblation so that you may live, from unknown consumption and from royal consumption.
If the Grāhi has seized him here, O Indra and Agni, release him from her!

Whether his life has been exhausted, or he has passed away, or has indeed been brought into the presence of Death— I bring him back from the lap of Destruction, untouched by it, for a hundred autumns.
With the thousand-eyed, hundred-fold powerful oblation that bestows a hundred-year lifespan, I have brought him forth;
so that Indra may lead him through the autumns to the further shore of all misfortune.
Live a hundred autumns, increasing in strength; live a hundred winters and a hundred springs.
May Indra, Agni, Savitṛ, and Bṛhaspati grant you a hundred years; with this oblation, I have brought him back to a life of a hundred years. 9.
I have brought you back; I have found you. You have returned, renewed. O whole-limbed one, I have found for you your entire sight and your entire life.
May Agni, in harmony with the sacred word (*brahman*), the slayer of demons, drive away from here that disease which,
having an evil name, lies within your womb and your birthplace.
Whatever disease of evil name has settled upon your embryo or your womb—
Agni, together with the sacred word (*brahman*), has driven that flesh-eater away.

(13a) Him who strikes at you as you fly, him who strikes at you as you sit, (13c) him who seeks to kill you as you crawl, or him who seeks to kill you once you are born—that one we cause to perish from here. //13//
He who spreads apart your thighs and lies between the husband and wife—
he who licks the interior of the womb, him we cause to perish from here.
Him who, having been your brother or your husband, or having become your lover, lies with you;
him who seeks to destroy your offspring—him we cause to perish from here. 15.
Whoever lies down after having deluded you with sleep and darkness,
whoever seeks to destroy your offspring— him we cause to perish from here.
From your two eyes, from your two nostrils, from your two ears, and from your chin—out from the brain of your head and from your tongue, I tear away the consumption that dwells there. 17.
From your neck, from your uṣṇihā-vertebrae, from your breastbones, and from your spine; from your shoulders and from your arms, I tear away the consumption that affects your forearms. 18.
From your heart, from your lungs, from your gallbladder, and from both your sides;
from your kidneys, from your spleen, and from your liver—we tear away the consumption. 19.
From your entrails, from your intestines, from the rectum, and from the belly;
from both sides of your abdomen, from the bladder, and from the navel—I pull the disease away from you.
From your thighs, from your knee-caps, from your heels, and from your forefeet—Yakṣma that dwells in the anus, and the disease of the buttocks, I tear away from your flesh. 21.
From the urethra, from the maker of the forest [the hair], from your body hairs and from your nails—from the entire self, that consumption (*yakṣma*) I now tear away from you. 22.
From your bones, from your marrow, from your sinews, and from your vessels—
from your hands, from your fingers, and from your nails— I tear away your consumption.
In every limb, in every hair, in every joint of yours—
whatever *yakṣma* resides in your skin— we root it out from all sides with the tearing-apart of Kaśyapa.
Depart, O Lord of the Mind; go away, O Desire, and move far off!
Look toward Nirṛti from afar; let the mind of the living man turn in many directions.
We have indeed nourished this wielder of the thunderbolt here;
therefore, bring him today the pressed juice in equal measure, and now attend upon him who is renowned.
Even the wolf, though he is a resistless devourer of sheep, abides within his appointed courses.
O Indra, graciously accepting this our hymn of praise, come hither with wondrous thought.
What manly deed of this Indra remains yet undone? By what renown has the slayer of Vṛtra not been heard of from his very birth? //3//
For we poets indeed invoke you for the winning of booty;
O Indra, lords of the brave, men invoke you against the Vṛtras, and you as the goal for our horses.
As such, O wondrous one, wielder of the thunderbolt, being boldly praised by us, O lord of the pressing-stones—
O Indra, bestow upon us cattle, horses, and chariots, like the total prize of victory for a conqueror.
O Indra, for the sake of the first draught, the Āyus have called out to you with hymns;
the R̥bhus, acting in unison, have raised their voices together, and the Rudras have sung in praise of the ancient one. //1//
In this [soma], Indra has increased his manly strength and power in the exhilaration of the pressed juice within the expanse of Viṣṇu.
Today, as in former times, men praise that majesty of his.
Now indeed, O Indra, lover of songs, we have released our great desires toward you, like those going upward with water. //1//
O Hero, the prayers increase you as the young women increase a man with their charms;
O wielder of the stone, though you have already grown great, they strengthen you day by day.
They harness the two bay steeds of the impetuous one with a song upon the broad-yoked chariot,
the bearers of Indra, yoked by a word.
We choose Agni as the messenger, the invoker, the all-knowing, the one of skillful intellect for this sacrifice. (1)
With invocations they ever call upon Agni, Agni, the lord of the people,
the bearer of oblations, the beloved of many.
O Agni, being born, bring the gods here for the one who has strewn the sacrificial grass;
you are our invoker, worthy of praise. //3//
Worthy of praise, worthy of homage, visible even through the darkness—Agni, the bull, is kindled. 1.
Agni, the bull, is kindled like a horse that carries the gods;
him, the possessors of oblations worship.
O Bull, we who are bulls shall kindle thee, the bull;
O Agni, shining mightily. 3.
Praise Agni with songs for his protection, him whose flame is fierce;
O Purumīḷha, men praise Agni for wealth, and Agni for a well-shining dwelling. 1.
O Agni, come with the fires; we choose you as the Hotṛ-priest.
Let the extended ladle, full of oblation, anoint you, the most excellent sacrificer, to sit upon the sacrificial grass.
For toward you, O Aṅgiras, Son of Strength, the sacrificial ladles move at the rite.
We pray to Agni, the Son of Vigor, whose hair is ghee—the foremost in sacrifices. 3.
(20.104.1a) May these songs of mine, O Lord of abundant wealth, increase you;
(20.104.1c) the wise ones, pure and bright-hued like fire, have sung aloud with hymns of praise. //1//
This one, made mighty by a thousand seers, has spread out like the ocean.
True is that greatness of his; his power is celebrated at the sacrifices in the kingdom of the inspired poets.
May Indra, who is to be invoked in all battles, be present for us;
may the slayer of Vṛtra, the supreme victor, worthy of praise, attend our prayers and libations. 3.
You are the first giver of riches; you are the true one who acts as a sovereign lord.
We choose the alliance of the son of great power, the one of abundant splendor. //4//
O Indra, in battles you prevail over all adversaries; you are the slayer of the malevolent, the progenitor, and the conqueror of all. Overcome those who seek to overcome you.
The two worlds have followed after your surging might, as two mother cows follow their youngling.
All your rivals yield to your wrath when you, O Indra, strike down Vṛtra.
From here, for your aid, [we call] the ageless one, the hurler who is not hurled;
the swift victor, the striker, the best of charioteers, the unconquered one who increased the Tugryas. //3//
The king of the people, who advances with his chariots irresistible, the overcomer of all hostile armies, the eldest, the slayer of Vṛtra— he is praised.
O Puruhanman, glorify that Indra for protection, he whose thunderbolt was placed in his hand from of old by the Ordainer, beautiful to behold like the great sun in the sky. //5//
That great power of yours, O Indra, your vigor and your will—
Dhiṣaṇā sharpens the desirable thunderbolt.
O Indra, heaven increases your manly power, and the earth increases your fame;
both the waters and the mountains urge you on.
Viṣṇu, the lofty dwelling, Mitra, and Varuṇa praise you;
the host of Maruts exults after you.
All the tribes and all the Kuṣṭayas bow down before his wrath,
just as rivers flow toward the ocean.
His vital power blazed forth when he brought the two worlds together, Indra, like a hide.
With his hundred-jointed thunderbolt, the virile one indeed split asunder the head of the violently shaking Vṛtra. //3//
That indeed was the eldest among all beings, from whom was born the fierce one of brilliant valor;
as soon as he was born, he overcomes his enemies, when all his helpers rejoice after him.

Increasing in strength and possessing abundant vigor, he, as an enemy, instills fear in the Dāsa. Both the non-moving and the moving he has won; they have shouted together at your offerings during the exhilarations.
They augment your abundant will when these helpers become twice or thrice [as many]. Mix that which is sweeter than the sweet with sweetness; with honey, overcome that [rival] with honey.
If indeed the inspired poets now rejoice after you as you win the spoils in battle after battle, O mighty one, exert your more powerful and firm strength; let not the evil-minded Kaśokas harm you.
Through you we prevail in battles, beholding many things worthy of combat.
I urge on your weapons with my words; I sharpen your vital powers with my sacred prayer.
Thou hast taken up that [power] in this lower and that higher dwelling wherein thou didst protect us with thy aid.
Set the swift Mother in her place; send forth many heroic deeds.
Praise him who dwells on the heights, whose paths are many, the skillful, the most powerful, the Aptya among the Aptyas.
He of abundant vigor shall display himself with might; he shall overcome the very measure of the earth.
May this priest Bṛhaddiva, seeking the light of heaven, perform a hymn of praise for Indra;
he rules as a self-sovereign king over the great stall of cattle, powerful, all-encompassing like the ocean, and full of fervor.
Thus has the great Atharvan Bṛhaddiva spoken to Indra as his own body;
the two stainless sisters dwelling in the mother [earth] impel him and strengthen him with power.
The bright banner of the gods, the radiant face, the sun rises toward the quarters;
the maker of day, with his splendors, has overcome the darkness—the pure one has crossed over all difficulties.
The brilliant face of the gods has risen—the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni.
Sūrya has filled heaven, earth, and the intermediate space; he is the soul of all that moves and stands still. 14.
The Sun follows after the shining goddess Uṣas, as a youth follows after a maiden;
where pious men extend the ages for the sake of auspiciousness upon the auspicious. 15.
O Indra, bring to us strength and manly vigor, O Lord of a hundred powers, O far-seeing one;
bring a hero who conquers in battle.
For you indeed have become our father, O Vasu; you have become our mother, O Śatakratu.
Therefore, we seek your favor.
To you, O impetuous one, much-invoked, who seek the prize, I speak, O Śatakratu;
as such, grant us great heroic strength.
Thus do the Gaurī cows drink of the sweet, pervasive honey;
they who, moving in company with the bull Indra, rejoice for the sake of splendor—being excellent, they follow their own sovereignty.
These dappled cows, longing for his touch, mix the Soma;
Indra’s beloved milch-cows urge on his bolt, his missile, toward the wealth of self-sovereignty.
With homage, those wise ones serve his conquering power;
they follow his many ordinances for the sake of primordial awareness, according to his excellent self-sovereignty.
For Indra, the exhilarated one, let our songs resound around the pressed juice; let the poets sing the hymn of praise. //1//
In whom all glories rejoice, in whom the seven assemblies delight—
that Indra we invoke when the soma is pressed.
At the Trikadruka rites, the gods performed the conscious sacrifice;
may our songs of praise increase that very one.
Whether you, O Indra, rejoice in Soma with Viṣṇu, or with Trita Āptya, or whether you delight among the Maruts with the drops—[we offer this to you]. //1//
Or if, O Śakra, you take delight in the far distance or upon the ocean,
rejoice only in our pressed juice together with the drops.
Whether you are the strengthener of the one who presses the soma, O Lord of the Good, or of the sacrificer for whose hymn you take delight along with the drops. //3//
Whatever has risen today, O Vṛtra-slayer, toward the sun—O Indra, all that is under your control. //1//
Or rather, O Lord of the Good, though you have grown great and think, "I shall not die," even that thought of yours is indeed true.
Those Soma juices which are pressed in the distance, and those which are pressed nearby—
all of them, O Indra, you go toward.
May Indra hear both these words of ours from nearby;
may the most powerful Maghavan come with his focused thought to drink the Soma.
For the two worlds have fashioned him as the self-ruling bull for the sake of power;
moreover, you sit down as the foremost of those who are compared, for your mind desires Soma.
O Indra, by your very birth you have from of old been without a rival, without kin, and without a friend;
yet through battle you seek companionship.
(2) You do not find the wealthy man for friendship; they revile you, O Surāśva.
When you make a roar and carry them away together, then indeed you are invoked like a father.
For from my father indeed I have seized the wisdom of the Eternal Order;
I have been born like the Sun. //1//
With an ancient thought, I adorn my songs like Kaṇva,
by which Indra has indeed assumed his vigor.
O Indra, those seers who have not praised you and those who have praised you—grow strong for me, being well-praised. //3//
May we not be like outcasts, O Indra, nor like strangers to you; O wielder of the stone, we have thought ourselves like forests abandoned to decay, difficult to overcome.
We thought ourselves slow and lacking in vigor, O slayer of Vṛtra;
yet, O Hero, through your great bounty we have been well-made. May we rejoice in our hymn of praise. 2.
Drink the Soma, O Indra; let that which the stone has pressed for you exhilarate you, well-guided by the arms of the presser like a war-horse.
That exhilarating draught of yours which is yoked and lovely, by which you slay the Vṛtras, O Lord of the Bay Steeds—
let that intoxicate you, O Indra, Lord of abundant wealth.
Take note well, O Maghavan, of this speech of mine, this hymn of praise which Vasiṣṭha recites for you. Enjoy these prayers at the shared feast. 3.
Be gracious to us, O Lord of Power, Indra, with all your aids; for we follow you, O Hero, the glorious finder of wealth, as we would follow Bhaga. //1//
The one who precedes the horse, the performer of many deeds for the cattle, is your golden spring, O God.
For no one can exhaust the gift within you; whatever I ask of you, bring that here. 2.
Indra alone we invoke for the assembly of the gods; Indra, as the sacrifice proceeds; Indra, like those seeking booty in battle; Indra, for the winning of wealth. //3//
Indra by his greatness has spread out the two worlds with power; Indra caused the sun to shine.
In Indra all beings have found their support; in Indra the pressed drops find their rest. //4//
The ancient hymn has been praised; speak the sacred prayer (*brahman*) to Indra.
Many lofty songs of Truth (*ṛta*) have resounded; the inspirations of the singer have been released. //1//
The swift, inspired singers have chanted the hymn that flows with honey and drips with ghee.
For us, wealth has spread forth, along with virile strength; for us, the pressed drops of Soma are flowing.
Whether you are invoked by men in the east, the west, the north, or the south, O Indra—you are the one who is truly much invoked among men; you are the bold one for Ānava and for Turvaśa.
Whether you take delight with Ruma, Ruśama, Śyāvaka, or Kṛpa, O Indra;
the Kaṇvas, bringing hymns of praise through their sacred formulations, draw you hither, O Indra—come!
We cry out to you, O Hero, like unmilked cows;
to you, Indra, the lord of this moving world, the beholder of heaven, the lord of all that stands still. //1//
No other like you exists—neither among the gods nor among mortals; none has been born, nor will there ever be.
O bounteous Indra, seeking horses and desiring cattle, we, the seekers of strength, call upon you. 2.
May there be for us, in our revelry with Indra, wealthy and abundant draughts of food, by which we may rejoice. //1//
O bold one, you who are like yourself, having come to us in person for the sake of your praisers, you have moved as swiftly as a wheel's axle.
When you, O Lord of a hundred powers, come to the service and the desire of those who sing your praises,
you turn [the wheel] by your mighty deeds as if it were a chariot-felly.

That is the godhead of Sūrya, that is his greatness: in the midst of his work he has withdrawn what was spread out. When he has unyoked his bay steeds from their station, then Night spreads her garment over all.
In the lap of heaven, Sūrya assumes that form of Mitra and Varuṇa for all to behold. One part of him is endless and radiant; the other, his dark portion, the green-hued ones bring together.
With what aid will the wondrous one come to us, he who is the ever-increasing friend? With what most powerful host? //1//
Which true one among the exhilarations, most bountiful, shall intoxicate you with the soma-juice?
He who shatters even the firmest wealth.
Come indeed as the protector of us, your friends and singers; may you be with us with a hundred aids.
(20.124.4a) Now, may we bring these worlds to fulfillment, O Indra and all the gods.
(20.124.4c) May Indra, together with the Ādityas, ordain for us the sacrifice, our own bodies, and our progeny. //4//
May Indra, together with the Ādityas and the host of Maruts, be the protector of our bodies.
Having slain the Asuras, the gods went forth, guarding their divine status. //5//

With our powers we have brought the hymn toward him; then indeed they beheld his vigorous self-power. Through this may we win the strength bestowed by the gods; may we rejoice for a hundred winters, blessed with brave sons.
O Indra, Maghavan, drive away our enemies to the east; O Overcomer, drive them away to the west.
Drive them away to the north and to the south, O Hero, so that we may rejoice in your wide protection. //1//
Surely, just as those possessing barley reap the grain in due order, separating it out, so bring here the food of those who have not come to the cutting of the sacred grass with their homage. //2//
For there is no chariot-pole for you when you come at the appointed time, nor has fame been found in your encounters.
Desiring cattle, the inspired singers seek Indra for friendship; desiring horses, they seek the bull while striving for strength. //3//
O Aśvins, lords of splendor, drinking deeply the surā-liquor from Namuci the Asura, you two aided Indra in his deeds. //4//
Like parents for their son, both Aśvins protected you, O Indra, with poetic wisdom and wondrous deeds;
when you drank the exhilarating Soma with your powers, Sarasvatī refreshed you, O Maghavan.
May Indra, the good protector, the possessor of wealth, through his aids, be gracious to us—he who possesses all knowledge.
May he drive away our enemies and grant us fearlessness; may we be masters of heroic vigor.
May he, the good protector, the self-strong Indra, drive the enemy far away from us.
May we abide in the favor of that worshipful one, and likewise in his auspicious goodwill.
For they have poured out from the presser, yet they did not regard Indra as a god;
where the bull-like Apsaras drank, my friend among the prosperities of the noble one—Indra is superior to all. //1//
O Indra, you run past the distress of Vṛṣākapi;
indeed, you find nothing else for the drinking of Soma. O Indra, you are superior to all. 2.
What has this Vṛṣākapi done to you, this tawny beast, that you are now envious of him? Whether it be the wealth of a nobleman or flourishing riches—Indra is superior to all. //3//
The dog that seeks wild boar shall now bite the ear of this Vṛṣākapi whom you, O Indra, protect as a dear friend. Indra is superior to all. 4.
The monkey has defiled my beloved, well-crafted, and polished [objects].
Now I shall rend his head; may I not be an easy path for the evildoer. Indra is superior to all. 5.
No woman has been more beautiful than I, nor more skilled in dalliance; no one has surpassed me in agility, nor excelled me in raising her thighs. Indra is superior to all. //6//
O Mother, O easily obtained one, alas, as if my limb were about to fail!
My mother, my thigh, my head—it all seems to tremble within me. Indra is supreme over all. //7//
(20.126.8a) Why, O Subāhu, fair-limbed one, broad-chested one, broad-hipped one?
(20.126.8c) Why do you, as the wife of a hero, threaten Vṛṣākapi on our behalf? Indra is superior to everyone. //8//
This malicious one regards me as if I were without a hero;
yet I am full of heroes, the wife of Indra, with the Maruts as my companions—Indra is superior to all. //9//

In former times, the woman went to the communal feast and indeed to the assembly. The ordainer of the cosmic order, the mother of heroes, the consort of Indra, is magnified. Indra is supreme over all. //10//
Among these women, I have heard that Indrāṇī is most fortunate;
for her husband shall never die of old age, nor even later. Indra is superior to all. 11.
O Indrāṇī, I have no joy without my friend Vṛṣākapi, he whose dear watery oblation goes to the gods; Indra is superior to all. //12//
O Vṛṣākapi’s wife, O wealthy one, you who have good sons and a good daughter-in-law—Indra shall eat your bulls, your dear oblation that brings all things into being; Indra is supreme over all. 13.
For fifteen oxen they cook for me all at once, even twenty;
and I eat fatness indeed; they fill both my flanks. Indra is superior to all. 14.
Like a sharp-horned bull bellowing amidst the herds, O Indra, this churning-drink is a joy to your heart, which the seeker presses for you; O Indra, you are supreme over all. 15.
He does not possess power whose member hangs limp between his thighs;
he possesses power whose hairy organ expands as he sits. Indra is superior to all. //16//
He does not master [the world] whose hairy member quivers as he sits;
he masters it whose member hangs down between his thighs. Indra is superior to all. //17//
O Indra, this Vṛṣākapi has found a slain wild beast;
he has found a sword, a slaughter-stool, a new cauldron, and a heap of fuel piled upon the firewood. O Indra, you are superior to all! 18.
Here I go, looking out and discerning both the Dāsa and the Ārya; I drink the soma pressed by the simple-hearted, and I have gazed upon the wise one. Indra is supreme over all. 19.
The desert and the ravine—how many *yojanas* apart are they?
O Vṛṣākapi, go home to your dwelling-place that is nearer; Indra is supreme over all. 20.
Come back again, O Vṛṣākapi; let us two arrange for our well-being.
You who go to your setting along the path that destroys sleep, Indra is superior to all. 21.
When you two, O Vṛṣākapi and Indra, went upward to the house, where was that beast so full of wealth? To what place did it go, that which brings people together? Indra is superior to all. 22.
Parśu by name, the daughter of Manu, gave birth at once to twenty [sons].
It was a blessing for her, even though her womb was in pain; Indra is superior to all. //23//
Listen to this, O people: Narāśaṃsa shall be praised. We have bestowed sixty thousand and ninety [cows] upon the Ruśamas at Kaurama. //1//
He whose draft-camels, provided with bridles, are twenty in number—
the height of his chariot, as it reaches toward heaven, causes the touchers [of the sky] to bow down in awe.
He has bestowed upon me for my arrow a hundred gold coins and ten garlands;
three hundred swift horses and ten thousand cattle.
Speak, O singer; speak like a bird on a ripe tree.
The tongue stirs in the lost [throat] like a razor in the hands of a barber.
The singers advance with inspired thought; like bulls they rush forward.
Their sons are not bound, and they sit like unbound cattle.
O singer, bring forward your inspired thought that finds cattle and finds wealth;
mix this speech for the gods, like a hero seeking to cross over with a boat.
For the king who belongs to all people, who surpasses both gods and mortals—
for Vaiśvānara, the dweller on high, press the well-uttered hymn of praise.
Enclosed, he made security for himself as he took to that seat;
building his nest, the Kauravya husband speaks with his wife.
Which of these shall I bring for you: curd, stirred drink, or the filtered soma?
The wife asks her husband in the realm of the king who dwells around his kingdom.
The ripe barley, facing heavenward, slips from its place on the path;
that person prospers in the auspicious realm of King Parikṣit.
Indra has awakened the artisan: "Arise and go among the people!
Praise me, the fierce one; let every enemy give you gifts."
Here let the cattle be born; here the horses, here the men.
Here Pūṣan himself, who bestows a thousandfold sacrificial fee, takes his seat.
O Indra, let these cows not suffer harm; let no one who guards them cause them injury. O Indra, let no hostile person nor any thief have power over them.
Do not take pleasure in us with your hymn, we [speak] with auspicious speech;
from the path of the forest, may our songs never come to harm at any time.
The man who is fit for the assembly, fit for the sacrificial rite, a presser of Soma, and a performer of sacrifice—
O gods, destroyers of enemies, you fashioned him first along with the sun and these two worlds.
When one seeks to harm a kinsman, or when a friend wishes to do evil;
when the eldest is devoid of wisdom—for all that, they say, "It is lower."
When the son of a blessed man becomes steadfast,
then the inspired sage has uttered that desirable speech, even as the Gandharva has.
The miser who is swift in conquest, and the one who does not worship the gods—of these, we have heard from the wise of old, "I have gone away from that. 4.
Those gods who have sacrificed and those who have bestowed gifts—
having ascended to heaven like Sūrya, may Maghavan roar for us.

He whose eyes are unanointed, who is unbesmeared, who has no jewels and no gold, who is without sacred formulation (*brahman*)—that son of the *brahman* is the singer praised in the ritual rules. //6//
He whose eyes are anointed, well-anointed, who possesses a fine jewel and fine gold, who is a true priest, the son of a priest—a praiser measured according to the ritual rules. //7//
The water-pools are without drinking-places, though they are full; the wealthy girl is beyond reproach. The auspicious maiden has been led away, she who is measured as equal to the sacred rites.
The reservoirs have excellent drinking places and are full of water, easy to access;
the maiden is beautiful, well-formed, and measured according to the ritual rules.
The discarded queen and the one who goes safely to battle— the swift one and the slow one, both measured out in their respective portions.
May the favorite wife and the chief queen go safely to the battle;
may the father-in-law and the son-in-law be joined together in the ritual ordinances.
O Indra, when you plunged into the human fray at the battle of the ten kings, Virūpa was on everyone's side; he is fit for the company of the Yakṣas.
O Maghavan, you made Vṛṣākṣu immortal, like the sun;
you rent Rauhiṇa asunder and split open the head of Vṛtra. 13.
He who established the mountains, he who plunged into the waters—he who is Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra; therefore, O Great One, let there be homage to you, O Indra. //14//
They spoke to Uccaiḥśravas as he ran behind the two bay horses:
"O well-faring horse, bring Indra, who wears a beautiful garland, for victory."
Those white, horseless, and famous ones who yoke thee, O Indra, as the right-hand steed— bearing them, thou, the first among the gods to be honored, exaltest thyself in greatness.
These mares leap forward. 1.
Against the one who presses [the Soma], against the opponent. //2//
Of them, one was Hariknikā. //3//
Hariknikā, what do you desire? //4//
A virtuous son made of gold. //5//
Where have you cast away that which was struck? //6//
Where those three *śiṃśapā* trees stand. //7//
(8) The three [fires] go around.
The adders. //9//
They sit blowing upon a horn.
This is your great course, O steed. //11//
He strikes the goat. 12.
"He strikes together, thinking, 'I am a possessor of cows, I am going among the cows. //13//
A man, you desire a woman. //14//
